items.title: Advances in personalized management strategies for ground-glass opacity–featured lung cancer
items.containerTitle: The Journal of Thoracic and Cardiovascular Surgery
items.abstract: Low-dose computed tomography has increased the detection of ground-glass opacity (GGO)-featured lung cancer. Evidence from radiologic-pathologic correlation, molecular profiling, and clinical outcome studies indicates that GGO-featured lung cancer is both a distinct clinical phenotype and a special stage in the evolution of lung adenocarcinoma. Its management differs from that of conventional solid lung cancer. As evidence accumulates for the surgical curative time window, selective mediastinal lymph node management, and active surveillance of multifocal GGO, the field is shifting from simple "early detection and early treatment" toward early precise intervention; from disease-centered treatment toward whole-course patient benefit; and from survival extension toward cure. The central strategy is to exclude benign or self-limited lesions, compare the lesion's natural course with the patient's life expectancy, and integrate nodule size, solid component, lesion location, frozen-section pathology, and expected pulmonary function loss to determine surveillance interval, surgical timing, and extent of resection. Under the concept of minimally invasive surgery 3.0, treatment should shift from maximally tolerated intervention to minimum effective treatment. This expert review summarizes recent advances in personalized management of GGO-featured lung cancer and discusses how surveillance, parenchyma-sparing surgery, selective lymph node management, and postoperative follow-up can be tailored to pursue cure while avoiding overtreatment.

items.title: Outcomes of Surgery After Neoadjuvant Chemoimmunotherapy in Selected N3 Stage III Non-small cell lung cancer: A Propensity Score-Matched Analysis
items.containerTitle: The Journal of Thoracic and Cardiovascular Surgery
items.abstract: Background While the conversion of unresectable stage III non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) to resectable status is a growing area of research, few studies have delineated the prognosis of clinical N3 patients undergoing surgery after neoadjuvant chemoimmunotherapy. This retrospective study compared the outcomes of stage III patients with NSCLC at clinical N3 who successfully underwent surgical resection after neoadjuvant chemoimmunotherapy with those of stage III N0-2 patients who received the same treatment followed by surgery in a matched cohort. Methods Drawing from a database of patients with NSCLC at Shanghai Pulmonary Hospital (2019-2023), we identified individuals with clinical Stage III (N3) disease, as well as those with Stage III (N0-2) disease, who underwent surgical resection following neoadjuvant chemoimmunotherapy. For these patients, after completion of neoadjuvant chemoimmunotherapy, mandatory re-biopsy of the originally involved N3 stations (via EBUS-TBNA or supraclavicular puncture) was required to confirm pathological negativity before surgical resection was subsequently performed only for cases validated as resectable by a multi-disciplinary team assessment. We utilized 3:1 propensity score matching to adjust for baseline imbalances between the study cohorts. The primary outcome was Disease-Free Survival (DFS). Results In the matched cohort, 57 patients with clinical Stage III (N3) NSCLC and 171 paired patients with clinical Stage III (N0-2) analysis showed that the objective response rate (ORR) was 62.2% in the N3 cohort and 69.1% in the N0-2 cohort. Additionally, the 3-year DFS rates were 67.2% vs 73.3% (hazard ratio = 1.37; 95% confidence interval = 0.76-2.49, P= .29). Further subgroup analysis revealed that the DFS rates of 22 patients with Biopsy-confirmed cN3 disease and 35 patients with PET/CT-confirmed cN3 disease were similar, and the 3-year DFS rates were 59.3% vs 72.2% (hazard ratio = 1.43; 95% confidence interval = 0.56-3.64, P = .45). Multivariate analysis suggested that pathological complete response (pCR) was an independent predictor of DFS prolongation in the N3 cohort. Conclusions For carefully selected patients with stage III (N3) NSCLC who achieve downstaging and undergo surgery after neoadjuvant chemoimmunotherapy, postoperative DFS is comparable to that of N0-2 patients, supporting surgical intervention as a component of multimodal therapy in this specific subset of patients who achieve surgical conversion.

items.title: The Congenital Heart Technical Skill Study: Can Peer Surgeon Assessment of Technical Skill Predict Outcomes?
items.containerTitle: The Journal of Thoracic and Cardiovascular Surgery
items.abstract: Objective Motivated to improve patient outcomes, we launched The Congenital Heart Technical Skill Study in 2015. In this proof-of-concept study, we sought to test the validity of leveraging single, representative, self-selected, video recordings of volunteer, operating congenital heart surgeons and a peer-review mechanism to assess surgeon technical skill. Methods In this national collaboration, volunteer surgeons submitted self-selected, "representative" videos of themselves performing: 1) Norwood procedures, 2) complete atrioventricular canal (CAVC) repairs, and/or 3) arterial switch operations (ASOs). Twenty-nine peer-surgeons from 21 centers rated pre-designated video segments, using a modified Objective Structured Assessment of Technical Skills Score (OSATS; scale 1-5). Operations were graded on five specific domains (gentleness, tissue exposure, instrument handling, time/motion, and flow of operation) and given summary scores. Scores were linked via NPI to all cases performed by participating surgeons over five contemporaneous years in The Society of Thoracic Surgeons-Congenital Heart Surgery Database. Logistic regression quantified risk-adjusted associations between skill scores and a composite outcome (major morbidity or mortality) among three, concentric, cohorts: 1) All Norwood, 2) all neonatal, and 3) all pediatric index cases. Models adjusted for clinical characteristics and clustered standard errors by surgeon. Results Seventeen surgeons from 14 centers submitted videos of themselves performing Norwood procedures (n=12), CAVC repairs (n=11), and ASOs (n=14). Over 5 years, these surgeons performed 234 Norwood, 1,755 index neonatal, and 8,559 index pediatric cases. Mean overall skill scores were 3.2 (SD ∼1.0) on Norwood, CAVC, and ASO videos. Scores correlated highly across sub-procedures (ρ's 0.8-0.9). Norwood and CAVC video scores were significantly associated with Norwood outcomes. One standard deviation increase in skill scores was associated with reduction in the risk-adjusted predicted probability of major morbidity or mortality among 5-years of surgeons' Norwood cases from 43% to 25%. Associations between skill scores and outcomes were weaker among all index neonatal and all index pediatric cases. Conclusions Congenital heart surgeons' technical skills can be measured directly via peer assessment of single, representative, self-selected, video recordings. These Congenital Heart Technical Skill Scores (CHTSS) are strongly associated with risk-adjusted morbidity-free survival across five years of surgeons' Norwood cases. This could serve as a valuable tool in surgeons' quest for technical mastery and-more importantly-in the quest to improve patient outcomes.

items.title: Are Bone Metastases A Contraindication? Role of Surgical Consolidation in EGFR-Mutated Stage IV NSCLC Patients Receiving Osimertinib
items.abstract: Background Prior studies suggested that osseous metastases (OM) may limit local consolidative therapy (LCT) benefits for stage IV non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). However, earlier cohorts were predominantly comprised of individuals lacking targetable oncogenic drivers. We evaluated the impact of pulmonary resection among EGFR -mutated stage IV NSCLC patients with OM receiving Osimertinib. Methods We conducted a single-center review of EGFR -mutated stage IV NSCLC patients with OM receiving Osimertinib from 2005-2023. Patients were stratified by pulmonary resection receipt. One-to-one propensity matching addressed demographic and clinical group differences. Outcomes were evaluated using Kaplan-Meier and multivariable Cox regression methodologies. Results 102 patients (51/group) were included, with similar median age of 60 years ( p =0.79). Median metastases were 3 (IQR:2-5) and 5 (IQR:3-8, p =0.10) for surgical and non-operative patients, respectively. Comprehensive LCT was more frequent among surgical patients (52.9% vs 15.7%, p <0.01). Among non-surgical patients, 26 (51.0%) underwent primary tumor radiation. At median follow-up of 37.9 months, median overall survival (OS) for surgical and non-operative groups were 60.2 (95% CI : 46.5-66.0) and 38.3 months (95% CI : 32.7-47.5, P =0.02), respectively. Median progression-free survival (PFS) was 31.8 (95% CI : 26.2-36.9) and 16.6 months for surgical and non-operative (95% CI : 12.2-23.9, P =0.03) patients, respectively. Pulmonary resection was independently associated with improved OS (HR=0.61, 95% CI : 0.38-0.89, P =0.01) and PFS (HR=0.72, 95% CI : 0.49-0.97, P =0.03). Conclusion Among selected patients with EGFR -mutated stage IV NSCLC and OM receiving Osimertinib, pulmonary resection was associated with improved outcomes. As such, OM alone should not preclude LCT consideration in this population.

items.title: All Strokes Aren’t Equal After Aortic Arch Surgery: Modified Rankin Score at Discharge is Associated with Long-Term Functional Outcomes
items.abstract: Objective Stroke remains a significant cause of morbidity following aortic arch surgery and is used by the STS as a key quality metric. We evaluated the utility of the modified Rankin score (mRS) to predict long-term stroke outcomes following elective aortic arch surgery. Methods A multi-institutional retrospective review was conducted of 930 patients undergoing elective hemiarch or zone 2 arch replacement at two high-volume aortic centers. Neurologic injury was graded using mRS and categorized as mild (mRS ≤2) or severe (mRS >2). Preoperative characteristics, operative variables, perioperative outcomes, and long-term neurologic outcomes were compared. Statistical significance was defined as p<0.05. Results Postoperative stroke occurred in 69 patients (7.4%). Stroke patients were older and had higher rates of diabetes, hypertension, and heart failure (p<0.05). They also experienced increased prolonged ventilation, tracheostomy, pneumonia, dialysis, in-hospital mortality, 30-day mortality (p<0.001), and readmission (p=0.02). Among stroke patients, 23 (33.3%) had mild stroke and 46 (66.7%) had severe stroke. At 3 months, complete neurologic recovery occurred in 66.7% of mild versus 30.2% of severe stroke patients (p=0.003). At 1 year, 86.7% of mild stroke patients were functionally asymptomatic compared with 50% of severe stroke patients (p=0.02). One year mortality was 52% in severe stroke patients versus 0% in mild stroke patients (p=0.003). Conclusion The modified Rankin score (mRS) effectively stratifies postoperative stroke severity and predicts long-term functional recovery and survival after aortic arch surgery. Incorporating stroke severity into surgical quality metrics may improve risk assessment and outcome reporting.

items.title: Tricuspid Valve Surgery in Hypoplastic Left Heart Syndrome: When and With What Outcomes?
Clinical Outcomes of Anatomy-Driven VSD Occluder Selection in Pediatric Patients: A Dual-Center Retrospective Study
items.abstract: Objective The choice between symmetric and asymmetric ventricular septal defect (VSD) occluders is primarily determined by aortic rim anatomy. However, the procedural characteristics and outcomes associated with each device when used according to this anatomy-driven algorithm have not been systematically described. Methods We retrospectively analyzed 426 pediatric patients who underwent perventricular VSD closure at two institutions over a 12-year period. Device selection was mandated by preoperative echocardiographic anatomy: symmetric occluders were used exclusively for aortic rim ≥2 mm (n=338), and asymmetric occluders for aortic rim <2 mm (n=88). Propensity score matching, inverse probability of treatment weighting were used to balance measured non-anatomical covariates. The primary outcomes were operative time, hospital stay, postoperative aortic regurgitation and arrhythmia. Results In this anatomy-driven cohort, the adequate-rim/symmetric-device pathway was characterized by a low incidence of increased AR grade, while the deficient-rim/asymmetric-device pathway was characterized by a 33% incidence of increased AR grade—all detected intraoperatively or before discharge and non-progressive on follow-up. Other complications were infrequent in both pathways. Conclusion In this anatomy-driven algorithm, each pathway had a distinct clinical profile. The adequate-rim/symmetric-device pathway carried a low burden of postoperative aortic regurgitation. The deficient-rim/asymmetric-device pathway carried an increased aortic regurgitation signal that was consistently mild, detected intraoperatively or before discharge, and non-progressive on follow-up; pre-existing aortic regurgitation did not worsen.

items.title: Machine Learning Performance and Fairness in Postoperative Atrial Fibrillation Prediction
items.abstract: Background Postoperative atrial fibrillation (POAF) occurs in 15-50% of cardiac surgery patients and is associated with increased morbidity and mortality. Risk scoring tools have been developed to predict POAF yet offer moderate discrimination performance. While machine learning models achieve better predictive performance, their fairness across demographic subgroups remains largely unexamined despite known racial and sex disparities in cardiac surgery outcomes. Methods We compared 9 risk scoring tools and 7 machine learning algorithms using data from 20,325 cardiac surgery patients (2010-2025), including >20% Black patients. Models used patient demographics, clinical conditions, and medications extracted from electronic health records. Performance was assessed using area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC) and area under the precision-recall curve (AUPRC). Fairness was evaluated across race (White vs. Black/Asian/Other/Unknown) and sex subgroups using demographic parity ratio (DPR) and equalized odds ratios (EQR). Results Machine learning models outperformed risk scores in discrimination (best AUROC 0.750 versus 0.614, p<0.001) but demonstrated lower racial parity. Random forest achieved highest AUROC but lowest racial fairness (DPR 0.236-0.790, EQR 0.205-0.693), while support vector machine balanced moderate discrimination (AUROC 0.703) with better racial fairness (DPR 0.572-0.868, EQR 0.562-0.870). Racial fairness varied widely among risk scores, from near-perfect to poor. Sex-based fairness was generally higher than racial fairness for ML models but inconsistent across risk scores. Conclusions Superior predictive performance may not guarantee equitable risk score. Future development of POAF prediction models must address the performance-fairness tradeoff through bias mitigation techniques and validation in diverse populations to prevent perpetuating healthcare disparities.

items.title: Optimal Temperature Determination in a Canine Model of Hypothermic Circulatory Arrest
items.abstract: Objective Hypothermic circulatory arrest (HCA) is required for certain aortic and cardiac operations, but postoperative neurologic injury remains prevalent. There is currently no consensus on the optimal temperature. We used a canine model to investigate neurologic outcomes after HCA at 18, 24, and 28°C. Methods Eighteen canines underwent peripheral bypass followed by prolonged HCA (90 min) at 18, 24, or 28°C (n=6, 5, and 7, respectively) with antegrade cerebral perfusion at 10 mL/kg/min. After HCA, animals were rewarmed, weaned from bypass, and extubated. Over three postoperative days (POD), behavior, cognition, and biomarkers were assessed. On POD 3, brains were removed for mitochondrial function testing and neuropathology. Results There were no significant differences between groups in behavior scores on POD 1-3. However, two 28°C animals had notable neurologic deficits, with none in the other groups. Cognition, assessed by novel object recognition, was not different between groups (all p>0.1). The 28°C group had increased serum enolase levels on POD 1 and 2 (both p<0.05). There were no significant differences in cellular respiration (all p>0.15). Prominent brain damage was noted without differences in regional or global neuropathologic injury between groups (all p>0.2). Conclusions Temperatures of 18, 24, and 28°C for prolonged HCA with cerebral perfusion yielded similar results for behavior, cognition, mitochondrial function, and neuropathology in this model after excluding one 28°C animal with severe injury. Neurologic deficits (n=2) and increased serum enolase in 28°C animals suggest that continued investigation of the safety of warmer temperatures for prolonged HCA is warranted.

items.title: Totally Endoscopic Mitral Valve Repair for Barlow’s Disease: Similar freedom from re-intervention to Isolated Posterior Leaflet Prolapse
items.abstract: Structured Abstract Objectives Totally endoscopic mitral valve repair (TE-MVR) is an established treatment for primary mitral regurgitation. However, TE-MVR in Barlow´s disease (BD) might be challenging due to its complex pathology. Herein, investigation of long-term outcomes after TE-MVR for BD is conducted and results are compared to TE-MVR for isolated posterior mitral leaflet (PML) prolapse. Methods Between 2012 and 2022, out of 1055 patients, 131 patients underwent TE-MVR due to BD (group 1) and 304 patients due to isolated PML prolapse (group 2) at our center. Baseline characteristics, surgical techniques and clinical/echocardiographic outcomes up to 10 years were retrospectively analyzed. Results BD patients were younger (group 1: 53.0±13.4 vs. group 2: 59.9±10.7 years, p<0.001) and more frequently female (46.6% vs. 31.6%, p=0.002). Cross-clamp time was longer in BD (110.8±38.3 vs. 103.1±32.2 min, p=0.046), cardiopulmonary bypass and procedure times were similar. Annuloplasty ring size was larger in BD (36.3±2.6 vs. 33.0±2.7 mm, p<0.001). Repair techniques in BD consisted of: neochordae to PML (55.0%), neochordae to AML (31.3%), leaflet resection (31.3%), Alfieri stitch (14.5%); 83.8% of PML patients received annuloplasty and neochordae to PML only. 30-day mortality was similar (0.8% vs. 0.3%, p=0.510). Ten-year survival (90.3% vs. 91.9%, p=0.879) and freedom from re-operation (95.5% vs. 97.8%, p=0.433) were similar. Conclusions TE-MVR in BD is safe and durable. Despite the need for more complex repair techniques, acute and long-term outcomes as well as durability were excellent. Durability of TE-MVR in Barlow's disease beyond 10 years of follow-up should be subject to further investigations. Abstract word count : 244

items.title: Aortic Valve Replacement During Acute Type A Dissection Repair: Bioprosthetic versus Mechanical, Does it Matter?
items.abstract: Objective Aortic valve replacement (AVR) is common during acute type A aortic dissection (ATAAD) repair, but preferences regarding prosthesis choice is unclear. We compared bioprosthetic and mechanical AVR and identified factors associated with valve selection and mortality. Methods From 1/2000-1/2022, 1,311 patients underwent ATAAD repair, 345(26%) included AVR (bioprosthetic N=289;mechanical N=56). Survival and reoperation, cumulative incidence estimated valve reintervention with death as a competing risk, and multivariable models identified factors associated with valve selection and with mortality including prosthesis type. Results Bioprosthetic recipients were older (64 vs 47 years, P<.001), less often had connective tissue disorder (9% vs 21%, P=.04), more often underwent extended aortic repair (26% vs 5.4%, P<.001), and had longer bypass times (189 vs 156 minutes, P<.001). Stroke was more frequent after bioprosthetic AVR (11% vs 1.8%, P=.03); in-hospital mortality did not differ statistically (12% vs 5.4%, P=.16). Ten-year freedom from valve reintervention did not differ; competing-risk incidence of reoperation was 18% versus 24% (P=.30). Unadjusted ten-year survival was lower after bioprosthetic AVR (47% vs 66%, P<.05), but adjusted for age, presentation, and complexity, prosthesis type was not independently associated (HR 1.11, P=.72). Conclusions Worse unadjusted survival after bioprosthetic AVR during ATAAD repair was associated with age, presentation, and operative complexity rather than prosthesis type; reintervention did not differ at ten years. We prefer valve sparing when feasible, a mechanical prosthesis in young patients with heritable aortic disease when it is not, and a bioprosthesis otherwise. Valve selection is not the driver of mortality risk is ATAAD.

items.title: Does Circulatory Arrest Add Operative Risk? A Propensity-Matched Comparison of Elective Hemiarch Replacement and Isolated AVR
items.abstract: Objective To determine whether brief-duration hypothermic circulatory arrest during elective hemiarch replacement is associated with increased perioperative risk or reduced long-term survival compared with isolated aortic valve replacement (AVR). Methods Adult patients undergoing elective hemiarch replacement (1993–2023) or isolated AVR (1993–2023) via primary sternotomy were identified. Propensity score matching generated 850 well-balanced pairs. Early postoperative outcomes were compared, and long-term survival was evaluated using Kaplan–Meier analyses. Temporal trends within the hemiarch cohort were also assessed. Results Among 850 matched pairs, mean circulatory-arrest duration in the hemiarch cohort was 19.3 ± 4.8 minutes. Operative mortality was low and comparable following hemiarch replacement and isolated AVR (0.7% vs 0.5%; P =0.75). Stroke occurred in 1.4% versus 0.5% of patients ( P =0.08), while long-term survival did not differ between groups ( P =0.30). Hemiarch replacement was associated with higher rates of postoperative atrial fibrillation (36.4% vs 30.2%; P=.009), pneumonia (2.5% vs 0.5%; P=.001), and prolonged ventilation (4.2% vs 1.6%; P=.003), as well as a modestly longer postoperative hospital stay (6.8 ± 3.7 vs 5.7 ± 2.6 days; P<.001). Within the hemiarch cohort, operative complexity increased over time, including longer cardiopulmonary bypass and cross-clamp times and more frequent aortic root replacement, yet operative mortality remained unchanged and postoperative stroke decreased significantly from 8.0% to 1.2% ( P =0.001). Conclusions Elective hemiarch replacement performed with brief-duration circulatory arrest averaging 20 minutes achieved operative mortality, neurologic outcomes, and long-term survival comparable to isolated AVR despite substantially greater procedural complexity and circulatory arrest. These findings provide contemporary outcome data to support consideration of hemiarch extension in appropriately selected patients when clinically indicated.

items.title: International Medical Graduates, Research and Residency: The Physician-Scientist Trajectory
Donor-Recipient Size Mismatch in Pediatric Heart Transplantation.
items.abstract: Objective To assess whether the association between donor-recipient total cardiac volume (TCV) mismatch and post-transplant outcomes is modified by etiology of underlying heart failure etiology in pediatric heart transplantation. Methods We identified isolated pediatric heart transplant recipients aged 1–17 years in the United Network for Organ Sharing database from 1987 to 2025. The association between TCV mismatch and post-transplant outcomes was evaluated using entropy-balanced, covariate-adjusted Cox proportional hazards models with restricted cubic splines for 1-,5-, and 10-year mortality conditional on 90-day survival and in the full cohort. Adjusted interaction analyses assessed heterogeneity by recipient heart failure etiology. Results Among 7,971 patients, TCV mismatch was associated with all-cause mortality at 1 year (P=0.022) and 5 years (P=0.014) among 90-day survivors, with significant nonlinearity (P=0.007 and P=0.004, respectively). TCV mismatch was not significantly associated with 10-year mortality (P=0.171) However, significant heterogeneity across etiologies of heart failure emerged at 10 years (P=0.021) and in full-cohort analysesDilated cardiomyopathy demonstrated a monotonic pattern characterized by relatively lower hazard with increasing mismatch, whereas congenital heart disease showed a distinct nonlinear pattern. No statistically significant dose-response relationships were identified at 10-years in less common etiologies. Conclusions In pediatric heart transplantation, the association between donor-recipient TCV mismatch and mortality varied by recipient etiology, suggesting that a single universal size-matching strategy may be overly simplistic. These findings challenge a unified size matching framework and suggest that the clinical significance of TCV mismatch may be etiology-dependent rather than uniform across heart failure etiologies.

items.title: Utilization and Outcomes of Root Enlargement and Aortic Valve Replacement in the United States
items.abstract: Background Aortic root enlargement (ARE) facilitates upsizing of prosthetic valves during aortic valve replacement (AVR) to reduce patient-prosthesis mismatch, particularly among women with smaller aortic annuli. We characterized national trends, outcomes, and interhospital variation in ARE utilization among patients undergoing isolated surgical AVR. Methods This retrospective cohort study used the 2017-2022 Nationwide Readmissions Database to identify adults undergoing isolated AVR with concomitant ARE, using the ICD-10-PCS. Temporal trends were assessed using Cuzick's nonparametric test for trend. Entropy balancing and multivariable regression estimated the independent association between ARE and outcomes. Multilevel mixed-effects models quantified hospital-level variation in ARE utilization. Results Of 182,467 isolated AVR hospitalizations, 16,406 (9.0%) involved ARE. While overall AVR volume declined (2017: 37,517 vs. 2022: 27,584), the proportion receiving ARE increased (7.6% vs. 9.4%, P<0.001), with divergent trends by age and sex. Following risk adjustment, ARE was associated with increased odds of in-hospital mortality (AOR 1.69, 95% CI 1.47-1.95), 30-day readmission (AOR 1.11, 95% CI 1.03-1.20), non-home discharge (AOR 1.18, 95% CI 1.09-1.28), and a $9,770 increment in costs. Risk-adjusted mortality decreased with increasing institutional volume. Hospital-level factors accounted for 23% of variation in ARE utilization, with rates rising nonlinearly to nearly 10% at the highest-volume centers. Conclusions ARE utilization is increasing despite declining overall AVR volume and is associated with modestly increased perioperative risk that appears attenuated at high-volume centers. Variation in ARE use across hospitals suggests unequal access, which may inform efforts to standardize referral pathways and expand training in this technically demanding procedure.

items.title: Evolution of Single Ventricle Assist Device Support Strategies for Stage II Physiology: A Single Center’s Decade of Experience
items.abstract: Central Picture Legend: Single ventricle assist device support for stage II physiology Central Message:Earlier VAD implantation with a staged continuous-flow-to-pulsatile strategy can achieve favorable survival to transplant in failing stage II single-ventricle physiology. Perspective StatementMechanical circulatory support for stage II single-ventricle physiology has historically been associated with poor outcomes.This series demonstrates improving survival through earlier implantation, staged continuous-flow to pulsatile support, and contemporary perioperative management, providing a practical framework for centers caring for this challenging population.

items.title: Risk Factors for Reintubation Following On Table Extubation in Congenital Cardiac Surgical Repair
items.abstract: Objective The objective of this study is to evaluate our experience with on-table extubation (OTE) following congenital surgery and identify risk factors for early reintubation. Methods Single-center, retrospective review of all patients undergoing OTE between January 2021 and February 2025. Patients who remained extubated were compared to patients requiring reintubation within 24 hours. Results 906 patients were extubated in the operating room with a median age and weight of 2 years (IQR 0.4-7.8) and 11.4 kg (IQR 6.4-24.3). Most patients (88%) had biventricular physiology (n=798). Cardiopulmonary Bypass (CPB) was used in 78% (n=709), and transfusion was avoided in 69.4% (n=629). Reintubation was required in 2.6% of patients (n=24). There was no difference in reintubation rates between CPB and non-CPB cases (3% vs 1%, p=0.13). 20% of neonates were extubated in the operating room (n=61) at a median 7 days (IQR 5-9) and weight of 3.3 kg (IQR 2.9-3.6). CPB was used in 30 neonates (49%). Transfusion was avoided entirely in 67% (n=41). Reintubation occurred in 4 patients (6.6%) and was not correlated with STAT category. Multi-variate logistic regression showed post-operative arrhythmia [OR 4.55 (CI 95% 1.84-11.26), p< 0.0001], and transfusion [OR 2.7(CI 95% 1.03-7.14), p=0.044] are independent predictors of reintubation. Age at repair, weight, gestational age, STAT Category, CPB time, Cross Clamp time, Intensivist, Anesthesiologist, and time of arrival to the CICU were not independent predictors of reintubation. Conclusions OTE is feasible, safe, and associated with low rates of reintubation, even in neonatal congenital repairs. Arrhythmia and transfusion are independent predictors of reintubation.

items.title: A Multidisciplinary Conference Routinely Changes Diagnostic and Therapeutic Care Plans for Thoracic Outlet Syndrome Evaluation
items.abstract: Structured Abstract Objective To evaluate the effect of a multidisciplinary case conference on treatment plans for patients with suspected thoracic outlet syndrome (TOS). Methods We performed an IRB-approved retrospective analysis of a prospective database. A monthly multidisciplinary TOS case conference was held over the study period. The treating physician recorded a proposed diagnostic and therapeutic plan for a patient with suspected TOS that was concealed until a multidisciplinary consensus plan was established by conference. The preconference plan of the individual physician was compared with the multidisciplinary consensus recommendation. The primary outcome was any change in plan. Secondary outcomes included diagnostic and therapeutic changes, consensus diagnosis, and implementation of recommendations. Results From September 1, 2024 to August 31, 2025, 12 conferences included 34 presentations for 29 patients. Suspected TOS was neurogenic in 22 presentations (64.7%), venous in 8 (23.5%), not otherwise specified in 3 (8.8%), and arterial in 1 (2.9%). Any plan change occurred in 25 presentations (73.5%). Diagnostic plans changed in 19 (55.9%), and therapeutic plans changed in 16 (47.1%). A consensus diagnosis of TOS was reached in 15 of 29 patients (51.7%). Diagnostic plan changes were not associated with any specific characteristic. Therapeutic plan changes were associated with treating specialty (P=.016). Recommendations were implemented for 28 presentations (82.4%). Conclusions Multidisciplinary consensus frequently differed from the treating physician's preconference plan. These changes were implemented in most cases. Thoracic outlet syndrome diagnosis was established in 51.7% of patients. Formal multidisciplinary review may improve diagnostic accuracy and coordinated management for patients referred for suspected TOS.

items.title: Intraoperative Alert Notifications Improve Perfusion Quality and Goal-Directed Perfusion During Cardiopulmonary Bypass
items.abstract: Background Goal-directed perfusion (GDP) during cardiopulmonary bypass (CPB) has been reported to reduce postoperative complications including acute kidney injury. However, conventional CPB monitoring systems lack individualized threshold settings and intraoperative alert notifications, which may delay corrective interventions when perfusion parameters deviate from target values. This study examined whether a CPB monitoring system with alert notifications could improve perfusion quality compared with a conventional system. Methods This retrospective study included 100 patients who underwent cardiac surgery with CPB between January 2023 and December 2025. Patients were divided into the Essenz group (n=50), managed with alert notifications, and the CONNECT group (n=50), managed without alert notifications. Perfusion quality indicators, including oxygen delivery index (DO 2 i), oxygen extraction ratio (O 2 ER), mixed venous oxygen saturation (SvO 2 ), and hemoglobin (Hb), were assessed using the mean, nadir (peak for O 2 ER), cumulative time, longest time of threshold violation, and cumulative area under/over the curve (AUC/AOC). Results No significant differences were observed in mean or nadir values of any perfusion quality indicator between the two groups. However, the Essenz group showed significantly lower cumulative AUC and largest AUC below the DO 2 i threshold compared with the CONNECT group (median, 184.0 [interquartile range (IQR), 34.1-453.2] vs. 383.4 [IQR, 179.2-754.7], p=0.013; 60.7 [IQR, 29.0-212.1] vs. 130.4 [IQR, 73.2-393.4], p=0.031, respectively). Threshold violation time and area were also significantly reduced in O 2 ER and SvO 2 . Conclusions A CPB monitoring system with intraoperative alert notifications significantly reduced the duration and magnitude of threshold violations across multiple perfusion quality indicators compared with a conventional system, suggesting that alert notifications may improve the quality of CPB management.

items.title: Aortic Calcium and Artificial Intelligence–Measured Ascending Aortic Diameter on Lung Cancer Screening CT: Mortality and Aortic Dissection
Does Off-hours or Weekend Transplantation Impact Pediatric Heart Transplant Outcomes?
items.abstract: We evaluated the role of temporal and institutional factors on pediatric heart transplant (HTx) outcomes. Using UNOS, we categorized first-time pediatric HTx patients (2005-25) into two: regular-hours (5am-10pm) and off-hours (10pm-5am). Primary outcome was 90d mortality. Secondary outcomes included 30d mortality, length of stay (LOS) and early (<72h) use of mechanical support. We also evaluated 90d mortality in high-risk groups as follows: a. weekend (Fri-Sun)+off-hours HTx, b. low-volume centers (<10 pediatric transplants/year), c. night-time (10pm-5am) procurement+off-hours HTx, and d. weekend+low-volume centers+nighttime procurement+off-hours HTx Out of 7832 transplants, 2316 (29.6%) were performed during off-hours. Baseline characteristics were similar for both groups, including mechanical ventilation (14% vs 14%, p=0.75), ECMO (4.1% vs 4.7%, p=0.24), and VAD (28% vs 28%, p=0.72). Outcomes were also similar in both groups including 90d mortality (7.6% vs 8.4%, p=0.19), median length of stay (21 vs 20 days, p=0.14), and early support use (1.0% vs 0.9%, p=1). In the sub-analysis of high-risk groups, 90d mortality risk was higher when transplants were done during off-hours on a weekend (9.8% vs 7.5%, p < 0.05) or when they were done during off-hours at low-volume centers (9.8% vs 7.5%, p < 0.05). Transplants done during off-hours+nighttime procurement+weekend+low-volume center had almost double the 90d mortality (13.2% vs 7.6%, p < 0.0005). While not affected solely by the time of surgery, off-hours transplants performed on weekends in low-volume centers with concurrent night-time procurement almost doubled the 90d mortality. These findings highlight the need for standardized peri-operative protocols during off-hour transplants in vulnerable settings.

items.title: Impact of Unplanned Coronary Interventions on Morbidity and Mortality in Aortic Root Replacement: A 20-Year, Multicenter Retrospective Study
items.abstract: Objectives This study aimed to evaluate the impact of unplanned coronary interventions (UCI) during aortic root replacement (ARR). Methods This retrospective study includes adult patients who underwent ARR at two centers between 2004 and 2024. Patients were stratified into three groups: isolated ARR, ARR + planned CABG, and ARR + UCI. The UCI group includes patients who underwent unplanned CABG during the index operation or postoperative CABG or PCI during the same hospitalization. Results Of 1,644 patients undergoing ARR, 153 (9%) underwent planned CABG for known atherosclerotic disease, and 52 (3%) underwent UCI. Endocarditis (aOR 2.66, p=0.07) was the strongest risk factor associated with UCI. Patients who needed UCI had worse outcomes compared to patients who underwent either ARR or ARR + planned CABG. Compared to isolated ARR, ARR + UCI was associated with higher odds of operative mortality (aOR 7.17, p < 0.001), renal failure requiring dialysis (aOR 3.64, p=0.008), and prolonged intubation (aOR 4.57, p < 0.001). Even when compared to ARR + planned CABG, ARR + UCI was associated with higher odds of operative mortality (aOR 9.91, p=0.001) and prolonged intubation (aOR 4.94, p < 0.001). Post-discharge survival did not significantly differ between the three groups. Conclusions UCI was associated with significantly increased perioperative morbidity and mortality associated with ARR, and is more common during surgery for endocarditis. However, patients with this complication who survive the index hospitalization do not have worse long-term survival. Surgeons should have a high index of suspicion and low threshold for intervening on suspected coronary issues during aortic root replacement.

items.title: The role of lymphangiography and thoracic duct embolization in the management of post-operative chylothorax
items.abstract: Structured Abstract: Objective Thoracic duct embolization (TDE) has been used for refractory chylothorax in patients unfit for surgical thoracic duct ligation (SDL). We hypothesized that TDE can be employed more broadly. Methods Retrospective review of postoperative chylothorax from 2018-2024. Data included, risk factors, chest tube outputs, and management. Descriptive, and univariate analyses were used to develop an algorithmic approach to chylothorax management. Results 73 patients developed postoperative chylothorax. The most common operations were pulmonary resection (n=27, 37%), and esophagectomy (n=24, 33%). 66 patients were treated with dietary modification (63 NPO, 3 low-fat) and 25/66 (38%) chyle leaks resolved. 40 patients had persistent chyle leak and underwent a procedure (35 TDE, 4 SDL, 1 sclerotherapy). Chest tube volume >=1130 mL before dietary modification (PPV 91%) and >=375 mL 48 hours after dietary change (PPV 97%) were predictive of failed conservative treatment. TDE was successful in 83% of cases (n=29/35) following failed dietary modification. Success of TDE did not vary by initial operation (p=0.69). There were 2 (2/40, 5%) major complications after TDE. Cisterna chyli cannulation (52% vs 83%, p=0.05), and successful intervention at lymphangiogram (65% vs 94%, p=0.05) improved over time (2018-2021 vs. 2022-2024). Conclusions Chest tube volume predicts failure and identifies patients who would benefit from early intervention. Within the context of our institutional capabilities, TDE is a safe and effective second line therapy regardless of the index operation. Technical success rates of TDE can improve over time with increased experience.

items.title: Mapping perfusion training and practice in Africa: a cross-sectional survey
items.abstract: Background Cardiovascular disease is a growing public health challenge in Africa, driven by an ongoing epidemiological transition and compounded by limited access to specialized care. While cardiac surgical capacity remains critically constrained, the role of perfusionists, essential for cardiopulmonary bypass and extracorporeal support, has received limited attention in workforce planning. Data on perfusion workforce availability and training pathways across the continent remain scarce. Objectives To map the availability of perfusionists, describe training pathways, and characterize cardiac surgical activity across African countries, to identify existing gaps and provide an overview of workforce organization. Methods We conducted a cross-sectional, web-based survey between December 2024 and July 2025 using a 28-item questionnaire distributed through perfusion networks. The survey collected data on national characteristics, workforce composition, perfusion training pathways, and cardiac surgical activity, including distinctions between permanent and mission-based services. Responses from African countries with populations exceeding 100,000 inhabitants were included. Partially completed questionnaires were retained and analyzed using available-case methods. Results Responses were obtained from 30 countries across all African macro-regions. Substantial heterogeneity was observed in perfusion workforce availability and training structures. Formal training programs were identified in 31.8% of countries and were unevenly distributed, while several countries relied on international missions or informal training pathways. Cardiac surgical activity varied widely, with 79.2% of countries reporting permanent programs, although capacity and volume differed markedly. National professional societies and regulatory frameworks were inconsistently present. Overall, the availability of perfusionists remained limited across many settings. Conclusions Major disparities in perfusion workforce capacity and training exist across Africa, reflecting broader inequities in cardiac surgical access. The absence of standardized training pathways, regulatory frameworks, and workforce benchmarks represents a key barrier to sustainable service expansion. Improving perfusion training and workforce structures may support the expansion of cardiac surgical care in Africa.

items.title: Boundary Lymph Node Metastasis Stratifies a Prognostic Intermediate Between R0 and R1 in Esophageal Cancer
items.abstract: Objectives The current residual tumor (R) classification for esophageal cancer relies on anatomical margins, which may ignore lymphatic residual risk. We aimed to evaluate the prognostic impact of boundary lymph node metastasis and introduce the uncertain resection (Run) classification. Methods We analyzed 3,730 patients who underwent esophagectomy with traditional R0 resection from 2018 to 2024. Boundary lymph nodes were defined as the highest or lowest resected nodes. Traditional R0 patients with positive boundary nodes were reclassified as having an uncertain resection (Run). We evaluated overall survival and recurrence-free survival. Results Boundary nodes were positive in 1,217 patients (32.6%). Positivity was associated with worse overall and recurrence-free survival in the original multivariable models, but not after stratification by pathological N stage (common hazard ratios, 1.17 and 1.04, respectively). Survival differed after excluding pN0 patients. Recurrence occurred in 26.3% of R(un) and 10.6% of boundary-negative R0 patients, with increases across local, nodal, and distant sites. Conclusions Boundary node metastasis identifies a higher-risk subgroup within traditional R0 resections. Its association with nodal burden limits claims of independent prognostic value. R(un) may complement margin assessment, but its biological interpretation and clinical utility require prospective validation.

items.title: Estimating Patient-Specific Benefits of Preoperative Statins in Aortic Valve Surgery Using Deep Learning Causal Inference
items.abstract: Objective Whether preoperative statins improve outcomes in cardiac surgery remains uncertain, arguing against uniform use and motivating patient-specific risk–benefit assessment. We evaluated patient-level heterogeneity in the modeled association between documented preoperative statin use and outcomes among patients undergoing aortic valve surgery. Methods We assembled a retrospective cohort of consecutive adults who underwent aortic valve surgery. Exposure was documented statin use within 24 hours before surgery. The preoperative-covariate model was designated the primary specification for the composite in-hospital outcome; the full perioperative model was secondary. Treatment overlap and characteristics of patients excluded for missing baseline data were assessed. Five-year mortality was examined descriptively with explicit accounting for incomplete follow-up. Results A total of 1,067 patients were analyzed, of whom 340 (31.9%) had documented preoperative statin use. The primary preoperative-covariate model estimated composite risks of 6.009% without statin and 4.449% with statin, corresponding to a risk difference of −1.560 percentage points (nominal 95% interval, −2.525 to −0.699). The secondary full perioperative estimate was −1.22 percentage points (95% CI, −2.22 to −0.26). Observed-range propensity-score common support included 97.8% of patients, although 15.0% had scores below 0.05 or above 0.95. Conclusions In this single-center cohort, documented preoperative statin use was associated with a lower model-estimated in-hospital composite risk in the preoperative-covariate analysis. These observational findings require external validation before clinical application.

items.title: Major Respiratory Complications After Pleurectomy/Decortication: Risk Factors and Association with Survival in Pleural Mesothelioma
items.abstract: Objectives To identify risk factors for major respiratory complications after pleurectomy/decortication for pleural mesothelioma and assess their association with survival. Methods We retrospectively reviewed 315 patients with pleural mesothelioma who underwent neoadjuvant chemotherapy and pleurectomy/decortication between September 2012 and April 2026. Major respiratory complications were defined as air leak lasting >10 postoperative days or Clavien–Dindo grade IIIb or higher respiratory complications. Logistic and Cox regression analyses were performed. Results Major respiratory complications occurred in 132 patients (41.9%). Male sex, lower body mass index (BMI), Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group performance status (PS) 1, and right-sided surgery independently predicted major respiratory complications. Patients with major respiratory complications had worse overall survival (median, 34.2 vs 60.8 months; 5-year, 33.6% vs 51.6%; P =0.0002) and progression-free survival (median, 19.8 vs 22.8 months; 5-year, 12.4% vs 18.2%; P =0.0063). The association between major respiratory complications and worse overall survival persisted in a 90-day landmark analysis ( P =0.0030). Multivariable Cox analysis identified non-epithelioid histology (HR, 2.42; 95% CI, 1.44–4.04), pathologic stage II–IV (HR, 2.34; 95% CI, 1.56–3.53), PS 1 (HR, 2.27; 95% CI, 1.48–3.50), major respiratory complications (HR, 1.45; 95% CI, 1.06–2.00), and lower BMI (HR, 1.07 per kg/m 2 decrease; 95% CI, 1.01–1.13) as independent predictors of worse overall survival. Conclusions Major respiratory complications are common after pleurectomy/decortication and independently associated with inferior overall survival. Male sex, lower BMI, PS 1, and right-sided surgery independently predict major respiratory complications and may help identify patients who warrant more careful preoperative risk assessment and optimization.

items.title: Maximizing the Promise of AI: Strategies for Governance?
items.abstract: As artificial intelligence is increasingly embedded in scholarly publishing, its promise will be realized through governance frameworks prioritizing transparency, integrity, and human accountability.

items.title: Sublobar Resection vs. Lobectomy for Patients with Clinical T1a-bN0M0 Non-Small-Cell Lung Cancer and Occult Nodal Metastases
items.abstract: Objective Sublobar resection is now considered appropriate for patients with ≤2cm non-small-cell lung cancer (NSCLC) who do not have nodal disease on preoperative imaging and intraoperative frozen section evaluation. It remains unknown whether sublobar resection is sufficient for patients with clinical T1a-bN0M0 non-small-cell lung cancer (NSCLC) who are found to have occult nodal metastases. Our objective was to determine whether patients found to have pN1 or N2 disease after sublobar resection for cT1a-bN0 NSCLC have similar survival as those undergoing lobectomy. Methods Patients without comorbidities in the National Cancer Database (2010-2022), who underwent sublobar resection for cT1a-bN0M0 NSCLC and were found to have pN1 or N2 disease were identified. Survival of patients undergoing wedge resection vs. lobectomy and segmentectomy vs. lobectomy was evaluated using multivariable-adjusted Cox proportional hazards modeling and propensity-score matched analysis. Results Of the 3,003 patients identified, 278 (9.3%) underwent wedge resection, 145 (4.8%) underwent segmentectomy, and 2,580 (85.9%) underwent lobectomy. There was no significant difference in 5-year overall survival between patients undergoing segmentectomy compared to lobectomy in unadjusted and multivariable-adjusted analyses. Patients with occult N2 disease undergoing wedge resection had worse overall survival than patients undergoing lobectomy in unadjusted 5-year overall survival analyses (5-Year OS: (55% vs. 62%, p=0.03) and in multivariable-adjusted Cox proportional hazards analysis (aHR 1.64 [95% CI: 1.21-2.23], p=0.001). Conclusions Among patients with cT1a-bN0M0 NSCLC found to have occult N1 or N2 disease, survival after segmentectomy was comparable to lobectomy, whereas wedge resection was associated with worse survival for patients with occult N2 disease. These findings support anatomic resection over wedge resection when preoperative risk factors for occult nodal disease are present.

items.title: Lower Mortality, Younger Patients: Development of Tricuspid Valve Surgery in Germany
items.abstract: Aims To evaluate national trends in surgical management and outcomes of tricuspid valve disease in Germany from 2011-2023. Methods In this nationwide retrospective observational study, all inpatient cases undergoing tricuspid valve surgery were identified using the German Diagnosis-Related Groups database. Procedure details, comorbidities, and perioperative outcomes were captured via classification codes. Results A total of 47,297 patients (46% female, 54% male, median age 71 years) underwent tricuspid valve surgery. Annual surgery volumes remained stable (p=0.10). Most patients received annuloplasty (N=39,276), valve replacement was less frequent (N=3,749). Concomitant left-sided valve surgery occurred in 77.1% (N=36,434), and coronary bypass surgery in 20.4% (N=9,663). Overall, in-hospital mortality was 12%, with significant reductions in mortality and major adverse cardiac and cerebrovascular events over the study period. Patients undergoing combined surgery of tricuspid valve, left-sided valves, cardiac rhythm surgery and coronary artery bypass surgery had a significantly higher mortality of 20%. Conclusion Tricuspid valve surgery volumes in Germany have remained stable despite the expansion of percutaneous options. Although perioperative outcomes have improved, mortality remains high, particularly for complex procedures, highlighting the importance of careful patient selection and risk stratification.

items.title: Acidosis During Deep Hypothermic Circulatory Arrest is Associated with Neurologic Injury in a Canine Model
items.abstract: Objective Hypothermic circulatory arrest is utilized for neuroprotection during aortic surgery. The associations between hemodynamic, metabolic and neurologic effects are not well characterized. We hypothesized that hypothermic circulatory arrest would be associated with significant physiological derangements which would correlate with neurological injury in a large animal model. Methods Twenty canines underwent deep hypothermic circulatory arrest for 90 minutes at 18 °C with a randomized antegrade cerebral perfusion flow rate (2.5, 5, or 10 cc/kg/min, n=6 for each). No cerebral perfusion was implemented in controls (n=2). In a post-hoc analysis, intraoperative hemodynamics and laboratory value from pre- and post-arrest were compared using t-tests, and Spearman correlation assessed associations between neurological scores from postoperative days 1-3 and post-arrest acid-base markers. Results There were significant differences in hemodynamics and acid-base balance in all canines before and after circulatory arrest: heart rate increased from 97.8 to 135.7 bpm (p<0.01), mean arterial pressure increased 70.6 to 85.6 mmHg (p=0.01), lactate increased 2.1 to 6.3 mmol/L (p<0.01), base excess shifted from -6.8 to -4.8 mEq/L (p=0.01), pH decreased 7.35 to 7.2 (p=0.040), and HCO 3 - increased 17.9 to 20.1 mEq/L (p=0.016). Base excess and pH on postoperative day 1 and lactate on postoperative days 1 and 2 were significantly correlated with worse neurologic performance (p<0.05). Conclusions Hypothermic circulatory arrest is associated with significant changes in canine physiology despite variation in antegrade cerebral perfusion flow rate, confirming our hypothesis. Post-arrest metabolic derangement and acidemia are associated with worse neurologic outcomes, warranting further investigation into mechanisms and prevention strategies.

items.title: Anti-Inflammatory Regimen Associated with Reduced Reintervention for Early Pulmonary Homograft Stenosis Following the Ross Procedure
items.abstract: Objectives The Ross procedure demonstrates favorable outcomes in patients with aortic valve disease. A significant challenge is early-onset pulmonary homograft stenosis, which is hypothesized to be inflammatory in etiology. This study aimed to evaluate the efficacy and safety of an anti-inflammatory regimen for prevention of homograft stenosis. Methods Consecutive patients who underwent the Ross procedure at our institution between 6/2020-11/2022 (standard group) were compared to those who underwent surgery 12/2022-7/2025 and were treated with a methylprednisolone taper and non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drug (NSAID) for 6-months post-operatively (anti-inflammatory group). Primary outcomes were pulmonic stenosis (PS) at 1-year and pulmonic valve reintervention. Safety outcomes were gastrointestinal bleeding, hypertension, and kidney injury. Results Median follow-up was 3.8 years in the standard group (n=53) and 1.8 years in the anti-inflammatory group (n=73). The incidence of moderate or severe PS at 1-year was 14%(7/50) in the standard group compared to 5%(3/58) in the anti-inflammatory group (p=0.18). Four patients (7%) in the standard group required pulmonic valve reintervention (median time 1.1 years), while no patients in the anti-inflammatory group required reintervention (p=0.04). Homografts were larger in the anti-inflammatory group (median size 30 vs 27 mm, p<0.001), although anti-inflammatory regimen completion was associated with lower pulmonic valve peak-gradient at 1-year regardless of homograft size (size<28mm, p=0.04; size≥28mm, p=0.03). There were no significant differences in safety outcomes. Conclusions Implementation of an anti-inflammatory regimen was associated with a significantly lower incidence of pulmonic valve reintervention following the Ross procedure. The incidence of homograft stenosis at 1-year was not statistically different.

items.title: Impact of Preoperative Aortic Regurgitation and Cusp Repair on Long-Term Valve Sparing Root Replacement Outcomes into the Second Decade
items.abstract: Objective Valve-sparing aortic root replacement (VSRR) is an established procedure for aortic root pathology. The impact of pre-op aortic regurgitation (AR) as well as the need for cusp repair on late valve durability remains controversial. Methods Retrospective review from two high-volume institutions identified 780 patients treated with VSRR from 2004-2021. 413 patients had pre-op AR graded <2 (NO-AR group), vs. 367 patients with pre-op AR >2+ (AR group). Analysis of the 367 AR patients also compared 138 patients who did not require cusp repair (NO REPAIR subgroup) vs. 229 patients requiring cusp repair (REPAIR subgroup). Conventional statistics were used for operative outcomes, Kaplan-Meier for survival and late reoperation, and Cox proportional hazard regression for independent predictors of late aortic valve/root reintervention. Results NO-AR vs. AR patients were well-balanced. 15-year reoperation-free survival for NO-AR vs. AR groups was not significantly different (81.4% vs. 74.8%, log-rank p=0.228). In the AR group, the NO REPAIR vs. REPAIR subgroups were also balanced except for more frequent BAV in REPAIR patients (8.7% vs. 38.0%, p<0.001). No differences occurred in recurrent >2+ AR, valve reoperation, or reoperation-free survival between NO REPAIR and REPAIR subgroups (p>0.1 for all). Multivariable regression identified BAV (hazard ratio 2.30 [1.13-4.66], p=0.021) as independently associated with late reoperation. Preoperative >Moderate AR, and cusp repair did not negatively impact long-term reoperation-free survival. Conclusion VSRR, including cusp repair, can be performed with durable outcomes. The impact of BAV anatomy on the need for late valve reoperation warrants careful pre-operative patient selection and valve surveillance.

items.title: Stage 2 and 3 Palliation in Single-Ventricles with Ductal-Dependent Pulmonary Blood Flow: Ductus Arteriosus Stenting vs Aorto-Pulmonary Shunts
items.abstract: Structured Abstract Objective Data on Fontan completion after patent ductus arteriosus stenting in single-ventricle patients with ductal-dependent pulmonary blood flow are limited. We describe progression through Stage 2 and 3 palliation after ductal stenting, with an earlier aorto-pulmonary shunt cohort as historical comparison. Methods We retrospectively reviewed single-ventricle patients with ductal-dependent pulmonary blood flow palliated at our center from 2010 to 2025. Fifty-nine patients met criteria, 49 with ductal stenting and 10 with aorto-pulmonary shunting, mostly from an earlier era. The primary outcome was overall survival; secondary outcomes (pulmonary artery growth and symmetry, somatic growth, perioperative course, reintervention) were compared with unadjusted nonparametric tests. Results Of 49 ductal-stenting patients, 33 completed Stage 2 and 12 Stage 3; 7 remain interstage and 3 achieved biventricular circulation. Crude survival was 45/49 (92%), without procedural mortality; 9 of 10 shunt patients survived (log-rank p=0.910) and 7 completed Stage 3. Nakata index did not differ at any stage. Pulmonary artery symmetry was greater after ductal stenting at Stage 2 (p=0.002), and weight-for-age Z-score was higher at Stage 3 (p=0.038). Ventilation (p<0.001) and post-procedure stay (p=0.004) were shorter after ductal stenting at Stage 1 but not at Stage 3. Conclusions In this cohort, ductal stenting supported progression through staged palliation to Fontan completion without procedural mortality, although reintervention remained frequent. Compared descriptively with a small historical shunt cohort, survival and pulmonary artery growth did not differ detectably, and greater early pulmonary artery symmetry and shorter early ventilation and stay were observed.

items.title: Community Surgeons as Mentors for Junior Cardiothoracic Faculty
Posterior Left Pericardiotomy for Prevention of Atrial Fibrillation After Off-Pump CABG: A Pilot Randomized Controlled Trial
items.abstract: Objective New-onset postoperative atrial fibrillation (POAF) is a common and costly complication after off-pump coronary artery bypass grafting (OPCABG). Posterior left pericardiotomy (PLP) has been shown to reduce POAF in on-pump cardiac surgery, but its efficacy and safety in OPCABG remain uncertain. This pilot randomized controlled trial (RCT) aimed to evaluate PLP specifically in the OPCABG population. Methods This was a single-center pilot RCT conducted between June 2024 and August 2025. Seventy-seven patients undergoing elective, primary, isolated OPCABG without prior atrial fibrillation were randomized using computer-generated simple randomization (1:1). They were allocated to the PLP group ( n = 33) or the control group ( n = 44). The primary endpoint was POAF (episode ≥ 30 seconds) within the first 7 postoperative days. Secondary endpoints included postoperative pericardial effusion, major adverse cardiac and cerebrovascular events (MACCE), and hospital length of stay. Results POAF occurred in 4/33 (12.1%) PLP patients versus 12/44 (27.3%) control patients. The pre-specified primary analysis using Firth's penalized logistic regression yielded an OR of 0.43 (95% CI 0.12–1.37; p = 0.078), corresponding to an absolute risk reduction of 15.2%, a relative risk reduction of 55.4%, and a number needed to treat of 6.6. All sensitivity analyses were directionally concordant (OR range 0.33–0.43). PLP was associated with the absence of detectable postoperative pericardial effusion (0% vs 20.5%; p = 0.005) and absent or minimal pericardial drain output (0 vs 200 mL; p < 0.001). Each 50 mL increment in pericardial drainage was independently associated with increased POAF odds (OR 1.70, 95% CI 1.22–2.38; p < 0.001). Hospital stay was shorter in the PLP group (5 vs 6 days; p = 0.04). MACCE rates were low and comparable (3.0% vs 2.3%). No PLP-attributable complications occurred. Conclusions In this first pilot RCT of PLP in OPCABG, PLP was associated with a clinically meaningful reduction in POAF and the absence of detectable pericardial effusion. The safety profile was favorable. These hypothesis-generating findings provide effect-size and mechanistic data to inform a definitive confirmatory RCT.

items.title: Evidence for Pre-emptive Impella 5.5 Support in Patients with Severe Left Ventricular Dysfunction Undergoing Isolated Coronary Artery Bypass Grafting
items.abstract: Patients with severe left ventricular (LV) dysfunction undergoing isolated coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG) face an elevated risk of postcardiotomy low-output syndrome. The Impella 5.5 provides temporary LV unloading and has been increasingly used pre-emptively in high-risk cardiac surgery, but whether planned prophylactic support improves outcomes compared with unsupported CABG remains unclear. Using the Best Evidence Topic methodology, we searched PubMed (1991–September 2026) for studies regarding this topic. Current evidence supports the technical feasibility and safety of pre-emptive Impella 5.5-supported CABG but does not demonstrate a survival benefit over unsupported CABG or alternative MCS. Its use may be considered on an individualized basis in selected high-risk patients pending prospective comparative studies.
