items.abstract: Immersive reality technologies, including virtual reality, augmented reality, mixed reality, and related extended reality platforms, are reforming how surgeons learn complex anatomy, rehearse procedures, develop technical skills, and manage unexpected or rare intraoperative crises. Cardiothoracic surgery is particularly well suited to these tools because postgraduate training occurs in a high-stakes environment characterized by complex 3-dimensional anatomy, limited operative exposure, minimally invasive/robotic approaches, open communication, and the need for synchronized team performance. Immersive platforms facilitate anatomy education and procedural planning and enable deliberate practice and nontechnical skills training. Although most studies remain small, heterogeneous, and focused on surrogate outcomes rather than patient outcomes, evidence from surgical education and cardiothoracic surgery literature demonstrates that these tools impart improvement in knowledge, confidence, procedural accuracy, and simulator performance. This article defines immersive reality technologies, reviews their educational rationale and emerging applications in cardiothoracic surgery, proposes an implementation framework for training programs, and highlights limitations related to haptics, validation, privacy, equity, and regulatory oversight. The next phase should focus on validation of outcome-linked curricula that integrate immersive simulation into competency-based surgical education.

items.title: Transapical Beating-Heart Septal Myectomy for Symptomatic Nonobstructive Hypertrophic Cardiomyopathy: Initial Clinical Experience
items.abstract: BACKGROUND: Nonobstructive hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (nHCM), defined as hypertrophic cardiomyopathy without left ventricular outflow tract obstruction, remains challenging to treat because of its heterogeneous pathophysiology. This study evaluated the safety and efficacy of transapical beating-heart septal myectomy in patients with symptomatic nHCM. METHODS: Patients with symptomatic, drug-refractory nHCM were prospectively enrolled to undergo transapical beating-heart septal myectomy through a left minithoracotomy. Under real-time transesophageal echocardiographic guidance, septal myectomy was tailored to relieve systolic cavity obliteration and mid-to-apical ventricular obstruction and to enlarge the left ventricular cavity. The primary end point was procedural success at 6 to 12 months postoperatively, defined as fulfillment of all prespecified criteria compared with baseline: ≥1-class improvement in New York Heart Association functional class, ≥10-point increase in Kansas City Cardiomyopathy Questionnaire score, ≥10-mL increase in stroke volume, and normal or grade I diastolic function. RESULTS: Between January 2023 and January 2025, 97 consecutive eligible patients with nHCM underwent transapical beating-heart septal myectomy at Tongji Hospital. At postoperative 6 to 12 months, procedural success was achieved in 87.6%. Specifically, New York Heart Association functional class I increased from 0% at baseline to 93.8% at follow-up, the median Kansas City Cardiomyopathy Questionnaire score improved from 64 (interquartile range, 56–69) to 87 (interquartile range, 82–92; P <0.001), the stroke volume increased from 53.5 mL (interquartile range, 41.0–66.6 mL) to 70.8 mL (interquartile range, 61.3–82.3 mL; P <0.001), and normal or grade I diastolic function increased from 65.6% to 97.9%. Among patients who underwent paired cardiopulmonary exercise testing (n=58), peak oxygen uptake increased by 1.1±2.9 mL/kg/min ( P =0.008). In an exploratory, hypothesis-generating analysis of 12 patients with paired 1 3 N-ammonia positron emission tomography, coronary flow reserve increased from 1.8±0.3 to 2.0±0.4 ( P =0.034). Adverse events included mitral valve injury (n=1) and ventricular septal perforation (n=1), the latter resulting in 1 postoperative death. CONCLUSIONS: Transapical beating-heart septal myectomy was associated with favorable left ventricular geometric remodeling and meaningful improvements in symptoms, health status, and functional capacity in selected patients with symptomatic nHCM. Being a potential therapeutic option for a previously difficult-to-treat population, it warrants further evaluation in controlled, multicenter studies. REGISTRATION: URL: https://www.clinicaltrials.gov ; Unique identifier: NCT05648825.

items.title: Thrombosed Left Ventricular Outflow Tract Pseudoaneurysm After Neonatal Ross-Konno Repair
Biatrial Versus Left Atrial Maze Ablation During Cardiac Valve Surgery for Persistent Atrial Fibrillation: The ABLATION Trial
items.abstract: BACKGROUND: Guidelines recommend concomitant surgical ablation during cardiac surgery in patients with atrial fibrillation (AF). However, the optimal lesion set remains uncertain, with ongoing debate regarding the relative benefits and risks of biatrial versus left atrial (LA) maze ablation. METHODS: In this multicenter, randomized, single-blind trial, patients with persistent or long-standing persistent AF undergoing rheumatic mitral valve surgery, with or without concomitant cardiac surgical procedures, were randomly assigned in a 1:1 ratio to undergo biatrial or LA maze ablation. The biatrial group underwent a complete Cox-Maze IV procedure; the LA group received a left-sided maze lesion set. To ensure standardization and consistency of the ablation procedures, surgeons underwent pretrial training and certification, and all procedures were videorecorded and centrally reviewed. The primary outcome was freedom from atrial tachyarrhythmias lasting >30 seconds without antiarrhythmic drugs within 12 months. The key secondary end point was freedom from permanent pacemaker implantation. RESULTS: All 323 randomized patients were included in the intention-to-treat analysis (mean age, 56.5 years; 72.1% women; mean LA diameter, 51.9 mm). At 12 months, 78.7% of patients (129 of 164) in the biatrial group and 68.6% (109 of 159) in the LA group were free from atrial tachyarrhythmias (adjusted difference, 10.7% [1-sided lower 95% CI, 3%]; P =0.01). Freedom from permanent pacemaker implantation was noted in 97.0% (159 of 164) of the biatrial group and 98.1% (156 of 159) of the LA group, meeting the predefined noninferiority criterion with a margin of −5% (adjusted difference, –1.1% [1-sided lower 95% CI, –3.9%]; P noninferiority =0.01). CONCLUSIONS: Among patients with persistent or long-standing persistent AF undergoing rheumatic cardiac valve surgery, biatrial maze ablation was superior to LA maze ablation in reducing recurrent atrial tachyarrhythmias, while maintaining noninferiority with respect to permanent pacemaker implantation. These findings provide direct evidence to inform lesion-set selection for surgical ablation during cardiac surgery. REGISTRATION: URL: https://www.clinicaltrials.gov ; Unique identifier: NCT05021601.

items.title: Surgical Treatment of Atrial Fibrillation
items.abstract: Atrial fibrillation is the most common sustained cardiac arrhythmia and is associated with an increased risk of stroke, heart failure, mortality, and reduced quality of life. Although catheter ablation is the most widely used rhythm control strategy, its efficacy is limited in patients with non-paroxysmal atrial fibrillation and large left atria. To address this therapeutic gap, surgical approaches, including minimally invasive ablation, hybrid epicardial-endocardial strategies, and left atrial appendage exclusion, have continued to evolve. In this review, we focus on recent evidence to guide clinical decision-making on patient selection, advances in minimally invasive surgical and hybrid techniques, left atrial appendage exclusion, and postoperative anticoagulation management. Minimally invasive standalone Cox-Maze IV procedure and hybrid epicardial-endocardial ablation have demonstrated superior long-term freedom from atrial tachyarrhythmias compared with thoracoscopic epicardial surgical ablation or catheter ablation alone. Five-year arrhythmia-free survival has approached 85% to 95% in experienced centers after the Cox-Maze IV procedure and approximately 60% to 70% after hybrid ablation, compared with 35% to 45% after thoracoscopic epicardial ablation and 30% to 35% after single catheter ablation alone. Surgical left atrial appendage exclusion performed at the time of ablation may further reduce thromboembolic risk, although the optimal strategy for postprocedural anticoagulation remains uncertain. Careful patient selection remains essential, with atrial fibrillation type, duration, left atrial size, and previous treatment failure known to be key predictors of procedural success. As surgical techniques and supporting evidence continue to grow, standalone surgical ablation may assume a more important role in the contemporary management of atrial fibrillation, particularly for patients with advanced disease who are unlikely to achieve durable rhythm control with catheter ablation alone.

Introduction to the 2026 Cardiovascular Surgery–Themed Issue of Circulation
Hedgehog Signaling-Dependent Heterochronic Control of Cardiomyocyte Differentiation Establishes Distinct Cardiac Progenitor Fields
items.abstract: BACKGROUND: The mammalian heart is formed from distinct cardiac progenitor fields: the first heart field (FHF), second heart field (SHF), and juxta-cardiac field (JCF). How these fields are established remains one of the oldest questions in cardiac biology and is central to understanding congenital heart disease, which differentially affects derivatives of the individual fields. Previous work has demonstrated that the fields emerge and differentiate at distinct times; however, the mechanisms underlying their establishment have remained elusive. Here, we implicate Hedgehog signaling–dependent heterochronic control of cardiac differentiation in the emergence of different heart fields. METHODS: We assessed Hedgehog signaling activity by assembling a cardio-mesodermal single-cell atlas. We analyzed Hedgehog ligand gene expression by confocal imaging in gastrulating mouse embryos. We investigated the necessity of Hedgehog signaling using 2 distinct genetic Hedgehog loss-of-function mouse models, analyzed by single-nucleus RNA sequencing analysis. RESULTS: Our results show that Hedgehog signaling mediates field-specific heterochronic control of differentiation timing that orchestrates the establishment of the SHF and JCF as distinct from the FHF. We identify a common cardiac progenitor transcriptomic state from which all 3 fields emerge. We show that the SHF and JCF are established coincident with Hedgehog signaling reception, whereas the FHF evades Hedgehog pathway activity and rapidly differentiates. We find that Hedgehog ligand expression sandwiches the cardiac mesoderm emerging from the primitive streak, spatially coordinating SHF and JCF establishment. Partial depletion of Hedgehog signaling causes premature activation of the cardiac differentiation program in the SHF and JCF. Complete ablation of Hedgehog signaling results in failed SHF and JCF establishment. CONCLUSIONS: Our findings reveal a Hedgehog signaling-dependent, non–cell-autonomous heterochronic mechanism required for SHF and JCF formation. This heterochronic mechanism provides a new paradigm for understanding the ordered temporal emergence of the cardiac progenitor fields that support the development of the 4-chambered heart, as well as a general model for the emergence of progenitor fields that drive organogenesis across the mammalian body plan.

Right Ventricular Reverse Remodeling Without Pulmonary Vascular Unloading During Sotatercept Therapy: An Invasive Pressure–Volume Loop Study
items.abstract: BACKGROUND: Sotatercept improves hemodynamics and functional capacity in pulmonary arterial hypertension; however, its direct actions on the right ventricle (RV) remain poorly understood. We investigated whether sotatercept exerts intrinsic RV protective effects beyond pulmonary vascular unloading. METHODS: In this registry-based cohort study, 28 consecutive patients with pulmonary arterial hypertension between April 2024 and September 2025 underwent right-heart catheterization with conductance-catheter RV pressure–volume analysis and cardiac magnetic resonance imaging before sotatercept initiation and again after a median of 6.1 months of treatment. Hemodynamic nonresponse was defined as a decrease in mean pulmonary arterial pressure by <10%. Reproducibility was tested in 2 independent sotatercept-treated cohorts (SPECTRA [Sotatercept Phase 2 Exploratory Clinical Trial in Pulmonary Arterial Hypertension], n=20, cardiac magnetic resonance; Cologne, n=20, echocardiography). RESULTS: Among 28 patients (17 [61%] female; median age, 48 [IQR, 34–67] years), 21 (75%) were responders and 7 (25%) nonresponders. In responders, sotatercept significantly decreased mean pulmonary arterial pressure (52.0 [IQR, 49.0–65.0] to 39.0 [IQR, 32.0–42.0] mm Hg; P <0.001) and pulmonary vascular resistance (10.7±3.9 to 6.7±2.3 Wood units; P <0.001) without changing cardiac output, reduced RV end-diastolic volume (222 [IQR, 183–242] to 160 [IQR, 129–204] mL; P <0.001) and RV mass (42.8 [IQR, 33.6–56.0] to 33.1 [IQR, 28.2–44.4] g; P <0.001), and improved 6-minute walk distance by +64 m (95% CI, 27 to 102; P =0.002). Ventricular–arterial coupling (end-systolic/arterial elastance) improved although load-independent contractility decreased alongside the decrease in effective arterial elastance. By contrast, nonresponders demonstrated a clinical–hemodynamic disconnect. Despite persistently elevated RV afterload and unchanged end-systolic/arterial elastance, a significant reduction in RV mass (56.1 [IQR, 45.9–81.0] to 46.4 [IQR, 35.9–59.4] g; P =0.003) was observed, accompanied by a significant decrease in B-type natriuretic peptide levels, whereas 6-minute walk distance did not change significantly (+15 m [95% CI, −12 to 42]; P =0.23); the difference in 6-minute walk distance change between groups did not reach significance ( P =0.10). Reduction in RV mass and chamber size was observed in the absence of pulmonary vascular unloading among hemodynamic nonresponders to sotatercept in 2 independent cohorts. CONCLUSIONS: In primary and validation cohorts, structural RV reverse remodeling after sotatercept initiation occurred independent of pulmonary vascular unloading. This pattern is not fully explained by pulmonary vascular unloading and raises the possibility of an effect of sotatercept on the myocardium itself. Improvement in exercise capacity was observed within the hemodynamic responder group only.

VAD Wean Recovery Network: Long-Term Outcomes of LVAD Weaning for Myocardial Recovery
items.abstract: BACKGROUND: Myocardial recovery facilitated by the combination of a left ventricular assist device (LVAD) and guideline-directed medical therapy can lead to sufficient myocardial improvement. This in turn may allow LVAD weaning in appropriately selected patients with chronic advanced heart failure. However, sufficient data on the long-term outcomes of this therapeutic strategy are lacking, thereby hindering widespread adoption of LVAD weaning. We present the primary results from the VAD Wean Myocardial Recovery International Network examining long-term outcomes after LVAD weaning for myocardial recovery. METHODS: We studied 603 patients with chronic advanced heart failure from 60 international centers who underwent LVAD weaning. Preimplantation, LVAD cardiac recovery assessment, and postweaning patient characteristics and outcomes were analyzed. The primary outcome was event-free survival (free of heart transplantation or re-LVAD) in the weaned-for-recovery cohort. RESULTS: The LVAD-weaned cohort had a mean age of 42±15 years; 33% were female; and 9.4% had ischemic cardiomyopathy. At LVAD implantation, 88% had Intermacs (Interagency Registry for Mechanically Assisted Circulatory Support) profiles 1 to 3, and 41.6% required temporary mechanical circulatory support. Median LVAD support duration was 440 days (interquartile range, 261–770) before weaning. At the time of weaning, median left ventricular ejection fraction was 50% (interquartile range, 45%–57.5%), and left ventricular internal diastolic diameter was 48 mm (interquartile range, 43–53 mm). One-year survival after weaning was 91%, with 2.3% requiring re-LVAD and 3.7% requiring heart transplantation. In a secondary exploratory matched analysis against LVAD bridge-to-transplantation recipients from the International Society for Heart and Lung Transplantation registry, long-term survival was similar between groups. CONCLUSIONS: This international, multicenter analysis suggests that in patients with chronic advanced heart failure achieving myocardial recovery with LVAD support, device weaning yields excellent long-term outcomes. These findings may help address the underuse of LVADs as a bridge-to-recovery strategy in select patients.

items.title: NR6A1 Drives Cardiac Remodeling by Transcriptionally Activating the Mineralocorticoid Receptor
items.abstract: BACKGROUND: Activation of the renin-angiotensin-aldosterone system (RAAS) and mineralocorticoid receptor (MR/NR3C2) signaling is a central driver of pathologic cardiac remodeling and heart failure (HF). The transcriptional regulation of NR3C2 and the amplification of RAAS-driven cardiac remodeling remain poorly understood. METHODS: Transcriptome and single-cell RNA sequencing data, along with HF samples from humans and mice, were used for gene expression analysis. Cardiomyocyte-specific Nr6a1 transgenic ( Nr6a1 −cTG ) and knockout ( Nr6a1 −cKO ) mice were subjected to transverse aortic constriction to evaluate cardiac remodeling and dysfunction. Adeno-associated virus 9–sh Nr3c2 was used to test whether Nr3c2 contributes to remodeling driven by Nr6a1 overexpression. Primary mouse cardiomyocytes were used for in vitro analysis. RNA sequencing, Western blot, chromatin immunoprecipitation, and luciferase assays were performed for the mechanism analysis. RESULTS: NR6A1 (nuclear receptor subfamily 6, group A, member 1) expression was increased in the heart tissue from human and mouse failing hearts. Activation of NR6A1 contributed to the hypertrophic growth of cardiomyocytes in vitro. In mice, a cardiomyocyte-specific Nr6a1 transgene aggravated left ventricular dysfunction, hypertrophy, and fibrosis after transverse aortic constriction, whereas a cardiomyocyte-specific Nr6a1 knockout protected the heart from failure and remodeling. Transcriptome analysis of NR6A1 downstream transcriptional targets revealed that Nr3c2 is a prominent RAAS-related downstream target in both hearts and cardiomyocytes. The transcription cofactor NR6A1 directly bound the Nr3c2 promoter, increased promoter activity, and enhanced Nr3c2 transcription in cardiomyocytes. Nr3c2 silencing attenuated NR6A1-associated cardiomyocyte hypertrophy in vitro and reduced cardiac dysfunction and hypertrophy in Nr6a1 −cTG mice after transverse aortic constriction. Analysis of the upstream regulation of NR6A1 in HF stress revealed that HF-related angiotensin II/AT1R signaling promoted NR6A1 expression and its downstream transcriptional and functional events in a STAT1 (signal transducer and activator of transcription 1)–dependent manner. CONCLUSIONS: RAAS (angiotensin II) increases the orphan receptor NR6A1, which transcriptionally activates MR/NR3C2 signaling and aggravates RAAS-associated pathologic remodeling under HF stress. This regulatory network represents an undefined feed-forward amplification mechanism linking angiotensin II signaling to MR/NR3C2 activation and may be a therapeutic target for HF with persistent MR activation.

items.title: Transcatheter Edge-to-Edge Repair for Severe Isolated Tricuspid Regurgitation After Extended Follow-Up: The TRI-FR Randomized Clinical Trial
items.abstract: BACKGROUND: Transcatheter tricuspid edge-to-edge repair (T-TEER) improves symptoms and health status at 1 year in patients with severe tricuspid regurgitation, but its association with clinical events during longer follow-up remains uncertain. METHODS: This secondary analysis reports extended follow-up of TRI-FR (URL: https://www.clinicaltrials.gov ; Unique identifier: NCT04646811), a prospectively registered, multicenter randomized trial comparing T-TEER plus optimized medical therapy (OMT) with OMT alone in patients with severe symptomatic tricuspid regurgitation. In total, 300 patients were randomized (152 to T-TEER plus OMT and 148 to OMT alone). Prespecified analyses included time to first heart failure hospitalization (HFH), tricuspid surgery, or cardiovascular death using cause-specific Cox proportional-hazards models and recurrent HFH using the Lin-Wei-Yang-Ying model. A 12-month landmark analysis included patients alive and under follow-up at 12 months. RESULTS: During a median follow-up of 30.8 months (75th percentile, 41.0; maximum, 56.4), 101 HFHs (17 fatal), 5 additional cardiovascular deaths, and 11 tricuspid surgeries were recorded. Among 81 patients with a first composite event, T-TEER plus OMT reduced the risk versus OMT alone (hazard ratio, 0.56 [95% CI, 0.36–0.88]; P =0.0109). Cardiovascular death or tricuspid surgery did not differ significantly (hazard ratio, 0.75 [95% CI, 0.33–1.71]; P =0.4911). T-TEER plus OMT reduced recurrent HFH (Lin-Wei-Yang-Ying rate ratio, 0.52 [95% CI, 0.32–0.84]; P =0.0073). In the 12-month landmark cohort (n=276), T-TEER plus OMT was associated with lower risks of a first composite event (hazard ratio, 0.40 [95% CI, 0.23–0.70]; log-rank P =0.0009) and recurrent HFH (Lin-Wei-Yang-Ying rate ratio, 0.44 [95% CI, 0.23–0.83]; P =0.0120). Severe or greater tricuspid regurgitation at the last core laboratory assessment was present in 6.77% with T-TEER plus OMT and 53.5% with OMT alone ( P <0.0001). CONCLUSIONS: In patients with severe symptomatic tricuspid regurgitation, T-TEER plus OMT reduced first composite events and recurrent HFH compared with OMT alone during extended follow-up. These associations persisted among patients alive and under follow-up at the 12-month landmark. REGISTRATION: URL: https://www.clinicaltrials.gov ; Unique identifier: NCT04646811.

items.title: AI-Enabled Echocardiography Identifies Prominent Epicardial Adipose Tissue Associated With an Adverse Cardiometabolic Profile
items.abstract: Background Excess epicardial adipose tissue (EAT) is associated with cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic dysfunction, but its assessment has traditionally required advanced imaging. Objectives We investigated whether artificial intelligence (AI)-enabled echocardiography could characterize epicardial adiposity and identify residual cardiometabolic risk. Methods We developed PanAdipo, a video-based deep learning model in 1,114,441 videos from 28,797 studies across the Yale-New Haven Health System (YNHHS) (2016-2022), using report-derived expert reader labels of prominent EAT (2.3% of studies). PanAdipo was evaluated in 5 testing cohorts: a temporally distinct YNHHS transthoracic echocardiography set (n = 4,588 patients contributing 5,130 studies), an emergency department point-of-care ultrasound cohort (n = 10,957), the geographically distinct MIMIC-IV (Medical Information Mart for Intensive Care, version IV) data set (n = 4,549), the community-based MESA (Multi-Ethnic Study of Atherosclerosis) Exam 6 (n = 2,740), as well as in held-out YNHHS patients with paired coronary computed tomography (CT) angiography within 12 months (n = 5,167). Analyses examined discrimination of the report label and of CT-defined high indexed EAT volume, correlation with paired cardiac CT phenotypes, and body mass index (BMI)-adjusted associations with cardiometabolic biomarkers and newly documented metabolic disease. Results In the held-out health system test set, PanAdipo identified prominent EAT documented in clinical reports with an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve of 0.86 (95% CI: 0.82-0.91) across views. Against paired CT-derived measurements, PanAdipo discriminated age- and sex-specific high EAT (EAT / heart volume ≥95th percentile) with an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve of 0.90 (95% CI: 0.89-0.92) overall and of 0.91-0.95 within age-sex groups, and correlated more strongly with indexed EAT volume (Spearman ρ = 0.76) than with BMI (Spearman ρ = 0.41; all P Conclusions AI-enabled echocardiography provides a scalable digital biomarker that characterizes prominent epicardial adiposity and is associated with an adverse cardiometabolic profile, highlighting a role for echocardiography in metabolic risk stratification.

Right Heart Dysfunction in Valvular Heart Disease
items.abstract: Right ventricular (RV) dysfunction is an important determinant of clinical outcomes across a wide range of cardiovascular pathologies. As the prevalence of valvular heart disease (VHD) increases with the aging population, the intersection between RV function and VHD will become all the more relevant for proper risk assessment, treatment selection, and prognostication. Even though RV dysfunction may not always be attributed to VHD, we aim to give clinicians, researchers, and regulators a deep understanding of how patients with VHD should be evaluated for RV dysfunction and treated when RV dysfunction coexists with VHD. We begin with a discussion of the epidemiology and diagnostic evaluation of RV dysfunction in patients with a variety of VHD subgroups, including right-side (ie, associated with the tricuspid valve) and left-side (ie, associated with the mitral and aortic valves) VHD. Attention is also given in that section to contemporary methods and evolving techniques for identifying and phenotyping different forms of RV dysfunction in patients with VHD. No single imaging test practically or comprehensively captures all degrees and forms of RV dysfunction in patients with VHD; therefore, the discussion emphasizes integrating evidence from different imaging modalities and hemodynamic assessments. The second component of the review discusses how RV dysfunction affects therapeutic options, including medical, transcatheter, and surgical therapies for VHD. The focus of the discussion is on the interplay between RV dysfunction in patients with right-side VHD, namely tricuspid regurgitation (TR). Unlike left-side VHD, where RV dysfunction is a marker of overall disease severity but does not necessarily indicate futility or nonresponse to therapy, right-side VHD and TR-associated RV dysfunction identifies a subset of patients where intervention may precipitate even worse RV function. The nuances of these interactions between ventricular and valvular function are the emphasis of this section, and we aim to provide a framework for understanding RV function in the context of these different forms of VHD. Finally, the review concludes with an eye to the future, discussing the ways in which RV dysfunction can be identified and managed with the use of novel techniques. This discussion is increasingly relevant as RV dysfunction and VHD frequently coexist, and accurate identification is critical to matching the right treatment for the right patient.

items.abstract: Background Percutaneous left atrial appendage closure (LAAC) is increasingly used as an alternative to oral anticoagulation for stroke prevention in atrial fibrillation. Its comparative effectiveness and safety in patients at a high risk of both stroke and bleeding remain uncertain. Objectives We evaluated the efficacy and safety of LAAC vs contemporary medical therapy in a high-risk population using individual participant data from randomized trials. Methods Bibliographic databases and trial registries through August 5, 2026, were searched for randomized trials comparing percutaneous LAAC with contemporary medical therapy in populations with a trial-level mean CHA 2 DS 2 -VASc score ≥4. A 1-stage common-effect analysis used Cox models stratified by trial and adjusted for age, sex, CHA 2 DS 2 -VASc score, and HAS-BLED score. Both primary outcomes were time to first stroke, systemic embolism, or cardiovascular/unknown death (efficacy) and time to first major bleeding (safety). A flexible time-varying Cox model was used for major bleeding. The protocol was submitted to PROSPERO (CRD420261335972). Results CLOSURE-AF (Left Atrial Appendage CLOSURE in Patients With Atrial Fibrillation Compared to Medical Therapy) and PRAGUE-17 (Left Atrial Appendage Closure vs. Novel Anticoagulation Agents in Atrial Fibrillation) contributed 1,290 participants (647 assigned to LAAC and 643 to control). Median age was 77.3 years (Q1-Q3: 71.4-81.9 years), and 809 participants (62.7%) were men. The primary efficacy outcome occurred in 142 LAAC participants (21.9%) and 133 control subjects (20.7%) (adjusted HR: 0.98; 95% CI: 0.77-1.24; P = 0.842). Major bleeding occurred in 86 LAAC participants (13.3%) and 80 control subjects (12.4%) (adjusted HR: 1.03; 95% CI: 0.75-1.39; P = 0.874). The treatment effect on major bleeding varied over time (P for treatment-by-time interaction Conclusions In high-risk patients with atrial fibrillation, no statistically significant difference was detected between LAAC and contemporary medical therapy for the primary efficacy outcome or major bleeding. The major bleeding hazard varied over time, with higher early and lower later conditional hazard estimates; however, a cumulative bleeding benefit was not demonstrated by 3 years. Long-term randomized data are needed to improve the precision of later treatment-effect estimates.

items.title: Left Atrial Appendage Closure or Anticoagulation for Atrial Fibrillation
items.abstract: Left atrial appendage closure (LAAC) has emerged as an alternative to long-term anticoagulation for preventing stroke or systemic embolism in selected patients with atrial fibrillation (AF) based on several randomized controlled trials (RCTs) that collectively enrolled >7,000 participants. In this JACC Evidence Review, we interpret the major RCTs as distinct experiments, clarify what each can and cannot establish, and offer a phenotype-based framework for interpreting the evidence. The most recent RCTs, OPTION, CLOSURE-AF, and CHAMPION-AF, have prompted efforts to pool the evidence into a single summary estimate. However, these trials are not one coherent evidence base; they are distinct clinical experiments that asked different questions. They differ in patient phenotype, comparator, device generation, postprocedure antithrombotic regimen, endpoint construction, and follow-up duration. Study-level meta-analysis of published reports remains methodologically valid for estimating the broad direction of effect of a device class, but when the component trials differ materially in patient phenotype, comparator, and outcome construction, the pooled estimate does not map to a common patient group or treatment decision. Patient eligibility as well as thromboembolic and bleeding risk varied markedly across trials. In addition, device technology has progressed, and comparators have evolved from warfarin to direct oral anticoagulants. Heterogeneity and insufficient details also exist about the antithrombotic therapy regimen in LAAC arms and adjunct antiplatelet therapy in control arms. Methodological issues further complicate interpretation, including the use of bleeding events (ie, the putative ancillary benefit of LAAC compared with anticoagulation) within composite endpoints tested for noninferiority, varying noninferiority margins, analytical approaches that may undermine the interpretation of noninferiority, and exclusion of periprocedural bleeding from primary safety endpoints in some trials. Finally, the standard of care for anticoagulation in AF has evolved, obviating concomitant aspirin use in stable individuals on therapeutic anticoagulation, thereby reducing bleeding risk compared with that of the control arm of LAAC RCTs. For most anticoagulation-eligible patients, anticoagulation remains the preferred first-line strategy. LAAC is a reasonable option when long-term anticoagulation is unsafe or unsustainable provided that procedural risk, adjunct antithrombotic feasibility, surveillance needs, and competing mortality are carefully considered. RCT evidence in this latter population is limited, and RCTs in other populations have features that limit their support for LAAC as an alternative to anticoagulation. Because LAAC and anticoagulation offer different types of risk, aligning the most applicable evidence with patient values through shared decision-making is central to care.

items.title: When and How to Consider Left Atrial Appendage Closure as a Management Option for Patients With Atrial Fibrillation
Antithrombotic Therapy Management After Left Atrial Appendage Closure
items.abstract: Percutaneous left atrial appendage closure is increasingly used for stroke prevention in patients with atrial fibrillation, particularly when long-term oral anticoagulation (OAC) is unsuitable. Although postprocedural antithrombotic therapy is necessary to prevent device-related thrombosis (DRT), it may increase bleeding and attenuate the benefit of avoiding long-term OAC. Uncertainty over the optimal antithrombotic strategy persists, with available randomized trials being small and heterogeneous. Direct oral anticoagulant (DOAC) monotherapy and dual antiplatelet therapy (DAPT) are 2 common early strategies. In ANDES, DRT was numerically less frequent with DOAC than with DAPT (1.5% vs 4.1%). In ADALA, low-dose apixaban was associated with greater net benefit than DAPT (HR: 0.19; P = 0.02), although enrollment was prematurely stopped. A meta-analysis of randomized trials found significantly lower DRT with DOAC than with DAPT (risk ratio: 0.17). Current guidelines endorse regimens largely based on device-specific trial protocols or low-certainty evidence. During the initial postimplantation period, antithrombotic therapy should primarily aim to support device healing and prevent DRT, with treatment intensity tailored according to risk profile, concomitant indications, patient preferences, and the feasibility of imaging follow-up. Reassessment at 45 to 90 days should guide de-escalation once adequate device healing has been confirmed, with no fixed treatment stop date. In the absence of device-related complications, long-term OAC or DAPT should be continued only for concomitant indications, whereas continuation of single antiplatelet therapy or complete withdrawal of antithrombotic therapy should be individualized according to thrombotic and bleeding risk. Finally, definite or probable DRT generally warrants OAC, when feasible; in contrast, treatment decisions should not be based solely on the presence or size of a peridevice leak. This review critically appraises the available evidence and guideline recommendations and discusses how treatment intensity and duration may be tailored over time according to evolving thrombotic and bleeding risks.

items.abstract: Background Women sex is an established, nonmodifiable risk factor for adverse outcomes in patients with atrial fibrillation (AF). Left atrial appendage closure (LAAC) has been proposed as an alternative to oral anticoagulation (OAC) for stroke prevention in patients with AF; however, there are limited data on sex-based outcomes of LAAC following catheter ablation. Objectives This study sought to compare outcomes of LAAC vs OAC after AF ablation in men and women. Methods Patients with AF and CHA 2 DS 2 -VASc ≥2 in men and ≥3 in women were randomized 1:1 to either ablation + LAAC or ablation + OAC. The primary safety endpoint was nonprocedural major or clinically relevant nonmajor bleeding at 36 months. The primary efficacy endpoint was a composite of all-cause death, stroke, or systemic embolism at 36 months. Results The study included 1,053 men and 546 women. LAAC and OAC demonstrated comparable primary efficacy events in men (HR: 0.96; 95% CI: 0.56-1.65; P = 0.88) and women (HR: 0.81; 95% CI: 0.41-1.62; P = 0.55), with no treatment-by-sex interaction (P interaction = 0.71). Procedural complication rates were similar at 2.3% in men and 3.7% in women with only 1 pericardial effusion in each group, not related to the index LAAC procedure. At 36 months, the primary safety endpoint was significantly lower in the device group among men (HR: 0.34; 95% CI: 0.23-0.50; P Conclusions In this prespecified analysis of the OPTION (Comparison of Anticoagulation With Left Atrial Appendage Closure After AF Ablation [OPTION]) trial, stroke, systemic embolism, and mortality outcomes were not significantly different between LAAC and OAC following AF ablation in either men or women. Compared with OAC, LAAC demonstrated a greater magnitude of major and clinically relevant nonmajor bleeding reduction in men as compared with women. (Comparison of Anticoagulation With Left Atrial Appendage Closure After AF Ablation [OPTION]; NCT03795298).

items.title: What Counts in a Stroke-Prevention Strategy?

Left Atrial Appendage Closure in Patients Considered Unsuitable for Oral Anticoagulation
items.abstract: Background Oral anticoagulation (OAC) use in atrial fibrillation is suboptimal due to real or perceived bleeding risks. Left atrial appendage closure (LAAC) is an alternative to OAC, but pivotal trials used OAC comparators. Objectives The study sought to assess the long-term safety and effectiveness of LAAC in patients deemed unsuitable for OAC. Methods The ASAP-TOO trial was a multinational randomized trial of patients with atrial fibrillation, CHA 2 DS 2 -VASc (congestive heart failure, hypertension, age ≥75 years, diabetes mellitus, prior stroke or transient ischemic attack or thromboembolism, vascular disease, age 65-74 years, sex category) score ≥2, and OAC unsuitability; target enrollment was 888 patients. Patients were assigned 2:1 to LAAC with a Watchman device or control treatment-single antiplatelet therapy or no therapy. Device patients received dual antiplatelet therapy for 3 months and aspirin through 12 months. The primary effectiveness endpoint was ischemic stroke or systemic embolism; the primary safety endpoint was death, ischemic stroke, systemic embolism, or 7-day device/procedure-related events requiring major intervention. Results Enrollment stopped early because of slow accrual, accentuated by the COVID-19 pandemic: only 481 patients were randomized (320 LAAC, 161 control treatment) and withdrawal was significant (7.8% LAAC, 24.2% control treatment), with disparate follow-up durations (median 876 days and 440.1 total patient-years of follow-up for control patients; median 1,768 days and 1,154.6 total patient-years of follow-up for LAAC patients), reducing statistical power. Patients were 75 ± 8 years of age, the CHA 2 DS 2 -VASc score was 4.6 ± 1.7, and 34% had prior intracranial/subdural hemorrhage. Implantation success was 97.8%. Only 31 of the 101 planned primary effectiveness events occurred, fewer than the 34 events required to trigger the first planned interim analysis. The primary safety endpoint occurred in 1.0% of implant-attempted patients, meeting the prespecified performance goal (P Conclusions In this prematurely terminated and underpowered trial, LAAC implantation was successful, with acceptable safety. Long-term estimates with LAAC were numerically favorable for thromboembolism but imprecise, while early bleeding was increased with the mandated antiplatelet regimen. These findings should be interpreted as exploratory and integrated with contemporary evidence and shared decision making. (Assessment of the WATCHMAN Device in Patients Unsuitable for Oral Anticoagulation [ASAP-TOO]; NCT02928497).

items.title: Left Atrial Appendage Closure for Stroke Prevention in Atrial Fibrillation
Intravascular Lithotripsy vs Super-High-Pressure Noncompliant Balloons for Treatment of Calcified Coronary Lesions
items.abstract: BACKGROUND: Although calcified coronary lesions are associated with poor outcomes after percutaneous coronary interventions (PCI), randomized data guiding lesion preparation are limited. Small studies suggest potential benefits of super-high-pressure noncompliant balloons (SH-NCB); however, they have not been directly compared with intravascular lithotripsy (IVL). OBJECTIVES: The goal of this study was to conduct a randomized comparison of SH-NCBs vs IVL in calcified lesions. METHODS: In this open-label, randomized controlled, noninferiority trial with blinded outcomes assessment (ie, the PROBE design), patients aged ≥18 years with calcified coronary lesions were randomly assigned (1:1) to undergo lesion preparation with SH-NCBs or IVL before PCI with drug-eluting stents. All patients were required to undergo optical coherence tomography (OCT). The primary endpoint was final stent expansion (%) according to OCT. Secondary endpoints included procedural success, strategy success, target vessel failure, stent expansion <80%, and safety outcomes (eg, coronary perforation). RESULTS: Between December 21, 2022, and August 11, 2025, a total of 278 patients underwent the randomly assigned study procedure using plaque modification with SH-NCBs or IVL before stent implantation. The majority of patients (68%) had severe calcium based on an OCT Fujino score ≥4. Study procedures involving IVL tended to be longer and require more auxiliary devices compared with SH-NCBs. The median pressure applied with SH-NCBs compared with IVL was 40 atmospheres vs 6 atmospheres. Regarding the primary endpoint of stent expansion, SH-NCBs were noninferior to IVL (85% vs 84%; Pnoninferiority < 0.0001). The results were consistent across all subgroups, including calcium severity. Use of SH-NCBs, compared with IVL, resulted in similar rates of procedural and strategy success. Safety outcomes, specifically coronary perforations, did not differ between the 2 groups. At 30 days' follow-up, target vessel failure events (including cardiac death, target vessel revascularization, or myocardial infarction) occurred in 4 (2.8%) patients in the SH-NCB group and in 8 (5.7%) patients in the IVL group (HR: 0.50; 95% CI: 0.15 to 1.66; P = 0.26). CONCLUSIONS: In calcified coronary lesions, SH-NCBs were noninferior to IVL for stent expansion and exhibited a comparable safety profile in experienced operators using intravascular imaging. (Value of IVL Compared To OPN Non-Compliant Balloons for Treatment of Refractory Coronary Lesions [VICTORY]; NCT05346068).

Lipid-Lowering Strategies in the Era of Early Atherosclerosis Detection: 2026 ACC Scientific Statement
items.abstract: Atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD) begins early in life, driven in large part by cumulative exposure to low-density lipoprotein cholesterol and other atherogenic lipoproteins. Contemporary evidence from epidemiologic cohorts, genetic studies, imaging studies, and lipid-lowering trials supports a paradigm of earlier identification and more sustained treatment of individuals at increased ASCVD risk. This American College of Cardiology Scientific Statement reviews the rationale for early adoption of lipid-lowering strategies, with emphasis on lifetime lipid burden, inherited and acquired risk enhancers, and the role of subclinical atherosclerosis assessment. Available clinical trial data suggest that greater absolute low-density lipoprotein cholesterol reduction and longer treatment duration can reduce ASCVD events, even though direct evidence remains limited in younger populations at low short-term risk. Atherosclerosis detected by imaging may identify individuals whose ASCVD risk is underestimated by traditional calculators, but optimal strategies for screening, treatment thresholds, safety, adherence, cost-effectiveness, and value require further study. Clinicians should integrate estimated short- and long-term risk, lipid burden, risk enhancers, imaging findings when appropriate, and patient preferences to guide individualized, shared decision making to reduce lifetime ASCVD risk.

From Measuring Recovery to Understanding Recovery After Cardiac Surgery
Center Performance Assessment in Congenital Heart Surgery Is Method Dependent
items.abstract: BACKGROUND: Causal inference methods combined with machine learning may improve center quality assessments through better balancing case mix and allowing for more tailored comparison groups, but they remain understudied. OBJECTIVES: We compared conventional parametric logistic regression with causal weighting approaches to estimate congenital heart surgery center performance. METHODS: Among benchmark operations (2016-2022) across 115 centers from the Society of Thoracic Surgeons Congenital Heart Surgery Database, we compared observed-to-expected (O:E) operative mortality estimated by regression with causal weighting using 3 different methods: entropy balancing weighting (EBW), stable balancing weighting (SBW), and covariate balancing propensity score (CBPS). Standardized mean differences (SMDs) assessed confounder balance for causal weighting estimates aiming for |SMD| < ±0.02. Bootstrap-based CIs classified centers into performance categories. Centers with performance categories differing from parametric regression were examined. RESULTS: We identified 42,579 benchmark operations among neonates (28%), infants (53%), and children (19%). Unadjusted mortality was 2.37% (range: 0%-9.7% across centers). Confounders were well balanced for center causal weighting estimates with exact balance for operation type. Compared with regression O:E estimates (mean: 1.37 ± 1.21), causal weighting estimates were higher and more variable (EBW: 1.43 ± 1.51; SBW: 1.74 ± 2.12; and CBPS: 1.77 ± 2.15), classifying more centers as higher than expected mortality (15.7% EBW, 20% SBW, and 13.9% CBPS, vs 7.8% regression) and fewer lower than expected. Centers with any causal weighting-regression disagreement had lower volumes, fewer higher-complexity operations, and more adults than centers with complete agreement. However, conventional regression disagreed with each causal weighting classification across all volume ranges. CONCLUSIONS: The same center with the same patients and observed outcomes can receive different performance classifications depending on the estimation approach adopted. Causal weighting approaches, constructing more tailored and less extrapolative comparison groups, classified 2 to 3 times as many centers as having higher than expected mortality, and fewer as lower than expected vs current conventional parametric regression.

items.title: Process, Heterogeneity, and Modifiable Risk Factors of Postoperative Recovery After Cardiac Surgery
items.abstract: Background Cardiac surgery improves clinical endpoints but imposes challenges in recovery. Understanding patient-reported postoperative recovery is crucial for optimal care. Objectives The goal of this study was to reveal the process, heterogeneity, and modifiable risk factors of patient-reported postoperative recovery. Methods In this multicenter prospective cohort study involving patients undergoing nonemergent cardiac surgery, patient-reported outcomes were assessed using the Fuwai-Cardiac Recovery Scale (a 9-item scale including symptoms and functional status) at baseline and 8 timepoints after surgery (days 1-4, weeks 2 and 3, and months 1 and 3). Total score and each item score of the Fuwai-Cardiac Recovery Scale were reported to characterize the recovery process. Group-based trajectory models were applied to detect heterogeneity, and trajectory with the largest area under trajectory curve was defined as poor recovery pattern. Multivariable stepwise regression was performed to uncover modifiable risk factors of poor recovery. Results From May 2023 to December 2024, 2,993 patients from 8 Chinese centers were enrolled. The proportions of patients achieving a total score ≤30 (less likely to experience 3-month unplanned readmission) were 77.4% at discharge (week 2) and 97.7% at month 3. Areas under the curve of the item score within 2 weeks, ranked from highest to lowest, were thirst, toileting dependency, poor mobility, fatigue, pain, poor sleep, poor appetite, shortness of breath, and nausea or vomiting. Three different poor recovery patterns were identified: 1) "initial worsening followed by improving" in shortness of breath, poor appetite, nausea or vomiting, poor sleep, and pain; 2) "persistently not improving" in thirst; and 3) "slowly improving" in fatigue, poor mobility, and toileting dependency. Several modifiable risk factors were significantly associated with poor recovery patterns, including smoking (shortness of breath, OR: 1.55; 95% CI: 1.07-2.24), obesity (poor mobility, OR: 1.52; 95% CI: 1.02-2.26), and anemia (poor appetite, OR: 1.47; 95% CI: 1.11-1.95; fatigue, OR: 1.36; 95% CI: 1.11-1.67). Conclusions Recovery after cardiac surgery is a dynamic trajectory that unfolds over time, differs substantially among patients, and offers opportunities for earlier recognition and intervention.

items.title: Aortic Sclerosis and Aortic Stenosis
items.abstract: Background Aortic valve sclerosis (ASc) and aortic stenosis (AS) are traditionally regarded as distinct entities with different clinical prognosis, yet their classification relies on arbitrary echocardiographic measurements. Whether these conditions represent separate diseases or a single disease continuum remains uncertain. Objectives This study aims to evaluate the progression and mortality in patients with early aortic valve disease based on the relationship between transvalvular peak velocity (V max ), clinical outcomes, and aortic valve replacement (AVR). Methods We retrospectively analyzed 181,167 adults with morphologically abnormal aortic valves and a V max of 1.0 to 3.9 m/s on transthoracic echocardiography between 2010 and 2022. Patients with severe AS, significant aortic regurgitation, or AVR within 6 months were excluded. Outcomes included AVR, all-cause mortality, and their composite. Cox proportional hazards models and penalized smoothing spline analyses were used to assess associations between V max and outcomes, adjusting for demographics, valve morphology, and comorbidities. Results During a median follow-up of 3.2 years, 4,112 patients underwent AVR and 61,654 died. The risk of AVR increased gradually across the entire V max range, particularly beyond 3 years, without an identifiable threshold separating ASc from AS. The cumulative incidence of AVR at 5 years increased progressively from 0.1% at 1.0 to 1.4 m/s to 31.2% at 3.0 to 3.9 m/s (P max and outcomes, including mortality, persisted after multivariable adjustment and across multiple sensitivity analyses. Conclusions Transvalvular velocity associated with AVR across V max 1.0 to 3.9 m/s gradually increase without a clear threshold, consistent with a disease continuum between ASc and AS.

items.title: Betting on Science
The Language of Inflammation in Cardiovascular Medicine
Location Matters
Cardiac Damage and Clinical Outcomes in Symptomatic Severe Aortic Stenosis Undergoing Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement
items.abstract: BACKGROUND: The extent of cardiac damage in patients with aortic stenosis (AS) is associated with worse clinical outcomes. OBJECTIVES: This study sought to investigate the clinical impact of cardiac damage using the updated criteria incorporating the echocardiographic probability of pulmonary hypertension. METHODS: This post hoc subanalysis of LANDMARK trial, which randomized 768 patients with severe AS to the Myval transcatheter heart valve (THV) series or to contemporary THVs (Sapien and Evolut series), used updated cardiac damage classification: stage 0, no cardiac damage; stage 1, left ventricular damage; stage 2, left atrial or mitral valve damage; stage 3, pulmonary artery or tricuspid valve damage; and stage 4, right ventricular damage. The impact of cumulative cardiac damage, defined as meeting all criteria for stages 1 to 4, was also assessed. The primary endpoint was 1-year all-cause mortality. RESULTS: Cardiac damage stages were assessed in 596 patients (stage 0, n = 36; stage 1, n = 88; stage 2, n = 284; stage 3, n = 84; stage 4, n = 104), with a mean age of 80.2 (5.7) years and a mean Society of Thoracic Surgeons score of 3.3% (2.4%). One-year mortality was 0%, 1.1%, 4.7%, 7.2%, and 20.4% in stages 0, 1, 2, 3, and 4, respectively (log-rank P < 0.001). The area under the curve for predicting 1-year mortality was 0.739. Patients with cumulative cardiac damage had the highest mortality (23.6%). In the multivariable analysis, stage 4 was independently associated with higher 1-year mortality. CONCLUSIONS: The updated cardiac damage staging stratified 1-year mortality after transcatheter aortic valve replacement, highlighting the importance of comprehensive echocardiographic assessment in severe AS. (LANDMARK Trial: a Randomised Controlled Trial of Myval THV [LANDMARK]; NCT04275726).

items.title: Is Bilateral Occlusion Mandatory?
Transcatheter vs Surgical Aortic Valve Replacement for Isolated Native Aortic Regurgitation
items.abstract: Background Transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) is well established for aortic stenosis, while its application for isolated native aortic regurgitation (AR) was previously off label and technically challenging. Comparative data between TAVR and surgical aortic valve replacement (SAVR) are limited. Objectives The aim of this study was to compare patient characteristics and outcomes of off-label TAVR vs SAVR among patients with isolated native AR. Methods Using the Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services Medicare Provider Analysis and Review database, patients ≥65 years of age who underwent TAVR or SAVR for isolated native AR (2017-2023) were identified. Propensity score matching (1:1) was performed to evaluate short- and long-term outcomes. Fine-Gray models accounted for death as a competing risk, reported as subdistribution HRs (SHRs). Results Among 9,859 patients, 1,742 propensity score-matched pairs were included, with balanced baseline characteristics (mean age 75.8 years vs 75.7 years; female sex 517 of 1,742 [29.7%] vs 528 of 1,742 [30.3%]). In the matched cohort, TAVR was associated with shorter hospitalization (OR: 0.33; 95% CI: 0.28-0.39; P Conclusions In this analysis, TAVR was associated with shorter hospitalization and comparable 5-year survival as SAVR, although pacemaker and long-term reinterventions rates were higher.

items.title: Prosthesis–Patient Mismatch and Patient-Centered Outcomes After TAVR
items.abstract: BACKGROUND: Prosthesis-patient mismatch (PPM) after transcatheter aortic valve replacement has been widely studied for its association with clinical outcomes, but its effect on patient-reported health status remains less defined. OBJECTIVES: This study sought to evaluate the association between PPM severity and health status through 3-year follow-up after transcatheter aortic valve replacement. METHODS: This post hoc analysis of the SCOPE I (Safety and Efficacy of the ACURATE Neo/TF Compared to the SAPIEN 3 Bioprosthesis) randomized trial categorized patients according to PPM severity using Valve Academic Research Consortium-3 criteria. Endpoints included survival and patient-reported health status, with an integrated outcome defined as being alive with good health status (Kansas City Cardiomyopathy Questionnaire Overall Summary score ≥75 without a decline of >10 points from baseline). RESULTS: Among 662 patients, moderate and severe PPM occurred in 184 (27.8%) and 69 (10.4%), respectively. All-cause mortality at 1 and 3 years was 7.0% and 20.5%, with no differences across PPM categories. Kansas City Cardiomyopathy Questionnaire Overall Summary score was similar through 1 year but lower at 3 years in patients with severe vs no PPM (median 71.1 vs 83.9; P = 0.027). Fewer patients with severe PPM were alive with good health status at 3 years (30.6% vs 49.4%; P = 0.021). In multivariable analysis, severe PPM was associated with a lower likelihood of the integrated outcome (OR: 0.51; 95% CI: 0.27-0.96; P = 0.036), but this association was no longer statistically significant after adjustment for 30-day mitral regurgitation (OR: 0.59; 95% CI: 0.30-1.15; P = 0.121). CONCLUSIONS: Among survivors, severe PPM was associated with a lower likelihood of good health status at 3 years. This association was attenuated after accounting for 30-day residual mitral regurgitation, suggesting a possible contributory role. Given the post hoc design, the findings are hypothesis-generating.

items.title: Mavacamten for Refractory Dynamic Intraventricular Obstruction After Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement
The Right-Sided Substrate for Sudden Cardiac Death
Prevalence and Consequences of Guideline-Directed Indications for Aortic Valve Replacement in the EARLY TAVR Trial
items.abstract: BACKGROUND: The current American College of Cardiology/American Heart Association valvular heart disease guidelines were published before several recent trials that provide greater support for early intervention in patients with asymptomatic severe aortic stenosis (AS). OBJECTIVES: This study sought to investigate the prevalence and clinical impact of American College of Cardiology/American Heart Association Class II recommendations for AVR in the EARLY TAVR trial. METHODS: The EARLY TAVR trial randomized patients with asymptomatic severe AS to transfemoral transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) with a balloon-expandable valve or clinical surveillance (CS) with conversion to TAVR based on development of ACC/AHA Class I indications. Patients in the intention-to-treat cohort were stratified by presence of a Class II indication for AVR at randomization. The primary endpoint of the present analysis was the composite of all-cause death, stroke, or heart failure hospitalization. Interaction tests were performed to assess whether the treatment effect differed by level of guideline recommendation. Timing of conversion to AVR in the CS group according to the presence/absence of Class II indications was also assessed. RESULTS: Of the 901 patients randomized to TAVR (N = 445) and CS (N = 446), 636 (70.6%) patients had no guideline recommendation, and 265 (29.4%) had at least1 1 Class II recommendation for AVR at the time of randomization. At a median follow-up of 3.8 years, patients with a Class II indication for AVR experienced higher rates of the primary endpoint (Class II: 24.5% vs no recommendation: 14.5%; HR = 1.78; 95% CI: 1.30-2.44; P < 0.001) and were more likely to have acute valve syndrome at the time of conversion. Compared with CS, the relative benefit of early TAVR on the primary endpoint was similar regardless of the presence or absence of a Class II guideline recommendation (HR = 0.62; 95% CI: 0.37-1.02 vs 0.61; 95% CI: 0.40-0.92; Pinteraction = 0.96). CONCLUSIONS: Among patients in the EARLY TAVR trial, Class II indications for AVR were present in almost one-third of patients at baseline. The benefit of early TAVR was consistent regardless of the presence or absence of Class II indications. These findings support the strategy of early TAVR over CS in asymptomatic patients with severe AS, independent of guideline indications. CLINICAL TRIAL REGISTRATION: https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT03042104; Unique Identifier: NCT03042104.

Sutureless Surgical Valve-in-Frame After SURPLUS for Failed Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement
Development of a Quantitative Contrast CT-Based TAVR-Risk Score to Reliably Predict Deformation in Bicuspid Aortic Valves
items.abstract: BACKGROUND: Bicuspid aortic valve (BAV) calcification affects clinical outcomes by causing transcatheter heart valve (THV) deformation after transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR). However, a computed tomography (CT)-based scoring system for grading BAV calcification severity and predicting THV deformation has not been established. OBJECTIVES: This study sought to develop a cardiac CT-based BAV TAVR-risk score for grading BAV calcification severity and predicting THV deformation. METHODS: This single-center retrospective study included consecutive patients with BAV who underwent TAVR using contemporary balloon-expandable valves between January 2016 and December 2024 and who had preprocedural and postprocedural CT imaging. The BAV TAVR-risk score integrated calcification severity and distribution across valve leaflets, raphe, annulus, and left ventricular outflow tract, quantified using a fixed HU-850 threshold of detection on contrast-enhanced CT scans. Score thresholds were derived by receiver operating curve analysis with Youden index optimization. Patients were categorized into low-, intermediate-, and high-risk score groups. RESULTS: Among 321 patients (median follow-up: 1,825 days; Q1-Q3: 765-1,825 days), 56 (17.4%) were classified into the high-risk score group. Both underexpansion and eccentricity of the THV occurred in 49 of the 321 patients (15.3%) and were predominantly observed in the high-risk score group. However, in the low-risk score group, 149 of 155 patients (96.1%) demonstrated no underexpansion or eccentricity of the THV. A high BAV TAVR-risk score independently predicted both underexpansion and eccentricity of the THV (OR: 89.13; 95% CI: 35.02-226.83; P < 0.001). CONCLUSIONS: This CT-based BAV TAVR-risk score provides a systematic method to precisely quantify BAV severity which reliably predicts THV deformation for BAV patients with contemporary balloon-expandable valves and may help guide decision-making in this challenging population.

items.title: Prognostic Impact of Paravalvular Regurgitation in Patients With Severe Low-Flow, Low-Gradient Aortic Stenosis Undergoing TAVR
items.abstract: Background Paravalvular regurgitation (PVR) is a frequent complication after transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) and may influence clinical outcomes in patients with high-gradient aortic stenosis. However, its prognostic relevance in patients with low-flow, low-gradient aortic stenosis (LFLG-AS) undergoing TAVR remains incompletely elucidated. Objectives This study sought to evaluate the prognostic significance of PVR severity in patients with LFLG-AS undergoing TAVR with current-generation prostheses. Methods This multicenter registry-based cohort study included consecutive patients with LFLG-AS undergoing TAVR from January 2019 to December 2024 at 17 high-volume Italian centers. PVR severity was classified using a 5-class grading scheme and stratified as Results A total of 1,358 patients were included. Kaplan-Meier analysis showed lower event-free survival among patients with ≥2+ PVR at discharge compared with those with Conclusions In this large, real-world study of patients with LFLG-AS treated with current-generation TAVR devices, PVR ≥2+ was independently associated with worse clinical outcomes after discharge, regardless of LFLG-AS subtype.

Sex-Related Differences in Patients Undergoing Transcatheter Edge-to-Edge Repair for Primary Mitral Regurgitation
items.abstract: BACKGROUND: Sex-related differences have been previously explored in patients with mitral regurgitation (MR) undergoing surgery as well as those with secondary MR treated with transcatheter edge-to-edge repair (TEER). OBJECTIVES: This study sought to evaluate sex-related differences in baseline characteristics and clinical outcomes in patients undergoing TEER for primary MR. METHODS: Outcomes of Patients Treated with M-TEER for Primary MR (NCT05332782) is an international, retrospective registry including patients undergoing TEER for primary MR in 27 centers. The primary outcome was a composite of 2-year all-cause mortality or heart failure hospitalization. RESULTS: A total of 2,078 patients, including 961 (46.3%) females, were analyzed. Females were older and had fewer comorbidities but presented with a different anatomy and more advanced symptoms. Compared with males, females were more frequently excluded from surgery because of advanced age and frailty. Optimal procedural results were lower in females, with a higher incidence of residual MR ≥2+ (38.5% vs 32.1%; P = 0.0037), and a significantly higher mean transmitral gradient (4.0 vs 3.6 mm Hg; P < 0.001). Kaplan-Meier curves showed significantly lower rates of all-cause mortality and cardiovascular mortality in female patients. In contrast, the incidence of the primary composite endpoint, as well as heart failure hospitalization alone, did not differ significantly. After adjusting for comorbidities, females demonstrated lower primary composite endpoint (HR: 0.77; P = 0.009), lower all-cause mortality (HR: 0.62; P < 0.001), and lower cardiovascular mortality (subdistribution HR: 0.53; P = 0.011). CONCLUSIONS: Among patients with primary MR, females were older and presented with a different clinical and anatomical profile compared with males. Although optimal procedural results were lower in females, higher survival rates in females vs males suggest that mitral transcatheter edge-to-edge repair can be a good option regardless of sex.

items.title: One-Year Outcomes of Transcatheter Tricuspid Valve Replacement
items.abstract: Background One-year real-world data following transcatheter tricuspid valve replacement (TTVR) are lacking. Objectives We investigated one-year outcomes of commercial TTVR at 11 expert European heart valve centers. Methods Consecutive patients undergoing TTVR with the EVOQUE system after regulatory approval (October 2023-July 2025) were included in this single-arm, retrospective, multicenter study. Results Among 237 patients undergoing TTVR (median age 80 [74-84] years; 158 [66.7%] women; median TRI-SCORE 5 [3-6]), one-year vital status was available in 226(95.4%). The median follow-up time was 367 (217-448) days. After TTVR, paravalvular leak (PVL)≥mild was present in 31/201 (15.4%) and ≥moderate in 4/201 (2.0%). In-hospital permanent pacemaker implantation (PPI) was required in 33/166 pacemaker-naïve patients (19.8%). At one-year, tricuspid regurgitation (TR) was reduced to mild or less in 136/138(98.6%), while NYHA class III/IV decreased from 83.1% (95%CI 76.3-88.3) to 18.9% (95%CI 13.4-26.0, P <0.001). RV basal diameter decreased by -4.0 mm (95%CI -6.0 to -2.0, P <0.001), while LV end-diastolic volume increased by +11.8 mL (95%CI +4.2 to +19.4, P =0.003) and left atrial volume by +15.2 mL (95%CI +4.6 to +25.8, P =0.006), with unchanged LVEF. Twenty-six patients died at follow-up (12.8%, 95%CI 8.9-18.3). Patients with PVL experienced higher rates of one-year mortality, whereas TRI-SCORE was independently associated with the composite endpoint of death or heart failure hospitalization (hazards ratio 1.26 per point, 95%CI 1.06-1.50). Conclusions Commercial TTVR provided durable TR reduction, functional improvement, and biventricular remodeling at one-year follow-up. Baseline disease stage characterized by higher TRISCORE and procedural complications might be associated with increased risk of adverse events.

items.title: Transcatheter Tricuspid Edge-To-Edge Repair Versus Transcatheter Tricuspid Valve Replacement for Severe Symptomatic Tricuspid Regurgitation
items.abstract: Background Transcatheter tricuspid edge-to-edge repair (T-TEER) and transcatheter tricuspid valve replacement (TTVR) are both approved for severe symptomatic tricuspid regurgitation (TR) but lack head-to-head comparison. Objectives This study sought to compare 1-year outcomes of T-TEER vs TTVR using causal inference in a harmonized real-world cohort. Methods TRIVALVE (International Multisite Transcatheter Tricuspid Valve Therapies Registry) (T-TEER, n = 384) and TRIPLACE (Global Multicenter Registry on Transcatheter TRIcuspid Valve RePLACEment) (TTVR, n = 398) registries were harmonized (n = 782). Inverse probability weighted survival time estimated study group average treatment effect (ATE) and treated-study group average treatment effect on the treated (ATET) effects on time to all-cause death, heart failure hospitalization (HFH), tricuspid valve (TV) reintervention, bleeding, and their composite major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE), balanced for 14 baseline clinical/echocardiographic covariates, were undertaken. Results Median follow-up by reverse Kaplan-Meier estimates was 276 days (IQR: 58-365). TTVR achieved near-complete TR elimination vs persistent mild-moderate residual TR post-T-TEER [median (IQR) grade 0 (0-1) vs 2 (1-2)]. Modeling demonstrated an early all-cause mortality penalty for TTVR (ATE: -81.3 days, P = 0.002; ATET: -79 days, P = 0.003) with a corresponding overall MACE signal (ATE: -70.7 days, P = 0.001; ATET: -69.3 days, P = 0.012). Conclusions Despite more complete TR reduction, orthotopic TTVR may be associated with earlier all-cause mortality and MACE penalty over T-TEER. This hypothesis-generating analysis should spur further research to identify the optimal patient phenotype for T-TEER and TTVR technologies.

items.title: Excimer Laser Coronary Atherectomy in Contemporary Percutaneous Coronary Intervention
items.abstract: Excimer laser coronary atherectomy (ELCA) was introduced over 4 decades ago for the modification and debulking of coronary atherosclerotic plaque. However, the adoption of ELCA has remained low, in part because of misperceptions around and limited understanding of its mechanism of action, the disappointing early experience with the device, and limited awareness of the significant body of safety and efficacy data generated after optimization of catheter design and procedural methods. The introduction of other techniques, such as rotational atherectomy, orbital atherectomy, and lately, intravascular lithotripsy, has further contributed to uncertainty regarding the optimal placement and value of ELCA within the percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) algorithm. This document clarifies the value and role of ELCA in contemporary PCI, with new insights on its mechanism of action as well as recommendations for settings and protocols for use to help cardiologists achieve successful procedural and clinical outcomes. ELCA is a valuable tool for uncrossable and undilatable thrombotic and stent-related lesions. Lesion composition, settings, and lasing medium affect the magnitude of ELCA's photoablative effects. This study contains recommendations for ELCA setup, settings, and protocols.

Double Pulmonary Artery Rail Technique for Kissing Balloon Valvuloplasty of Degenerated Bioprosthetic Tricuspid Stenosis
Transcatheter Valve Repair of Tricuspid Regurgitation
items.abstract: Background Tricuspid transcatheter edge-to-edge repair is a viable option for patients with ≥severe tricuspid regurgitation (TR). Objectives This study aims to evaluate 2-year outcomes with the PASCAL transcatheter valve repair system from the TriCLASP European, single-arm, postmarket clinical follow-up study, including outcomes stratified by baseline TR severity. Methods The TriCLASP study evaluated the safety and effectiveness of tricuspid transcatheter edge-to-edge repair with the PASCAL system. TR reduction and clinical, functional, and quality of life outcomes were assessed at 2 years. Outcomes were also assessed by baseline TR severity (≤moderate vs ≥severe TR). Results In 300 enrolled patients, mean age was 80.1 years, 52.0% were women, and 75.8% had ≥severe TR. Significant and sustained TR reduction was observed from baseline to 2 years, with ≤moderate TR achieved in 81.3% (P Conclusions Outcomes from the TriCLASP study confirm durable safety and effectiveness of the PASCAL system at 2 years in a postmarket setting. Results demonstrated significant and sustained TR reduction, favorable survival, reduced HFH, and clinically meaningful improvements in symptoms, function, and quality of life, which were consistent across patients with moderate and severe TR.

items.title: Predicting Ischemic and Bleeding Risk in Patients on DAPT After PCI
items.abstract: Background Dual antiplatelet therapy after coronary stenting prevents ischemic complications but increases bleeding risk. Individualized assessment of these combined risks may inform treatment strategies. Objectives This study sought to develop a machine learning algorithm for clinical outcomes after percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) with potential to support clinical decisions around antiplatelet therapy. Methods Data from 11 clinical trials encompassing 19,106 patients who underwent PCI with everolimus-eluting stents were randomly split 3:1 to train and validate 2 separate machine learning algorithms for ischemic (cardiovascular death, myocardial infarction, stroke, or stent thrombosis) and bleeding (Bleeding Academic Research Consortium type 3 or 5) risk prediction at 1 year. The Boruta algorithm was used to select the top 11 variables (providing >80% of predictive information) for final model development. An independent cohort of 10,696 patients undergoing PCI at a tertiary-care center (Mount Sinai Hospital) was used for external validation. Results There were 594 (4.1%) ischemic and 448 (3.1%) bleeding events in the training data set. Random survival forest was selected as the best-performing model (mean time-dependent area under the curve of 0.76 for ischemic events and 0.81 for bleeding). Internal and external validation yielded a mean time-dependent area under the curve of 0.72 and 0.70 for ischemic events and 0.72 and 0.71 for bleeding, respectively. The 2 models met the prespecified performance goal in both validation cohorts. Conclusions A machine learning-based tool exhibited good discriminative ability for the prediction of ischemic and bleeding events at 1 year post-PCI and warrants prospective evaluation in clinical decisions surrounding antithrombotic therapies.

items.title: Pharmacodynamic Effects of Different Ticagrelor Dosing Regimens With and Without Aspirin in Patients With Diabetes
items.abstract: Background Although P2Y 12 inhibitor monotherapy with ticagrelor is efficacious for secondary prevention in coronary artery disease (CAD) patients with diabetes mellitus (DM), there are limited data on its pharmacodynamic (PD) effects and the impact of drug dosing. Objectives The aim of this study was to assess the PD effects of ticagrelor monotherapy at a 60-mg dosing regimen and how this compares with ticagrelor- and clopidogrel-based dual antiplatelet therapy (DAPT). Methods OPTIMUS-7 (Optimizing Antiplatelet Therapy in Diabetes Mellitus-7) is a randomized PD study in CAD patients with DM (n = 81). After a 7-day run-in with DAPT using aspirin (81 mg once daily) plus ticagrelor (90 mg twice daily), followed by ticagrelor 90 mg monotherapy for 10 days, patients were randomized to: 1) ticagrelor 60 mg monotherapy; 2) aspirin plus ticagrelor 60 mg; or 3) aspirin plus clopidogrel 75 mg. PD assessments included VerifyNow P2Y 12 reaction units (PRU), whole-blood vasodilator-stimulated phosphoprotein, and light transmittance aggregometry. The primary endpoint was noninferiority of ticagrelor 60 mg monotherapy vs aspirin plus ticagrelor 60 mg on trough levels of PRU after 10 days (noninferiority margin 45 PRU). Markers of thromboxane-mediated platelet reactivity and total platelet-mediated global thrombogenicity were also assessed. Results Ticagrelor 60 mg monotherapy led to similar PRU levels compared with aspirin plus ticagrelor 60 mg (47 PRU [95% CI: 24-69 PRU] vs 40 PRU [95% CI: 18-61 PRU]; mean difference 7 PRU; 95% CI: -23 to 38 PRU), meeting the noninferiority primary endpoint. Clopidogrel-based DAPT showed higher PRU than both ticagrelor dosing regimens. Light transmittance aggregometry and whole-blood vasodilator-stimulated phosphoprotein showed parallel findings. Markers of thromboxane-mediated platelet reactivity and total platelet-mediated global thrombogenicity were increased with ticagrelor monotherapy compared with DAPT. Conclusions In CAD patients with DM, ticagrelor 60 mg monotherapy achieved similar P2Y 12 inhibition compared with aspirin plus ticagrelor 60 mg and greater inhibition than clopidogrel-based DAPT. Ticagrelor monotherapy showed increased thromboxane-mediated aggregation and total platelet-mediated global thrombogenicity compared with DAPT regimens. (Ticagrelor With and Without Aspirin in Patients With Diabetes Mellitus [OPTIMUS-7]; NCT04484259).

items.title: Impact of Targeted Bleeding Source Treatment on Recurrent Bleeding Following Percutaneous Coronary Intervention
items.abstract: Background Whether targeted treatment (TT) to potentially cure the cause of bleeding before percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) is effective in preventing recurrent bleeding or death after PCI is unknown. Objectives This study sought to assess whether TT affects recurrent bleeding or survival after PCI. Methods We included patients from the Cardiobase Bern PCI registry with Bleeding Academic Research Consortium (BARC) 2 to 4 bleeding before index PCI. TT was defined as surgical, interventional, or medical therapy targeted to cure the cause of prior bleeding. The primary endpoint was recurrent BARC 2 to 5 bleeding at the identical location; secondary endpoints were any BARC 2 to 5 bleeding and mortality throughout 1 year (median: 390 days [Q1-Q3: 371-430 days]) after PCI. We report inverse probability weight-adjusted hazard ratios (IPW-HRs) with TT as dependent variable, and as covariates we report the Academic Research Consortium for High Bleeding Risk variables associated with ≥4% 1-year BARC 3 to 5 bleeding, antithrombotic treatment, and bleeding location. Results Of 19,352 patients, 847 (4.4%) had prior bleeding, 358 of 847 (42.3%) with and 489 of 847 (57.7%) without TT. Recurrent BARC 2 to 5 bleeding at the identical location occurred in 8.9% (32/358) with TT vs 5.1% (25/489) without TT (IPW-HR: 1.88; 95% CI: 1.10-3.19; P = 0.020). There were no differences in any recurrent BARC 2 to 5 bleeding (TT 14.5% [52/358] vs no TT of 10.6% [52/489]; IPW-HR: 1.41; 95% CI: 0.95-2.08; P = 0.087) or mortality (TT 14.0% [50/358] vs no TT 12.3% [60/489]; IPW-HR: 1.16; 95% CI: 0.79-1.70; P = 0.455). Conclusions Among patients with prior bleeding before PCI, despite TT of the bleeding source, the risk of recurrent bleeding remained significantly higher at the identical location when compared with patients without TT, without a reduction in any recurrent bleeding or mortality after PCI. (CARDIOBASE Bern PCI Registry; NCT02241291).
