Mean arterial pressure showed higher values in the V-Pa group compared with RA-Pa at 2 hours (65 ± 10 vs . 48 ± 8 mm Hg; p = 0.010) and 3 hours (62 ± 9 vs . 47 ± 10 mm Hg; p = 0.042). Mean pulmonary artery pressure was higher after V-A ECMO (20 ± 5 mm Hg) initiation compared with V-Pa (11 ± 5 mm Hg, p = 0.013) or RA-Pa (11 ± 3 mm Hg, p = 0.006) support. During support, the V-A ECMO group exhibited the lowest EtCO 2 and highest carotid flow ( p = 0.039 and p < 0.001, respectively). Challenges were noted with double-lumen cannulation due to anatomical constraints. Pulmonary artery cannulation–based support was noninferior to V-A ECMO in terms of oxygen delivery, with lower pulmonary pressures and preserved transpulmonary flow. Femoral vein-to-pulmonary artery configuration showed favorable short-term hemodynamics and easier cannulation compared with RA-Pa.

items.title: Limited Discrimination of Risk Scores for Right Ventricular Failure After Left Ventricular Assist Device Implantation
items.abstract: Right ventricular failure (RVF) remains a major complication after left ventricular assist device (LVAD) implantation and is associated with increased morbidity and mortality. Multiple preoperative risk scores and hemodynamic parameters have been proposed to predict RVF; however, their generalizability remains uncertain. We performed a retrospective single-center study of 331 patients undergoing centrifugal-flow LVAD implantation between 2011 and 2025, excluding axial-flow devices. Right ventricular failure, defined by Interagency Registry for Mechanically Assisted Circulatory Support (INTERMACS) criteria, occurred in 105 patients (31.7%). We evaluated established hemodynamic parameters and published risk scores using logistic regression, standalone receiver operating characteristic analysis, calibration assessment, and sensitivity analyses. Although several risk scores, including European Registry for Patients with Mechanical Circulatory Support (EUROMACS), Utah, and STOP-RVF, were associated with RVF, their discriminative performance was modest, with area under the curve values around 0.70. Discrimination remained modest in the HeartMate 3 subgroup and when postoperative right-sided mechanical circulatory support requirement was used as a more objective endpoint. Calibration analyses showed that published risk strata did not consistently reproduce original absolute event rates, and the incremental improvement beyond preoperative models for predicting a dynamic, institution-dependent complication. Center-specific risk awareness and proactive perioperative management strategies may better mitigate RVF risk.

items.title: Respiratory System Compliance Trajectory and Mortality in COVID-19 Patients Supported by Venovenous Extracorporeal Membrane Oxygenation
Response to the Letter to the Editor: Revascularization Timing on Venoarterial Extracorporeal Membrane Oxygenation: Building on an Important Signal
Letter to the Editor: Revascularization Timing on Venoarterial Extracorporeal Membrane Oxygenation
Vector Flow Mapping Energy Loss and Pump Flow in Left Ventricular Assist Device Patients: A Transesophageal Echocardiography Pilot Study
items.abstract: Left ventricular assist device (LVAD) support redirects intraventricular flow toward the inflow cannula. We examined whether vector flow mapping-derived energy loss (EL), a measure of viscous dissipation related to spatial velocity gradients, was associated with controller-displayed pump flow. This prospective single-center pilot enrolled 33 patients undergoing LVAD-related surgery with intraoperative transesophageal echocardiography; 31 HeartMate 3 recipients were analyzable. The maximum available peak EL across three views was the primary measure. Log-transformed maximum peak EL was associated with displayed flow after adjustment for pump speed and left ventricular end-diastolic diameter ( B = 0.181, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.033–0.330), cannula angle ( B = 0.204, 95% CI: 0.052–0.356), or aortic regurgitation grade ( B = 0.204, 95% CI: 0.050–0.358). Among 28 complete cases, associations persisted using the mean of three view-specific peaks ( B = 0.213–0.245; p = 0.007–0.019). In a 10-case interobserver reanalysis, maximum peak EL had an intraclass correlation coefficient of 0.759 (95% CI: 0.294–0.934), with ratio limits of agreement of 0.56–2.41. Cannula angle and aortic regurgitation grade were not associated with EL. These preliminary findings support larger prospective studies but do not establish mechanism, measurement interchangeability, or clinical utility.

items.title: ProtekDuo Cannulation Through the Left Internal Jugular Vein: A First-in-Human Technique
Medical Students Want More Exposure to Biomedical Innovation
items.abstract: Biomedical innovation is a core concept not traditionally included in medical school curricula, and exposure to and hands-on use of diagnostic and therapeutic technologies typically occur only during clinical rotations. By potentially delaying their exposure to innovation, entrepreneurship, and technology development, we may be missing an opportunity for early engagement. We surveyed medical students at a single US institution for an exploratory needs assessment to characterize their experiences and identify unmet educational opportunities in biomedical innovation, which we then used to guide our development of an interdisciplinary extracurricular program. Sixty-nine percent of medical students reported they had no exposure to biomedical innovation, yet 90% wanted to get involved, citing limited knowledge and resources as barriers. We developed an interdisciplinary extracurricular program to address this need, which emphasizes early exposure to technology development, experiential learning, multidisciplinary collaboration, and mentorship. Participants’ evaluation forms (n = 229) indicated that each event (n = 38) was a worthwhile educational experience (98%). Despite having little exposure, medical students want to participate in biomedical innovation and valued our interdisciplinary educational program, which aligns well with ASAIO’s mission of inspiring the next generation of early-stage biomedical innovators.

items.title: Impact of Cannulation on Venous Congestion, Right Ventricular Function, and End-Organ Protection During VV ECMO: A Computational Study
items.abstract: Cannulation strategy during veno-venous extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (VV-ECMO) may influence venous drainage, right ventricular loading, and end-organ perfusion beyond gas exchange. We compared four cannulation strategies using a computational hemodynamic framework: pulmonary dual-lumen, Avalon dual-lumen, femoro-jugular, and femoro-femoral VV-ECMO, with three cannula sizes/configurations for each strategy and 10 virtual adult patients per configuration (120 simulations). Cannulation strategy was strongly associated with residual venous congestion and simulated organ dysfunction. Pulmonary dual-lumen support showed the most favorable size-dependent profile. The 31 Fr configuration achieved the lowest central venous pressure (8.8 ± 1.2 mm Hg), smallest inferior vena cava diameter (17.6 ± 1.6 mm), and greatest improvement in tricuspid annular plane systolic excursion (+5.4 ± 1.0 mm). It was also associated with the lowest creatinine, bilirubin, simulated dialysis risk, and hepatic dysfunction. Femoro-femoral VV-ECMO showed the least favorable profile despite preserved flow capability. These findings suggest that cannulation geometry may be an important determinant of venous decongestion, right-heart interaction, and simulated cardio-renal-hepatic protection beyond extracorporeal flow alone.

items.title: Recognition Requires Nomination: The People Who Make Excellence Visible
A Multicenter Randomized Controlled Trial of a Digital Health Intervention for Medication Optimization in Heart Failure: The ENGAGE-HF Trial Outcomes
items.abstract: Background: Despite clear evidence that guideline-directed medical therapy (GDMT) significantly reduces mortality and hospitalizations in patients with heart failure (HF) with reduced and mildly reduced ejection fraction, real-world implementation remains suboptimal. Digital health interventions may promote GDMT titration after hospital discharge. Methods: The ENGAGE-HF trial was a multicenter, two-arm, open-label, randomized controlled trial across three academic centers, funded by the AHA Strategically Focused Research Network (SFRN) for Health Technology and Innovation. Patients recently hospitalized with HF, with or without a primary hospital diagnosis of HF, and LVEF <50% receiving suboptimal GDMT were randomized 1:1 to either the ENGAGE-HF app or usual care for 90 days. The ENGAGE-HF intervention consisted of a patient-facing mobile app and a clinician dashboard overseen by study coordinators. The primary outcome was the Medication Optimization Score (MOS, scale 0-100%) at 90 days. Secondary outcomes were individual GDMT therapies and the Kansas City Cardiomyopathy Questionnaire Clinical Summary Score at 90 days. Results: A total of 134 participants were randomized. At 90 days, the adjusted MOS was significantly higher in the ENGAGE-HF group compared to the control group (83.7% vs. 74.0%, p = 0.010). Results remained consistent across multiple sensitivity analyses. Overall prescribing prevalence increased more in the ENGAGE-HF group for MRAs (+15.9 vs. +2.5 percentage points) and SGLT2 inhibitors (+10.9 vs. +2.5 percentage points). Furthermore, the ENGAGE-HF group demonstrated greater increases in achieving target doses for ARNI (+18.8% vs. +6.3%) and beta-blockers (+8.5% vs. +0.6%). KCCQ-23 CSS at 90 days was 75.2 (SE 2.6) in the intervention group versus 72.2 (SE 2.6) in the control group (between-group p = 0.40). Conclusions: ENGAGE-HF, a digital health intervention that integrates remote monitoring, patient engagement, and clinical decision support, significantly improved GDMT optimization at 90 days compared with usual care among patients with HF. Registration: URL: https://clinicaltrials.gov Unique Identifier: NCT06750549

items.title: Current Patterns and Best Practices for Prescribing Novel Heart Failure Medications in Children: A Science Advisory From the American Heart Association
items.abstract: Robust evidence from randomized controlled trials of novel heart failure medications in adults has demonstrated improved quality of life, reduced hospitalizations, and decreased mortality, informing current treatment guidelines. In contrast, data supporting the clinical benefits of newer heart failure therapies in children remain limited. To assess contemporary prescribing practices and clinician perspectives, we surveyed pediatric heart failure physicians across the United States and Canada regarding the use of angiotensin receptor-neprilysin inhibitors, sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 inhibitors, and iron replacement therapy in children. We also reviewed the existing pediatric literature and summarized reported side effects, dosing experience, and practical guidance for the use of these therapies in the absence of rigorous evidence.

items.title: Assessment of Medical Urgency for Heart Transplant in Patients With Cardiac Amyloidosis and Hypertrophic Cardiomyopathy Using a Continuous Risk Score
items.abstract: BACKGROUND: The current 6-status US heart allocation system uses a treatment-based framework for heart transplantation listing, with status 1 representing the highest urgency. However, this system may inadequately risk-stratify patients with restrictive cardiomyopathy, specifically cardiac amyloidosis (CA) and hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM), for whom many high-intensity medical and device-based therapies are less effective. METHODS: We identified all adult heart transplantation candidates listed between 2019 and 2024 using the Scientific Registry of Transplant Recipients. We determined the medical urgency of candidates with CA and HCM using the validated 50-point US-Candidate Risk Score, which incorporates laboratory data and use of mechanical circulatory support. RESULTS: The study cohort included 26 545 candidates (median age, 56 years; 74% male), of whom 534 were diagnosed with CA (2.0%) and 860 with HCM (3.2%). Overall, patients with CA had significantly higher overall median UC-CRS scores compared with those with HCM and other diagnoses (36, 26, 30; P <0.01), and across statuses 1 to 4. A higher proportion of patients with CA were categorized as high risk (CRS >40) compared with other diagnoses (33% versus 27%; P <0.01), while patients with HCM had the lowest proportion of high-risk scores (22%). Status 2 was the most common status at transplant across all groups, with exceptions at status 2 most frequently used among patients with CA and HCM compared with all others (58%, 70%, 46%; P <0.01). CONCLUSIONS: Patients with CA have higher medical acuity by US-Candidate Risk Score than is reflected in the current 6-status system. Both CA and HCM rely heavily on exceptions to achieve transplantation, highlighting the need for a continuous risk-based allocation model.

items.title: Cardiac and Metabolic Effects of Semaglutide in Obesity-Related HFpEF
items.abstract: Background Two-thirds of patients with heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF) have obesity, and >90% have increased visceral adiposity. Adiposity-associated HFpEF is characterized by hemodynamic congestion driven by impaired cardiac reserve, volume overload and altered blood distribution, adverse cardiac remodeling, pericardial constraint, systemic vascular stiffening, myosteatosis, metabolic dysfunction, and altered adipokine signaling profiles. Recent clinical trials have demonstrated that glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists alleviate symptoms and improve exercise capacity in patients with obesity-related HFpEF, but the mechanisms underlying these benefits remain uncertain. Objectives This study aims to elucidate the mechanisms by which semaglutide improves clinical status in patients with HFpEF and obesity. Methods The CAMEO-SEMA trial is a single-center, prospective, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled mechanistic trial evaluating the effects of semaglutide in obesity-related HFpEF. Results Eighty-one participants have been randomized in a 2:1 ratio to semaglutide subcutaneously once weekly or matching placebo for 52 weeks. Comprehensive pathophysiological characterization is being performed at baseline and following treatment, including invasive exercise hemodynamic status, transcardiac (arterial and coronary sinus) blood sampling at rest and with exercise, cardiac magnetic resonance imaging, submaximal and peak aerobic capacity through expired gas analysis, comprehensive rest and exercise echocardiography, body composition and visceral adiposity assessment, blood volume analysis, oral glucose testing, subcutaneous adipose tissue biopsy, and inflammatory-adipokine profiling. Conclusions The CAMEO-SEMA trial will provide comprehensive, novel insights into the mechanisms by which the glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists semaglutide affects the key pathophysiological factors causing symptoms, exercise limitation, and morbidity in patients with obesity-related HFpEF. (Cardiac and Metabolic Effects of Semaglutide [CAMEO-SEMA]; NCT05371496).

items.title: Remote Voice Analysis for Monitoring Ambulatory Heart Failure Patients: Results of the DETECT-HF Study
items.abstract: Background The Cordio HearO System is a software medical device that analyzes daily voice recordings to identify changes associated with worsening HF. Objective The objective of the DETECT-HF study was to evaluate the ability of the HearO System to detect impending HF events (HFEs) using a voice-based monitoring algorithm. Methods DETECT-HF was a prospective, international, multicenter, single-arm, blinded, noninterventional study in HF patients who performed daily voice recordings on their smartphones. Co-primary endpoints were sensitivity for detecting adjudicated first HFEs (HF hospitalization or outpatient HFE requiring intravenous therapy) and the unexplained priority notification rate (UPNR). Performance was assessed against predefined criteria of a lower 95% confidence interval (CI) ≥60% for sensitivity and <3 notifications/person-year for UPNR. Analyses were also performed using all HFEs (first and recurrent events). Secondary endpoints included safety and usability assessments, including patient adherence to daily voice recordings. Results Between March 2021 and July 2025, 563 patients were enrolled. Mean age was 67.6±11.5 years, and 70.9% were male. The HearO System detected 52 of 76 first HFEs, yielding a sensitivity of 68.4% (95% CI: 58.0%-78.9%; p=0.0573), which was below the pre-specified performance target. For all HFEs (n=112), sensitivity was 70.5% (95% CI: 60.8%-78.7%). On average, HFEs were detected 24.1 days before clinical presentation. UPNR was 2.65 notifications/patient-year (95% CI: 2.53-2.76; P<0.001) for first HFEs, meeting the pre-specified performance criterion, and 2.59 notifications/patient-year (95% CI: 2.48-2.70) for all HFEs. Sensitivity and UPNR estimates were consistent across prespecified subgroups. A questionnaire demonstrated excellent usability (mean scores ranging from 4.7 to 4.9 on a 5-point scale across usability questions). Mean adherence to daily recordings was 85%, and no device-related adverse events occurred. Conclusions Voice-based monitoring with the HearO System detected impending HFEs weeks before clinical presentation with reasonable sensitivity, low alert burden, high adherence, and an excellent safety profile.

items.title: A Multi-Center Cluster-Assigned Trial of Electronic Alerts to Improve Prescribing of Mineralocorticoid Receptor Antagonist Therapy for Heart Failure
Ultraprocessed Food Consumption and Incident Heart Failure
items.abstract: BACKGROUND: Ultraprocessed foods (UPFs) are associated with adverse cardiometabolic outcomes and increased atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease risk. However, the relationship between UPF intake and incident heart failure (HF) remains incompletely understood. OBJECTIVES: The aims of this study were to examine the relationship between UPF consumption and incident HF and to evaluate potential biological mediators. METHODS: A sample of 6,531 U.S. adults 45-84 years of age without cardiovascular disease at baseline from MESA (Multi-Ethnic Study of Atherosclerosis) was analyzed. UPF intake was classified according to the Nova system. Multivariable Cox proportional hazards models evaluated associations between UPF intake and incident HF. Phenotypes were classified as heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF) (ejection fraction <50%) and heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF) (ejection fraction ≥50%). Mediation analyses were conducted to evaluate the potential mediating role of waist-to-height ratio as a surrogate measure for central adiposity. RESULTS: Higher UPF intake was significantly associated with increased risk of incident HF across sequentially adjusted models. In the primary model (model 2), each additional daily serving of UPF was associated with a 5% higher risk of incident HF (HR: 1.052; 95% CI: 1.002-1.103). When stratified by phenotype, UPF intake remained significantly associated with HFpEF (HR: 1.096; 95% CI: 1.016-1.183) but not HFrEF. Participants in the upper 80% of UPF intake had a >2-fold higher risk for HFpEF than those in the lowest 20% (HR: 2.234; 95% CI: 1.289-3.874). In mediation analyses, waist-to-height ratio statistically accounted for ∼51% of the association between UPF intake and total HF and 49% of the association between UPF intake and HFpEF. CONCLUSIONS: Higher UPF consumption was significantly associated with an increased risk for incident HF, with associations driven primarily by the HFpEF phenotype. Central adiposity, measured by waist-to-height ratio, demonstrated a potential mediating role, suggesting that obesity-related cardiometabolic pathways may represent an important pathway linking UPF consumption to HF risk.

items.title: Rethinking Authorship in Large Multicenter Clinical Trials
Safety and Efficacy of Omecamtiv Mecarbil by QRS Duration and Cardiac Resynchronization Therapy in GALACTIC-HF
items.abstract: BACKGROUND: Prolonged QRS duration portends worse outcomes in heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF). In GALACTIC-HF, omecamtiv mecarbil (OM) reduced the primary composite endpoint of first heart failure (HF) event or cardiovascular death. OBJECTIVES: The objectives of this study were to evaluate whether QRS duration and the presence of cardiac resynchronization therapy (CRT) modify the treatment effect of OM. METHODS: GALACTIC-HF enrolled patients with symptomatic HF, HFrEF (≤35%), and elevated natriuretic peptides. Baseline QRS duration was available in 8,089 of 8,232 participants (98.0%), who were classified into 3 groups: QRS duration <120 ms without CRT (n = 3,724), QRS duration ≥120 ms without CRT (n = 3,225), and CRT regardless of QRS duration (n = 1,140). The authors assessed whether the effect of OM on the primary composite endpoint, first HF hospitalization, cardiovascular death, and all-cause death differed across these groups. RESULTS: Patients with QRS ≥120 ms without CRT and those with CRT were older, had lower EF, worse health status, and higher N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide levels than those with QRS <120 ms without CRT. When modeled as a continuous variable, baseline QRS duration was associated with clinical outcomes among patients without CRT but not among those with CRT. Among patients with QRS ≥120 ms without CRT, OM appeared to confer less benefit for the primary composite endpoint (Pinteraction = 0.072), for cardiovascular death (Pinteraction = 0.003), and for all-cause death (Pinteraction = 0.009). In contrast, among patients treated with CRT, OM was beneficial regardless of QRS duration. CONCLUSIONS: In GALACTIC-HF, OM appeared less effective in patients with prolonged QRS duration who did not have CRT, whereas it remained beneficial in CRT-treated patients. (Global Approach to Lowering Adverse Cardiac Outcomes Through Improving Contractility in Heart Failure [GALACTIC-HF]; NCT02929329).

items.title: Systemic Microvascular Endothelial Dysfunction in Heart Failure with Preserved Ejection Fraction and Type 2 Diabetes
items.abstract: BACKGROUND: Heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF) is increasingly recognized as a systemic disorder featuring microvascular dysfunction and metabolic comorbidities such as type 2 diabetes (T2D). However, the extent to which systemic microvascular abnormalities reflect HFpEF or coexisting T2D remains incompletely understood. OBJECTIVES: The aim of this study was to characterize systemic microvascular dysfunction in patients with HFpEF and to evaluate the contribution of comorbid T2D. METHODS: Systemic microvascular function, defined as flow responses expressed as cutaneous vascular conductance, was assessed using laser speckle contrast analysis with iontophoresis of acetylcholine, insulin, and sodium nitroprusside. Analysis adjusted for age and sex were performed across healthy controls (n = 23), T2D (n = 138), HFpEF without T2D (n = 63), and HFpEF with T2D (n = 27). RESULTS: Insulin-mediated microvascular perfusion was reduced in participants with T2D (-0.30 arbitrary perfusion units [APU]/mm Hg; P < 0.001) and in HFpEF with T2D (-0.32 APU/mm Hg; P = 0.004) compared with controls, whereas responses in HFpEF without T2D were not different from controls. Perfusion responses to sodium nitroprusside were reduced in T2D and HFpEF with T2D, while responses to acetylcholine were preserved. No statistically detectable interaction between HFpEF and T2D was observed. Sex did not modify the relationship between HFpEF and microvascular dysfunction, but exploratory sex-stratified analyses showed reduced insulin-mediated microvascular perfusion in T2D (mean difference: -0.30 APU/mm Hg; P = 0.020) and HFpEF + T2D (mean difference: -0.51 APU/mm Hg; P = 0.002) compared with controls. CONCLUSIONS: Systemic microvascular dysfunction, particularly impaired insulin-mediated vasodilation, was observed in HFpEF. The observed abnormalities were predominantly present in participants with comorbid type 2 diabetes.

items.title: Effect of Aficamten in Obstructive Hypertrophic Cardiomyopathy With Comorbidities: Obesity, Hypertension, and Diabetes
items.abstract: What is the clinical question being addressed? Does aficamten provide similar benefits in patients with oHCM and common cardiometabolic comorbidities, and do these comorbidities modify the treatment effect? What is the main finding? Aficamten benefits patients with oHCM regardless of common cardiometabolic comorbidities.

items.title: The Gut-Heart-Muscle Hypothesis in Heart Failure
Efficacy and Safety of Mineralocorticoid Receptor Antagonists Across Geographic Regions in Heart Failure
items.abstract: What is the clinical question being addressed? Does the efficacy and safety of MRA therapy differ by geographic region in patients with HF across the spectrum of LVEF? What is the main finding? Despite substantial regional differences in event rates, treatment effects of MRAs on efficacy and safety outcomes were broadly consistent across geographic regions and HF phenotypes.

items.title: Epigenetic DNA Methylation Patterns Stratify Heart Failure Phenotypes and Predict Clinical Outcome
items.abstract: BACKGROUND: Environmental and lifestyle exposures contribute substantially to heart failure (HF) development and progression. DNA methylation integrates cumulative environmental exposures and may provide insight into biological pathways and risk stratification across HF phenotypes. OBJECTIVES: The aim of this study was to identify phenotype-specific DNA methylation patterns across HF subtypes and evaluate their association with clinical outcomes. METHODS: Individuals with symptomatic HF (universal definition stage C or D; HF with preserved ejection fraction, HF with mildly reduced ejection fraction, and heart failure with reduced ejection fraction [HFrEF]) from the MyoVasc (An Epidemiological Cohort Study to Investigate the Development and Progression of Heart Failure and the Interaction With Vascular Disease) cohort (N = 3,289) and individuals without cardiovascular disease from the population-based GHS (Gutenberg Health Study) (N = 18,700) were analyzed. Genome-wide DNA methylation from whole blood was measured using the Illumina Infinium MethylationEPIC array. Phenotype-specific DNA methylation scores were derived using penalized regression models adjusted for cardiovascular risk factors. RESULTS: Distinct and partially overlapping DNA methylation patterns were identified across HF phenotypes, with limited overlap at the CpG level but substantial convergence at the gene level. Phenotype-specific methylation scores discriminated patients with HF from control subjects with high accuracy (area under the curve: 0.97-0.98). Methylation signatures in HF with preserved ejection fraction were associated predominantly with metabolic and inflammatory markers, whereas HFrEF signatures were more strongly linked to markers of myocardial injury and vascular disease. All methylation scores were independently associated with composite of cardiac death or hospitalization for worsening HF and all-cause mortality, with the strongest association observed for the HFrEF score (HR: ∼1.7 per SD). CONCLUSIONS: Symptomatic HF phenotypes are characterized by distinct and shared DNA methylation signatures. These epigenetic profiles reflect relevant biological pathways and are associated with adverse clinical outcomes, supporting their potential utility in HF risk stratification and precision medicine.

items.title: Predicting Incident Heart Failure in CKD
Pulmonary Artery Pressures Predict Heart Failure Events Following Heart Failure and Non–Heart Failure Events
items.abstract: BACKGROUND: It is uncertain whether pulmonary artery pressure (PAP) within the first week after either hospitalization for a non-heart failure event (HFE) or hospitalization or urgent visit for a HFE predicts the risk of recurring events. OBJECTIVES: This study aims to determine if PAP following a non-HFE or HFE predicts subsequent events within 90 days. METHODS: The authors examined non-HFE and HFE in patients with heart failure (HF) treated with remote hemodynamic-guided management using a wireless PAP sensor in the GUIDE-HF study. They compared PAP trends before and after a non-HFE or HFE and stratified the admitting and discharge PAP during the index event into groups with a subsequent HFE, non-HFE, or no further events within 90 days. RESULTS: Following index non-HFE (615 events, n = 425), post-discharge diastolic PAP was significantly higher in patients with a subsequent HFE (23.3 ± 7.9 mm Hg) (n = 97) vs patients with a subsequent non-HFE (20.4 ± 7.3 mm Hg; P = 0.0046) (n = 189) or no further events (20.9 ± 7.4 mm Hg; P = 0.015) (n = 329). Following index HFE (539 events, n = 358), post-discharge diastolic PAP was numerically higher in patients with a subsequent HFE (23.9 ± 6.9 mm Hg) (n = 199) than in patients with a subsequent non-HFE (22.0 ± 7.1 mm Hg; P = 0.078 (n = 102) and in those with no further events (22.0 ± 7.6 mm Hg; P = 0.021) (n = 238). Similar trends were observed for HF with reduced ejection fraction and HF with preserved ejection fraction subgroups and with systolic and mean PAP. CONCLUSIONS: Persistently elevated PAP early after discharge following either an index non-HFE or an HFE is associated with the risk of a subsequent HFE. (Hemodynamic-GUIDEd Management of Heart Failure [GUIDE-HF]; NCT03387813).

items.title: The Heart Speaks in Watts, Not Liters
Are Higher NT-proBNP Thresholds for Atrial Fibrillation Necessary in Trials of HFrEF?
Effects of Digoxin in Modern Heart Failure Treatment
items.abstract: Background The DIG-Mod HF trial is the first trial to evaluate the mechanistic effects of low-dose digoxin on myocardial work and functional exercise capacity in patients with heart failure (HF) with reduced ejection fraction receiving contemporary guideline-recommended medical therapy (GRMT). Although a recent meta-analysis demonstrated clinical benefit of cardiac glycosides in addition to contemporary GRMT, the mechanistic basis for this effect remains unexplored. Objectives The authors aimed to investigate whether low-dose digoxin improves myocardial work and functional exercise capacity when added to optimized GRMT. Methods An open-label, randomized crossover trial enrolled 50 patients with HF with reduced ejection fraction on maximally tolerated GRMT. Patients were randomized 1:1 to digoxin 0.125 mg/day plus standard of care or standard of care alone, each for 24 weeks, for a total study duration of 48 weeks. Co-primary endpoints were within-patient changes in peak oxygen consumption (Vo 2 ) and left ventricular global work index. Results The study population was highly optimized, with 88% in NYHA functional class II on near-universal quadruple GRMT. Digoxin did not significantly improve peak Vo 2 (mean difference: -0.08 mL/kg/min; 95% CI: -1.64 to 1.47 mL/kg/min; P = 0.914). Global work index improved significantly (mean difference: 157.8 mm Hg%; 95% CI: 12.2-303.4 mm Hg%; P = 0.034). N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide and Kansas City Cardiomyopathy Questionnaire-12 score also improved during the digoxin period. The composite safety endpoint did not differ significantly between arms (P = 0.089). Conclusions Low-dose digoxin significantly improved myocardial work without improving peak Vo 2 . Demonstrating these effects in a clinically stable, well-treated population is consistent with an independent pharmacologic effect of digoxin in addition to modern guideline-directed therapy. (Effects of Digoxin in Modern Heart Failure Treatment [DIG-Mod HF]; EU Clinical Trials Register Number: 2024-513448-26-00).

items.title: Effect of Aficamten vs Metoprolol on Cardiac Biomarkers in Obstructive Hypertrophic Cardiomyopathy
items.abstract: BACKGROUND: Biomarkers associated with clinical outcomes in obstructive hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (oHCM) may change with therapy. OBJECTIVES: The aim of this study was to examine biomarker responses to aficamten vs metoprolol monotherapy in patients with oHCM in the randomized MAPLE-HCM (Phase 3 Trial to Evaluate the Efficacy and Safety of Aficamten Compared to Metoprolol Succinate in Adults With Symptomatic oHCM) trial and assess if changes parallel treatment effects. METHODS: Differences in N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide (NT-proBNP) and high-sensitivity cardiac troponin I (hs-cTnI) from baseline to end of therapy were compared by treatment. RESULTS: Participants receiving aficamten (n = 88) or metoprolol (n = 87) were generally well matched for baseline characteristics. After 24 weeks, geometric mean NT-proBNP decreased by 73% with aficamten but increased by 42% with metoprolol (treatment effect -81% [-85% to -76%]; P < 0.001). Mean hs-cTnI decreased by 43% with aficamten and by 17% with metoprolol (treatment effect -28% [-41% to -13%]; P = 0.001); both biomarkers reverted to baseline after washout. Regardless of treatment, the correlation between changes in biomarkers was significant for NT-proBNP and peak oxygen uptake (-0.42; P < 0.001) and Kansas City Cardiomyopathy Questionnaire-Clinical Summary Score (KCCQ-CSS) (-0.26; P < 0.001) and between changes in hs-cTnI and KCCQ-CSS (-1.9; P = 0.013) but not peak oxygen uptake (-0.11; P = 0.22). When considering treatment, there were significant correlations between improvements in NT-proBNP and Valsalva left ventricular outflow tract gradient (LVOT-G) (r = +0.25; P = 0.02) and the ratio between early transmitral filling and early diastolic tissue Doppler velocity (r = +0.50; P = 0.001) with aficamten. Correlations between improvements in hs-cTnI and Valsalva LVOT-G (r = +0.17; P = 0.03) and maximal left ventricular wall thickness (r = +0.25; P = 0.001) were observed with aficamten. CONCLUSIONS: Aficamten treatment resulted in lower NT-proBNP and hs-cTnI vs metoprolol. Reduction in NT-proBNP correlated with improved exercise capacity, LVOT-G, and health status. These results provide mechanistic insights regarding the benefit of aficamten over metoprolol in MAPLE-HCM. (Phase 3 Trial to Evaluate the Efficacy and Safety of Aficamten Compared to Metoprolol Succinate in Adults With Symptomatic oHCM [MAPLE-HCM]; NCT05767346).

items.title: Video-Based Care Transition Intervention and Self-Care in Patients With Heart Failure With Reduced Ejection Fraction (EVIT-HF)
Genetic and Clinical Predictors of Myocardial Recovery in Biopsy-Proven Pediatric Myocarditis Requiring Ventricular Assist Device
items.abstract: BACKGROUND: Myocardial recovery with ventricular assist device (VAD) support is a rare but favorable outcome. OBJECTIVES: This study aims to identify genetic and clinical determinants of myocardial recovery in pediatric patients with myocarditis requiring VAD support. METHODS: This multicenter study included 86 pediatric patients with biopsy-proven myocarditis on VAD support from MYKKE (Myocarditis Registry for Children and Adolescents). A subcohort (n = 57) underwent next-generation sequencing of cardiomyopathy-associated genes. Patients were stratified by outcome (recovery vs nonrecovery). The least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) model and logistic regression were applied to identify clinical variables of recovery. Gene burden and rare variant enrichment analyses were conducted. RESULTS: Recovery occurred in 37% (32/86) of patients. Cardiomyopathy-associated variants were enriched in the cohort compared with population control subjects (P < 0.001). Likely pathogenic/pathogenic (LP/P) cardiomyopathy-associated variants were more common in the nonrecovery group (P = 0.045). Gene burden analyses implicated TNNI3 (cardiac troponin I), BAG3 (BAG cochaperone 3), and LMNA (lamin A/C) in nonrecovery. Patients with findings of chronic myocarditis on biopsy more often carried LP/P variants or high-probability variants of uncertain significance compared with patients with acute myocarditis (P = 0.027). The LASSO-derived model showed good discrimination for recovery (area under the curve: 0.90; 95% CI: 0.83-0.98), identifying 11 variables. In multivariable logistic regression analysis, young age, female sex, and acute myocarditis on biopsy were significantly associated with recovery. Genetic variants provided independent negative predictive value for recovery beyond the LASSO-derived model (LP/P: P = 0.065; LP/P/high-probability variants of uncertain significance: P = 0.008). CONCLUSIONS: In pediatric myocarditis, myocardial recovery is associated with absence of cardiomyopathy-associated genetic variants, severe inflammation, and young age. Incorporating genetic analyses into the diagnostic workflow may improve identification of recovery candidates and guide personalized treatment strategies.

items.title: Renal Dysfunction and Predictors of Improvement in Ventricular Assist Device Recipients, in the CKD-LVAD Registry
Characteristics and Long-Term Outcomes of Patients With History of Malignancy Undergoing Heart Transplantation
Bioelectrical impedance analysis and treatment response to dapagliflozin, spironolactone, and their combination: a SOGALDI-PEF analysis
When Risk Becomes a Diagnosis: Biomarker-Driven CKM Stage Migration in Chronic Kidney Disease
Early Implementation of Guideline-Directed Medical Therapy and Outcomes in Cardiogenic Shock Supported by Micro-Axial Flow Pumps
items.abstract: Background The role of guideline-directed medical therapy (GDMT) in patients with cardiogenic shock (CS) supported by mechanical circulatory support remains poorly defined. The feasibility and potential benefits of early GDMT initiation during Impella support are uncertain. Methods We analyzed a multicenter prospective registry of consecutive patients with CS treated with Impella between 2020 and 2024. GDMT exposure was defined as the number of heart failure therapies administered at device explantation. The primary outcome was in-hospital mortality. Multivariable logistic regression adjusted for clinical severity and early shock trajectory. Landmark analysis excluded patients dying within 5 days, while mixed-effects models accounted for center-level clustering. Results Among 140 patients (mean age 61 years; 20% female), 40% received concomitant ECMO (ECPella). In-hospital mortality was 38%. At explantation, 43% received at least one GDMT agent. Greater GDMT exposure was independently associated with lower mortality (OR 0.28 per additional therapy; 95% CI 0.14–0.58; p<0.001). This association remained consistent in landmark analysis (adjusted OR 0.31; 95% CI 0.16–0.66; p<0.001) and after excluding patients with cardiac arrest (adjusted OR 0.48; 95% CI 0.23–0.88; p=0.002). A graded relationship between GDMT intensity and survival was observed. Center-level variability was negligible (intraclass correlation coefficient 0.02). Conclusions In patients with CS supported by Impella, early GDMT implementation was feasible in a substantial proportion of patients. Greater GDMT exposure at device explantation was associated with lower in-hospital mortality. Ventricular unloading may provide an opportunity to initiate outcome-modifying therapies during the acute phase of CS.

items.title: Rehabilitation across the hemodynamic continuum: Opportunities for better functional recovery in cardiogenic shock
Biventricular support without blood contact: an early assessment of soft robotic mechanical circulatory support
Proposal for Preference-Informed Win Statistics and Use to Re-Analyze Seven Heart Failure Pharmacotherapy Trials
items.abstract: Aims Win ratios (WRs) allow simultaneous evaluation of multiple outcomes using hierarchical composite endpoints, but outcome hierarchies are typically determined by researchers without patient input. We sought to develop a patient preference-informed approach to constructing hierarchical composite endpoints for WR analysis and use it to re-analyze heart failure (HF) pharmacotherapy trials. Methods We synthesized patient preference data from multiple sources to derive two preference-informed hierarchical composite endpoints: tolerability-over-quality of life (QoL) (in descending order, primary: death, HF hospitalization, side-effects, QoL) and QoL-prioritized (QoL, death, HF hospitalization, side-effects). We then re-analyzed individual participant-level data from seven RCTs (n=15,357) using these preference-informed hierarchies and, for comparison, a conventional hierarchy (death, HF hospitalization, QoL, side-effects) with two to four components. Results Of seven re-analyzed trials, five showed consistent results across preference-informed and conventional WRs, indicating preference insensitivity. Two trials exhibited preference-sensitive findings. In TOPCAT-Americas, benefit with spironolactone over placebo was attenuated in the tolerability-over-QoL hierarchy (WR 1.03 [95% confidence interval 0.92-1.15] versus conventional four-component WR 1.13 [1.01-1.26]), reflecting large between-group differences in side-effects. In BEST, the benefit of bucindolol over placebo was attenuated and no longer statistically significant with the QoL-prioritized hierarchy (WR 1.07 [0.98-1.16] versus conventional four-component WR 1.15 [1.05-1.26]), despite favorable effects on all four components. Conclusions Integrating empirically-derived patient preferences into hierarchical composite endpoints provides a pragmatic and generalizable approach to evaluating the net clinical benefit of HF pharmacotherapy using WRs. These results highlight the value of incorporating patient priorities into trial design and interpretation, and in therapeutic decision-making.

items.title: Clinical profiles and associated outcomes of distinct inflammatory phenotypes in patients with acute heart failure
items.abstract: Background Elevated levels of inflammatory biomarkers are common in acute decompensated heart failure (ADHF) and have been associated with disease progression, diminished diuretic response and adverse outcomes, but a comprehesive understanding of specific inflammatory phenotypes remains elusive. We aimed to identify clinical characteristics, decongestion trajectories and outcomes across inflammatory profiles. Methods Plasma levels of 34 cytokines were measured in 270 patients hospitalized for ADHF enrolled in PUSH-AHF. Unsupervised clustering analyses were performed on cytokine levels to identify patient subgroups based on their inflammatory phenotype. Clinical characteristics, diuresis, natriuresis and clinical outcomes were compared among clusters. We validated our findings in the Japanese JEDI-AHF cohort (n=301) using Random Forest-based cluster projection derived from cytokine levels. Results Four distinct inflammatory clusters were identified: a low-inflammation cluster, a low-grade eotaxin-dominant cluster, and two NF-κB-related inflammatory clusters characterized by IFN-γ/Th1 and Th17/IL-17–dominant responses, respectively. Patients in the low-inflammation and eotaxin-dominant-clusters had the most favourable outcomes. Patients within the IFN-γ/Th1-dominant cluster more often had pre-existing heart failure and reduced kidney function. Patients in the Th17/IL-17–dominant cluster predominantly presented with new-onset heart failure, preserved kidney function, the highest NT-proBNP levels and the most impaired natriuresis and diuresis. The IFN-γ/Th1-dominant cluster was associated with an increased risk of 180-day all-cause mortality (HR=2.59 95%CI [1.22–5.49]) compared to the low-inflammation cluster. External validation in JEDI-AHF showed similar findings. Conclusion Distinct inflammatory phenotypes are present in patients with ADHF and associate with distinctly different clinical profiles, decongestion trajectories and outcomes. This underscores the heterogeneity of inflammation in ADHF and suggests a potential for personalized anti-inflammatory interventions.

items.title: The challenges with add-on trials in transthyretin amyloid cardiomyopathy
Dual Pathway Modulation with SGLT2 Inhibitors and Aldosterone Synthase Inhibitors in Cardio-Kidney Disease: Rationale and Trial Design of the EASi Program
items.abstract: Cardio-kidney diseases share interconnected pathophysiology where renin-angiotensin-aldosterone system (RAAS) overactivation drives pathologic hemodynamic, neurohormonal, inflammatory, and fibrotic changes leading to progressive cardiac and kidney dysfunction. Current RAAS-modulating therapies are limited by residual RAAS risk and aldosterone breakthrough despite angiotensin-converting enzyme inhibitor or angiotensin receptor blocker therapy, incomplete blockade of aldosterone with mineralocorticoid receptor (MR) antagonists, hyperkalemia, and suboptimal implementation. Aldosterone synthase inhibitors (ASi) act upstream of the MR to lower aldosterone production, modulating both MR-dependent and MR-independent aldosterone effects without competing for receptor occupancy. Sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 inhibitors (SGLT2i) reduce adverse cardiovascular and kidney events through cellular, hemodynamic and metabolic effects. The complementary mechanisms of SGLT2i/ASi (SASi) may provide improved cardio-kidney protection. The EASi program will determine whether SASi therapy, added to background guideline-directed therapy including an ACE inhibitor, ARB, or ARNI as appropriate, can improve cardiovascular and kidney outcomes beyond SGLT2 inhibitor monotherapy. EASi-PROTKT (∼11,800 participants) evaluates prevention of incident heart failure events or cardiovascular death in patients with hypertension, type 2 diabetes, and established cardiovascular disease. EASi-HF Preserved (∼6,000) and EASi-HF Reduced (∼4,200) evaluate cardiovascular death and first heart failure events across the LVEF spectrum. EASi-KIDNEY (∼11,000) evaluates kidney disease progression and cardiovascular endpoints in chronic kidney disease patients with and without type 2 diabetes. EASi-SYNC (∼500) is a Phase 2 trial comparing SASi versus staggered initiation of SGLT2i and ASi in patients with CKD. Together, these trials will enroll >33,000 participants and test whether SASi can redefine standard of care across the cardio-kidney disease spectrum.

items.title: Correction to: Early effects of SGLT2 inhibitors in acute heart failure: an individual patient-level meta-analysis
Left Atrial Stiffness Index and Prognosis Across Heart Failure Phenotypes in Acute Heart Failure: Insights from the STRATS-AHF Registry
items.abstract: Aims The left atrial stiffness index (LASI), calculated as mitral E/e′ divided by LA reservoir strain, reflects atrial myopathy and elevated filling pressure but has been studied mainly in heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF). We examined whether LASI predicts all-cause mortality and HF hospitalization, and adds to established risk factors, across HF phenotypes in acute heart failure (AHF). Methods and results We analyzed 3,133 patients with AHF from the multicenter STRATS-AHF registry, classified by LVEF into HFrEF, HFmrEF, and HFpEF. During a median follow-up of 32.5 months, 616 (19.7%) had HF admissions, and 1,281 (40.9%) died. After adjustment, each doubling of LASI was associated with mortality (HR 1.13, 95% CI 1.08–1.19), as was LASI above the exploratory cutoff of 1.0 (HR 1.27, 95% CI 1.11–1.46). The association was similar across phenotypes (P for interaction = 0.65) and extended to HF hospitalization and the composite of death or HF hospitalization. LASI added modestly to established predictors; after adjustment for NT-proBNP, its association was not significant in patients with a measured value (HR 1.03, 95% CI 0.97–1.10) but persisted after multiple imputation in the whole cohort (HR 1.10, 95% CI 1.04–1.15). Conclusion In patients hospitalized for AHF, a higher LASI independently predicted all-cause mortality and HF hospitalization across HF phenotypes. Obtained from the admission echocardiogram, LASI captures an atrial component of risk that LVEF does not reflect, although part of this information overlaps with that of NT-proBNP; whether it can guide management remains to be tested.

items.title: Pulmonary hypertension, pulmonary vascular disease, and right ventricular adaptation in transcatheter tricuspid valve intervention
items.abstract: Background Severe tricuspid regurgitation (TR) commonly coexists with pulmonary hypertension (PH), which is associated with adverse outcomes after transcatheter tricuspid valve intervention (TTVI). However, the prognostic impact of PH subtypes and pulmonary vascular resistance (PVR) thresholds in this setting remains insufficiently defined. We evaluated guideline-based PH classifications and their association with outcomes in a large real-world TTVI cohort. Methods In an international multicenter registry, 903 patients with severe TR undergoing TTVI underwent pre-procedural right heart catheterization and were followed for up to two years. PH was defined as mean pulmonary artery pressure >20 mmHg, and PVR was stratified according to guideline thresholds. Endpoints included procedural success, New York Heart Association (NYHA) functional class, and all-cause mortality. Results PH was present in 88% of patients; among patients with PH, median PVR was 2.7 WU. A pre-capillary component (PVR >2 WU) was observed in 68%, including 13% with PVR >5 WU. Procedural success was 81%. NYHA functional class improved significantly from baseline to follow-up irrespective of PH status or PVR. Mortality increased with PH and higher PVR. A PVR threshold of >2 WU alone did not discriminate survival, whereas PVR >5 WU identified a high-risk phenotype. An integrated classification combining PH status, PVR >5 WU, and RV–PA uncoupling (TAPSE/PASP <0.30 mm/mmHg) provided effective prognostic stratification. Conclusion High procedural success and symptomatic improvement were observed following TTVI across PH subgroups. Although infrequent among TTVI patients, a PVR >5 WU identifies a high-risk phenotype with increased mortality. Comprehensive hemodynamic profiling improves risk stratification and may support patient counselling and informed decision-making.

items.title: Impact of the Safety-Net Kidney-After-Heart Transplant Policy on Simultaneous Heart-Kidney Transplant Volume and Outcomes in the United States
items.abstract: On 6/29/2023, the Organ Procurement and Transplantation Network (OPTN) implemented a safety-net policy providing priority kidney transplant (KT) listing status to heart transplant (HT) recipients who develop persistent kidney dysfunction within one year of HT, with the intent of incentivizing isolated HT over simultaneous heart-kidney transplantation (sHKT) in patients with potentially reversible kidney dysfunction. The impact of this policy on sHKT utilization and post-transplant outcomes is unknown. We used interrupted time series analysis of quarterly sHKT volume and compared one-year mortality and kidney graft failure between pre- and post-policy sHKT recipients using multivariable Cox models. In this OPTN registry analysis of HTs performed from 1/1/2020-12/31/2025, among 21,688 HT recipients, 1,133 pre-policy and 877 post-policy recipients underwent sHKT, and 183 received a safety-net KT. We found that 1) following policy implementation, the quarterly change in slope of sHKT utilization was -4.45 procedures per quarter (95% CI -5.94, -2.95), with a concurrent rise in safety-net KT of 2.52 per quarter (95% CI 1.44, 3.59), 2) mortality and kidney graft failure were similar among sHKT recipients post- vs pre-policy implementation (hazard ratio [HR] 0.94, 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.68, 1.29 and HR 0.91, 95% CI 0.67, 1.24, respectively).

items.title: Induction immunosuppression in kidney transplant recipients treated with early corticosteroid cessation: A propensity score case-matched analysis
items.abstract: Early corticosteroid cessation is recommended for low immune risk kidney transplant recipients, but the optimal induction immunosuppression is uncertain. We compared the outcomes of 4,770 first kidney only transplant recipients in the U.S. between 2010 and 2022 treated with tacrolimus and mycophenolate without corticosteroids induced with interleukin-2 receptor antagonists (IL-2Ra) to a matched cohort induced with anti-thymocyte globulin rabbit ( Thymoglobulin.) Only 13% of patients treated with early corticosteroid cessation were induced with IL-2Ra and these patients were more likely to be older and have diabetes. After 1:1 matching, patients treated with IL-2Ra had a higher adjusted risk of allograft loss from any cause (Hazard Ratio (HR) = 1.20, 95% confidence interval (CI) 1.12 to 1.29), death with allograft function (HR = 1.20, 95% CI 1.10 to 1.31), and allograft loss with death as a competing risk (sub hazard ratio SHR = 1.20, 95% CI 1.04 to 1.38). We conclude that IL-2RA induction is selectively used in older, sicker patients but is associated with a higher risk of transplant failure compared to matched patients treated with Thymoglobulin. The findings highlight the need for prospective trials to define optimal induction in patients who may benefit most for early corticosteroid cessation.

items.title: Combined Rituximab and Daratumumab Induces Remission in Refractory Post-Transplant Crescentic IgA Nephropathy
items.abstract: Recurrent crescentic IgA nephropathy (IgAN) after kidney transplantation is rare, aggressive, and often refractory to standard immunosuppression. We report a 17-year-old recipient with biopsy-confirmed recurrent crescentic IgAN two years after transplantation despite corticosteroids and targeted-release budesonide. Rescue therapy comprised one rituximab infusion with daratumumab, followed by four daratumumab infusions. Proteinuria decreased from 5.21 to 0.06 g/g, serum albumin normalized, and allograft function remained stable through day 482 after the first rescue infusion. Longitudinal CyTOF and flow cytometry showed sustained peripheral B-cell depletion and transient NK-cell reductions. One mild upper respiratory infection occurred. Sequential biopsies showed resolution of the active cellular crescent, although mesangial IgA staining and electron-dense deposits persisted. These clinical, histologic, and immune changes were temporally associated with combined CD20- and CD38-targeted therapy. This single case cannot establish efficacy, distinguish the contributions of rituximab and daratumumab, or exclude effects of preceding and supportive treatments, but supports further study of this rescue approach.

items.title: Landscape Of Post-Donation Follow-up of Living Kidney Donors in the United States, 2013-2023
items.abstract: Post-donation follow-up is critical for living kidney donor (LKD) care, facilitating early detection of unusual decrease in renal function and providing opportunities for early intervention. Herein, we update and characterize temporal trends in LKD follow-up (LDF) using Organ Procurement and Transplantation Network data. We identified 64,488 LKDs (2/2013-12/2023) and used logistic regression to assess donor characteristics associated with complete and timely (defined per current OPTN policy) LDF at 6-months, 1-year and 2-years post-donation. The proportion of complete and timely LDF submissions was generally consistent since 2013 for clinical and laboratory data at each time point. Overall, complete and timely 6-month, 1-year, and 2-year LDF were 84%, 81% and 75% for clinical data, and 80%, 75% and 68% for laboratory data. Across all time points, LKDs with pre-donation BMI≥30, Black race, and of younger age had higher odds of incomplete follow-up. We also observed substantial center-level variation, with the proportion of transplant centers meeting 6-month LDF thresholds ranging from 56-81% each year. In this retrospective registry analysis, LDF remained suboptimal and varied by center and donor characteristics, demonstrating the need for targeted approaches to improve LDF, particularly among those at increased risk of kidney disease or facing barriers to care.

items.title: Reevaluation of the role of HBsAg testing in deceased tissue and cornea donor eligibility determination
items.abstract: The utility of hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg) testing in deceased tissue and cornea donor eligibility screening is uncertain in the era of concurrent hepatitis B virus (HBV) nucleic acid testing (NAT) and hepatitis B core total antibody (anti-HBc) screening. We performed an analysis of 300,112 deceased tissue and cornea donors. screened for eligibility between January 2021 and May 2026. Donors were screened for HBV NAT, HBsAg, and anti-HBc; results were analyzed to characterize HBV screening profiles and evaluate the incremental yield of HBsAg reactivity among donors with nonreactive NAT results. Overall, 97.02% of donors (n=291,180) had HBsAg-nonreactive/HBV NAT-nonreactive results and 0.11% (n=318) of donors had HBsAg-reactive/HBV NAT-reactive results. In 0.57% of donors (n=1,697) HBsAg-nonreactive/HBV NAT-reactive results were obtained and 2.30% of donors (n=6,917) were HBsAg-reactive/HBV NAT-nonreactive. Among HBsAg-reactive/HBV NAT-nonreactive donors, 97.79% (n=6,764) were also anti-HBc-nonreactive. HBsAg testing identified 22.5 additional reactive screening results (per 1,000 donors) among donors without HBV NAT and anti-HBc reactivity. A subset of reactive HBsAg specimens were evaluated by supplemental confirmatory testing (n=1,131); only 17.28% were confirmed reactive. In this cohort, HBsAg testing identified potential donors for whom the biological significance of HBsAg reactivity remains uncertain, and current eligibility requirements result in donor exclusion.

items.title: CD154 Blockade Improves Polyfunctionality of T Cells Specific for a Murine Homolog of Epstein-Barr Virus
items.abstract: Anti-CD154 is a promising therapeutic for solid organ transplantation with ongoing clinical trials, but its impact on the immune response to EBV is unknown. Here, B6 animals were infected with a murine homolog of EBV (MHV68) and treated with anti-CD154 costimulation blockade. Results indicate that the ratio of virus-specific CD8 + T cells to MHV68-infected cells was not significantly reduced following in vivo anti-CD154. Interestingly, frequencies of multi-cytokine producing CD4 + and CD8 + T cells were increased following treatment with anti-CD154 compared to either CTLA4-Ig or tacrolimus. This increased polyfunctionality was mechanistically underpinned by an increase in the frequency of CD8 + T cells expressing the memory/stem-like transcription factors TCF-1 and Eomes in the anti-CD154 group compared to CTLA-4Ig, tacrolimus, or untreated controls. Moreover, anti-CD154-treated mice exhibited smaller spleens with a significant decrease in the number of MHV68-YFP + germinal center B cells compared to untreated mice. These data demonstrate that CD154 blockade does not significantly decrease the ratio of virus-specific T cells to infected cells and increases the quality of MHV68-specific CD8 + T cells in a mouse model. Overall, these findings suggest that an anti-CD154 costimulation blockade-based immunosuppression regimen may be beneficial regarding its ability to preserve protective anti-viral immunity during transplantation.

items.title: CD8 T cell phenotype diagnoses graft-versus-host disease after liver transplantation
items.abstract: Graft-versus-host disease (GVHD) is a rare but highly fatal complication following liver transplantation (LT). While donor T cell chimerism is a specific diagnostic indicator, its detection via short tandem repeat (STR) analysis is compromised in LT-GVHD. Here, peripheral blood from nine patients diagnosed with LT-GVHD by STR chimerism or histopathology was analyzed using HLA-specific antibody-based flow cytometry for simultaneous donor T cell chimerism and immunophenotyping. Flow cytometry detected macrochimerism in all patients, including three with negative leukocyte STR results. All patients exhibited lymphocytopenia, with the three cases specifically exhibiting significantly elevated granulocyte-to-lymphocyte ratios, suggesting donor DNA dilution by recipient granulocytes underlies STR false-negatives. Donor-derived CD8 + T cells were predominant and exhibited a TEM-biased phenotype with heightened proliferation, activation, exhaustion, and cytotoxicity compared to GVHD recipient-derived T cells or non-GVHD donor-derived T cells. This immunophenotypic signature was readily detectable within the total CD8 + TEM population, allowing Ki-67-based diagnosis without requiring HLA-specific antibodies. Its diagnostic relevance was further confirmed in an independent external cohort. We conclude that lymphocyte enrichment is essential for reliable STR-based chimerism detection in LT-GVHD. HLA-specific flow cytometry or Ki-67 assessment on total CD8 + TEM cells offers a practical alternative tailored to the lymphopenia context of LT-GVHD.

items.title: Varied trajectories through the transplant evaluation process: Results of a sequence analysis among a national cohort of Veterans with advanced kidney disease
items.abstract: Efforts to improve access to kidney transplant are limited by an incomplete view on the full arc of the evaluation process. We performed a retrospective cohort study among 39,691 adults receiving care within the US Veterans Affairs Health Care System (VA) with incident advanced kidney disease (eGFR≤20 mL/min/1.73 m2) between 10/1/2011 and 12/31/2018. We used sequence analysis to describe sequential steps in the transplant process over 5 years of follow-up. Cohort members' median age at cohort entry was 70.1 (IQR 63.9, 80.2) years and 97.2% were men. Sequence analysis yielded 7 distinct trajectories through the transplant process: 1) early death (50.5%), 2) transplant not mentioned (24.6%), 3) not pursuing transplant (6.2%), 4) prolonged deliberation (4.6%), 5) prolonged evaluation (8.9%), 6) timely waitlisting (3.3%), and 7) timely transplant (1.9%). Older age, higher comorbidity index, and higher area deprivation index were associated with a lower likelihood of experiencing trajectories representing timely progression through the transplant process and a greater likelihood of not engaging with the process or spending prolonged periods of time in early steps. Our findings suggest that current efforts to encourage broader referral for transplant should be complemented by a more streamlined evaluation process and support for shared decision-making.

items.title: Risk Assessment for Transmission of Porcine Endogenous Retrovirus in Clinical Xenotransplantation
items.abstract: Porcine to human xenotransplantation clinical trials are underway. Concerns remain regarding potential transmission of infections including porcine endogenous retroviruses (PERVs) to human xenotransplant recipients with adverse health outcomes. All pigs contain subtypes PERV-A and PERV-B, and some also carry PERV-C. Human cells carry receptors for PERV-A and -B but not for PERV-C. PERV-A can recombine with PERV-B to form PERV-A/B hybrids and recombine with PERV-C to form PERV-A/C hybrids in vivo and in vitro. No evidence of PERV transmission to non-human primates or other laboratory animals, human primary cells, or to humans from surgical or non-surgical exposures has been reported, although transmission of PERV A/C hybrids has been observed in certain permissive transformed human cell lines. PERV inactivation has been achieved via genetic editing in some pig lines. Here, we review the data related to the potential for PERV infection in human xenograft recipients based on published data on PERV structure and host cellular and species tropisms. Despite the lack of evidence regarding transmissibility of PERVs to humans, we advocate the rigorous monitoring of patients and, possibly, their close contacts in initial clinical trials for possible PERV transmission following xenotransplantation.

items.title: Targeted inhibition of Bcl6 effectively suppresses alloactivation of CD4+ T cells with potential for T cell-directed immunosuppression
items.abstract: Bcl6 is a key transcriptional repressor regulating T cell fate; however, its role in T cell alloimmune responses is largely unknown. We investigated Bcl6 expression in T cells within allografts and the potential of targeting Bcl6 to modulate CD4+ T cell alloactivation. Using mIFISH, we found that Bcl6+CD4+ T cells were highly prevalent in kidney transplant biopsies during rejection. In mixed lymphocyte reactions, pharmacological Bcl6 inhibition (Bcl6i) potently suppressed proliferation and effector cytokine production of human CD4+ T cells in a dose-dependent manner. Acting in PBMC and isolated T cell subsets alike, Bcl6i effects were direct, T cell-specific and irrespective of T cell differentiation state. Gene expression and flow cytometry showed Bcl6i reshaped T cell fate by altering key transcriptional programs. Bcl6i suppressed Th1, Th2 and Th17 transcription factors and upregulated TCF1. In addition, T cell inhibitory receptor TIGIT was up- and costimulatory receptor ICOS downregulated. Importantly, we validated the response to Bcl6i in donor-reactive CD4+ T cells from kidney transplant patients, highlighting the translational potential of Bcl6 as a target for T cell-directed immunosuppression in transplantation.

items.title: Anti-Nephrin Antibodies in Focal Segmental Glomerulosclerosis Recurrence After Transplantation: A Multicenter Study from the TANGO Consortium
items.abstract: Anti-nephrin antibodies have been implicated in the pathogenesis of autoimmune podocytopathies, yet their prevalence and predictive value for post-transplant recurrence remain poorly defined. We conducted a retrospective multicenter cohort study through the TANGO Consortium, screening 49,536 kidney transplant recipients across 23 international centers and enrolling 136 patients with biopsy-proven primary FSGS and available pre-transplant serum samples. Circulating anti-nephrin IgG levels were measured by ELISA and validated against an immunoprecipitation assay in a nested cohort. Anti-nephrin antibodies were detected in 11 of 136 patients (8%). Antibody-positive patients were significantly younger at diagnosis compared with antibody-negative patients (median 7 vs. 26 years, p=0.003). Antibody-positive patients had a significantly higher risk of post-transplant recurrence compared with antibody-negative patients (73% vs. 38%; HR 2.62; 95% CI 1.23-5.55; p = 0.012). Recurrence occurred rapidly, with a median time of 1 month post-transplantation. Despite the higher recurrence rate, no significant difference in allograft failure was observed between antibody-positive and antibody-negative patients. Although rare, pre-transplant anti-nephrin antibodies identify a distinct, early-onset FSGS subgroup at markedly increased risk of post-transplant recurrence. These findings support further evaluation of podocyte-targeting autoantibodies for risk stratification in kidney transplantation. Brief communication.

items.title: Hepatitis A outbreak associated with travel to Cuba—Florida, 2024-2026
Acute lung allograft dysfunction: incidence, etiology, severity, alloimmune burden and graft outcomes in a single-centre cohort
items.abstract: Acute lung allograft dysfunction (ALAD) was recently defined by ISHLT consensus. Its severity scale has not been evaluated against outcomes, and the contributions of etiology and alloimmune injury are uncertain. This retrospective single-centre cohort included recipients transplanted between 2018 and 2024 surviving ≥30 days. Every post-transplant visit was reviewed; episodes were adjudicated for etiologies and graded on the ISHLT severity scale and a pre-specified six-point scale. Graft loss within 90 days was modelled by landmark Cox regression; graft loss and chronic lung allograft dysfunction (CLAD) over the whole follow-up by time-dependent Cox models. ALAD occurred in 238 of 303 patients (78.5%), with 862 episodes. Infection predominated; 130 episodes (15%) were alloimmune (cellular or antibody-mediated rejection) and 268 (31.1%) had no FEV1 decline. Severity according to the ISHLT scale predicted graft loss at 90 days (severe, HR 14.8 (4.97-44.0)) and over follow-up (adjusted HR 3.67 (1.78-7.57)), but not CLAD (1.32 (0.67-2.59)). Each additional alloimmune episode predicted both graft loss (1.64 (1.31-2.04)) and CLAD (1.57 (1.06-2.32)). ALAD affects most lung transplant recipients, with nearly a third of episodes lacking documented spirometric decline. Episode severity predicts graft loss, while each additional alloimmune episode is associated with both graft loss and CLAD.

items.title: Corrigendum to: “Novel insights into donor-induced thrombotic microangiopathy: A case series of grafts with TMA in both mate recipients” [American Journal of Transplantation Volume 26, Issue 1, Supplement 1S86 January 2026]
Human CD47 Expression on Porcine Endothelial Cells Regulates Natural Killer Cell Function via SIRPα
items.abstract: Natural killer (NK) cells are pivotal in xenograft rejection, targeting porcine endothelial cells. CD47 acts as a "don't eat me" signal by binding to signal regulatory protein alpha (SIRPα),suppressing immune activation. While this axis has been well characterized in macrophages, its influence on NK cell-mediated xenograft rejection remains unclear. We investigated whether expression of human CD47 (hCD47) on porcine aortic endothelial cells (PAECs) from transgenic pigs inhibits human NK activity. Under static conditions, hCD47 expression on PAECs significantly reduced direct NK cytotoxicity. In microfluidic systems simulating physiological conditions, GGTA1-KO/hCD47-TG PAECs were associated with reduced NK cell-mediated lysis and motility compared with WT PAECs. However, with heat-inactivated human plasma containing anti-pig non-αGal antibodies, hCD47 expression did not protect αGal-knockout PAECs from NK cell-mediated antibody-dependent cellular cytotoxicity (ADCC). Single-cell RNA sequencing showed overall homogeneous NK subtype distribution between WT and hCD47-expressing PAEC conditions. However, a small set of differentially expressed genes showed increased inhibitory receptor expression and reduced effector, activation, and proliferation signatures in NK cells exposed to hCD47. These findings identify hCD47 as an effective checkpoint against direct NK cytotoxicity, but insufficient to prevent ADCC, underscoring the need for combinatorial strategies to achieve durable protection from NK-driven xenograft rejection.

items.title: Comment on “De novo Belatacept based immunosuppression is not associated with increased risk of invasive fungal infection in kidney transplant recipients”
Second multistate outbreak of tuberculosis caused by a bone allograft product
items.abstract: In 2021 and 2023, two different bone allograft products caused nationwide tuberculosis outbreaks. We assessed the morbidity and mortality of the second outbreak and reviewed donor and tissue screening to identify deficiencies. Thirty-six people residing in nine states received the product during spinal and dental procedures. Twenty-seven recipients had tuberculosis infection, 11 had microbiologic or imaging evidence of tuberculosis disease, and two died from tuberculosis within 12 months of outbreak detection. Another recipient died from tuberculosis nearly 3 years after product implantation. The bone donor died of pneumonia and septic shock. Polymerase chain reaction testing of the product before and after distribution did not detect Mycobacterium tuberculosis. Mycobacterial culture was not performed until after outbreak detection, when M. tuberculosis was isolated from 2 of 6 unused product units. This outbreak demonstrates persistent gaps in tissue transplant safety. Appropriate selection of donors and mycobacterial culture of donated tissues could reduce but not eliminate the risk of M. tuberculosis transmission. Therefore, it is important that clinicians monitor tissue recipients and promptly report adverse events to tissue establishments and health authorities.

items.title: The problem of turning PD-1 on
Updates on management of pretransplant and peritransplant infections: Guidance from the American Society of Transplantation Infectious Diseases Community of Practice
items.abstract: An expert panel of the American Society of Transplantation Infectious Diseases Community of Practice reviewed and updated guidance highlighting developments since the prior version published in 2019. A 5-article series provides guidance on screening, diagnosis, and treatment of infections in transplantation. This section focuses on donor and recipient screening and assessment of donor-derived infections, pretransplant ventricular assist device infections, and perioperative prophylaxis. The assessment and management of posttransplant infectious syndromes, including intra-abdominal infection, pneumonia, urinary tract infections, and diarrhea are presented. Recommendations are made based on the modified Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development, and Evaluation approach.

items.title: Liver transplantation for portal vein tumor thrombus in the immunotherapy era: outcomes and risk stratification in a multicentric study
items.abstract: Immune-checkpoint-inhibitors (ICIs) role in liver transplantation (LT) for hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) and portal vein tumor thrombus (PVTT) remains undefined. This study defines outcomes and selection criteria in patients with PVTT. Seventy patients with HCC and PVTT across 14 international centers were analyzed. Three cohorts were studied: ICI+LT (n=24), LT without ICI (n=31), and ICI without LT (n=15). Cox regression analysis identified predictors of survival and defined a high-risk subgroup. Compared with LT-alone patients, ICI+LT achieved higher radiographic response rates (95.8%vs54.8%, p=0.01), longer downstaging time (6vs2.5 months, p=0.028), smaller tumor diameter (1.5vs2.3 cm, p=0.01) and lower Vp3-Vp4 burden (4.2%vs25.8%, p=0.04) at LT. Independent predictors of improved OS were complete radiographic response (HR 0.27, p<0.001), AFP reduction ≥50% (HR 0.48, p=0.01), and meeting Milan criteria (HR 0.35, p<0.001). Vp3-4 (HR 6.00, p=0.008) predicted worse survival. In an exploratory, high-risk subgroup, (no radiographic response, AFP reduction ≤50%, no downstaging, and PVTT at LT), ICI+LT was associated with improved survival compared with LT alone (3-year OS 80.0%vs54.9%, p=0.048; 3-year RFS 68.6%vs41.6%, p=0.023). Well-selected, high-risk patients with PVTT achieved encouraging post-transplant survival. ICI-based therapy may improve oncologic outcomes, highlighting tumor biology's role in patient selection and immunotherapy use in transplant pathways.

items.title: Outside Front Cover
Robotic Single-Port Retroperitoneal Donor Nephrectomy: Surgical Technique and Early Outcomes
items.abstract: Single-port robotic systems are a significant innovation in minimally invasive surgery, allowing surgery through a small incision with the potential for less morbidity and better outcomes. This study reports a novel experience performing robotic donor nephrectomy (RDN) using a single-port platform at the authors' institution. Thirty-eight patients underwent Single-Port RDN (SP-RDN) from January 01 to May 31, 2026. All procedures were performed by the retroperitoneal approach through a single skin incision in the left lower quadrant and no additional laparoscopic assistant ports were required. All left kidney SP-RDN were performed without the need for conversion to open or standard multiport approach. The median operation time, console time, and extraction time were 190, 143 and 3 minutes, respectively. The median warm ischemia time (WIT) was 5 minutes. Blood loss for each procedure was <50mL. Thirty-six of 38 donors were discharged on postoperative day 1, within 24 hours from the end of the surgery. No major (Grade≥3a) complications occurred. Retroperitoneal SP-RDN is a feasible and safe procedure with adequate outcomes. Future studies are needed to define long-term outcomes and compare with established techniques for donor nephrectomy. IRB APPROVAL ID: RAC 2121012.

items.title: Single port robotic kidney-pancreas transplantation with ipsilateral graft placement: initial feasibility report
items.abstract: Simultaneous kidney-pancreas transplantation is the most definitive treatment for type 1 diabetes with end-stage renal manifestations. While most kidney-pancreas transplants are performed via open approaches, select groups have begun performing multiport robotic transplants with and without hand assistance. Here we describe our techniques of fully robotic kidney/pancreas transplantation. We trace our evolution from multiport robotics with contralateral graft placement to single-port, ipsilateral implantation through a 5cm incision, preserving the contralateral vessels for a future transplant. Of six robotic kidney/pancreas transplants, our mean operative time was 5 hours, 56 minutes (range 5:26-6:45) with mean kidney and pancreas vascular anastomotic times of 31 and 40 minutes (range 26-36, 27-45 minutes). Three single-port cases averaged 5 hours, 49 minutes (range 5:33-6:12) with kidney and pancreas vascular anastomotic times of 31 and 39 minutes (range 26-35, 27-45 minutes). All recipients experienced immediate graft function and were discharged after a median of 3.5 hospital days. At 30 days, all patients had functioning allografts and did not require reintervention related to their transplant organs. We believe this could indicate a technical advancement in kidney/pancreas transplantation, justifying further study of robotic techniques.

items.title: The association of air pollution with death and deterioration on the United States transplant waiting list
items.abstract: Ambient air pollution may worsen outcomes among patients with organ failure awaiting transplant. We evaluated associations between residential ambient air pollution exposure and death or deterioration among United States transplant candidates. This retrospective cohort study used Scientific Registry of Transplant Recipients data from 2005-2025, including heart, kidney, liver, and lung candidates in the United States linked to ZIP Code-level pollutant estimates. Exposures were particulate matter (PM2.5), nitrogen dioxide (NO2), and ozone (O3) before listing and during waitlist follow-up. The primary outcome was death or deterioration, with transplant or clinical improvement treated as competing events. Cause-specific Cox models adjusted for demographic, social vulnerability, center, and organ severity measures. Among 1,007,801 candidates, during the waitlist period, each 5-μg/m3 higher PM2.5 exposure was associated with higher hazards among heart (HR, 1.14; 95% CI, 1.11-1.18) and lung candidates (HR, 1.09; 95% CI, 1.04-1.14). Each 10-ppb higher NO2 exposure showed stronger associations among heart (HR, 1.28; 95% CI, 1.23-1.34) and lung candidates (HR, 1.15; 95% CI, 1.09-1.21). Liver and kidney associations were inconsistent. In this study, air pollution was associated with adverse waitlist outcomes, especially among thoracic organ candidates, supporting evaluation and inclusion of environmental stressors in organ allocation policy.

items.title: Ex-vivo xenoperfusion of transgenic pig livers with human whole-blood to evaluate obstacles to short-term xenografting
items.abstract: Extra-corporeal liver cross-circulation, in which a patient's blood is perfused through a donor liver maintained on a machine, may address the unmet need for temporary hepatic support.
