Swine are a promising source of livers but obstacles remain to clinical translation. We established an ex-vivo xenoperfusion model to evaluate perfusion viability, hepatic function, drug metabolism, haematological complications, and immunological compatibility of transgenic pig livers (EGEN-5784) exposed to human whole-blood. EGEN-5784 livers were engineered with triple glycan knockout and insertion of seven human transgenes, with or without inactivation of porcine endogenous retrovirus. Five EGEN-5784 livers were perfused with pooled human whole-blood for 48 hours. Hepatic metabolic, detoxification, and excretory function were preserved. Drug metabolism comparable to human CYP450 pathways was demonstrated. Significant erythrophagocytosis was not observed. IgG and IgM deposition and monocyte/macrophage infiltration occurred. To investigate xenograft-associated thrombocytopenia, four additional EGEN-5784 livers underwent short-duration perfusion with human whole-blood. Severe thrombocytopenia occurred rapidly in control and complement C3-inhibited perfusions. This was attenuated by inhibiting von Willebrand factor using caplacizumab. The ex-vivo xenoperfusion model preserves porcine liver function while enabling mechanistic investigation of human-pig metabolic, immunological, and haematological interactions, providing a valuable platform to evaluate targeted interventions before in-vivo translation.

items.title: FTO stabilizes TRPM8 mRNA to induce calcium overload and ferroptosis in steatotic donor livers during cold preservation
items.abstract: Steatotic donor livers are vulnerable to cold preservation-associated ischemia-reperfusion injury (IRI), but the upstream mechanism is unclear. We investigated whether the m6A demethylase FTO regulates cold-sensitive TRPM8 signaling in steatotic liver grafts using human biopsies, diet-induced murine steatotic grafts, multi-omics, RNA stability assays, and hepatocyte-specific genetic models. FTO was upregulated in steatotic grafts and correlated with early post-transplant injury. FTO bound, demethylated, and stabilized TRPM8 mRNA, increasing TRPM8 expression. During hypothermic preservation, TRPM8 drove hepatocellular Ca2+ overload, lipid peroxidation, ferroptosis, and post-transplant graft injury. Hepatocyte-specific FTO deletion, pharmacologic FTO inhibition, and TRPM8 knockdown or deletion reduced Ca2+ accumulation, ferroptotic injury, and graft dysfunction. Ferrostatin-1 rescue placed ferroptosis downstream of FTO-TRPM8-Ca2+ signaling. The effect of FTO was preservation-temperature dependent: FTO deletion protected grafts under hypothermic preservation but did not provide additional benefit under normothermic machine perfusion (NMP). NMP reduced cold-triggered Ca2+ overload and ferroptosis in experimental models and was associated with lower early injury markers in recipients of steatotic grafts. These findings identify a temperature-dependent FTO-TRPM8-Ca2+-ferroptosis pathway that promotes cold IRI in steatotic grafts.

items.title: Corrigendum to “The allograft survival of kidneys from living donors aged ≥65 years is similar to that of younger living donors in recipients aged ≥35 years” [American Journal of Transplantation Volume 26, Issue 8, August 2026, Pages 1923–1932]
Impact of Removing the Mandatory Sobriety Period on Waitlist and Posttransplant Outcomes of Patients With and Without Alcohol-associated Liver Disease
items.abstract: Background. This single-center study assessed the impact of eliminating the mandatory 6-mo sobriety requirement on waitlist and post-liver transplant (LT) outcomes among patients with and without alcohol-associated liver disease (ALD). Methods. Adult patients listed for LT from 2010 to 2023 and followed through 2025 were analyzed. Era 1 (<2018) required ≥6 mo of sobriety, whereas era 2 (≥2018) did not. Competing risk models compared waitlist outcomes across eras. Post-LT survival was compared across eras, followed by a subgroup analysis of era 2 ALD recipients stratified by pre-LT sobriety duration. Results. ALD listings increased (26% versus 42%), whereas non-ALD declined in era 2 (74% versus 58%). In era 2, listed ALD candidates had a higher likelihood of transplant (hazard ratio, 1.90; P < 0.001), lower likelihood of death/deterioration (hazard ratio, 0.48; P = 0.03), and shorter listing-to-LT time (204 versus 98 d; P = 0.004), whereas non-ALD likelihood of transplant, death/deterioration, and time-to-LT were unchanged. One-year post-LT survival was similar across eras, whereas 3- and 5-y survival were higher in era 2 (83% versus 91%; P = 0.01), driven by improved ALD survival with unchanged non-ALD survival. In a subgroup analysis of era 2 ALD transplant recipients, the <6-mo sobriety group had higher transplant Model of End-stage Liver Disease scores (34 versus 28; P < 0.001) lower unadjusted 1-y survival (88% versus 97%; P = 0.04) but similar survival after adjustment for Model of End-stage Liver Disease score ( P = 0.29) compared with the 6-mo sobriety group. Recidivism, rejection, and nonadherence rates were similar between groups. Conclusions. Liberalization of sobriety policy improved access to LT and long-term survival for ALD patients without compromising non-ALD outcomes.

items.title: Operationalizing Cardiac Xenotransplantation: An Administrative Playbook
items.abstract: As the field of xenotransplantation advances, institutions must navigate a complex landscape of nonclinical challenges to ensure safe and ethical implementation. This article presents a detailed account of the planning and execution of the first 2 human cardiac xenotransplants performed at the University of Maryland School of Medicine and Medical Center. Beyond the surgical innovation, these procedures required extensive coordination across regulatory, ethical, financial, legal, administrative, and operational domains. Drawing from institutional experience—including after-action analyses and interdisciplinary collaboration—we outline key strategies for Food and Drug Administration authorization, staff education, infection control, financial structuring, and communications planning. We also explore ethical considerations in patient selection and consent, emphasizing transparency, autonomy, and public health safeguards. This article serves as a practical guide for institutions preparing to undertake xenotransplantation, offering insights into the infrastructure and foresight necessary to support this transformative but complex medical advance.

items.title: Histopathological and Transcriptomic Features of Immune Checkpoint Inhibitor-related T-cell–mediated Rejection in Liver Transplantation
items.abstract: Background. Immune checkpoint inhibitor-related T-cell–mediated rejection (irTCMR) leads to greater steroid resistance and graft loss compared with conventional T-cell–mediated rejection (cTCMR) in liver transplant recipients. However, their histopathological and transcriptomic features remain poorly understood. Methods. Thirty-one adult recipients with biopsy-proven T-cell–mediated rejection (12 irTCMR and 19 cTCMR) were enrolled. Biopsies were assessed using the Banff and Ishak scoring systems, with immunohistochemical staining for CD3, CD4, CD8, CD20, programmed death-ligand 1, and C4d. Spatial transcriptomic analysis was performed on the CD45-enriched portal areas. Results. irTCMR showed higher alanine aminotransferase/aspartate aminotransferase peaks, steroid-resistant rejection (33.3% versus 0%; P = 0.016), and graft loss (41.7% versus 0%; P = 0.005). IrTCMR had a higher rejection activity index (median 6 versus 5; P = 0.020), driven by more severe bile duct inflammation and venous endothelialitis. Ishak scoring revealed a higher histological activity index with greater confluent necrosis ( P = 0.046). Both groups showed CD8 + predominant T-cell aggregates with sparse CD20 + B cells; CD4 + abundance ( P = 0.079) and the CD4/CD8 ratio ( P = 0.096) tended to be higher in irTCMR. Portal C4d deposition and programmed death-ligand 1 expression showed no significant differences. Spatial transcriptomics revealed distinct transcriptomic profiles in irTCMR, with 75 differentially expressed genes and enrichment of allograft rejection and antigen processing pathways. Immune deconvolution demonstrated increased CD4 + T cells, dendritic cells, and M1 macrophages but reduced regulatory T cells in irTCMR. Conclusions. irTCMR is a distinct aggressive rejection phenotype with severe bile duct inflammation, venous endothelialitis, confluent necrosis, and transcriptomic features distinct from cTCMR. These features underscore the need for further research on the pathogenesis of irTCMR.

items.title: Paul Snowden Russell, Past President of The Transplantation Society, Medawar Award Recipient, Pioneer Award Recipient, The American Society of Transplant Surgeons and Transplant Visionary
A National Study of Ischemic Times and Outcomes in DCD Liver Transplantation in the Era of Normothermic Regional Perfusion
items.abstract: Background. Liver donation after circulatory death (DCD) is associated with severe graft ischemia and poorer outcomes, forcing stringent graft selection and reducing utilization. Outcomes after donor normothermic regional perfusion (NRP) are superior to standard DCD liver transplantation, with less cholangiopathy and better survival. These observations prompted re-assessment of DCD selection criteria when NRP is used. Methods. United Kingdom Transplant Registry data (2011–2023) were interrogated for donor and recipient demographics, ischemic timings, and graft and patient outcomes. Contemporaneous cohorts of standard DCD and NRP liver donors and transplants were collated and compared. Results. Compared with standard DCD (n = 1629), NRP donors (n = 263) were significantly older, had a greater body mass index, longer functional warm ischemic time (FWIT), donor warm ischemic time (DWIT) and cold ischemic times (CIT), yet had superior death-censored (96.0% versus 89.0%; P < 0.001) and uncensored (93.0% versus 86.7%; P = 0.004) graft survival. NRP liver recipients had greater mobility by day 90 (No restrictions; 51% versus 27%; P <0.001), less postoperative renal support (11% versus 19%; P = 0.002) and fewer biliary readmissions (6% versus 12%; P = 0.018) by 1 y, despite higher transplant acuity (UK model for end-stage liver disease 54 versus 53; P = 0.001). There were no significant effects of FWIT, DWIT, or CIT on NRP liver transplantation for graft, patient, or transplant survival. Conclusions. In spite of adverse donor factors, NRP doubled utilization of DCD livers and improved outcomes. Prejudice against prolonged FWIT, DWIT, and CIT in DCD NRP liver donation needs re-evaluation to prevent unnecessary organ discard.

items.title: Outcomes of Pediatric Heart Transplantation at China’s Largest Center: A 10-Year Retrospective Analysis of Survival and Associated Factors
items.abstract: Background. Pediatric heart transplantation (HTx) is a critical therapy for end-stage heart failure. We analyzed 202 pediatric HTx cases from a large cardiac transplant center in China to describe survival outcomes, perioperative management, and factors associated with mortality. Methods. We retrospectively analyzed 202 pediatric HTx recipients from 2015 to 2024. The primary endpoint was survival after HTx. Baseline characteristics, survival, and mortality risk factors were analyzed. Results. Annual volume increased from 4 to 32 cases. Mean recipient age was 9.28 ± 4.34 y, and dilated cardiomyopathy was the most common indication (48.51%). The 1, 3, and 5-y survival rates were 89.2% (95% CI, 0.849-0.937), 84.3% (95% CI, 0.790-0.899), and 84.3% (95% CI, 0.790-0.899), respectively. In multivariable Cox regression, preoperative mechanical ventilation was associated with mortality at 1 y (HR = 7.84, 95% CI, 2.62-23.48; P < 0.001) and 5 y (HR = 4.98, 95% CI, 1.83-13.54; P = 0.002). Longer postoperative ventilation time was also associated with mortality at 1 y (HR = 1.01 per day, 95% CI, 1.00-1.03; P = 0.043) and 5 y (HR = 1.01 per day, 95% CI, 1.00-1.03; P = 0.022). Conclusions. This 10-y cohort describes pediatric HTx outcomes in China. Survival was comparable with contemporary registry outcomes. Distinct cohort features included prolonged cold ischemia time, broader donor to recipient weight ratios, and limited ventricular assist device use. Preoperative mechanical ventilation and longer postoperative ventilation time were associated with higher mortality. These findings provide a center perspective for programs with different donor availability, recipient profiles, and support strategies.

All About the Meds: Contraception, Infertility, and Immunosuppression in Reproductive-aged Female Transplant Recipients
items.abstract: The number of reproductive-aged solid organ transplant recipients continues to rise, underscoring the need for comprehensive reproductive health counseling that spans throughout the transplant continuum. Fertility is often impaired in end-stage organ disease but often resumes within months after transplantation, which may cause unintended pregnancy during a period of heightened maternal, fetal, and allograft vulnerability. This review synthesizes the evidence and expert consensus from the American Society of Transplantation Women’s Health Community of Practice Controversies Conference on contraception, infertility, and immunosuppression in reproductive-aged female transplant recipients. Recommendations are largely US-based, although reference to international variability is noted, where relevant. We outline contraceptive options with attention to efficacy and safety in transplant recipients. Data on infertility and assisted reproductive technologies in solid organ transplant recipients remain limited, although emerging evidence supports the feasibility and safety of ovulation induction, in vitro fertilization, and single-embryo transfer with careful monitoring for complications such as ovarian hyperstimulation syndrome. Immunosuppressive regimens require individualized adjustment before, during, and after pregnancy: calcineurin inhibitors, corticosteroids, and azathioprine are generally considered safe, whereas mycophenolate is strictly contraindicated due to teratogenicity; the safety of mammalian target of rapamycin inhibitors and belatacept remains incompletely defined. Lactation is supported with most immunosuppressants, although caution is warranted with mycophenolate and mammalian target of rapamycin inhibitors. Ultimately, preconception counseling, shared decision-making, and coordination amongst transplant, maternal-fetal medicine, and reproductive endocrinology specialists are essential to optimize outcomes for recipients, grafts, and infants. Closing persistent knowledge gaps and enhancing access to reproductive care should remain a research and policy priority in transplant medicine.

items.title: Glucagon-like Peptide-1 Receptor Agonists Versus Dipeptidyl Peptidase-4 Inhibitors in Heart Transplant Recipients With Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus: A Propensity Score–Matched Analysis
items.abstract: Background. Heart transplant (HT) recipients with type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) face elevated risks of cardiac allograft vasculopathy (CAV), rejection, and cardiovascular events. Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1 RAs) confer cardiorenal protection in general T2DM patients, but data specific to HT recipients are scarce. Methods. We conducted a retrospective propensity score–matched cohort study using the TriNetX Global Collaborative Network. Adult HT recipients with T2DM who initiated a GLP-1 RA or a dipeptidyl peptidase-4 (DPP-4) inhibitor after transplantation between January 1, 2016, and December 31, 2025, were matched 1:1 on 36 covariates. The primary outcome was a 3-year graft-specific composite of CAV (T86.290), HT rejection (T86.21), or HT failure (T86.22). All-cause mortality and myocardial infarction (I21) or ischemic stroke (I63) were analyzed separately. Results. After matching, 712 patients per group were analyzed. At 3 y, the graft-specific composite occurred in 12.1% of GLP-1 RA recipients versus 29.2% of DPP-4 inhibitor recipients (risk ratio [RR] 0.416; 95% confidence interval, 0.299-0.579; P < 0.001), driven by lower HT rejection (8.2% versus 22.4%; RR 0.365) and HT failure (3.5% versus 6.2%; RR 0.560); CAV did not differ (9.6% versus 10.5%; P = 0.609). All-cause mortality was 7.5% versus 17.5% (RR 0.426), and myocardial infarction/ischemic stroke 6.9% versus 15.3% (RR 0.450). Acute kidney injury and gastrointestinal adverse events did not differ. Findings were consistent at 1 and 5 y. Residual imbalance persisted for body mass index and HbA1c. Conclusions. In this multicenter electronic health record–based cohort, GLP-1 RA use was associated with lower graft-specific outcomes and all-cause mortality than DPP-4 inhibitor use. CAV did not differ significantly. These observational findings are hypothesis-generating and require prospective validation.

items.title: Anti-HLA Alloantibody Responses in Living Donor Uterus Transplantation: A Single-center Case Series
items.abstract: Background. Until 1 decade ago, absolute uterine infertility invariably prevented women from bearing their own biological child. A major causative factor is Mayer-Rokitansky-Küster-Hauser syndrome. However, uterus transplantation (UTx) has recently emerged as a successful treatment strategy, with >70 children being born to UTx recipients. This clinical situation represents a unique immunological scenario—namely the combined sensitization risk from solid organ transplantation and exposure to paternal alloantigens of the fetus. Methods. Given the rarity of such cases, we assessed HLA sensitization in this context using a microbead-based assay (Luminex) with HLA screening as well as single-antigen beads in 7 UTx patients. Results. We observed broad, strong IgG alloimmune responses in 3 UTx recipients, directed against both donor and paternal alloantigens. These responses primarily emerged and amplified after graft hysterectomy and withdrawal of immunosuppression, while intermittently also being evidenced before hysterectomy in 1 case. This contrasts with 4 women with transplants remaining in situ and on immunosuppressive treatment, who lack sensitization signs so far. Conclusions. These scarce preliminary data already suggest a relevant risk of broad sensitization in this unusual setting. UTx may therefore (1) represent a unique model for studying HLA sensitization under combined physiological and nonphysiological conditions, (2) warrant informing recipients about the risk of HLA alloimmunization, and (3) require further investigation to understand the implications and long-term consequences, demanding the generation of larger datasets.

items.title: Professor Maria Siemionow, MD, PhD, DSc, 2026 Medawar Prize Recipient
Longitudinal Urinary C-X-C Motif Chemokine Ligand 9: Inflammatory Trajectory Phenotypes and Contemporaneous Association With Graft Injury After Kidney Transplantation
items.abstract: Background. Urinary C-X-C motif chemokine ligand 9 (uCXCL9) is an interferon-gamma-induced chemokine associated with kidney allograft inflammation. However, the longitudinal patterns of uCXCL9 after kidney transplantation, their histological correlates, and the prognostic value of uCXCL9 for graft function and survival remain incompletely characterized. Methods. In this single-center observational study, we analyzed 10 447 uCXCL9 measurements obtained during the first posttransplant year from 817 adult kidney transplant recipients with at least 3 samples available. Latent-class mixed models were used to identify distinct longitudinal uCXCL9 trajectories. Longitudinal uCXCL9 were examined in relation to kidney biopsy findings, clinical diagnoses, estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) trajectories, and graft survival. Results. Eight distinct uCXCL9 trajectories were identified, differing in level and temporal pattern. Histological inflammation varied significantly across trajectory classes, with differences observed in microvascular, tubulointerstitial, and vascular Banff lesion scores (all P ≤ 0.01). uCXCL9 trajectory classes were associated with antibody-mediated rejection, with a trend toward higher T cell–mediated rejection ( P = 0.067) and donor-specific antibody positivity (10.9%–41.2%, P = 0.013). eGFR trajectories differed across uCXCL9 classes (class effect P = 0.019; class-by-time interaction P < 0.001). Modeled as a time-varying covariate, higher contemporaneous uCXCL9 was associated with concurrent decline in graft function (–0.96 mL/min/1.73 m 2 per doubling) and with an increased risk of graft loss or eGFR <15 mL/min/1.73 m 2 (adjusted hazard ratio 1.32 per doubling, 95% confidence interval, 1.14-1.54). Conclusions. Distinct longitudinal uCXCL9 trajectories define inflammatory phenotypes with distinct histological correlates, whereas contemporaneous uCXCL9 was independently associated with concurrent graft function and graft loss. These hypothesis-generating findings warrant prospective validation.

items.title: Love, Sex, and Immunosuppression: A Sexual Health Overview for the Transplant Clinician
items.abstract: Sexual health is a critical, yet often overlooked, aspect of comprehensive care for solid organ transplant recipients. While transplantation can restore overall health and quality of life, patients may continue to experience sexual dysfunction because of physiological, psychological, and pharmacological factors. Furthermore, transplant recipients remain at risk for sexually transmitted infections (STIs), including HIV, human papillomavirus (HPV), syphilis, and others, with implications for both patient and graft outcomes. HPV-associated malignancies, particularly anal squamous cell carcinoma, occur at significantly higher rates in this population, highlighting the need for recommendations on targeted screening and vaccination. This review addresses the spectrum of sexual health issues across transplant populations—including liver, kidney, heart, and lung recipients—with practical guidance on sexual function, STI screening, and risk reduction strategies. We outline current evidence and recommendations for preexposure and postexposure prophylaxis against HIV and bacterial STIs, including the use of tenofovir-based preexposure prophylaxis and doxycycline postexposure prophylaxis. We also aim to highlight the role of immunization against HPV, hepatitis B, hepatitis A, and monkeypox virus, emphasizing safety, timing, and efficacy considerations in immunocompromised individuals. Despite growing awareness, implementation of routine sexual health assessment and STI prevention strategies remains inconsistent in transplant medicine. We call for greater integration of sexual health into transplant care pathways and identify key research priorities to optimize outcomes. Clinicians should feel empowered to initiate open conversations, advocate for vaccination and prophylaxis, and tailor care based on individualized risk. This comprehensive update offers practical tools and recommendations to improve sexual health in solid organ transplant recipients.

items.title: Longitudinal Changes in Left Atrial Stiffness Index Improve Risk Stratification in Patients with Hypertension
items.containerTitle: Journal of the American Society of Echocardiography
items.abstract: Background Left atrial (LA) stiffness index is a non-invasive echocardiographic parameter reflecting left ventricular filling pressure; however, its prognostic significance in hypertension remains unclear. We aimed to assess the prognostic value of the longitudinal change in LA stiffness index in patients with hypertension. Methods We analyzed 1,442 hypertensive patients from the STRATS-HHD registry who underwent echocardiography including LA and left ventricular (LV) strain at baseline and 6-18 months. Patients were categorized into four groups according to longitudinal changes in LA stiffness index: Low-Low, High-Low, Low-High, and High-High, using a data-driven prognostic cut-off of 0.63 (Low Results Among 1,442 patients, 996 (69.1%) were classified as Low-Low, 173 (12.0%) as High-Low, 91 (6.3%) as Low-High, and 182 (12.6%) as High-High. Over 5 years, Low-High (adjusted hazard ratio [aHR] 2.175, 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.048-4.515, P=0.037) and High-High (aHR 2.935, 95% CI 1.697-5.076, P Conclusion LA stiffness index was associated with clinical outcomes in hypertension, and longitudinal changes provided additional prognostic information. Trajectory assessment may refine risk stratification.

items.title: Mitral Annular Calcification – Association with Comorbidities and Left Ventricular Mechanics
items.containerTitle: Journal of the American Society of Echocardiography
items.abstract: Aims Mitral annular calcification (MAC) is common in the general population, more pronounced in women and patients with left ventricular (LV) pressure overload conditions, which may increase stress on the mitral valve inducing and exacerbating the calcification process. The pathogenesis of MAC is presumed multifactorial but remains poorly understood. Women display a different LV response to pressure overload compared to men, but this association has rather not been thoroughly investigated. Methods and results The DANCAVAS (Danish Cardiovascular Screening) pilot study included randomly selected individuals from the general population aged 60-75 years to undergo a computed tomography (CT)-based screening program. MAC was graded by mitral valve calcification (MVC) score assessed by CT and compared to echocardiographic data. Among 463 participants, MAC was found in 165 (35.6%) with MVC scores ≤100 AU in 20.7%, 100-400 AU in 8.2% and >400 AU in 6.7%. While MAC was most prevalent in men, women presented with higher MVC scores and severe MAC on echocardiography. Patients with MAC were elderly with cardiovascular risk factors. Concentric LV geometry with smaller LV cavities and higher relative wall thickness were highly associated with MAC (p MV ) strongly associated with MAC (SD-adjusted OR 28.8, 95% CI [15.6;53.5] and 2.97 [2.25;3.91], respectively) and MAC severity (10.9 [7.74;15.5] and 2.98 [2.33;3.82], respectively). The predictive performance was high with AUC of 0.78 [0.74;0.82] by including Stress MV in the model of age, sex and cardiovascular comorbidity (p Conclusion MAC is common in the general population with the highest prevalence among men. LV geometry and the pressure on the mitral valve are crucial factors in the pathogenesis of MAC, and sex-specific differences in LV response to pressure overload may elucidate why more extensive grades of MAC mainly affect women.

items.title: Echocardiographic Left Atrial Stiffness Index as a Predictor of All-Cause Mortality in Non-Ischemic Dilated Cardiomyopathy
items.containerTitle: Journal of the American Society of Echocardiography
items.abstract: Aims Reliable predictors of adverse outcomes in non-ischemic dilated cardiomyopathy (NIDCM) remain limited. We aimed to evaluate the association between the left atrial stiffness index (LASI) and all-cause mortality in patients with NIDCM and to assess its prognostic value beyond established left atrial and diastolic markers. Methods Retrospective analysis of a prospectively recruited cohort of patients diagnosed with NIDCM between 2018 and 2022. All patients underwent comprehensive transthoracic echocardiography at the time of diagnosis. Left atrial (LA) strain was measured retrospectively from stored baseline echocardiograms using two-dimensional speckle-tracking analysis, and LASI was calculated as the ratio of E/e' to LA reservoir strain. Multivariable analyses were performed to identify variables independently associated with all-cause mortality. Results Among 200 patients (mean age 61.7 years; 40% women), 33 (16.5%) died over a median follow-up of 43.8 months. In multivariable Cox regression analysis, variables independently associated with all-cause mortality were LASI (adjusted hazard ratio [HR] 1.92, 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.33-2.77), age (HR 1.05, 95% CI 1.02-1.08) and right ventricular-pulmonary artery (RV-PA) coupling index (HR 0.25, 95% CI 0.07-0.89); the model showed good discrimination (optimism-corrected C-index 0.766). LASI remained independently associated with mortality when modeled together with left atrial volume index (LAVi) and with E/e'. Conclusion In NIDCM, LASI provides prognostic information for all-cause mortality beyond other morphological and functional LA markers. Given the single-center design and the limited number of events, these findings warrant external validation.

items.title: Clinical Risk, Carotid Plaque Burden, Cardiac Remodeling, and Left Ventricular Diastolic Dysfunction in Asymptomatic Adults Referred for Exercise Stress Echocardiography
items.containerTitle: Journal of the American Society of Echocardiography
items.abstract: BACKGROUND: Exercise stress echocardiography (SE) assesses inducible ischemia but may not identify subclinical atherosclerosis or early cardiac remodeling. We evaluated the prevalence of subclinical carotid atherosclerosis and its relationships with clinical risk estimates, cardiac remodeling, and diastolic function in asymptomatic adults referred for exercise SE. METHODS: In this prospective, blinded cohort study, 73 consecutive asymptomatic adults without known cardiovascular disease (CVD) underwent treadmill SE, carotid ultrasonography for carotid intima-media thickness (CIMT), plaque presence and burden, and resting echocardiography. Radial-artery tonometry (RAT) was performed in 33 participants. Ten-year risk was estimated using the Framingham general CVD risk score (FRS), Pooled Cohort Equations for atherosclerotic CVD (PCE-ASCVD), and Predicting Risk of Cardiovascular Disease EVENTs (PREVENT) equations for ASCVD, total CVD, and heart failure (PREVENT-HF). RESULTS: Among 70 evaluable participants, 69 (98.6%) had negative SE findings for inducible ischemia; one demonstrated a hypertensive myopathic response. Carotid plaque was present in 46 participants (65.7%), and isolated CIMT >75th percentile without plaque was present in 6 (8.6%), yielding a combined prevalence of subclinical carotid atherosclerosis of 74.3%. Plaque prevalence increased across FRS, PCE-ASCVD, and PREVENT-ASCVD categories but remained 45.8% among participants classified as low risk by PREVENT-ASCVD. All five clinical risk estimates correlated with plaque number, maximum plaque thickness, total plaque area, and relative LV wall thickness. Greater plaque area was associated with higher relative wall thickness, left ventricular (LV) mass index, and diastolic-function grade. PREVENT-HF showed the strongest numerical correlations with diastolic-function grade and average E/e'. In a model incorporating plaque area and PREVENT-HF, PREVENT-HF was independently associated with diastolic dysfunction (OR per SD, 2.60; 95% CI, 1.30-5.20; P=.007), whereas plaque area was not. Exercise duration and rate-pressure product were not associated with plaque burden. CONCLUSIONS: Among asymptomatic adults with CVD risk factors referred for exercise SE, inducible ischemia was uncommon despite a high prevalence of subclinical carotid atherosclerosis. Carotid plaque burden and clinical risk estimates were associated with cardiac remodeling and diastolic function, while PREVENT-HF was independently associated with diastolic dysfunction. These findings support complementary characterization of subclinical vascular and cardiac abnormalities but do not establish incremental outcome prediction, altered treatment eligibility, or replacement of clinically indicated stress testing by carotid imaging.

items.title: Prevalence and Impact of Different Patterns of Left Ventricular Remodeling on Chronic Severe Aortic Regurgitation Outcomes
items.containerTitle: Journal of the American Society of Echocardiography
items.abstract: Background Chronic aortic regurgitation (AR) leads to increased left ventricular (LV) preload and afterload, most commonly manifesting as eccentric hypertrophy, although other remodeling patterns may occur. This study aimed to characterize the prevalence of different patterns of LV remodeling in patients with chronic severe AR and to evaluate their associations with all-cause mortality and symptoms. Methods We retrospectively analyzed 1,009 patients with ≥moderate-severe chronic AR identified by echocardiography. LV geometry was classified as normal, concentric remodeling, concentric hypertrophy, or eccentric hypertrophy based on relative wall thickness and LV mass index; concentric remodeling and hypertrophy were combined because of small sample size. Associations with outcomes were assessed using multivariable Cox proportional hazards and logistic regression models. Results Eccentric hypertrophy was the most prevalent pattern (65%), followed by concentric remodeling/hypertrophy (17%) and normal geometry (18%). Concentric remodeling/hypertrophy was more common in older patients with systemic hypertension and chronic kidney disease and was associated with less severe AR. This remodeling pattern was associated with increased all-cause mortality (hazard ratio, 2.17; 95% confidence interval, 1.34-3.52; p Conclusions In severe AR, concentric remodeling/hypertrophy and normal geometry are present in a substantial proportion of patients. Concentric remodeling/hypertrophy is associated with increased all-cause mortality, whereas LV remodeling patterns are not associated with symptoms.

items.title: Rethinking Normal: Estimated Right Ventricular Systolic Pressure Below 35mmHg and Mortality Risk
items.containerTitle: Journal of the American Society of Echocardiography
items.abstract: Right ventricular systolic pressure estimated by echocardiography (eRVSP) >35mmHg has been shown to be a predictor of mortality in several disease states. This study aims to investigate the prognostic implications of eRVSP within the accepted normal range (<35mmHg) in different patient populations. Consecutive echocardiographic reports (2007-2024, N=293,433) linked to clinical data from a large tertiary medical center were reviewed. The primary outcome was all-cause mortality available for all subjects from the national population register. A smooth hazard ratio (HR) Cox regression model was applied with adjustment for other predictors of poor survival. The final cohort included 107,905 tests of unique subjects (mean age 63±17 years, 56% men). Mean eRVSP was 34±12mmHg; 72,574 (67%) had eRVSP <35mmHg. Cox regression analysis of the entire cohort showed that an increase in eRVSP was associated with a significant, though nonlinear, independently increased risk of death (p<0.001). The association of eRVSP with overall survival was robust and consistent in the entire cohort as well as in the <35mmHg cohort in models adjusted for known predictors of poor survival and across different patient population sub-cohorts. The association with survival was more pronounced among younger patients < 60 years. Higher eRVSP within the normal range of <35 mmHg constitutes an independent risk factor for long term mortality. Our findings were significant, robust, and consistent across different patient populations. These findings suggest that eRVSP, even below the conventional threshold of 35 mmHg, may provide valuable prognostic information, particularly in younger patients.

Beyond the coronary tree: can AI-derived myocardial radiomics from routine computed tomography angiography refine long-term prediction of myocardial infarction?
items.abstract: This editorial refers to ‘Prognostic Value of AI-derived Ventricular Imaging Phenotypes from Cardiac CTA for Long-term Risk of Myocardial Infarction—Analysis of SCOT-HEART Trial’, by J. Chen et al., https://doi.org/10.1093/ehjci/jeag252. Cardiac computed tomography angiography (CCTA) is now an established anatomical test for patients with suspected coronary artery disease (CAD), providing diagnostic and prognostic information from coronary stenosis, calcium burden, plaque characteristics, and pericoronary adipose tissue.1,2 The ventricular myocardium is captured within the same acquisition, yet its quantitative information is rarely incorporated into routine risk assessment. The study by Chen et al. therefore asks a clinically relevant question: does the left ventricular myocardium contain reproducible imaging information that provides prognostic value beyond conventional clinical and coronary CCTA measures?3 The study provides evidence that the answer may be yes, although the findings are better interpreted as proof of incremental prognostic information than as validation of a clinically actionable biomarker. This post hoc analysis of the SCOT-HEART trial included 1736 participants with CCTA images suitable for myocardial segmentation and radiomic analysis. During a median follow-up of 8.6 years, 82 participants experienced a fatal or non-fatal myocardial infarction (MI).3 The investigators segmented the left ventricular myocardium using TotalSegmentator and extracted 105 prespecified radiomic features with PyRadiomics, with feature definitions following the Image Biomarker Standardization Initiative (IBSI) framework.3 These features were organized into six descriptive domains—global variance, local dimness, global intensity, morphological structure, bright region, and local uniformity—and subsequently reduced to eigen-features for survival modelling.3 A particular strength is the staged analytical design, which attempts to provide biological context before evaluating prognosis. The investigators first examined age- and sex-related variation in a small reference group without cardiovascular disease or conventional risk factors (n = 109), then assessed associations with cardiovascular risk factors and coronary calcium in a larger risk-enriched group (n = 1627), before evaluating prognostic associations in the overall cohort.3 This approach provides a physiological framework for interpreting the radiomic features rather than selecting them solely on the basis of their relationship with subsequent clinical events. Importantly, data-dependent prognostic procedures, including feature selection and PCA/eigen-feature derivation, were confined to the training folds within the nested cross-validation framework, limiting information leakage and outcome-driven optimism.3 This biological contextualization should not, however, be confused with biological validation. Associations with age, sex, cardiovascular risk factors, and coronary calcium indicate that the imaging patterns relate to recognized phenotypic determinants, but they do not establish that individual radiomic features correspond to specific myocardial pathological processes. Similar relationships between myocardial radiomic signatures, age, sex, and vascular risk factors have previously been demonstrated using cardiovascular magnetic resonance (CMR) in the UK Biobank, providing external biological context for the overall approach.4,5 The methodology is further strengthened by several validation steps. The segmentation pipeline showed high agreement with expert reference masks in an independent CCTA cohort, with a mean Dice coefficient of 0.93, while approximately 93% of radiomic features were robust to small perturbations of myocardial contours.3 The preprocessing strategy was also informed by previous work evaluating the reproducibility of radiomic features in SCOT-HEART CCTA data.6 Together with nested cross-validation, these measures reduce some of the technical instability and optimistic bias that have limited earlier radiomics studies. An important question is whether the radiomic signal simply recapitulates simpler measures of myocardial size and attenuation that can already be obtained from conventional post-processing. The authors directly explored this possibility and found additional prognostic information when radiomic phenotypes were added to models containing simpler myocardial measurements of size and attenuation.3 This suggests that the radiomic representation may capture information beyond these basic structural measures. Nevertheless, interpretation should remain cautious. In the fully adjusted Cox model, only the morphological component remained individually associated with MI (HR 1.07, 95% CI 1.02–1.13; P = 0.011).3 The incremental prognostic signal should therefore be understood at the level of the multivariable radiomic feature set rather than as evidence for seven independently validated imaging biomarkers. The magnitude of this incremental prediction is also important. Adding myocardial radiomic phenotypes to a model containing the ASSIGN risk score, coronary artery calcium (CAC) score, and obstructive CAD increased the cross-validated C-index from 0.693 to 0.722 (Δ = 0.029; P < 0.001), with improved model fit (likelihood-ratio χ2 = 13.5; P = 0.009).3 Calibration was preserved and numerically improved: the calibration slope increased from 0.762 to 0.914, calibration-in-the-large remained close to zero, and the Brier score decreased slightly from 0.038 to 0.037.3 These results support incremental prognostic information without evidence of deterioration in calibration, but they do not yet establish clinical utility. Indeed, no prespecified treatment thresholds or clinically validated risk categories were available, and categorical reclassification was therefore not evaluated. The study consequently cannot establish whether the additional radiomic information would meaningfully reclassify patients or alter preventive treatment, surveillance, or downstream testing. This distinction is important: a statistically significant improvement in discrimination does not necessarily translate into clinically meaningful changes in patient management. Several other limitations deserve emphasis. The number of MI events was relatively small (n = 82), while the healthy reference group included only 109 participants, limiting the precision of the underlying associations and the robustness of prognostic modelling. Generalizability also remains uncertain. Although SCOT-HEART was a multicentre trial, the present cohort was derived from a Scottish population and imaging was performed using scanners and reconstruction protocols that may not reflect contemporary CCTA practice.1–3 Moreover, no post hoc statistical harmonization across scanners was performed, and scanner vendor or imaging site was not included as a covariate in the primary prognostic models.3 External validation of the complete pipeline across contemporary scanners, vendors, reconstruction methods, and more diverse populations is therefore essential. The biological basis of the radiomic signal also remains unresolved. The association between coronary calcium burden and myocardial texture could plausibly reflect altered perfusion, microvascular dysfunction, diffuse fibrosis, shared cardiovascular risk factors, or some combination of these processes. Previous work has shown that CCTA-derived myocardial radiomic features can identify CMR-defined myocardial fibrosis in patients with hypertrophic cardiomyopathy,6 supporting the possibility that radiomics may be sensitive to tissue-level heterogeneity. However, the present study included no direct myocardial perfusion or CMR tissue-characterization measurements, and these mechanistic interpretations therefore remain hypothesis-generating rather than demonstrated. Technical factors, including contrast timing, cardiac motion, partial-volume effects, and reconstruction noise, may also contribute to the observed radiomic patterns. The present findings sit naturally alongside the emerging CMR radiomics literature. Raisi-Estabragh et al. demonstrated independent associations between myocardial radiomic signatures and sex, age, and vascular risk factors in large UK Biobank populations.4,5 In a subsequent analysis, Ruiz Pujadas et al. showed that CMR radiomics could contribute to the prediction of incident cardiovascular events, including MI, heart failure, atrial fibrillation, and stroke.7 The distinctive contribution of the present study is to suggest that potentially prognostic myocardial information can also be recovered from a modality already performed for another purpose—coronary anatomical assessment—without additional imaging, radiation, contrast administration, or scan time.3 This possibility is attractive, but clinical translation will require external validation of the complete radiomics pipeline, from segmentation and image preprocessing through feature extraction, harmonization, eigen-feature derivation, and prognostic modelling. Standardization and technical reproducibility are particularly important challenges for quantitative radiomics.7,8 Ideally, future multicentre studies should also incorporate direct measures of myocardial biology, including perfusion or tissue characterization, to determine what these imaging phenotypes actually represent. Equally important will be establishing whether the incremental prognostic information persists when radiomics is compared with a more comprehensive contemporary CCTA assessment. The reference model in the present study included ASSIGN score, CAC, and obstructive CAD, but did not incorporate quantitative total or non-calcified plaque burden, plaque composition, or high-risk plaque characteristics.3 The relevant comparator for any future CCTA-derived biomarker will increasingly be a comprehensive quantitative CCTA assessment rather than stenosis and calcium score alone. Overall, Chen et al. provided a methodologically careful proof-of-concept that the myocardium captured on routine coronary CCTA contains imaging information associated with long-term MI risk. The incremental prognostic value is modest and does not yet establish clinical utility, but the study highlights an underused source of information already contained within routine CCTA and provides a rigorous framework for its further investigation. The next step is not simply to extract more radiomic features, but to establish what these signals represent biologically, whether they are reproducible across contemporary imaging platforms, and whether they provide clinically meaningful information beyond the increasingly comprehensive CCTA assessment already available. PET imaging for cardiac sarcoidosis: a prospective comparison of 64Cu-DOTATATE and 18F-FDG
items.abstract: Aims Diagnosing cardiac sarcoidosis with 18F-FDG positron emission tomography/computed tomography (PET/CT) is complicated by high physiological myocardial 18F-FDG uptake. We conducted a prospective clinical trial to assess the value of 64Cu-DOTATATE—a preparation-free alternative to 18F-FDG—in cardiac sarcoidosis. Methods and results We included 66 patients ≥ 18 years: 22 with suspected cardiac sarcoidosis, 22 with previously diagnosed cardiac sarcoidosis; and 22 controls without known inflammatory heart disease. Patients with suspected and previously diagnosed cardiac sarcoidosis underwent 18F-FDG and 64Cu-DOTATATE PET/CT; controls underwent 64Cu-DOTATATE PET/CT. Two expert nuclear medicine physicians performed blinded scan readings. Median age was 55.2 years (82% men) in suspected cardiac sarcoidosis; 57.4 years (91% men) in previously diagnosed cardiac sarcoidosis; and 57.2 years (82% men) in controls. Median scan interval was 9 days (IQR 6–18). In suspected cardiac sarcoidosis, scan interpretation (active vs. no active cardiac sarcoidosis) was concordant in 20/22 patients (91%), showing substantial agreement (Cohen’s kappa = 0.70). In previously diagnosed cardiac sarcoidosis, scan interpretation was concordant in 20/22 patients (91%), showing almost perfect agreement (Cohen’s kappa = 0.82). No controls had ⁶⁴Cu-DOTATATE uptake suggestive of active cardiac sarcoidosis. In patients with suspect foci on both scans (n = 13), myocardial-to-background ratio was 3.28 (IQR 2.81–5.13) for 18F-FDG and 2.63 (IQR 2.11–3.46) for 64Cu-DOTATATE (P = 0.24). Inter-observer agreement was high (Cohen’s kappa = 1.00 for 18F-FDG and 0.84 for 64Cu-DOTATATE). Conclusion 18F-FDG and 64Cu-DOTATATE PET/CT showed high scan interpretation agreement and strong inter-observer agreement. Unlike 18F-FDG, 64Cu-DOTATATE requires no patient preparation. Our findings support a potential clinical value of 64Cu-DOTATATE PET/CT in cardiac sarcoidosis.

items.title: Standards defining echocardiography core laboratory (ECL) in clinical practice and research
items.abstract: Echocardiography is extensively utilized in both clinical practice and research due to its accessibility. Echocardiography core laboratories (ECLs) adhering to societal guidelines offer superior readings and interpretations compared with on-site assessments by reducing measurement variability and enhancing study precision. In the present work, we aim to define minimum standards for clinical echocardiography laboratories and research ECLs based on recommendations from the American Society of Echocardiography and the European Association of Cardiovascular Imaging, as well as on expert opinion and our experience in European countries. Accurate acquisition of high-quality images is crucial for ensuring reproducibility, repeatability, and reliability of the echocardiographic measurements. In addition to the commonly used workstations, an academic ECL must also possess the necessary capacities and skilled personnel to conduct sophisticated research projects. Personnel should hold advanced certification in echocardiography, indicating postgraduate training and experience beyond the basic cardiovascular ultrasound education. They should be capable of designing, performing, and interpreting complex echocardiography studies. Reproducibility of the ECL should be validated using a small, randomly selected sample, preferably in the early analytic phase. ECL readings and interpretations are superior to site-reported measurements and serve as the gold standard in observational studies and clinical trials. To ensure internal validity, an academic ECL should continuously evaluate/report reproducibility, repeatability, and reliability. ECL should be formally acknowledged and accredited by an international scientific imaging society.

items.title: Night shift work and subclinical cardiac remodelling: a multi-omic CMR study in 42 671 individuals
items.abstract: Aims Whether frequent night-shift work is associated with a distinct subclinical cardiac phenotype and accompanying molecular alterations remains uncertain. Methods and results We analysed 42 671 UK Biobank participants without baseline cardiovascular disease who underwent cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR). Night-shift frequency was classified into four categories, and 15 CMR measures were assessed using multivariable regression. Compared with day workers, frequent night-shift workers showed greater left ventricular global wall thickness [standardized β = 0.092, 95% CI 0.050–0.135; false discovery rate (FDR) < 0.001] and left ventricular mass-to-volume ratio (β = 0.072, 95% CI 0.021–0.123; FDR = 0.019), with lower left ventricular end-diastolic volume index, right ventricular end-diastolic volume index, right ventricular stroke volume index, and maximal right atrial volume index (all FDR < 0.05). Left ventricular global circumferential strain was less favourable (β = 0.092, 95% CI 0.040–0.144; FDR = 0.002), whereas left ventricular ejection fraction and global longitudinal strain were not significantly associated. Proteomic (n = 4889) and metabolomic (n = 42 671) analyses identified exploratory inflammatory, vascular, and lipid-related correlates. Mediation analyses identified FDR-significant indirect-effect estimates involving left ventricular end-diastolic volume index for three proteins and four metabolites. Two-sample Mendelian randomization identified associations between selected molecular features and CMR traits, although directions were not uniformly concordant with the observational estimates. Conclusion Frequent night shift work was associated with greater concentric left ventricular geometry, lower cardiac chamber volumes, and less favourable circumferential strain, together with inflammatory and lipid-related molecular correlates. Prospective studies are required to determine temporal relationships and long-term clinical relevance.

items.title: What Does Right Atrial Conduit Strain Tell Us About Heart Failure?

Systematic Transesophageal Echocardiographic Identification of Tricuspid Valve Commissures and Subvalvular Apparatus
items.abstract: Transcatheter tricuspid valve (TV) intervention is rapidly evolving and several classes of therapeutic devices are currently in development. The anatomic knowledge of the TV is the cornerstone for transcatheter patient selection, and the successful implantation of the devices depends on imaging guidance. Anatomically, leaflets are separated by the commissures, which have peculiar findings: they are supported by fan-shaped chords and do not open directly into the annulus, but a few millimeters of the leaflet tissue remain, similar to small scallops. While a comprehensive echocardiographic assessment of TV has been extensively reported, few papers have focused on analyzing commissures and their impact on interventions. This paper aims to introduce a novel echocardiographic approach focusing on TV commissures, and provide a dedicated transesophageal imaging protocol and methodology for recognizing their anatomic landmarks. Multiple dedicated transesophageal views are comprehensively reported for each commissure, in order to ensure a guide for emerging transcatheter procedures.

items.title: Integrated Multimodality Imaging of Cardiac Involvement in Burkitt Lymphoma
Implementation Feasibility and Clinical Utility of Phenomapping in Dilated and Hypokinetic Non-dilated Non-ischemic Cardiomyopathy
items.abstract: Aims Despite phenotypic heterogeneity, the management of idiopathic non-ischemic cardiomyopathy (NICM) remains generalized and dominantly guided by left ventricular (LV) ejection fraction (EF) and NYHA class. We aimed to develop a point-of-service phenomapping pathway for dilated cardiomyopathy (DCM) and hypokinetic non-dilated cardiomyopathy (HNDC) at time of CMR imaging leveraging the integration of i) patient self-reported health status, ii) imaging phenotype, and the iii) electronic health record (EHR). Methods and results 1,355 patients (752 DCM and 603 HNDC) were followed for the composite MACE outcome of mortality, heart failure hospitalization or ventricular arrhythmia. K-means clustering was independently applied to DCM and HNDC derivation cohorts using 55 routinely captured features (16 patient-reported health variables, 19 CMR-derived, 14 EHR-derived, and 6 combined features), identifying three phenogroups in each cohort. Over a median of 3.9 and 3.7 years, 145 DCM patients (22%) and 65 HNDC patients (13%), respectively, experienced MACE. Adjusting for age, sex, NYHA class, and LV EF, phenogroup membership was independently associated with future outcomes. In DCM, the adjusted HR (95% CI) of phenogroups 2 and 3 versus Phenogroup 1 were 2.8 (1.6-4.8) and 3.5 (1.9-6.5), respectively (p<0.001 for both). In HNDC, Phenogroup 3 demonstrated an adjusted HR of 4.2 (1.7-10.2; p=0.001) versus Phenogroup 1. Prospective phenogroup assignment was enabled by a decision tree-classifier and validated in a temporal hold-out cohort. Conclusion Phenomapping delivers incremental value to LVEF and NYHA for identification of high-risk NICM patients. These findings support value from standardized, point-of-service data integration for the delivery of phenomics-driven personalized care.

items.title: Optical Coherence Tomography can identify Non-Ischemic Lesions that have a Benign Outcome from those with High-Risk of Future Events. Insights from a Patient Level Pooled Analysis of COMBINE (OCT-FFR) and PECTUS-Obs Prospective Natural History Studies
items.abstract: Background Whether all lipid-rich plaques (LRP) or only thin-cap fibroatheromas (TCFA) are at risk for future events, remains unclear. Methods Individual patient data from two prospective studies, the COMBINE FFR-OCT and PECTUS-obs trials, performed respectively in a diabetes mellitus (DM) and myocardial infraction, (MI) patients, were pooled. Patients carrying ≥1 fractional-flow reserve (FFR) negative, optical coherence tomography (OCT) -assessed, lesions (target lesions) were divided in two groups. The first group represented patients with non-LRP and the second those with LRP. The second group was further divided in LRP-TCFAs and LRP thick-cap fibroatheromas (ThCFAs). Patients with plaque rupture or erosion were further excluded from the Non-LPR and ThCFA groups. The primary endpoint was target-lesion failure, defined as cardiac death, target-vessel myocardial infarction and target-lesion revascularization at 2 years. Results Pooling of the two trials resulted in 722 patients carrying non-destabilized, ≥1 FFR-negative, OCT assessed lesions, of which 165 (22.8%) had non-LRP while 557 (77.2%) had LRP. In the LPR group, 224 patients (40.2%) had TCFA morphology. The primary endpoint was 29(5.2%) vs 4(2.4%) (HR 2.21, CI: (0.78-6.28), p= 0.14) in the LRP versus non-LRP groups. However, within LRP groups TCFAs were associated with a significantly higher primary endpoint rate than ThCFAs; 20 (8.9%) vs 9 (2.7%), (HR 3.22, CI: 1.46–7,11, p < 0.01). Conclusion At 2 years only TCFAs were associated with a high rate of TLF while the remaining non-ischemic LRP and non-LRP plaques had a very benign outcome under optimal statin-based medical treatment.

items.title: Right atrial reservoir strain and clinical outcomes after mitral transcatheter edge-to-edge repair
items.abstract: Background The clinical relevance of right atrial (RA) function in patients undergoing mitral transcatheter edge-to-edge repair (M-TEER) remains unclear. We investigated the association between RA reservoir strain (RASr) and clinical outcomes in patients undergoing M-TEER. Methods We retrospectively assessed RASr using automated two-dimensional strain analytical software in patients undergoing M-TEER. The primary outcome was a composite of all-cause mortality and heart failure hospitalization after M-TEER. Results Of 298 patients undergoing M-TEER (age 78.1 ± 9.6 years; male 61.1%; and functional mitral regurgitation 64.4%), the median RASr was 19.6% (interquartile range: 10.3–32.5%). Atrial fibrillation, larger RA area, lower left atrial reservoir strain, and lower tricuspid annular plane systolic excursion or right ventricular fractional area change were correlated to lower RASr. Lower RASr was associated with a higher risk of the primary outcome, independently of clinical and echocardiographic characteristics and procedural results (adjusted hazard ratio: 0.96 per 1% increase in RASr, 95% confidence interval: 0.92–0.99, p=0.031). Our maximally selected log-rank statistics showed that the optimal cut-off value of RASr to discriminate the primary outcome was 24%. Incorporating RASr into conventional clinical and echocardiographic parameters improved model fit, with a modest improvement in discrimination for clinical outcome after M-TEER. Conclusion Reduced RASr is associated with adverse clinical outcomes after M-TEER. Our findings highlight the potential importance of RASr as a component of right-sided cardiac function. The assessment of RASr may improve risk stratification in patients undergoing M-TEER.

Computed Tomography Angiography–Derived Carotid Plaque Features and Risk of Vascular Events in Stroke Patients With Carotid Atherosclerosis
Genotype and Phenotype in Concert
Association Between Peripheral and Coronary Subclinical Atherosclerosis Burden in Midlife
items.abstract: BACKGROUND: Atherosclerosis, silent in its early stages, underlies most cardiovascular manifestations. The inter-relation between silent atherosclerosis across vascular territories remains insufficiently characterized. OBJECTIVES: The aim of this study was to assess the association between peripheral and coronary atherosclerosis in asymptomatic individuals. METHODS: A subgroup of individuals of the PESA (Progression of Early Subclinical Atherosclerosis) cohort underwent contrast-enhanced coronary computed tomography angiography in addition to peripheral (carotid and femoral) atherosclerosis assessment using 3-dimensional vascular ultrasound. Peripheral global plaque volume was calculated as the sum of bilateral carotid and femoral plaque burden using an artificial intelligence-based automated approach. Coronary computed tomographic angiographic images were qualitatively evaluated for the presence and severity of coronary atherosclerosis (percentage stenosis) and quantitatively for coronary artery calcium score (CACS) and global coronary plaque volume measurement. RESULTS: A total of 374 participants (mean age: 55 years, 34% women, 63% with CACS = 0) were included. Peripheral atherosclerosis was present in 75%. Peripheral global plaque volume was significantly associated with the presence, severity, and burden of coronary atherosclerosis (coronary plaque volume) (r = 0.69; P < 0.001). After adjustment for age, sex, and conventional risk factor profile, individuals with peripheral atherosclerosis had nearly 3 times greater odds of having coronary atherosclerosis than those without (OR: 2.66; 95% CI: 1.50-4.72; P = 0.001). Both carotid and femoral atherosclerosis remained significantly and independently associated with coronary plaque. Among participants with CACS = 0, noncalcified coronary plaque was detected in 12.0%, nearly all of whom (93%) had concomitant peripheral atherosclerosis. CONCLUSIONS: Peripheral and coronary atherosclerosis were strongly correlated in asymptomatic persons. Both carotid and femoral atherosclerosis were associated with coronary artery disease independently of each other.

items.title: Dulaglutide and Coronary Plaque Characteristics in Type 2 Diabetes
Beyond Calcium
items.abstract: Aortic stenosis is characterized by progressive fibrocalcific remodeling driven by inflammation, fibrosis, and calcification. Although echocardiography and noncontrast computed tomographic calcium scoring (aortic valve calcium score) remain the clinical standards for hemodynamic and structural assessment, computed tomographic angiography, already routinely performed for transcatheter aortic valve replacement planning, provides complementary tissue-level characterization of fibrotic and calcific valve remodeling. Artificial intelligence is increasingly being applied to facilitate the quantitative assessment of fibrocalcific burden and periaortic adipose tissue inflammation. This review examines emerging applications of computed tomographic angiography for fibrocalcific tissue characterization, inflammatory phenotyping, and artificial intelligence-enabled risk assessment in aortic stenosis and discusses their potential role in complementing conventional hemodynamic assessment.

items.title: Beyond the blind epidural: sensing, robotics, and artificial intelligence for safer neuraxial anesthesia
items.abstract: Neuraxial block techniques, including lumbar and thoracic epidural blockade, and spinal anesthesia, are not entirely accurate or reliable. Cerebrospinal fluid return confirms intrathecal access during spinal anesthesia; epidural placement relies heavily on subjective loss of resistance, supplemented after catheter insertion by aspiration for blood or cerebrospinal fluid, response to a test dose when appropriate, and clinical assessment. This Daring Discourse proposes objective sensing, standardized performance reporting, and ultimately, robotic and artificial intelligence assistance as a path to safer, more reproducible practice. Variable outcomes may be attributed to inconsistent definitions of efficacy and side effects, subjective needle insertion endpoints, uncertainty over catheter positioning, and operator cognitive overload. Opportunities for improvement include consistent adoption and reporting of established key performance indicators, better procedural planning and guidance, objective sensing of tissue planes, catheter tip position, and improved operator feedback. A modular development path could combine preprocedural imaging, real-time sensing, artificial intelligence–based interpretation, and, where justified, supervised robotic assistance; not every procedure requires every component. However, technical performance alone will not guarantee adoption. New technologies must also be easy to learn, quick to set up, interoperable, and cost-effective. Health-economic evaluation should compare their full costs with potential improvements in safety, patient experience, and workflow. The goal is not technology for its own sake but scalable assistance that improves safety, efficiency, and accountable clinical decision-making.

items.title: Association between cerebrospinal fluid confirmation during attempted combined spinal–epidural placement and documented early neuraxial analgesic failure: a retrospective cohort study
items.abstract: Background Combined spinal–epidural (CSE) analgesia is widely used in obstetric anesthesia, yet the clinical significance of cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) confirmation during attempted CSE placement remains uncertain. We evaluated whether CSF confirmation during attempted CSE placement was associated with documented early neuraxial analgesic failure during labor analgesia. Methods We performed a retrospective cohort study of patients undergoing attempted CSE placement for labor analgesia at a tertiary care center between June 2016 and January 2018. The primary analysis compared Any CSF Confirmation versus No CSF Confirmation. The primary outcome was documented early neuraxial analgesic failure within 3 hours of neuraxial placement. Multivariable logistic regression adjusted for demographic and procedural covariates. A secondary exploratory analysis evaluated CSF Confirmation at Initial Loss of Resistance, Eventual CSF Confirmation, and No CSF Confirmation groups. Results Among 1520 patients, documented early neuraxial analgesic failure occurred in 22 of 63 patients (34.9%) with No CSF Confirmation compared with 76 of 1457 patients (5.2%) with Any CSF Confirmation. After multivariable adjustment, absence of CSF confirmation remained strongly associated with documented early neuraxial analgesic failure (adjusted OR 10.30; 95% CI 5.71 to 18.58; p<0.001). In the secondary exploratory analysis, documented early neuraxial analgesic failure occurred in 5.0% of patients with CSF confirmation at initial loss of resistance, 10.1% with eventual CSF confirmation, and 34.9% with no CSF confirmation. Conclusions Absence of CSF confirmation during attempted CSE placement was strongly associated with documented early neuraxial analgesic failure during the subsequent 3-hour clinical management period. CSF-confirmation status was associated with early neuraxial analgesic outcomes but should not be interpreted as a direct measure of epidural catheter function or reliability.

items.title: Evaluating the analgesic effectiveness of erector spinae plane block for patients undergoing cardiac surgery: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized trials
items.abstract: Background Cardiac surgery is associated with severe acute postoperative pain. The erector spinae plane (ESP) block has been reported to provide effective analgesia following cardiac surgery; however, evidence supporting ESP compared with traditional parenteral analgesia remains conflicting. This meta-analysis compares the analgesic effectiveness of single injection and continuous ESP to parenteral analgesia (Control) in adult patients undergoing cardiac surgery. Methods Randomized trials were identified that compared the analgesic effectiveness of single injection or continuous ESP to Control in patients undergoing cardiac surgery. The primary outcome was rest-pain severity at 24 hours postoperatively. Secondary outcomes included rest pain at 0, 6, and 12 hours; analgesic consumption at 24 hours in milligrams of oral morphine; time to first analgesic request; time to extubation; duration of hospital stay; duration of intensive care unit stay; and block- and opioid-related side effects. Statistical pooling was conducted using the Hartung-Knapp-Sidik-Jonkman (HKSJ) method for random effects. Results A total of 27 trials, encompassing 1963 patients, were included. When compared with Control, single injection- and continuous-ESP did not improve VAS rest pain severity at 24 hours, with a mean difference (MD) (HKSJ 95% CI) of −0.46 cm (−1.14 to 0.22) (p=0.167, I2=95% (92% to 96%)) and −0.65 cm (−1.41 to 0.11) (p=0.080, I2=91% (83% to 95%)), respectively. The 95% prediction interval was observed to be −3.02 cm to 2.09 cm and −2.55 cm to 1.25 cm for the single-injection- and continuous-ESP comparisons, respectively. For rest pain at 24 hours, the Grades of Recommendation, Assessment, Development and Evaluation (GRADE) quality of evidence was rated as low for the single-injection comparison, and very low for the continuous-ESP comparison. Similar results were observed when assessing analgesic consumption at 24 hours when single-injection ESP was compared with control, with an MD (HKSJ 95% CI) of -38.95 mg (−78.98 to 1.08) (p=0.055, I2=99% (99% to 99%)). In contrast, continuous ESP appeared to improve analgesic consumption at 24 hours by an MD (HKSJ 95% CI) of -26.15 mg (−51.44 to −0.86) (p=0.045, I2=88% (75% to 94%)). The 95% prediction interval was observed to be −107.52 mg to 29.62 mg and −97.58 mg to 45.28 mg for the single-injection- and continuous-ESP comparisons, respectively. For 24-hour opioid consumption, the GRADE quality of evidence was rated as very low for both comparisons. Conclusions In adult patients undergoing cardiac surgery, low to very low certainty of evidence suggests that neither single-injection nor continuous ESP block provides clinically meaningful improvements in postoperative pain severity or opioid consumption at 24 hours compared with parenteral analgesia alone. Single-injection ESP may offer modest, short-term analgesic benefits during the early postoperative period, but these effects are transient and not sustained. Overall, the findings do not support the routine use of ESP for durable postoperative analgesia following cardiac surgery; however, the heterogeneity of results calls for cautious interpretation. PROSPERO registration number CRD420251149441.

items.title: Effect of esketamine on postoperative sleep disturbance in patients undergoing spine surgery: a randomized, double-blinded, placebo-controlled clinical trial
items.abstract: Background Postoperative sleep disturbance (PSD) is common after spine surgery and is associated with perioperative pain, anxiety, and depression. Recent studies have shown that esketamine may have the potential to improve postoperative sleep, but evidence primarily relies on subjective sleep assessments, with limited objective data. This trial therefore investigated whether intraoperative infusion of esketamine improves subjective and objective postoperative sleep quality in patients undergoing spine surgery. Methods In this double-blinded, randomized controlled trial, patients aged 18–65 years undergoing elective spine surgery were randomized 1:1 to receive intravenous esketamine or normal saline at 0.3 mg/kg/h during surgery. The primary outcome was the incidence of PSD, defined as an Athens Insomnia Scale (AIS) score ≥6 at any of the first three postoperative days. Secondary outcomes included objective sleep measures, Numerical Rating Scale (NRS) scores, and Hospital Anxiety and Depression Scale (HADS) scores. Results A total of 154 patients were included. The incidence of PSD in the esketamine group was significantly lower than in the control group (45.5% vs 77.9%; χ2=17.17; p<0.01). Mean total sleep time on the first postoperative night did not differ significantly between groups (466±142 vs 429±133 min; p=0.11). Pain, anxiety, and depression scores did not differ between the two groups. Esketamine also reduced the proportion of patients requiring hypnotics on postoperative day 2 (1.3% vs 11.7%; χ2=6.84; p< 0.01). Conclusions Intraoperative esketamine infusion reduced the incidence of PSD during the first 3 days after spine surgery. Optimal dosing and mechanisms warrant further investigation.
