In exploratory analyses, the Phoenix sepsis criteria identified 95.2% of PICU deaths, but the positive predictive value of the score for mortality was no different from the 2005 International Pediatric Sepsis Consensus Conference criteria. Conclusions: In 2024, in Ibero-Latin American PICUs, sepsis affected approximately one in four admissions, and the diagnosis was associated with mortality. Both patient vulnerability and institutional resource availability were associated with greater odds of mortality, underscoring the potential influence of health system capacity on pediatric sepsis outcomes in the region.

items.title: Electronic Children’s Hospital Early Warning Score: Development and Validation of a Novel Machine Learning Algorithm Predicting Critical Deterioration Events in a Retrospective, Single-Center Cohort
items.abstract: Objective: To develop and validate a novel, machine learning prediction model for critical deterioration events. Design: Retrospective cohort study. Setting: Single quaternary care freestanding pediatric hospital. Patients: All patients up to 21 years old admitted to acute care wards (excluding cardiac and psychiatry units) between January 2012 and June 2023. Interventions: None. Measurements and Main Results: The primary outcome was a critical deterioration, defined as utilization of advanced respiratory support or continuous IV medication infusions not administered on acute care units. Secondary outcome was ICU transfer. Each outcome was evaluated between 6 and 30 hours after each prediction score. Among 179,074 unique hospitalizations with 2,803,017 windows of scoring data, 10,656 (0.4%) had a subsequent critical deterioration event. Compared with the legacy Children’s Hospital Early Warning Score (CHEWS), the model, which we call electronic CHEWS (eCHEWS), had a higher area under the precision-recall curve (0.157; 95% CI [0.150–0.164]) vs. 0.017; 95% CI [0.013–0.027]). At sensitivity approximately 44%, CHEWS had positive predictive value (PPV) 1.8% (number needed to alert [NNA] 55), whereas eCHEWS had PPV 11.4% (NNA 9). Conclusions: eCHEWS outperforms traditional early warning scores for predicting critical deterioration among acute care inpatients and can detect critical deterioration at least 6 hours before occurrence. If prospectively validated, eCHEWS could serve as an early warning trigger integrated into the electronic health record to support proactive rounding, escalation decisions, and timely transfer to ICUs.

items.title: Physiological Impact of Chest Wall Closure in Infants Post-Cardiac Surgery. Implications for Mechanical Ventilation
items.abstract: Objectives: To assess the effect of delayed sternal closure post-cardiac surgery on respiratory system mechanics and hemodynamics. Design: Prospective single-center physiologic study. Setting: Cardiac PICU. Patients: Infants (< 1 yr old) with delayed sternal closure post-cardiopulmonary bypass for correction or palliation of a congenital heart disease. Interventions: Four ventilation conditions were studied: 1) baseline: positive end-expiratory pressure (PEEP) 5 cm H 2 O and low tidal volume (V t ; 6–7 mL/kg); 2) PEEP 5, high V t (9–10 mL/kg); 3) PEEP 3, low V t ; and 4) PEEP 8, low V t . Respiratory rate was adjusted to end-tidal carbon dioxide. Measurements were repeated after sternal closure. Measurements and Main Results: Esophageal pressure (Pes), transpulmonary pressure (P L ), normalized respiratory system elastance (Ers) in cm H 2 O/(mL/kg), and hemodynamics, including transmural pressures, were obtained before and after sternal closure. The open-sternum model used assumes that the chest wall maintains a vertical pleural pressure gradient, with the most nondependent lung exposed to atmospheric pressure. A nondependent inspiratory P L greater than 23 cm H 2 O was used as a marker of overdistention, and end-expiratory P L 0–2 cm H 2 O was considered to prevent collapse. Ten patients were included: median (interquartile range) age 32 days (18–50 d) and weight 3.1 kg (3.0–3.5 kg). Chest closure increased Pes in all conditions and Ers in most conditions, except for PEEP 8 low V t . Chest closure reduced expiratory P L in all conditions, at baseline from –0.5 cm H 2 O (–1.2 to –0.1 cm H 2 O) to –2.5 cm H 2 O (–3.1 to –1.8 cm H 2 O). Sternal closure impacted nondependent inspiratory P L differently depending on the ventilator settings. High V t was the condition more frequently associated with high nondependent inspiratory P L greater than 23 cm H 2 O. Blood pressure was maintained with fluids or vasopressors. Central venous pressure increased after closure, but the transmural filling pressure remained unchanged. Conclusions: Infants with delayed sternal closure exhibited elevated Pes and Ers after chest wall closure. Under the model assumptions, during the open-chest phase, high V t was more frequently associated with high nondependent P L , suggesting overdistention. Sternal closure made expiratory P L more negative. These findings suggest that individualized PEEP and V t adjustments guided by Pes could be considered to help preserve expiratory P L and minimize the risk of overdistension before and after chest closure.

items.title: Residents’ Ventilator Management Performance in an Online Pediatric Acute Respiratory Distress Syndrome Case Scenario: Secondary Analysis of the Game-Based Education in Residency Study, 2015–2017
items.abstract: Objectives: To evaluate resident performance in an online pediatric acute respiratory distress syndrome (PARDS) case scenario of mild/moderate severity, with the provision of individualized feedback. Design: A secondary analysis of the Game-based Education in Residency study. Setting: The dataset comprised residents in their first clinical rotation in any of 28 international PICUs, recruited between October 2015 and December 2017. Subjects: Residents who used the online mechanical ventilation (MV) simulator and completed PARDS tasks were included in the analysis. Interventions: None. Measurements and Main Results: The simulated MV parameters analyzed among 125 residents were positive end-expiratory pressure (PEEP), F io 2 , tidal volume (V t ), peak inspiratory pressure (PIP), Pa o 2 , and pH. Residents’ MV selections in relation to recommended scoring goals were: median (interquartile range [IQR]) PEEP, below or in the lower range (8 cm H 2 O [IQR, 7–8 cm H 2 O]); median F io 2 , above or in the higher range (60% [IQR, 51–60%]); and median V t , within range (5.36 mL/kg [IQR, 4.98–5.73 mL/kg]). Residents had higher than recommended median Pa o 2 (93 mm Hg [IQR, 83–99 mm Hg]), pH (7.37 [IQR, 7.33–7.40]), and median PIP (30 cm H 2 O [IQR, 28–31 cm H 2 O]). Progress through the case scenario was associated with greater odds (odds ratio [OR] and 95% CI) of adherence to goals in PEEP, F io 2 , and V t : PEEP (OR, 2.68; 95% CI, 1.65–4.34; p < 0.001); F io 2 (OR, 2.48; 95% CI, 1.29–4.76; p = 0.007); and V t (OR, 2.66; 95% CI, 1.11–6.38; p = 0.028). Conclusions: In an international PICU residents’ educational dataset from 2015 to 2017, we found that progression through the simulated PARDS case was associated with greater odds of adherence to PEEP, F io 2 , and V t goals, which suggests that repeated practice and individualized feedback were of benefit. However, residents did not wean F io 2 or MV parameters when Pa o 2 and pH were above goal. These results may help educators design contemporary MV teaching.

items.title: Long-Term Neurologic Complication and Healthcare Burden in Infants Receiving Extracorporeal Life Support: A Nationwide Population-Based Cohort Study
items.abstract: Objectives: To evaluate survival, neurologic complications, and healthcare burden in infant extracorporeal life support (ECLS) recipients using nationally representative administrative data from a single-payer healthcare system. Design: Retrospective, population-based cohort study. Setting: South Korea’s National Health Insurance Service, covering 97% of the population. Patients: Infants under 1 year who received ECLS between 2009 and 2022. Interventions: None. Measurements and Main Results: Of 698 infants who underwent ECLS, 212 infants (30.4%) survived during follow-up (estimated 1-yr mortality: 67.1%). Among survivors, 128 (60.4%) developed neurologic injuries, including acute events such as ischemic stroke, hemorrhagic stroke, and hypoxic-ischemic brain injury (HIBI), as well as long-term sequelae such as cerebral palsy, epilepsy, hearing loss, and developmental delay. Most acute neurologic injuries were diagnosed within the first year, whereas developmental delay showed prolonged diagnostic windows extending up to 12 years. Survivors with neurologic injury had significantly longer hospital stays (432.1 vs. 182.3 d; p < 0.001) and higher cumulative healthcare costs during long-term follow-up. Median index hospitalization costs were USD 36,000–37,000. The burden analysis showed distinct profiles across neurologic complications: developmental delay was the most prevalent sequela, whereas HIBI was associated with the highest cumulative healthcare cost despite lower prevalence. Conclusions: Neurologic complications following ECLS in infants are common and impose substantial long-term healthcare burden. These findings highlight the need for early risk stratification, structured neurologic and neurodevelopmental monitoring, and sustained rehabilitation planning in this high-risk population. This study provides a foundation for international benchmarking and health policy planning in pediatric critical care.

items.title: Clinical Factors Associated With Physical Restraint Use in Critically Ill Children: A Secondary Analysis of the PICU Up! Pilot Trial, 2019–2020
items.abstract: Objectives: To identify clinical factors associated with physical restraint use in critically ill children. Design: This is a secondary analysis of prospectively collected observational daily data from the baseline (preintervention) phase of the PICU Up! multicenter stepped-wedge cluster randomized trial (NCT03860168). The analytic dataset represents a shared subset of the larger parent study population. Setting: Six PICUs in the United States, from May 2019 to March 2020. Patients: A total of 1153 patients younger than 18 years admitted to a PICU for 3 or more days. Interventions: None. Measurements and Main Results: Children younger than 18 years old admitted for 3 or more consecutive PICU days were included. Daily data on sedation level, medication exposure, device use, and restraint status were collected, and multivariable generalized estimating equation models were used to evaluate associated factors. Physical restraints were used in 216 patients (18.7%) and 1,043 of 11,491 patient-days (9.07%), with a median duration of 3 days (interquartile range, 2–5). In multivariable analysis, the strongest predictor of restraint use was previous-day restraint (adjusted odds ratio [aOR], 22.79; 95% CI, 16.72–31.07). Other significant factors included age 3–17 years vs. 0–2 years (aOR, 2.46–2.69), mechanical ventilation (aOR, 2.98; 95% CI, 1.39–6.38), benzodiazepine use (aOR, 1.49; 95% CI, 1.05–2.10), and opioid use (aOR, 1.99; 95% CI, 1.42–2.78). Light sedation (State Behavioral Scale [SBS] –1) was associated with restraint use compared with calm/alert status (SBS 0; aOR, 1.72; 95% CI, 1.24–2.37), while agitation (SBS > 0) showed no association (SBS 1 [aOR, 0.97; 95% CI, 0.52–1.80] and SBS 2 [aOR, 1.10; 95% CI, 0.47–2.54]). Invasive devices were associated with increased restraint use ( p < 0.001). Notably, 51 patients (12.5%) of 407 patients receiving neuromuscular blocking agents (NMBA) remained restrained, and 30 patients were restrained on the day of ICU discharge. Conclusions: Contrary to previous reports linking agitation to restraint use, agitation (SBS > 0) was not associated with restraint use; only light sedation (SBS –1) was associated with increased odds of being restrained. Previous-day restraint use was the strongest predictor of continued restraint, highlighting persistence of previous-day practices with limited reassessment. The presence of restraints during periods of NMBA administration and at discharge days further suggests the need for improved reevaluation practices.

items.title: Utility of Renal Replacement Therapy for Infants With Congenital Diaphragmatic Hernia Receiving Extracorporeal Life Support
items.abstract: Objectives: To evaluate the association between renal replacement therapy (RRT) use and survival outcomes in infants with congenital diaphragmatic hernia (CDH) receiving extracorporeal life support (ECLS). Design: Multicenter retrospective cohort study using the Extracorporeal Life Support Organization database (2011–2020). Propensity score (PS) matching was used to account for pre-ECLS disease severity. Setting: International multicenter ECLS centers. Patients: Infants with CDH requiring ECLS. Interventions: None. Measurements and Main Results: Of 2815 infants, 749 infants (26.6%) received RRT. Before matching, +RRT patients had significantly lower survival to discharge (35.5% vs. 60.2%; p < 0.0001). PS matching generated 413 pairs with balanced pre-ECLS characteristics. After matching, +RRT remained associated with significantly lower survival to discharge (36.3% vs. 57.4%; survival odds ratio, 0.42; 95% CI, 0.32–0.56; p < 0.0001). +RRT patients also experienced longer median ECLS durations (15 vs. 9.4 d; p < 0.0001) and higher rates of severe on-ECLS AKI (10.9% vs. 3.6%; p < 0.0001). Stratified analysis showed that RRT was associated with significantly worse survival only in patients undergoing on-ECLS CDH repair. Conclusions: In infants with CDH on ECLS, RRT use is strongly associated with increased ECLS duration and decreased survival to discharge. Although PS matching suggests this association persists regardless of baseline severity, RRT likely serves as a marker for significant clinical deterioration during the ECLS course.

items.title: The Current State of Ventilator Liberation Practices and Outcomes in the United States—A Report From the Ventilator Liberation For Kids (VentLib4Kids) Collaborative
items.abstract: Objectives: Describe and explore interunit baseline ventilator liberation practices and outcomes related to the 2023 Pediatric Ventilator Liberation Guidelines within the original cohort of Ventilation Liberation For Kids (VentLib4Kids) Collaborative units. Design: Observational cohort study. Setting: Nineteen VentLib4Kids ICUs in the United States (13 general medical/surgical, five cardiovascular, and one mixed). Patients: First planned extubation attempt where code status allowed reintubation in patients younger than 19 years old, endotracheally intubated for any indication between July 1, 2023, and June 30, 2024. Interventions: None. Measurements and Main Results: A total of 2315 ventilator courses were included. Most were 28 days to younger than 6 years old (65.5%) and had a lower respiratory infection diagnosis (23.8%). Prematurity (13.2%) was the most common comorbidity. Spontaneous breathing trial exposure demonstrated the highest guideline concordance at 74.6% (median; interunit range [IUR], 49.6–100%), whereas maximal inspiratory pressure testing was lowest (3.7%; IUR, 0–62.4%). Most courses (55.5%; IUR, 19.8–99%) included an air leak test. Among those without an air leak noted or greater than 25 cmH 2 O, 70.1% were exposed to dexamethasone in concordance with the guidelines. Initiation of dexamethasone greater than or equal to 6 hours before extubation predominated (81.1%) at a median dose of 0.5 mg/kg/dose in exposed groups. Planned postextubation high-flow nasal cannula (44.3%) and bilevel positive airway pressure (18.6%) were most common. Unit-level use of any planned postextubation noninvasive respiratory support ranged from 20.6% to 100%. Among infants, planned continuous positive airway pressure was used in 6.7% of subjects. Among all courses, 10.4% (IUR, 4.5–19.2%) ended with extubation failure (reintubation within 48 hr). Conclusions: Baseline VentLib4Kids practices demonstrate varying degrees of concordance with guideline recommendations along with significant interunit variation. These results align with prior international survey data and support the need for structured, multicenter quality improvement and guideline implementation strategies.

items.title: Serum Renin As a Prognostic Biomarker in Children With Sepsis-Associated Acute Kidney Injury
items.abstract: Objectives: Renin-angiotensin-aldosterone system (RAAS) derangement contributes to acute kidney injury (AKI) and is associated with poor outcomes in critical illness. Serum renin, a clinically available biomarker of RAAS derangement, is associated with poor outcomes in critically ill adults and children. Renin has not been evaluated in children with sepsis-associated AKI (SA-AKI), either alone or in combination with other prognostic enrichment tools, including the recently derived pediatric sepsis-associated AKI (pSAKI) subphenotypes. Design: Secondary analysis of a multicenter, prospective, observational study of pediatric septic shock. Setting: Ten U.S. PICUs from January 2002 to February 2025. Patients: Patients 0–18 years old with early SA-AKI (serum creatinine-based Kidney Disease: Improving Global Outcomes stage 1–3 on days 1–2 of admission) with residual day 1 serum available for renin measurement. Interventions: None. Measurements and Main Results: Seven hundred eight patients were examined by renin tertiles. The highest renin tertile cohort (T3, > 247 pg/mL) had one fewer severe AKI-free day (4 [0–6] vs. 5 [1–7] T2 vs. 5 [2–7] T1; p < 0.001), higher day 7 severe AKI rates (47% vs. 32% vs. 27%; p < 0.001), fewer PICU-free days, and higher 28-day mortality rates. In multivariate analysis incorporating markers of illness severity, including age, T3 was independently associated with fewer severe AKI-free days (β = –0.5; se = 0.2; p = 0.01), fewer PICU-free days, and higher adjusted odds of day 7 severe AKI and 28-day mortality. Patients were assigned to either the pSAKI-1 or pSAKI-2 subphenotype to assess for additional enrichment. T3 patients had uniformly worse outcomes among the less severe pSAKI-1 subphenotype but not among pSAKI-2 patients. Conclusions: Worsening RAAS derangement, as evidenced by increasing renin concentrations, is associated with worse outcomes in children with SA-AKI. Serum renin may provide clinically useful prognostic enrichment in this population, both alone and in combination with the pSAKI subphenotypes.

items.title: Critical Pertussis in Gulf Region PICU
Authors’ Reply: Defining Critical Pertussis Across Clinical Phenotypes
Extent of resection for poorly differentiated lung adenocarcinomas ≤2 cm: a narrative review
items.abstract: Background and Objective: Histological differentiation is an important determinant of prognosis in lung adenocarcinoma. Although sublobar resection may be an effective surgical strategy for selected lung adenocarcinomas measuring ≤2 cm, poorly differentiated lung adenocarcinomas appear to have more aggressive biological behavior. This narrative review summarizes and critically evaluates the available evidence regarding the pathological characteristics, preoperative and intraoperative assessment, lymph node evaluation, and surgical management of poorly differentiated lung adenocarcinoma ≤2 cm. Methods: A structured literature search was conducted in PubMed/MEDLINE and Web of Science from inception to September 2026, using terms related to lung adenocarcinoma, high-grade histological features, and surgical resection. Relevant randomized and observational studies, as well as pathological and imaging studies, were considered. Reference lists of relevant articles were also screened, with emphasis on study design, pathological definitions, potential confounding, and lymph node assessment. Key Content and Findings: Poorly differentiated lung adenocarcinoma ≤2 cm is characterized by high-grade components such as micropapillary, solid, and complex glandular patterns. These components are associated with adverse clinicopathological features, including lymphovascular invasion, lymph node metastasis, spread through air spaces, local recurrence, and inferior survival outcomes. Randomized trials support sublobar resection for selected peripheral lung adenocarcinomas ≤2 cm, but these trials were not designed specifically for poorly differentiated tumors. Histology-specific retrospective studies suggest that lobectomy may provide better oncological outcomes than limited resection for poorly differentiated adenocarcinoma, although differences in study populations, pathological assessment, lymph node assessment, and potential selection bias limit the interpretation of these findings. Conclusions: Current evidence suggests that high-grade histological components may increase the risk of recurrence after limited resection and may help identify patients who could benefit from lobectomy. Accurate assessment of radiographic and pathological high-risk features, together with adequate lymph node evaluation, is therefore important for individualized surgical decision-making. Although most histology-specific evidence is retrospective, high-grade features may be considered alongside tumor size, radiographic findings, and patient-related factors when selecting the extent of resection. Prospective multicenter clinical studies are needed to further define the optimal surgical strategy for lung adenocarcinomas with high-grade histological components.

items.title: Functional limitation associated with chest tubes after video-assisted thoracoscopic lung resection: spirometric evidence from a prospective enhanced recovery cohort
items.abstract: Background: Chest tubes may limit pulmonary function after video-assisted thoracoscopic lung resection. Objective spirometric evidence quantifying this impact remains limited. Methods: The Pulmonary Function after Thoracic Surgery (PATHOS) trial was a prospective, single-arm, single-center observational study conducted within an enhanced recovery pathway. Spirometry was performed preoperatively and daily from postoperative day (POD) 1 to POD 5 or until discharge. Recovery was calculated as the percentage of the individual preoperative value. Changes over time were analyzed using mixed-effects models. Spirometric values obtained before and after chest tube removal were compared using paired t-tests. Results: Sixty-three patients were included in the spirometric analysis. Forced expiratory volume in 1 second (FEV 1 ), vital capacity (VC), and peak expiratory flow (PEF) showed significant recovery from POD 1 to POD 5 (all P<0.001). Chest tube removal was associated with significant improvements in FEV 1 (P<0.001), VC (P<0.001), and PEF (P=0.009). Conclusions: Chest tubes are associated with measurable functional limitation after thoracoscopic lung resection. Chest tube removal was associated with significant spirometric improvement within the early postoperative period.

items.title: Rescue strategy for unexpected dense pleural adhesions during local anesthetic thoracoscopy using monopolar electrocautery and pleural cryobiopsy
Machine learning predicts major adverse cardiovascular events following modified Morrow surgery for hypertrophic obstructive cardiomyopathy
items.abstract: Background: Although modified Morrow surgery relieves left ventricular outflow tract obstruction, patients remain at risk of postoperative cardiovascular events. This study aimed to develop and validate an interpretable machine learning (ML) model for predicting 24-month major adverse cardiovascular events [MACEs; comprising cardiovascular death, non-fatal myocardial infarction (MI), non-fatal stroke, and heart failure hospitalization (HFH)] following modified Morrow surgery in patients with hypertrophic obstructive cardiomyopathy (HOCM). Methods: We retrospectively studied 354 adult patients with HOCM who underwent modified Morrow surgery at Beijing Anzhen Hospital (approval No. KS2025079) between July 2015 and July 2024. We developed an ensemble ML model integrating recursive feature elimination (RFE) with a voting classifier [support vector machine (SVM), random forest, decision tree, extreme gradient boosting (XGBoost)]. The model was trained and tuned using five-fold cross-validation, with performance rigorously compared against conventional logistic regression (LR) and least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) regression. Model interpretability was achieved through SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) analysis. Results: The ML model demonstrated robust performance in five-fold cross-validation and superior predictive capability on the independent test set compared to conventional LR and LASSO regression. On the test set, the ML model achieved an area under the receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve (AUC) of 0.88 [95% confidence interval (CI): 0.82–0.94], significantly outperforming LR (AUC: 0.70) and LASSO (AUC: 0.71). It also attained the highest accuracy (0.82 vs. 0.62 and 0.68), highest balanced accuracy (0.74 vs. 0.52 and 0.63), and highest F1-score (0.83 vs. 0.66 and 0.68), indicating excellent discrimination and classification performance. SHAP analysis identified a positive family history of hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM) as the most influential predictor, highlighting the critical role of familial risk phenotype in postoperative prognosis. Conclusions: This study developed and internally validated HOCM-ML Risk, an interpretable ML-based tool for stratifying the risk of MACEs after modified Morrow surgery. By identifying key prognostic predictors such as familial history and modifiable clinical factors, the model provides a data-driven framework to support more personalized postoperative assessment.

items.title: Liposomal bupivacaine for thoracic paravertebral nerve block in patients with multiple rib fractures: a randomized controlled trial protocol
Intercostal single-port robotic thoracic surgery: technical description and tips
items.abstract: Single-port (SP) robotic platforms represent the latest evolution in minimally invasive thoracic surgery, extending the principles of uniportal surgery to dedicated robotic technology. Most reported thoracic applications of the da Vinci SP system have relied on subcostal access; however, alternative approaches may facilitate exposure of upper-lobe structures and posterior hilar anatomy. To address these challenges, we developed a standardized intercostal SP robotic technique for anatomical pulmonary resection. The procedure is performed through a single 4–5 cm incision in the anterior axillary line (sixth or seventh intercostal space). Key technical features include a standardized instrument configuration, structured team communication protocols, loop-guided traction to facilitate stapler insertion through the service channel, selective use of carbon dioxide (CO 2 ) insufflation, and indocyanine green (ICG) fluorescence imaging for segmentectomy. The technique is illustrated through representative procedures, including right upper lobectomy (RUL), posterior segmentectomy (S2), and inferior anterolateral bisegmentectomy (S8+S9). The intercostal approach provides a direct working corridor to the pulmonary hilum while preserving the advantages of a single-incision robotic platform. In our initial experience, five consecutive anatomical pulmonary resections were completed without conversion to thoracotomy or additional ports. Median operative time was 168 minutes (range, 139–258 minutes), and median length of hospital stay (LOS) was 5 days (range, 2–10 days). Technical challenges related to rib-arc constraints were effectively managed through operating-table flexion, standardized arm configuration, loop-guided stapling, and coordinated instrument movements. The intercostal SP robotic approach represents a feasible option for anatomical pulmonary resection. Standardization of operative steps may support its implementation among teams experienced in robotic thoracic surgery, while further studies are required to assess reproducibility across different surgical settings and to define its role relative to subcostal SP and conventional multiport (MP) robotic approaches.

items.title: Evaluation of pulmonary tuberculosis using ultra-low-dose computed tomography based on artificial intelligence iterative reconstruction
items.abstract: Background: Computed tomography (CT) plays a crucial role as an imaging modality in the evaluation of pulmonary tuberculosis (PTB). It is frequently employed for screening active PTB and longitudinal assessments during anti-PTB therapy, raising increasing concern regarding the associated radiation exposure. Ultra-low-dose CT (ULDCT) scanning protocols based on artificial intelligence iterative reconstruction (AIIR) have been utilized for the diagnosis of pulmonary diseases. This study aims to investigate the feasibility of ULDCT-AIIR in assessing PTB. Methods: Forty-seven patients diagnosed with PTB were prospectively enrolled and underwent both moderately reduced-dose CT (RDCT) and ULDCT scans. The effective dose (ED) of the two scanning protocols was compared. All RDCT and ULDCT images were reconstructed using filtered back projection (FBP) and hybrid iterative reconstruction (HIR). Additionally, ULDCT images were reconstructed using AIIR. Objective image quality metrics [noise, contrast-to-noise ratio (CNR)] and subjective evaluation criteria (clarity of the image, thoracic anatomy, and active PTB features) were assessed. Confidence in evaluating PTB treatment response was compared among the different image sets. Results: The ED for ULDCT was significantly lower than that for RDCT (0.06 vs 4.33 mSv). ULDCT-AIIR yielded image noise and CNR values that were not significantly different from those of RDCT-HIR (P>0.05) but were significantly better than those of the other image series (P<0.05). Image quality, clarity of normal thoracic structures, and features of active PTB on ULDCT-AIIR were not significantly different from those on RDCT-FBP and RDCT-HIR (P>0.05), but were significantly better than those on ULDCT-FBP and ULDCT-HIR (P<0.05). Confidence in assessing PTB treatment response was significantly higher with ULDCT-AIIR compared to ULDCT-HIR (P<0.05) and was not significantly different from that with RDCT-HIR (P>0.05). Conclusions: ULDCT-AIIR yields image quality not significantly different from RDCT, with an ED of less than 2% of that for RDCT. It may serve as a tool for monitoring PTB activity and treatment response, with potential implications for PTB management.

items.title: Histopathological correlates of endobronchial optical coherence tomography airway features in patients with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease
items.abstract: Background: Endobronchial optical coherence tomography (EB-OCT) provides high-resolution, cross-sectional imaging of airway microstructure and has generated candidate biomarkers of airway remodeling, including mucus accumulation, airway wall edema, and buckling. However, the histopathological substrates of these OCT features remain incompletely defined. We aimed to evaluate the airway-level histopathological correlates of these EB-OCT features in patients with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD). Methods: We conducted a prospective observational imaging-histopathology correlation study in 26 patients with COPD undergoing lung resection. Preoperative in vivo EB-OCT images were matched at the airway level with histopathological measurements from the corresponding resected airway segments. OCT-derived mucus accumulation, edema-positive frame proportion, and buckling parameters were correlated with the Reid index, composite inflammatory score, and airway smooth muscle area fraction, respectively. Interobserver reproducibility was assessed independently for OCT-derived and histopathological measurements. Results: OCT-derived mucus biomarkers were strongly associated with histological mucous gland hypertrophy. Mean mucus area fraction and mucus-positive frame proportion correlated with Reid index (Spearman’s ρ=0.850 and ρ=0.711, respectively; both P<0.001). Edema-positive frame proportion correlated with composite inflammatory score (ρ=0.772; P<0.001). Buckling measurements correlated strongly with airway smooth muscle (ASM) area fraction, including mean buckling length fraction (ρ=0.895; P<0.001) and buckling-positive frame proportion (ρ=0.896; P<0.001). Interobserver reproducibility was high for both OCT-derived and histopathological measurements. After adjustment for age, pack-years, and GOLD grade, four of the five prespecified associations remained significant after Bonferroni correction; the adjusted edema-inflammation association did not. Conclusions: Major EB-OCT airway imaging biomarkers were associated with their corresponding histopathological features of airway remodeling. These findings support EB-OCT as a biologically interpretable imaging platform for evaluating secretory, inflammatory, and smooth muscle remodeling in COPD.

items.title: Development and internal validation of a Day 0 prediction model for prolonged postoperative length of stay (>7 days) after non-small cell lung cancer resection
items.abstract: Background: Prolonged postoperative length of stay (PLOS) remains an important recovery and resource-use outcome after non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) surgery despite Enhanced Recovery After Surgery (ERAS) pathways. We aimed to develop and internally validate an exploratory Day 0 model using information available by surgical completion. Methods: This single-center retrospective prediction-model development and internal-validation study included adults undergoing surgical management of NSCLC at Beijing Anzhen Hospital from January through December 2025. PLOS was defined as postoperative hospitalization >7 days. The candidate predictors were age, sex, body mass index (BMI), neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR), B-type natriuretic peptide (BNP), operative duration, and blood loss. NLR and BNP were natural-log transformed. One missing BMI value and 92 missing/non-numeric BNP values were replaced by cohort medians in the primary analysis. Ten-fold cross-validated least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) was followed by multivariable logistic regression; internal validation used 500 bootstrap resamples. Results: Among 247 analyzed patients, 45 (18.2%) experienced PLOS. Compared with the normal-stay group, the PLOS group comprised older patients (median, 68.0 vs. 64.0 years), had a higher proportion of male patients (68.9% vs. 47.5%), and showed higher NLR, longer operative duration, and greater blood loss (all P<0.05). The final model included age, BMI, Ln (NLR), Ln (BNP), operative duration, and blood loss. The apparent area under the curve (AUC) was 0.834 [95% confidence interval (CI): 0.761–0.907] and bootstrap-corrected AUC was 0.810. Apparent and optimism-corrected Brier scores were 0.105 and 0.116; corrected calibration intercept was −0.197 and slope was 0.838. At the exploratory, post hoc threshold of 0.172, the apparent estimates were 80.0% (95% CI: 65.4–90.4%) for sensitivity, 77.7% (71.4–83.3%) for specificity, 44.4% (33.4–55.9%) for positive predictive value (PPV), and 94.6% (90.0–97.5%) for negative predictive value (NPV). Optimism-corrected decision-curve analysis showed net benefit over treat-all and treat-none strategies across thresholds 0.05–0.50 in the development cohort. Conclusions: The Day 0 model showed good internally validated discrimination, but substantial BNP missingness, limited events, a restricted candidate set, and single-center development make it exploratory. Prospective external validation and impact evaluation are required before clinical use.

items.title: VATS complex/combined pulmonary (sub)segmentectomies: four proprietary surgical techniques based on the watershed analysis—a case series study
items.abstract: Background: Complex/combined pulmonary (sub)segmentectomy for small peripheral lung nodules faces major technical obstacles including confusing anatomical variations, prolonged bronchovascular dissection, elevated intraoperative hemorrhage risk, and postoperative venous stasis hemoptysis caused by accidental inter(sub)segmental vein transection. The novel watershed territory-guided resection redefines the surgical resection unit as a functional vascular watershed territory, yet standardized proprietary surgical workflows designed specifically for high-difficulty combined sublobar resections are still absent, with limited systematic clinical evidence validating its perioperative safety and long-term oncological efficacy. This single-center retrospective study aimed to preliminarily evaluate perioperative indicators and medium-term follow-up outcomes of four self-developed Watershed Analysis-based core techniques applied in complex/combined thoracoscopic pulmonary (sub)segmentectomies. Methods: We consecutively enrolled 24 patients carrying peripheral pulmonary nodules ≤2.0 cm who received watershed territory-guided complex/combined thoracoscopic (sub)segmentectomy between November 2023 and April 2026. Four original core surgical techniques were uniformly implemented: (Ⅰ) Watershed Compensation, (Ⅱ) Concurrent Analysis of Multifocal Watershed Vasculature, (Ⅲ) Integrated Analysis of Arteriovenous Watershed Vasculature, (Ⅳ) Refined Dissection of Arteriovenous Watershed Vasculature. Preoperative 3D vascular reconstruction and intraoperative modified inflation-deflation plane demarcation were adopted as standardized procedures. Baseline demographics, intraoperative operative parameters, postoperative pathological results, complication profiles, and follow-up oncological data [database locked on June 30, 2026; median follow-up 22.5 months; interquartile range (IQR), 14–27 months; range, 2–31 months] were retrospectively analyzed, with descriptive stratified comparisons (no formal hypothesis testing) grouped by watershed vessel type, total nodule quantity, and postoperative pathological subtype. Results: All 24 thoracoscopic operations were successfully finished without conversion to open thoracotomy or lobectomy, and no severe intraoperative hemorrhage occurred; R0 radical resection was achieved for all malignant pulmonary lesions. The average operative time reached 158.1±56.3 min, median intraoperative blood loss was 50 mL, median hospital stay was 9.0 days (IQR, 8.0–10.0; mean 10.0±3.2 days), and the overall postoperative complication rate was 8.3%. No inter(sub)segmental vein injury-related hemoptysis, bronchopleural fistula, tumor recurrence, distant metastasis, or all-cause death was observed during follow-up. The perioperative profiles were broadly comparable across the three watershed territory types (arterial, venous, and arteriovenous). The arteriovenous group had a numerically longer operative time, with a median of 170.0 min, versus 132.5 min in the arterial group and 137.5 min in the venous group. Patients with multiple pulmonary nodules had a numerically longer operative duration than those with a single nodule, with median values of 165.0 vs. 137.5 min, and mean values of 189.5±64.4 vs. 135.7±38.0 min, respectively, while postoperative recovery measures were descriptively comparable between the two groups. The subgroup with more invasive disease demonstrated numerically higher values in hospital stay. Conclusions: The four proprietary watershed analysis-derived techniques enable individualized and potentially simplified surgical planning for complex/combined pulmonary (sub)segmentectomy. For malignant lesions, these techniques ensure R0 radical resection while potentially preserving a greater volume of normal lung parenchyma. This vascular watershed territory-oriented surgical strategy is clinically feasible, and theoretically may reduce the risk of postoperative hemoptysis caused by misdivided inter(sub)segmental veins, with a low perioperative complication profile and stable short-to-medium term oncological safety in this selected cohort. Large-sample, multicenter prospective clinical trials are still warranted to further evaluate the presumed long-term lung function preservation benefit of this technique, as well as its broad clinical applicability in early-stage lung malignancies predominantly featuring ground-glass opacity.

items.title: The 10-year revisit rate and its influencing factors among patients with obstructive sleep apnea
items.abstract: Background: Obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) is a common chronic sleep-disordered breathing that requires revisits and long-term management. However, revisits after the initial visit are low, leading to suboptimal treatment in clinical practice. The evidence on revisits and determinants is limited. This study aims to report the 10-year revisit rate and assess its influencing factors in OSA. Methods: Data from patients seen at our sleep center during 2015 were used to assess revisit status over 10 years. Revisit information, including timing, frequency, destination, reasons, and treatments, was collected through telephone interviews, the hospital information system (HIS), and the national health database. Logistic regression, Kaplan-Meier survival analysis, and Cox proportional hazards models were used to assess revisit patterns and influencing factors. Results: Of 528 enrolled patients, 356 were included in the subsequent analysis. The overall revisit rate was 64.3%, with a sleep center revisit rate of 5.9%. In moderate-to-severe OSA, 49.0% had used positive airway pressure (PAP); 10.4% both remained on long-term PAP and revisited for OSA. Age showed a nominal association with revisit behavior [odds ratio (OR), 1.02; 95% confidence interval (CI): 1.00–1.04; nominal P=0.02] that did not survive false discovery rate (FDR) correction. In the Cox analysis, patients aged ≥65 years showed a greater tendency to revisit than those aged <50 years (P=0.07) or 50–<65 years (P=0.01). Conclusions: The revisit rate was low among OSA patients, particularly at sleep centers, and PAP follow-up was suboptimal. Age-related differences in revisit behavior were observed. Improving continuity of care may help optimize long-term OSA management.

items.title: Low incidence of thromboembolism with ambulation-focused enhanced recovery protocol for lung cancer after minimally invasive resection
items.abstract: Background: There is a lack of consensus among thoracic surgeons on the subject of venous thromboembolism (VTE) prophylaxis in lung cancer patients undergoing resection. We aim to report our experiences under a framework of ambulation-focused thoracic-specific Enhanced Recovery after Surgery (ERAS) protocol. Methods: Study cohort comprised patients undergoing minimally invasive resection for confirmed or suspected lung cancer from 2012 to 2022. Patients were included if they had documentation of post-operative ambulation and available VTE information during hospitalization. Individual Caprini scores were calculated and categorized into four risk groups: low [0–4], moderate [5–6], high [7–8], highest [≥9]. Observed/predicted (O/P) ratios in terms of VTE occurrences were computed for each risk group. Results: Eight hundred and eighty-six patients were eligible for inclusion, with 804 (90.7%) patients not receiving any VTE prophylaxis during hospitalization. In patients without VTE prophylaxis, VTE was recorded in 14 cases among 12 distinct patients (1.4%). Deep venous thrombosis (DVT) was recorded post-operatively in 6 (0.7%) patients and pulmonary embolism (PE) in 8 (0.9%) patients. There were 2 patients where both DVT and PE occurred. The Caprini score distribution among included patients was 3 (0.4%) in the low-risk group, 192 (23.9%) moderate risk, 461 (57.3%) high risk, and 148 (18.4%) highest risk. The O/P ratios were less than 1 for each group. Conclusions: Ambulation-focused thoracic ERAS protocol can maintain a low rate of VTE in lung cancer patients without use of chemoprophylaxis.

items.title: Dual bronchoscopic barium-ICG marking for wedge resection of small peripheral pulmonary lesions
items.abstract: Background: Accurate localization of non-palpable small peripheral pulmonary lesions is essential for wedge resection, particularly during thoracoscopic and robot-assisted surgery. We evaluated the feasibility of a dual bronchoscopic marking method combining barium and indocyanine green (ICG), which was designed to support preoperative computed tomography (CT)-based planning and intraoperative fluorescence-guided localization. Methods: This retrospective single-center case series included 30 consecutive patients who underwent preoperative bronchoscopic barium/ICG marking followed by thoracoscopic or robot-assisted wedge resection between July 2022 and May 2025. The primary outcome was successful intraoperative localization using either component of the dual-marker method. Secondary outcomes included ICG fluorescence visualization, the relationship between the surgical margin and pathological invasive size, perioperative outcomes, postoperative complications, and staple-line recurrence. Results: Overall localization was successful in all 30 patients (100%). ICG fluorescence visualized the marking site in 29 patients (96.7%); in one patient, the lesion was localized using the barium marker under fluoroscopy. The median surgical margin was 1.5 cm, and the surgical margin was at least equal to the pathological invasive size in 27 patients (90%). In three patients, all of whom underwent compromised limited resection, the invasive size exceeded the surgical margin; one developed staple-line recurrence. Postoperative complications occurred only in patients who underwent simultaneous anatomical lung resection. Conclusions: Dual bronchoscopic barium/ICG marking achieved reliable localization of non-palpable small peripheral pulmonary lesions and provided complementary radiographic and fluorescence guidance. Larger comparative studies are required to determine whether this approach improves margin adequacy, safety, or workflow relative to other localization techniques.

items.title: Development of a preliminary risk model for postoperative acute kidney injury in patients with hypertrophic obstructive cardiomyopathy: a single-center retrospective study
items.abstract: Background: Acute kidney injury (AKI) is a common complication after cardiac surgery, but procedure-specific risk assessment in patients with hypertrophic obstructive cardiomyopathy (HOCM) undergoing the modified Morrow procedure remains insufficiently characterized. This study aimed to develop a clinically interpretable preliminary risk model for postoperative AKI using variables available before or during surgery and to describe the early postoperative AKI trajectory in this population. Methods: We retrospectively analyzed 161 consecutive patients who underwent the modified Morrow procedure between March 2019 and April 2025. Postoperative AKI was defined according to Kidney Disease: Improving Global Outcomes criteria within the first 7 postoperative days. Hierarchical logistic regression models were constructed using an analytic cohort of 158 patients, sequentially incorporating baseline clinical variables, aortic cross-clamp time, and HOCM-specific echocardiographic characteristics, including interventricular septal thickness and 100 minus ejection fraction (100−EF). Model performance was evaluated using discrimination, calibration assessment, and internal validation with bootstrap resampling. Results: Postoperative AKI occurred in 58 of 161 patients (36.0%). In the final model, hypertension was independently associated with postoperative AKI [adjusted odds ratio (OR)=4.547, 95% confidence interval (CI): 1.801–11.484; P=0.001], and higher 100−EF was also associated with increased AKI risk (adjusted OR =1.216, 95% CI: 1.042–1.420; P=0.01). Interventricular septal thickness showed a borderline association with AKI (adjusted OR =1.093, 95% CI: 0.996–1.199; P=0.06). The final model demonstrated an apparent area under the curve (AUC) of 0.763 in the development cohort. Bootstrap internal validation showed an optimism-corrected AUC of 0.709, with a calibration slope of 0.728, calibration intercept of −0.123, and optimism-corrected Brier score of 0.214. Conclusions: A preliminary risk model incorporating clinical factors, perioperative exposure, and HOCM-specific echocardiographic characteristics may help identify patients at increased risk of postoperative AKI after modified Morrow surgery. Hypertension and higher 100−EF, a mathematical transformation of left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) reflecting lower resting left ventricular systolic function, were associated with postoperative AKI. However, the model requires external validation in larger multicenter cohorts before clinical application.

items.title: Erratum: Thoracic SMARCA4-deficient undifferentiated tumor: a systematic review and meta-analysis of individual patient data with cross-cohort survival comparison
Bronchial generation difference as an operational reach-gap metric in radial endobronchial ultrasonography-guided bronchoscopy for malignant peripheral pulmonary lesions
items.abstract: Background: Failure to obtain malignant tissue during bronchoscopy for peripheral pulmonary lesions may occur despite lesion localization by radial endobronchial ultrasonography. We hypothesized that the gap between the computed tomography (CT)-defined target bronchial generation and the distal bronchial generation actually reached by the bronchoscope would be associated with unsuccessful tissue acquisition, but this bronchoscopic reach gap has not been routinely quantified. We defined bronchial generation difference (BGD) as the difference between the CT-defined target bronchial generation and the most distal bronchial generation reached by the bronchoscope. This study evaluated the association between BGD and successful malignant tissue acquisition in malignant peripheral pulmonary lesions. Methods: This retrospective single-center study included 89 pathologically confirmed malignant peripheral pulmonary lesions in 88 patients sampled by diagnostic bronchoscopy with available procedure videos. BGD was determined using preprocedural thin-section CT images and procedure videos. The primary outcome was successful malignant tissue acquisition during bronchoscopy. Logistic regression analysis was performed using BGD, radial endobronchial ultrasonography image category, and lesion size. An exploratory BGD threshold and intraobserver and interobserver reproducibility were also assessed. Results: Successful malignant tissue acquisition was achieved in 61 of 89 lesions (68.5%). Each 1-generation increase in BGD was associated with lower odds of successful acquisition in the main multivariable model (adjusted odds ratio, 0.50; 95% confidence interval, 0.32–0.76; P=0.001). An exploratory BGD threshold of ≤1 was associated with a higher acquisition rate than BGD ≥2 (83.3% vs. 51.2%). For BGD, the intraobserver and interobserver intraclass correlation coefficients were 0.911 (95% confidence interval, 0.868–0.941) and 0.793 (95% confidence interval, 0.701–0.859), respectively. Conclusions: In this malignant, video-analyzable cohort, BGD was an operational bronchoscopic reach-gap metric associated with successful malignant tissue acquisition. This metric may provide a practical framework for post-procedural review and for future CT-based prediction of bronchoscopic reachability, although its role in real-time procedural decision-making and preprocedural planning requires prospective validation.

items.title: Admission-based scoring model for predicting in-hospital mortality in secondary spontaneous pneumothorax: a multicenter retrospective cohort study
items.abstract: Background: Secondary spontaneous pneumothorax (SSP) is associated with higher in-hospital mortality than primary spontaneous pneumothorax. However, no admission-based predictive model has been reported for this population. This study aimed to develop an exploratory admission-based scoring model to stratify the risk of in-hospital mortality in hospitalized patients with SSP. Methods: We retrospectively analyzed data from 780 hospitalized patients with SSP enrolled in a multicenter cohort. The data were divided into a development cohort (admitted between April and December 2019, n=603) and a validation cohort (admitted between January and March 2020, n=177). Multivariate Cox proportional hazards regression was used to identify variables associated with in-hospital mortality. A mortality risk score was developed by assigning integer points to each variable. Results: In-hospital mortality occurred in 42 cases (5.4%) in the total cohort and 11 cases (2.6%) in those who underwent surgical intervention. The model included three variables: performance status ≥3, home oxygen therapy, and serum C-reactive protein level ≥3.59 mg/L. The scoring model showed good discrimination, with an area under the curve of 0.844 in the development cohort and 0.83 in the validation cohort. Scores were stratified into three groups (scores 0–2, 3–4, and 5–6), corresponding to low (0% and 0%), intermediate (4.4% and 6.2%), and high (25.3% and 35.3%) observed in-hospital mortality rates in the development and validation cohorts, respectively. Conclusions: The admission-based score stratified the risk of in-hospital mortality in hospitalized patients with SSP. Further validation using clinical data collected at the time of SSP diagnosis is required before the score can be considered for clinical application.

items.title: Association between obstructive sleep apnea phenotypes and severity in the Chinese population: a cross-sectional study
items.abstract: Background: A novel phenotype, uniform obstructive sleep apnea (OSA), has been proposed, but its association with disease severity remains unclear in the Chinese population. This study aims to evaluate the distribution of OSA phenotypes and their association with severity in Chinese individuals. Methods: This single-center cross-sectional study included consecutive patients with OSA [apnea-hypopnea index (AHI) ≥5] aged 14–80 years who underwent polysomnography (PSG) between 2019 and 2021. OSA phenotype was treated as a nominal three-category variable, including rapid eye movement (REM)-dependent OSA (REM-OSA), non-REM-dependent OSA (NREM-OSA), and uniform OSA, based on AHI ratios. Severity was classified as mild, moderate, or severe. The distribution of OSA severity across phenotypes was compared using the Pearson chi-square test with Holm-adjusted pairwise comparisons. Multinomial logistic regression was performed to identify factors associated with phenotypes. Results: Among the 238 OSA patients [82.4% male; median age 49 years; median body mass index (BMI) 27.1 kg/m²], uniform OSA was the most prevalent (55.9%), followed by REM-OSA (31.9%) and NREM-OSA (12.2%). The distribution of OSA severity differed significantly among phenotypes (χ²=99.040, df =4, P<0.001; Cramér’s V =0.456). REM-OSA predominantly comprised mild-to-moderate disease, whereas uniform OSA predominantly comprised severe disease (73.7%). Multivariable analysis indicated that, compared with severe OSA, mild-to-moderate OSA was associated with higher odds of REM-OSA than uniform OSA. Compared with uniform OSA, higher minimum peripheral oxygen saturation (SpO 2 ) was associated with REM-OSA and NREM-OSA, while older age was associated with NREM-OSA. Conclusions: Uniform OSA is highly prevalent and associated with severe disease in this Chinese cohort. These findings highlight the necessity of phenotype-specific screening and individualized management strategies to optimize OSA care.

items.title: Single-center experience with surgical site infection following adult pectus repair
items.abstract: Background: Infections after pectus repair are uncommon but significant due to implanted hardware. Data on surgical site infections (SSIs) after adult pectus repair are limited. This study aimed to quantify the infection rate and identify associated risk factors. Methods: A retrospective review was conducted of consecutive patients undergoing pectus repair (ages 16 and over) by a single surgeon between January 1, 2010, and December 31, 2025. Patients were stratified into primary minimally invasive repair of pectus excavatum (MIRPE) and complex procedures, which included hybrid and revision procedures. SSIs were classified as superficial or deep/organ-space according to the Infectious Diseases Society of America criteria. Both univariable and multivariable Firth regression analyses were performed to evaluate factors associated with infection. Results: In total, 1,364 patients were included (mean age 31.1±10.7 years). There were 1,060 primary MIRPE repairs (77.7%) and 304 complex procedures (22.3%). Infection was significantly less frequent following primary MIRPE than complex procedures (superficial SSI: 3.4% vs. 5.2%; deep/organ-space SSI: 0.75% vs. 2.9%; P<0.001). In the overall cohort, higher odds of postoperative infection were observed among patients undergoing complex procedures [odds ratio (OR) 2.71, 95% confidence interval (CI): 1.62–4.43; P<0.001], those with a history of smoking (OR 2.21, 95% CI: 1.19–3.89; P=0.01), prolonged operative duration (OR 1.01 per minute, 95% CI: 1.00–1.01; P<0.001), and pleural effusions requiring intervention (OR 2.16, 95% CI: 0.99–4.24; P=0.053). Extensive adhesiolysis exceeding 45 minutes demonstrated a strong trend toward increased infection risk (OR 2.13, 95% CI: 0.98–4.17; P=0.057). In the primary MIRPE subgroup, smoking history (OR 2.25, 95% CI: 1.06–4.41; P=0.04) and postoperative intervention for pleural effusion (OR 2.92, 95% CI: 1.31–5.91; P=0.01) were significantly associated with infection, while concurrent breast surgery demonstrated a near-significant association (OR 2.75, 95% CI: 0.97–6.52; P=0.057). Conclusions: The rate of SSIs following adult pectus excavatum (PE) repair was low; however, subgroups experienced higher risks.

items.title: Surgical outcomes and long-term survival of chronic pulmonary aspergillosis: a 13-year single-center experience
items.abstract: Background: In tuberculosis-endemic regions, chronic pulmonary aspergillosis (CPA) remains a challenging surgical entity. The clinical characteristics and surgical outcomes of different CPA phenotypes, the evolving role of video-assisted thoracic surgery (VATS), and risk factors for major postoperative complications remain incompletely defined. This study aimed to characterize phenotype-specific clinical and surgical outcomes, examine temporal trends in VATS use, and identify factors associated with major postoperative complications and overall survival. Methods: This single-center retrospective study included 314 patients who underwent pulmonary resection for CPA between 2013 and 2025. Patients were classified by imaging as simple aspergilloma (SA), Aspergillus nodule (AN), chronic cavitary pulmonary aspergillosis (CCPA), or chronic fibrosing pulmonary aspergillosis (CFPA). Perioperative metrics, major complications (Clavien-Dindo grade ≥III), and overall survival (OS) were analyzed. Temporal trends were compared between the early era [2013–2019] and recent era [2020–2025]. Results: Completed VATS utilization increased from 45% in the early era to 73% in the recent era. CCPA and CFPA were associated with longer operative times with greater blood loss (both P<0.001). Major complications occurred in 17% of patients, most frequently in CFPA (21%) and CCPA (20%). Longer operative time, diabetes mellitus, and chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) were independently associated with major complications. The estimated 10-year OS was 88.7%, with no significant difference among CPA phenotypes. In an original exploratory multivariable model with only 17 deaths, completed VATS was associated with lower observed mortality than primary thoracotomy or VATS-to-thoracotomy conversion [hazard ratio (HR) 0.25, 95% confidence interval (CI): 0.08–0.77; P=0.02]. Conclusions: CPA phenotypes were associated with substantially different surgical complexity and perioperative risk. Completed VATS was associated with better long-term OS, but this observational association should be interpreted cautiously because surgical approach was not randomized and may be confounded by case selection, resection extent, and surgical era. These findings support phenotype-informed perioperative risk assessment and careful selection of minimally invasive surgery rather than a prescriptive surgical algorithm.

items.title: A nomogram based on peripheral blood CD4/CD8 ratio and treatment regimen for predicting disease progression in lung cancer patients
items.abstract: Background: Current polygenic prediction models for lung cancer are complex, costly, and difficult to implement in routine clinical practice, particularly in resource-limited hospitals. There is a lack of low-cost, easily scalable tools for individualized risk stratification of disease progression. We aimed to develop a simple nomogram using only two routinely available clinical variables—the baseline peripheral blood CD4/CD8 ratio and treatment regimen—to predict disease progression in lung cancer patients. Methods: A total of 119 patients with lung cancer who received radiotherapy, chemotherapy, targeted therapy, or immunotherapy between January 2025 and January 2026 were retrospectively enrolled. Peripheral blood lymphocyte subsets, including CD4 + and CD8 + T cells, NK cells, and B cells, were measured by flow cytometry before treatment. The CD4/CD8 ratio was calculated. Univariate and multivariate logistic regression analyses were performed to identify independent predictors of disease progression. A simple nomogram based on routinely available variables was constructed and evaluated by receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curves, calibration curves, and decision curve analysis (DCA). Results: The baseline CD4/CD8 ratio was significantly higher in the disease control (DC) group compared to the progression group (P=0.02). Multivariate analysis revealed that the CD4/CD8 ratio and targeted therapy were independent predictors of disease progression. The nomogram incorporating these two factors achieved an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.755, with good calibration. DCA demonstrated that the nomogram provided a superior net benefit over individual predictors. Conclusions: The baseline peripheral blood CD4/CD8 ratio was an independent predictor of disease progression in this single-center retrospective cohort. The nomogram integrating the CD4/CD8 ratio and treatment regimen showed good predictive performance; however, external validation is required before it can be recommended for individualized risk stratification in broader clinical settings.

Parsimonious and interpretable machine learning model for early prediction of acute kidney injury in acute respiratory distress syndrome: a multicenter development and validation study
items.abstract: Background: Acute kidney injury (AKI) frequently complicates acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) and increases mortality, yet current risk assessment relies on late functional markers like serum creatinine and urine output. These markers reflect established injury, limiting opportunities for preemptive intervention. Machine learning (ML) approaches may improve early risk stratification, but existing models lack rigorous external validation and clinical interpretability. We therefore aimed to develop and externally validate a parsimonious and interpretable machine learning model for the early prediction of AKI in patients with ARDS using routinely collected clinical variables. Methods: This multicenter retrospective study included 2,477 ARDS patients from five randomized controlled trials (RCTs) for model development and an independent external cohort of 3,357 patients from three additional RCTs and two intensive care unit (ICU) databases [Medical Information Mart for Intensive Care IV (MIMIC-IV) and the eICU Collaborative Research Database (eICU)]. Six ML algorithms used predictors collected during hours 0–24 relative to cohort-specific time zero to predict new-onset AKI during hours 24–72 among patients without AKI at the 24-hour landmark. AKI was defined using only the serum-creatinine components of the Kidney Disease: Improving Global Outcomes (KDIGO) criteria in both cohorts. SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) informed model interpretation and development of a parsimonious 10-feature model. Results: AKI occurred in 686 of 2,477 patients (27.7%) in the development cohort. A parsimonious 10-feature CatBoost model demonstrated good discrimination, with an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) of 0.823 [95% confidence interval (CI): 0.779–0.863] in the internal test set. The difference from the 53-feature counterpart (AUC 0.811) was not statistically significant (paired ΔAUC 0.013, 95% CI: −0.007 to 0.033; DeLong P=0.21). The 10-feature model exceeded the Acute Physiology and Chronic Health Evaluation II (APACHE II) score (AUC 0.688) and baseline serum creatinine (AUC 0.735; both paired DeLong P<0.001). In the independent external validation cohort, the model's discrimination remained strong with an AUC of 0.767 (95% CI: 0.732–0.802). SHAP analysis identified blood urea nitrogen (BUN), total bilirubin, and urine output as key predictors, revealing clinically relevant non-linear relationships. Conclusions: We developed and externally validated a parsimonious and interpretable 10-feature ML model that predicts AKI in ARDS patients using routinely collected clinical data. By providing early risk stratification through a web-based tool, this model holds the potential to facilitate timely intervention of AKI.

items.title: Machine learning-based prediction of recurrence-free survival after microwave ablation in patients with lung cancer: a retrospective study
items.abstract: Background: Microwave ablation (MWA) is an effective treatment for selected patients with lung cancer; however, reliable tools for predicting recurrence-free survival (RFS) after MWA are lacking. This study aimed to develop and evaluate machine learning models for predicting RFS after MWA. Methods: We retrospectively included patients with lung cancer who underwent MWA at the Affiliated Hospital of Nantong University between January 2013 and January 2023. Structured and unstructured data extracted from electronic medical records were used for model development. Candidate predictors of RFS were identified by univariable Cox regression in the training set. Five models were developed using Cox regression, eXtreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost), random survival forest (RSF), gradient boosting machine (GBM), and support vector machine (SVM). Model performance was evaluated using time-dependent receiver operating characteristic curves, the area under the curve (AUC), the concordance index (C-index), and decision curve analysis (DCA). Results: A total of 100 patients were included, of whom 46 (46.0%) experienced recurrence. Among the five models, XGBoost achieved the highest C-index in the test set (0.856), with AUCs of 0.933, 0.855, and 0.891 for predicting 1-, 2-, and 3-year RFS, respectively. Conclusions: The XGBoost model showed good performance in predicting RFS after MWA in patients with lung cancer. Further external validation is warranted before clinical implementation.

items.title: Phenotype-guided individualized interventional bronchoscopy for benign central airway stenosis: a narrative review and proposed treatment algorithm
items.abstract: Background and Objective: Benign central airway stenosis (BCAS) arises from diverse etiologies and complex pathological mechanisms. Despite the availability of numerous interventional bronchoscopic modalities, standardized strategies based on the biophysical characteristics of the stenosis are lacking, and clinical decisions remain heavily experience-dependent. This review aimed to critically appraise the evidence on mainstream interventional techniques and to propose a phenotype-guided treatment framework. Methods: A targeted literature search of PubMed, Web of Science, and the China National Knowledge Infrastructure (CNKI) was performed from database inception to October 2025, limited to English-language publications. Search terms combined disease-specific and intervention-specific keywords. After screening, 51 references were selected. Key Content and Findings: Balloon dilation remains the cornerstone for simple annular cicatricial stenosis, whereas carbon dioxide (CO₂) laser is preferable for dense fibrous rings and argon plasma coagulation (APC) for superficial granulomatous lesions. Silicone stents are preferred when malacia or complex mixed stenosis requires temporary support. Low-temperature plasma and local drug injection are useful adjuncts. We identified that the most critical deficiency of existing studies is the failure to stratify patients by pathological phenotype—cicatricial, granulomatous, cartilaginous malacic, or mixed—rendering their conclusions difficult to generalize. Conclusions: Therapeutic success now depends on matching technique combinations to pathobiological phenotypes rather than on selecting a single "best" modality. We propose an individualized treatment decision framework grounded in precise pre-procedural phenotyping and outline future research directions, including a core outcome set (COS) and phenotype-stratified prospective trials.

items.title: Imaging-guided biopsy techniques for peripheral pulmonary lesions: a bibliometric study from 1977 to 2026
items.abstract: Background: Imaging-guided biopsy plays a central role in the tissue diagnosis of peripheral pulmonary lesions (PPLs). This study aims to map the global research landscape, identify dominant contributors, and characterize recently active research themes. Methods: Relevant publications from 1977 to April 2026 were retrieved from the Web of Science Core Collection. VOSviewer, CiteSpace, and the R package "bibliometrix" were used for network visualization, cluster analysis, and trend mapping. Results: A total of 1,181 original articles from 48 countries published in 282 journals were analyzed. The annual output accelerated after 2014, peaking at 110 articles in 2025. China, the United States, and Japan led in productivity, while the United States accumulated the highest total citations. Journal of Thoracic Disease was the most prolific journal and Chest accumulated the most citations. Keyword co-occurrence analysis identified four thematic clusters covering bronchoscopic navigation, percutaneous biopsy and complications, oncologic management, and preoperative localization. Burst analysis revealed that radial endobronchial ultrasound, diagnostic yield, safety, and transthoracic needle biopsy are the most bibliometrically active recent topics. Conclusions: Imaging-guided biopsy research for PPLs has expanded from foundational technique description to additionally encompass navigation-based precision, harmonized outcome reporting, and integrated diagnostic-therapeutic workflows, with bronchoscopic, percutaneous, oncologic, and localization themes persisting concurrently rather than replacing one another. As bibliometric findings describe research activity rather than comparative clinical performance, they offer a hypothesis-generating reference framework for future research rather than evidence of clinical superiority.

items.title: How to manage residual aortic regurgitation at aortic valve-sparing operation: consideration for aortic reclamping
Week-1 blood counts for early risk stratification of grade 3–4 neutropenia during concurrent chemoradiotherapy for stage III non-small cell lung cancer
items.abstract: Background: Concurrent chemoradiotherapy (CCRT) for locally advanced non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) frequently causes myelosuppression, and grade 3–4 neutropenia often forces treatment interruption or dose reduction. Risk prediction in this setting has largely relied on pre-treatment information. We examined whether risk could be screened from end-of-week-1 data. Methods: We retrospectively studied 237 patients with stage III NSCLC given platinum-based CCRT at a single institution. The endpoint was grade 3–4 neutropenia [Common Terminology Criteria for Adverse Events (CTCAE) v5.0], an absolute neutrophil count nadir below 1,000/µL during weeks 2–6. Risk was estimated by L2-penalized logistic regression on eight variables—five week-1 blood counts, age, sex and the prescribed radiotherapy dose—with performance assessed by internal cross-validation. Neutrophil and monocyte trajectories were compared by paired nadir timing and by the fall from each patient's own baseline. Results: Grade 3–4 neutropenia occurred in 48 patients (20.3%). The area under the curve was 0.673 (95% confidence interval: 0.593–0.753) with good calibration (slope 0.978, Brier 0.153), exceeding the same model refitted with pre-treatment instead of week-1 blood counts (0.590; DeLong P=0.03). Week-1 neutrophil, platelet and monocyte counts were the strongest predictors, though the neutrophil count read alone discriminated as well (0.688; DeLong P=0.64). The monocyte nadir preceded the neutrophil nadir by a median of 6 days (P<0.001), the monocyte count having already fallen further by week 1 (69% versus 88% of baseline, P<0.001). The upper tertile of predicted risk carried a 31.6% event rate against 14.6% in the lower two tertiles (negative predictive value 0.854), but on decision-curve analysis the confidence bands did not separate the model from both reference strategies at any single threshold. Conclusions: Blood counts at the end of week 1 carry information about the eventual nadir that pre-treatment counts do not, and the monocyte lineage supplies its timing. The landmark model turns this into a calibrated absolute risk rather than better discrimination; its high negative predictive value defines a low-risk group in which reduced monitoring—and with it the burden of repeated blood sampling—could be tested prospectively. External validation is warranted.

Factors associated with adherence to inhaled medications in patients with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease: a systematic review and meta-analysis
items.abstract: Background: Poor adherence to inhaled medications remains a major barrier to effective disease control in chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD). We conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis to identify factors associated with adherence to inhaled medications in patients with COPD and to summarise adherence levels reported in the included studies. Methods: PubMed, Embase, the Cochrane Library, and Web of Science were systematically searched from database inception to 21 August 2025. Observational studies enrolling adults with COPD receiving maintenance inhaled therapy were eligible. We performed meta-analyses of factors associated with poor adherence and a secondary pooled analysis of study-defined adherence among the included studies. For associated factors, categorical variables were summarised as odds ratios (ORs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs), and continuous variables were summarised as weighted mean differences (WMDs). Study selection, data extraction, and quality assessment were performed independently by two reviewers. This study was prospectively registered in PROSPERO (CRD420251130295). Results: A total of 35 studies were included. The adherence-level analysis included 34 studies and 167,062 participants, and the associated-factor analysis included 35 studies and 266,211 participants. In the secondary descriptive synthesis, 45% (95% CI: 38–52%) of patients were classified as adherent according to study-defined criteria, with substantial heterogeneity. When poor adherence was used as the outcome, lower odds of poor adherence were observed for age ≥65 years (overall OR =0.60, 95% CI: 0.41–0.89), former smoking (overall OR =0.73, 95% CI: 0.54–0.98), use of two or more inhaled medications (unadjusted OR =0.71, 95% CI: 0.61–0.83), and a history of hospitalisation (unadjusted OR =0.81, 95% CI: 0.75–0.89). Higher odds of poor adherence were observed for female sex (overall OR =1.15, 95% CI: 1.06–1.25), living alone (unadjusted OR =1.28, 95% CI: 1.19–1.38), depression (overall OR =1.33, 95% CI: 1.19–1.49), and COPD Assessment Test (CAT) score ≥10 (unadjusted OR =1.59, 95% CI: 1.03–2.44). In contrast, no significant associations were found for body mass index (BMI), marital status, income level, employment status, comorbidity, polypharmacy, acute exacerbation history, modified Medical Research Council (mMRC) grade, or current smoking. Substantial heterogeneity was observed in the adherence-level analysis and in many factor-specific analyses; therefore, these findings should be interpreted cautiously. Conclusions: Adherence to inhaled medications was frequently suboptimal across the included studies. Several sociodemographic, clinical, and lifestyle-related factors were associated with better or poorer adherence, but some associations were sensitive to the omission of individual studies. Given the observational designs, substantial heterogeneity, and residual confounding, these findings should be interpreted as hypothesis-generating rather than causal or predictive.
