items.title: Thoracoscopic N3-station lymphadenectomy following multimodal conversion therapy in highly selected cN3 non-small cell lung cancer: a single-institution retrospective study
items.abstract: Background: Clinical stage III (cN3) non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) is traditionally considered unresectable, and data on surgical management after modern systemic therapy remain scarce. This study describes our experience with thoracoscopic N3-station lymphadenectomy following multimodal conversion therapy in highly selected patients. Methods: We retrospectively reviewed six highly selected patients with histologically confirmed, clinically staged cN3 (stage IIIB–IIIC, M0) NSCLC treated at a single institution between December 2019 and December 2023. All received conversion therapy—defined as systemic treatment intended to render initially unresectable disease operable, with surgery considered only after treatment response was demonstrated. Clinical N3 disease was established by contrast-enhanced computed tomography (CT) and positron emission tomography-CT (PET-CT). As a descriptive study, no inferential statistics were performed; continuous data are reported as median (range). Results: The cohort included four males and two females (median age, 64.5 years). Four received chemoimmunotherapy and two received targeted therapy; all achieved a partial response by Response Evaluation Criteria in Solid Tumors (RECIST) v1.1. All patients underwent lobectomy [five uniportal video-assisted thoracoscopic surgery (VATS), one converted to thoracotomy for severe adhesions] with R0 resection achieved in all. Median operative time was 359 minutes, median estimated blood loss was 450 mL, and a median of 18 lymph nodes were removed. One intraoperative adverse event occurred (injury to the superior vena cava-innominate vein junction during station 2R dissection, repaired by suture with 1,000 mL blood loss). One postoperative complication (pulmonary infection, Clavien-Dindo grade II) occurred. Pathologically, one patient achieved a complete pathological response (pCR) and three achieved a major pathological response (MPR); the single patient with residual viable tumor in an originally involved N3 station (ypN3) remains disease-free. At a median follow-up of 21 months, five patients were alive without progression and one was alive with progression; no deaths occurred. Conclusions: In this small, highly selected cohort, thoracoscopic N3-station lymphadenectomy following multimodal conversion therapy was technically feasible with acceptable perioperative outcomes. However, these descriptive findings do not establish general safety or any survival benefit. Larger prospective studies with appropriate control groups are warranted to define the role of surgery in this traditionally unresectable population.

items.title: Prognostic value of baseline CT-derived fibrosis score in idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis: relationship with functional decline and the GAP index
items.abstract: Background: Chest computed tomography (CT)-derived fibrosis score has shown prognostic significance in idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF); however, whether it provides incremental prognostic value beyond conventional measures such as the Gender-Age-Physiology (GAP) index remains uncertain. We evaluated whether baseline fibrosis score predicts rapid forced vital capacity (FVC) decline and mortality, and whether its integration into the GAP index improves prognostic discrimination. Methods: In this retrospective cohort of 112 IPF patients, fibrosis score was obtained using automated CT texture analysis. Rapid decliners were patients with a relative FVC decline >10% predicted within any 1-year interval. Cox proportional hazards regression with landmark analysis and logistic regression assessed the association of fibrosis score and rapid decliner status with mortality. Four models were compared using Harrell’s C-index and time-dependent area under the curve (TD-AUC). Results: Over a median follow-up of 3.91 years, 29 patients (25.9%) died. Fibrosis score was independently associated with increased mortality [hazard ratio (HR) 1.07 per 1-percentage-point increase, 95% confidence interval (CI): 1.02–1.13, P=0.003] but not with rapid decliner status, nor was rapid decliner status associated with mortality. A fibrosis score ≥4.5% conferred substantially higher mortality risk (HR 8.13, 95% CI: 1.92–34.40; log-rank P<0.001). Adding the fibrosis score to the GAP index did not significantly increase the C-index, but the model with continuous fibrosis score showed a higher 5-year TD-AUC than the GAP index alone (0.72 vs. 0.63, P=0.02). Conclusions: In patients with IPF, the CT-derived fibrosis score was independently associated with all-cause mortality. Although adding the fibrosis score to the GAP index did not significantly improve overall discrimination, it improved discrimination for 5-year mortality, suggesting a potential role in long-term risk stratification that warrants validation in larger cohorts.

items.title: Anxiety and other psychological outcomes in patients with pectus excavatum: a systematic review
items.abstract: Background: Pectus excavatum (PE) is the most common congenital chest wall deformity and has been increasingly associated with adverse psychological outcomes. However, anxiety-related symptoms and other psychological manifestations in PE have not been comprehensively synthesized. This systematic review aimed to summarize the available evidence regarding anxiety-related and other psychological outcomes in individuals with PE. Methods: PubMed, Scopus, and EMBASE were searched from database inception through August 2026 according to the PRISMA 2020 Statement. Original clinical studies evaluating anxiety or related psychological outcomes in patients with PE were eligible. Methodological quality and risk of bias were assessed using the National Institutes of Health (NIH) Quality Assessment Tool for observational studies and the Cochrane Risk of Bias 2 (RoB 2) tool for randomized controlled trials. Owing to substantial methodological heterogeneity, a qualitative synthesis was performed; categorical prevalence estimates were summarized descriptively, while weighted summaries were calculated only for sufficiently comparable continuous outcomes. Results: Seventeen studies including 1,695 participants were included, predominantly adolescents and young adults. Most studies exclusively enrolled patients with PE, whereas two included mixed PE/pectus carinatum (PC) cohorts. Anxiety-related prevalence estimates ranged from 32.0% to 65.0%, while depression-related estimates ranged from 7.0% to 65.0%; these values reflected heterogeneous constructs, instruments, and thresholds and were therefore not pooled. Weighted baseline State-Trait Anxiety Inventory (STAI) scores were 40.8 for state anxiety and 35.6 for trait anxiety. Anxiety-related manifestations were frequently reported alongside impaired body image, reduced self-esteem, diminished self-efficacy, psychological distress, and lower health-related quality of life. Uncontrolled longitudinal studies reported improvements in several psychological outcomes following minimally invasive repair of pectus excavatum (MIRPE), although causal attribution to surgery cannot be established. Overall methodological quality ranged from poor to good, with most studies rated as fair or good. Conclusions: Patients with PE, predominantly evaluated in tertiary or surgical settings, experience a substantial multidimensional psychological burden in which anxiety-related manifestations are frequently reported. Psychological assessment should be considered as part of multidisciplinary care, although generalizability to milder or incidentally identified PE remains uncertain. Future prospective studies using standardized psychological assessments are needed to clarify relationships among thoracic morphology, clinical characteristics, and psychological well-being.

Comparison of invasive mechanical ventilation and noninvasive mechanical ventilation in patients with acute heart failure: a retrospective study
items.abstract: Background: In patients with acute heart failure (AHF) exhibiting hypoxia or respiratory distress, mechanical ventilation is often required, yet the relative efficacy of noninvasive compared to invasive ventilation remains unclear. This study was designed to compare the clinical outcomes of noninvasive mechanical ventilation (NIV) with those of invasive mechanical ventilation (IMV) in patients with AHF and symptoms of hypoxia or respiratory distress. Methods: A retrospective analysis was performed on patients admitted to Nanjing First Hospital between 2020 and 2022. The primary outcome was in-hospital mortality, while secondary outcomes included the length of hospital stay, the duration of mechanical ventilation, N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide (NT-proBNP) level, and blood gas parameters. Results: After propensity score matching, each cohort included 81 patients. The IMV group exhibited a significantly higher in-hospital mortality rate as compared with the NIV group (43.21% vs. 27.16%, P=0.03). Conditional logistic regression analysis further revealed that the risk of mortality for the IMV group was 1.93-fold greater than that of the NIV group [odds ratio (OR) =1.93; 95% confidence interval (CI): 1.01–3.68; P=0.046]; moreover, the IMV group had a longer hospital stay (13 vs. 10 days, P=0.03). Generalized estimating equations (GEE) analysis indicated significant differences in partial pressure of oxygen in arterial blood (PaO 2 ) levels between the groups (P<0.001) and over time (P<0.001). Conclusion: Although IMV is associated with enhanced oxygenation, it may be linked to prolonged hospitalization and increased mortality rates relative to NIV. The results of this study highlight the importance of careful monitoring and the timely adjustment of ventilator settings as a means of improving the clinical outcomes of patients treated with IMV.

items.title: Deformation of pulmonary tissue and ribs between supine and left lateral decubitus positions: a cross-sectional analysis using high-resolution computed tomography and 3D reconstruction
items.abstract: Background: Accurate localization of pulmonary nodules is critical for the safety and precision of video-assisted thoracoscopic surgery (VATS). Preoperative computed tomography (CT)-guided localization is routinely performed in the supine position, while most thoracic surgeries are conducted in the lateral decubitus position. Changes in body position induce relative deformation between pulmonary tissue and the rib cage, which shifts the relative position of nodules to bony landmarks, reducing localization accuracy and necessitating repeated intraoperative CT scans with increased radiation exposure and procedural risks. Existing deformation studies predominantly use internal deep structures as registration anchors, which are not directly compatible with transthoracic needle localization that relies on external rib landmarks. This study aimed to quantify the relationship between lung tissue deformation and rib displacement during the transition from supine to left lateral decubitus position using high-resolution CT and three-dimensional (3D) reconstruction, to provide an anatomical basis for clinical localization correction. Methods: Eleven eligible healthy male volunteers underwent high-resolution CT scans in both supine and left lateral decubitus positions, with a 10-cm axillary cushion applied in the lateral position to replicate the surgical setup. All scans were acquired at end-full-inspiration using identical protocols. Lung lobe volumes and two-dimensional (2D) morphological parameters were measured via 3D reconstruction software. Simulated 10-mm pulmonary nodules were placed at subsegmental broncho-vascular bifurcations, evenly distributed across the upper, middle and lower lobes. Five key coordinate points were defined along the central axis of each adjacent rib, and distances from nodule centroids to each reference point were calculated. Paired t-tests were used for comparison, with normality testing and nonparametric sensitivity analysis performed. Results: Compared with the supine position, total right lung volume increased significantly in the left lateral decubitus position (2,653.03±604.18 mL vs. 2,930.43±507.67 mL, 95% confidence interval (CI): 66.47–488.33 mL, P=0.01). The right lower lobe showed the largest volumetric increase (P=0.01), while no significant change was found in the right middle lobe (P=0.25). Lung height and hemidiaphragmatic height increased significantly. The relative distance change between simulated nodules and adjacent ribs was less than 13 mm in the upper and middle lobes, but reached a maximum of 27 mm in the lower lobe (P<0.001). Conclusions: Transition from supine to left lateral decubitus position causes significant changes in lung volumes and morphology, especially in the right lower lobe. The deformation relationship between pulmonary tissue and ribs is relatively consistent in the upper and middle lobes, but differs substantially in the lower lobe. These findings provide preliminary anatomical baseline data for developing position correction models for pulmonary nodule localization, and clinical applicability requires further validation.

items.title: Longitudinal hemodynamic and clinical outcomes after sutureless vs. transcatheter aortic valve replacement in septuagenarians: a propensity-weighted study
items.abstract: Background: The expansion of transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) into younger, lower-risk patients has raised concerns regarding long-term durability, while the advent of sutureless aortic valve (AV) prostheses underscores the need for comparative evidence to define the optimal bioprosthetic strategy in patients with longer life expectancy. Given the paucity of direct comparative data in septuagenarians, we sought to assess the relative clinical and longitudinal hemodynamic outcomes of these two treatment strategies. Methods: We retrospectively analyzed 210 patients aged 70–79 years with severe aortic stenosis (AS) who underwent either sutureless AV replacement (SAVR) (n=94) or TAVI (n=116) between 2015 and 2021. Longitudinal echocardiographic and clinical outcomes were evaluated. Hemodynamic trajectories were analyzed using mixed-effects models, and clinical outcomes were compared using Cox and Fine-Gray competing-risk models. Propensity score (PS)-based inverse probability of treatment weighting (IPTW) was applied to mitigate selection bias. Results: Rates of early adverse events, including mortality, permanent pacemaker (PPM) implantation, and myocardial infarction (MI), were comparable between the SAVR and TAVI groups. During a median follow-up duration of 36.7 months [interquartile range (IQR), 17.8–52.3 months], SAVR demonstrated more favorable longitudinal hemodynamic performance, with divergent transvalvular pressure gradient trajectories compared with TAVI (group-by-time interaction, P=0.007). Paravalvular leakage (PVL; ≥ moderate) occurred exclusively in the TAVI group (12.7% at 5 years). Although overall survival did not differ between the groups, fewer strokes occurred after SAVR than after TAVI [2 vs. 7 events; adjusted hazard ratio (HR), 5.47; 95% confidence interval (CI): 1.46–20.46; P=0.01]. The risk of other valve-related adverse events did not differ significantly. Conclusions: In septuagenarian patients with severe AS, SAVR was associated with more favorable longitudinal hemodynamics and fewer observed strokes than TAVI, with comparable survival.

items.title: Rib-space counts for practical ultrasound estimation of pleural effusion volume: a brief report
items.abstract: Thoracic ultrasonography is standard of care for evaluating pleural effusions. Existing approaches to estimate effusion volume via ultrasound have relied on anatomic measurement-based formulas; however, these formulas have not been incorporated into routine clinical practice. We hypothesized that counting the vertical rib spaces occupied by pleural effusion on ultrasound, or "rib-space counts," are a practical and accurate alternative method of assessing pleural effusion volume. Patients with free-flowing, non-septated pleural effusions and complete pleural space evacuation by thoracentesis were enrolled from a prospective, multicenter study. Complete pleural space evacuation was defined as no effusion identified by two blinded radiologists on chest X-ray (CXR) images and no effusion identified on anterior, mid-axillary, and posterior, post-drainage ultrasound views by two blinded pulmonologists. Drained effusion volumes were compared with pre-procedural upright thoracic ultrasound assessments for volume estimation by two methods: (I) the number of vertical rib interspaces (height) occupied by fluid and (II) effusion volume measurement using the Goecke-2 formula. Multivariable linear regression models were used to examine the association between rib-space count and effusion volume, adjusting for age and sex. A total of 257 ultrasound images and 45 post-procedural CXR images were obtained in 45 patients with complete pleural space evacuation and included for analysis. Rib-space count demonstrated a strong correlation with effusion volume, with significant variation observed by sex and ultrasound view. Rib-space counts performed similarly to Goecke-derived estimates across all views, with optimal performance in the anterior view. Notably, anterior rib-space counts corresponded to higher total volume estimates compared with equivalent mid-axillary and posterior counts, with differences influenced by sex. Rib-space counts are a simple and accurate method for pleural effusion volume estimation and are a candidate for integration into a standardized thoracic ultrasound evaluation.

Biportal video-assisted thoracoscopic surgery for stage III tuberculous empyema involving the costodiaphragmatic recess: a single-center retrospective cohort study
items.abstract: Background: Biportal video-assisted thoracoscopic surgery (VATS) for stage III tuberculous empyema (TE) involving the costophrenic angle remains understudied. We aimed to describe its feasibility, perioperative outcomes, and pulmonary-function and radiographic findings. Methods: We retrospectively reviewed 51 patients who underwent biportal VATS decortication at Wuhan Jinyintan Hospital between January 2019 and January 2022. Pulmonary-function measurements obtained before surgery, at the first postoperative follow-up (1–3 months after surgery), and at 1 year were analysed as paired observations. Results: There were no conversions to thoracotomy, rib resections, or perioperative deaths. Mean operative time was 3.7±1.4 hours, median blood loss was 354 mL (range, 250–825 mL), and one patient underwent thoracoscopic reoperation for haemostasis. Prolonged air leak (>5 days) occurred in 39 of 51 patients (76.5%). Median postoperative hospital stay was 8 days (range, 7–12 days), and median chest tube duration was 21 days (range, 17–25 days). In 51 paired observations, forced expiratory volume in 1 second (FEV1) increased by 20.3 percentage points [95% confidence interval (CI): 18.6–22.1; P<0.0001] at the first postoperative follow-up and by 27.1 percentage points (95% CI: 25.3–28.8; P<0.0001) at 1 year. Forced vital capacity (FVC) increased by 20.0 percentage points (95% CI: 18.0–22.0; P<0.0001) and 26.8 percentage points (95% CI: 24.8–28.8; P<0.0001), respectively. Conclusions: In this single-centre retrospective case series, biportal VATS with port-role switching was technically feasible for stage III TE involving the costophrenic angle. The observed pulmonary-function improvements should be interpreted without claims of superiority because the study had no concurrent control group.

items.title: Surgical management of non-small cell lung cancer with single-station N2 disease: a nationwide cohort analysis
items.abstract: Background: The role of surgery in single-station N2 (ssN2) disease non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) is expanding in the era of immunotherapy. We aimed to describe national trends in the utilization of surgery and identify factors associated with surgery utilization for this patient population. Methods: We performed a retrospective cohort analysis of 8,659 clinical ssN2 patients in the National Cancer Database (NCDB) treated between 2004 to 2022. We tested for a trend in surgery utilization using the Jonckheere-Terpstra test and subsequently built a hierarchical logistic regression model to identify demographic, facility, or tumor factors associated with surgery. Results: The minority of ssN2 received surgery (43.3%; n=3,750/8,659). This rate increased over the time frame of the study (38.6% in 2004 up to 68.5% in 2022; P<0.007). After adjusting for tumor, patient, and structural characteristics including treating facility, patients were more likely to receive surgery if they were younger than 60 years {odds ratio (OR) 0.533 [95% confidence interval (CI): 0.405–0.700]; P<0.001}, female [1.144 (1.016–1.288); P=0.03], traveled more than 5 miles to the treating facility [1.168 (1.001–1.362); P=0.049], were in the top two income quartiles [1.363 (1.086–1.710); P=0.007], had histology other than squamous cell carcinoma [1.313 (1.018–1.693); P=0.04], or did not receive immunotherapy [0.26 (0.195–0.346); P<0.001]. Kaplan-Meier curves showed that surgery may be associated with long term survival when included in the treatment paradigm, with the best survival observed in patients who received both surgery and immunotherapy. Conclusions: Although utilization of surgery in the ssN2 population seems to be rising, disparities remain. Our retrospective cohort analysis of NCDB data suggests surgery may be associated with improved long-term survival; additional studies should aim to understand how to improve utilization.

items.title: Two-lung ventilation combined with carbon dioxide artificial pneumothorax in thoracoscopic surgery: a narrative review
items.abstract: Background and Objective: Adequate lung collapse is essential for visualization in thoracoscopic procedures. Although one-lung ventilation (OLV) using a double-lumen endotracheal tube remains the standard technique, it has several limitations. Two-lung ventilation (TLV) combined with carbon dioxide (CO2) artificial pneumothorax has emerged as an alternative in minimally invasive thoracic surgery. Existing studies lack comprehensive, stratified integration across adult, pediatric and various thoracic procedures, and no narrative overview has systematically summarized its systemic effects or long-term oncological prognosis. This review systematically summarizes the clinical application, physiological impacts, insufflation pressure protocols, and short- and long-term outcomes of TLV with CO2 artificial pneumothorax in thoracoscopic surgery, providing intraoperative management references for anesthesiologists and thoracic surgeons. Methods: This review synthesizes evidence from PubMed, EMBASE, Cochrane Library, Web of Science and Wanfang databases up to October 2nd, 2026, focusing on clinical studies evaluating TLV with CO2 artificial pneumothorax across thoracic procedures. Key Content and Findings: Compared with OLV, TLV with CO2 artificial pneumothorax demonstrates advantages including simplified airway management, reduced airway trauma, enhanced intraoperative oxygenation stability, and potential attenuation of the systemic inflammatory response. However, CO2 insufflation induces physiological alterations: elevated intrapleural pressure compromises hemodynamic stability, while transpleural CO2 absorption contributes to respiratory acidosis and hypercapnia; these changes may affect coagulation and cerebral hemodynamics. Pediatric applications warrant carefully regulated insufflation parameters and rigorous monitoring, particularly regarding cerebral oxygenation. Conclusions: TLV combined with low-pressure CO2 artificial pneumothorax appears to be a safe and feasible alternative ventilation mode for carefully selected patients, with advantages in airway protection and intraoperative oxygenation maintenance. Clinicians should adopt individualized insufflation pressure schemes according to operation type and patient age. Given the predominantly retrospective and heterogeneous nature of the available evidence, multicenter randomized controlled trials are required to formulate unified intraoperative monitoring standards and to explore the long-term pulmonary and oncological outcomes of this technique.

items.title: Durability of minimally invasive degenerative mitral repair: does mild residual mitral regurgitation matter?
items.abstract: Background: Mild residual mitral regurgitation (MR) after minimally invasive degenerative mitral valve repair remains a frequent clinical dilemma. The prognostic significance of residual mild MR is unclear, with limited long-term data. This study evaluated the long-term clinical and echocardiographic outcomes of patients with mild residual MR after minimally invasive mitral repair. Methods: We retrospectively reviewed the data of patients who underwent minimally invasive degenerative mitral valve repair via right mini-thoracotomy between October 2008 and June 2025. We compared patients who had mild residual MR on intraoperative transesophageal echocardiography (TEE) after mitral valve repair with those who had trivial or no residual MR. The primary endpoint was recurrence, defined as moderate-or-greater MR or mitral valve reoperation. Death was treated as a competing event, and cumulative incidence functions were compared using Gray's test. Secondary endpoints included overall survival (OS) and event-free survival (EFS), analyzed using Kaplan-Meier methods. Cox proportional hazards models were used to identify independent predictors of recurrence. Results: Baseline characteristics were comparable between the two groups. Patients in mild residual MR group had a higher prevalence of anterior leaflet involvement and longer cardiopulmonary bypass (CPB) and aortic cross-clamp (ACC) times, suggesting greater operative complexity. During follow-up, recurrence accumulated gradually in both groups, and no significant difference was observed in cumulative incidence of recurrence between two groups (Gray's test, P=0.25). Kaplan-Meier analysis showed no significant differences in OS or EFS between the two groups. In multivariable Cox regression, larger left atrial (LA) size [hazard ratio (HR) 1.05, 95% confidence interval (CI): 1.01–1.08, P=0.01], and anterior leaflet pathology (HR 2.18, 95% CI:1.09–4.37, P=0.03), and use of an Alfieri stitch (HR 6.03, 95% CI:1.70–21.40, P=0.005) were independently associated with recurrence, whereas mild residual MR was not. Conclusions: Mild residual MR after minimally invasive degenerative mitral repair was uncommon and was not significantly associated with recurrent moderate-or-greater MR or mitral valve reoperation during long-term follow-up. Most patients remained free from clinically significant MR progression during long-term follow-up, suggesting that although complete elimination of MR remains the surgical goal, routine immediate re-intervention for mild residual MR may not always be necessary. However, given the small number of patients with mild residual MR and the limited number of events, a clinically meaningful increase in recurrence risk cannot be excluded.
