Dual versus single chest drainage after uniportal video-assisted thoracoscopic lower lobectomy or lower-lobe segmentectomy: a retrospective cohort study
items.abstract: Background: Uniportal video-assisted thoracoscopic surgery (U-VATS) commonly uses a single apically directed chest tube after anatomic pulmonary resection, but this route may be less effective for dependent basal fluid evacuation. This study evaluated whether adding a basal pigtail catheter was associated with less residual pleural effusion after lower-lobe anatomic resection. Methods: This retrospective cohort study included adults with pulmonary malignancy who underwent U-VATS lower lobectomy or lower-lobe segmentectomy between January 2024 and April 2026. Patients received either a single chest tube or a chest tube plus a basal pigtail catheter. The primary outcome was moderate-to-large radiographic residual pleural effusion at 1 month. Secondary outcomes included radiographic, drainage-related, inflammatory, infectious, and pain outcomes, clinical events, and patient-reported symptoms. Available 3- and 6-month computed tomography (CT) scans were reviewed in exploratory analyses. Results: Among 164 patients, 107 were in the single chest tube group and 57 in the combined drainage group. Moderate-to-large radiographic residual pleural effusion at 1 month occurred in 24.3% and 5.3%, respectively (P=0.002). In multivariable logistic regression, combined drainage remained associated with lower odds of the primary outcome [adjusted odds ratio (OR), 0.13; 95% confidence interval (CI): 0.04–0.47; Wald P=0.002]. The concurrent-period estimate was imprecise and nonsignificant (OR, 0.21; 95% CI: 0.02–1.88; Wald P=0.16). In exploratory subgroup analysis, the association was statistically significant after lower lobectomy (OR, 0.09; 95% CI: 0.02–0.42; Wald P=0.002) but not segmentectomy. The drainage strategy-by-procedure interaction was not significant (P=0.24). Combined drainage had greater cumulative drainage volume [median (interquartile range), 950 (640–1,350) vs. 340 (165–455) mL; P<0.001], longer time to removal of the last drain [5 (4–7) vs. 2 (2–3) days; P<0.001], and longer postoperative hospital stay [6 (5–7) vs. 3 (3–4) days; P<0.001]. One-month symptom scores did not differ significantly between groups. Three single-tube patients were readmitted for pleural effusion and underwent repeat drainage at approximately 3 months; none were identified in the combined group. Among patients with available CT, scores ≥2 occurred in 4/35 versus 12/52 at 3 months (P=0.26) and 0/26 versus 4/65 at 6 months (P=0.58), respectively (combined vs. single). Conclusions: Among patients undergoing U-VATS lower-lobe anatomic pulmonary resection, combined drainage was associated with a lower incidence of moderate-to-large radiographic residual pleural effusion at 1 month, but also associated with longer tube duration and hospital stay. A net patient-centered benefit was not demonstrated, and the independent contribution of basal catheter positioning remains uncertain. Prospective studies comparing combined drainage with optimized single-drain strategies are needed.

items.title: Three sequential implementation eras of robotic-assisted bronchoscopy at an academic interventional pulmonology program: Monarch™, Galaxy™, and Ion™—a retrospective cohort analysis
items.abstract: Background: Three robotic-assisted bronchoscopy (RAB) platforms are available at academic centers across the United States: the Monarch™ system [Johnson & Johnson MedTech (Auris Health), Redwood City, CA], the Galaxy™ system (Noah Medical, San Carlos, CA), and the Ion™ Endoluminal System (Intuitive Surgical, Sunnyvale, CA). Real-world comparative performance data among all three systems are lacking. We compared strict diagnostic yield and safety across three sequential platform eras at one center and examined factors associated with yield. Methods: We conducted a retrospective single-center cohort study at the University of Southern California Keck Medical Center of consecutively enrolled adults who underwent RAB for pulmonary lesion evaluation during each platform’s operational phase. The primary outcome was strict diagnostic yield, defined by the American Thoracic Society/American College of Chest Physicians (ATS/ACCP) Delphi consensus and analyzed with multivariable logistic regression. Secondary endpoints included pneumothorax rate, bleeding (Nashville scale), and biopsy tool performance. A dedicated analysis examined characteristics of non-diagnostic cases. Results: Between July 2022 and January 2026, 270 patients underwent RAB procedures in which 297 lesions were biopsied: Monarch™ (90 patients, 92 lesions), Galaxy™ (90 patients, 94 lesions), and Ion™ (90 patients, 111 lesions). Median lesion size was 22, 21, and 18 mm, respectively (P=0.007), and a bronchus sign was present in 78.3% (72/92), 59.6% (56/94), and 43.2% (48/111) of lesions (P<0.001). The 1.1-mm cryoprobe was used in 2.2%, 33.0%, and 99.1% of lesions, with per-tool diagnostic yields of 0% (0/2), 80.6% (25/31), and 91.8% (101/110). Mobile cone-beam computed tomography (mCBCT) was used in 66.7% (74/111) of Ion™ lesions. Strict diagnostic yield was 56.5% [52/92; 95% confidence interval (CI): 46.3–66.2%] for Monarch™, 68.1% (64/94; 95% CI: 58.1–76.6%) for Galaxy™, and 91.9% (102/111; 95% CI: 85.3–95.7%) for Ion™ (P<0.001). After adjustment, platform was not independently associated with yield (P=0.32), whereas cryoprobe use [adjusted odds ratio (aOR) 5.57; 95% CI: 1.67–18.62] and a bronchus sign (aOR 2.30; 95% CI: 1.18–4.50) were. Pneumothorax occurred in 1.1% (Monarch™; 1/92), 12.8% (Galaxy™; 12/94), and 1.8% (Ion™; 2/111) of lesions (P<0.001). Conclusions: Strict diagnostic yield increased across three sequential robotic platform eras even as target lesions became smaller and less often had a bronchus sign, although the platform itself was not independently associated with yield. Cryoprobe adoption, intraprocedural imaging, and operator experience changed in step with the platform, so their separate contributions cannot be isolated in this design.

items.title: Narrative review of open repair of acute type A aortic dissection: rethinking extended aortic arch repair in acute aortic syndrome
items.abstract: Background and Objective: The extant literature addresses all available evidence on the distinctive features of a group of three life-threatening acute aortic pathologies gathered under the name of acute aortic syndrome (AAS). It has been demonstrated that the epidemiology, diagnostic strategy and management of these patients are inherently complex. The goal of this literature review is to provide a timely overview of surgical interventions for patients with acute type A aortic dissection (ATAAD). Specifically, it will focus on aortic arch involvement in the context of the surgical management of the ascending thoracic aorta in patients with AAS. Methods: A thorough search was conducted in MEDLINE, Embase, and the Cochrane Library using a combination of search terms related to acute aortic syndrome, acute aortic dissection, and type A acute aortic dissection. Key Content and Findings: The management of AAS is a complex process, and it becomes even more challenging in cases where surgical intervention on the arch of the aorta is necessary in the presence of ATAAD. Surgery for aortic arch is a developing field, with a variety of options. A growing body of research has identified the most effective approach for ATAAD in cases involving aortic arch. This is particularly crucial in cases where there is a high risk of malperfusion syndrome and repeated surgical intervention at the distal level. Conclusions: Recent guidelines have outlined key statements for the management of aortic arch in patients with ATAAD. These statements aim to guide healthcare professionals in selecting the optimal surgical option, which may involve supracoronary ascending replacement, valve-sparing root replacement, partial arch replacement, total arch replacement, or frozen elephant trunk (FET). Factors such as patient anatomy, entry location, and the expertise of the surgical team determine the selection of the most appropriate surgical approach. Achieving optimal outcomes necessitates tailoring the surgical approach according to the distinct characteristics of each patient population.

items.title: No cure yet, but some advances: future treatment outlook for idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis based on clinical trials
Characterization of cough patterns using an artificial intelligence-based automatic cough monitor in patients with asthma and interstitial lung disease
items.abstract: Background: Cough is a common symptom in respiratory diseases, but conventional assessment methods are time-consuming and primarily focus on cough frequency. We aimed to explore whether an artificial intelligence (AI)-based automatic smartphone cough monitoring system can provide detailed characterization of cough patterns in patients with asthma exacerbation and interstitial lung disease (ILD). Methods: We analyzed data from two prospective studies of cough measurement in patients with asthma and ILD. An AI-based smartphone cough monitoring system, CoughyTM, was applied using a smartphone and armband. Forty-five patients (24 with asthma exacerbation and 21 with ILD) were monitored during awake and sleep periods over 5–7 consecutive days. Cough events were quantified as cough frequency, epoch frequency, and coughs per epoch. Leicester Cough Questionnaire (LCQ) and cough symptom-visual analogue scale (CS-VAS) were collected using embedded questionnaire in the application, and baseline pulmonary function was measured. Results: Baseline CS-VAS scores were similar between patients with asthma exacerbation and those with ILD. Both cough frequency and epoch frequency demonstrated moderate to strong correlations with CS-VAS scores. The ILD group showed significantly higher awake cough frequency [median, 47.2 hr−1, interquartile range (IQR), 19.3–74.1 vs. 13.8 hr−1, IQR, 7.5–30.5, P=0.002] and awake epoch frequency (median, 14.5 hr−1, IQR, 8.7–24.6 vs. 5.5 hr−1, IQR, 3.3–12.1, P=0.001) than the asthma group. Coughs per epoch tended to be lower in patients with ILD, indicating fewer consecutive cough events per epoch. No significant differences were observed in sleep-time cough frequency. In the asthma group, cough frequency decreased with treatment, whereas it remained persistently high in ILD. Conclusions: The AI-based automatic cough monitoring application, CoughyTM, provided detailed cough data that enabled exploratory characterization of cough patterns and assessment of temporal changes in patients with asthma exacerbation and ILD. These findings suggest the potential utility of CoughyTM as a remote monitoring tool across respiratory diseases.

items.title: Blueprint for successful launch of a robotic bronchoscopy program
items.abstract: Background: Lung cancer remains the second most common cancer in the United States with the highest mortality rate of all cancers. The mainstay of decreasing mortality includes early detection and diagnosis, the latter of which robotic bronchoscopy helps facilitate, particularly for small peripheral pulmonary nodules where it demonstrates high yields and low rates of complications. However, the initial setup and implementation requires substantial investment of infrastructure, personnel training, and workflow optimization. In this manuscript, we present our data regarding the launch of a robotic bronchoscopy program in an academic tertiary care center and document our implementation timeline as well as provide a checklist for successful implementation. We further include data showing the efficacy of utilizing this technology Methods: We documented the implementation steps upon starting our robotic bronchoscopy program and performed a retrospective analysis from the launch period of patient data and nodule characteristics including lesion size and location, pathology and microbiology data, procedure length, and diagnostic yield. Results: We included robotic bronchoscopy cases performed during the first four months after implementation from January 2023 to May 2023. Start-up involved a collaborative group including an interventional pulmonary physician champion, four performing providers, a dedicated nurse navigator, cardiothoracic surgery, specialized respiratory therapists trained in bronchoscope management, endoscopy leadership, information technology (IT) integration, and radiology leadership. Average patient age was 69.4±10.1 years (median of 71 with range of 35 to 95 years of age) and 51% were female. 102 patient cases were reviewed with lesion mean size of 20.4±9.5 mm (median 19 mm with range of 5.0 to 50.0 mm). Sensitivity for malignancy was 85.5% with an overall diagnostic yield of 89.7%. Conclusions: Successful implementation of robotic bronchoscopy required a broad multidisciplinary team and resulted in a high procedural volume and an overall diagnostic yield of 89.7% during the first four months of use.

items.title: Prognostic association of the triglyceride-glucose-body mass index for postoperative major adverse cardiovascular events after rheumatic mitral valve surgery: a retrospective cohort study
items.abstract: Background: The prognostic relevance of metabolic markers in patients undergoing surgery for rheumatic mitral valve disease remains insufficiently characterized. This study aimed to examine the associations of the triglyceride-glucose index (TyG index) and the triglyceride-glucose-body mass index (TyG-BMI) with postoperative major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) and all-cause mortality in patients with rheumatic heart disease (RHD) undergoing mitral valve surgery. Methods: A retrospective cohort of 800 patients with RHD who underwent mitral valve repair or replacement at Beijing Anzhen Hospital (2016–2022) was analyzed. TyG and TyG-BMI were stratified by quartiles and upper quartiles; the cohort-specific upper-quartile cutoff for the primary categorical TyG-BMI analysis was 220.87. The primary outcome was postoperative MACE, defined as the first occurrence of heart-failure rehospitalization, stroke, valve dysfunction requiring intervention, or arrhythmia events recorded as severe; death was excluded from MACE and assessed separately as a secondary outcome. Cox regression, Kaplan-Meier curves, and restricted cubic spline (RCS) analysis were applied. Exploratory subgroup analyses included age strata (<70 vs. ≥70 years) determined before examination of subgroup results. Results: Higher TyG-BMI was associated with a higher MACE incidence (42.5% vs. 31.5%) and remained independently associated with MACE after multivariable adjustment [hazard ratio (HR)=1.98, 95% confidence interval (CI): 1.48–2.64, P<0.001]. RCS analysis suggested an approximately linear association, with no evidence of nonlinearity. No statistically significant effect modification by age or diabetes status was detected. In the fully adjusted model, TyG-BMI, but not TyG, was significantly associated with MACE. Conclusions: Higher preoperative TyG-BMI was independently associated with an increased risk of MACE in patients with RHD undergoing mitral valve surgery. TyG-BMI may therefore warrant further evaluation as a candidate prognostic marker. Prospective multicenter studies should assess its incremental value beyond TyG, body mass index (BMI), and established clinical risk factors.

items.title: Refining patient selection for immune checkpoint inhibitors in epidermal growth factor receptor-mutant non-small cell lung cancer after tyrosine kinase inhibitor resistance: a real-world analysis
items.abstract: Background: The role of immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) in epidermal growth factor receptor tyrosine kinase inhibitor (EGFR-TKI) resistant non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) remains unclear. Although recent trials suggest potential benefits of ICIs in this setting, optimal patient selection, treatment timing, and combination strategies remain poorly established. This real-world study aimed to evaluate the efficacy and safety of ICIs in EGFR-mutant NSCLC patients following EGFR-TKI resistance. Methods: We retrospectively analyzed 31 patients with advanced NSCLC harboring EGFR mutations who received ICI-based therapy after progression on EGFR-TKIs between 2020 and 2023. Clinical outcomes included progression-free survival (PFS), overall survival (OS), objective response rate (ORR), disease control rate (DCR), and treatment-related adverse events (TRAEs). Subgroup analyses were performed based on EGFR mutation subtype, T790M status, programmed death-ligand 1 (PD-L1) expression, metastatic sites, and treatment regimen. Results: The median PFS was 7.8 months [95% confidence interval (CI): 6.0‒9.5]. The ORR and DCR were 35.5% and 87.1%, respectively. Multivariate analysis identified liver metastases [hazard ratio (HR)=10.534, P=0.047], brain metastases (HR =20.348, P=0.01), presence of T790M mutation (HR =14.651, P=0.02), and EGFR mutation subtype (L858R associated with better PFS; HR =0.080, P=0.03) as significant prognostic factors. ICI combined with chemotherapy was associated with a more favorable PFS compared with other treatment strategies. No treatment-related deaths were reported; grade 3–4 TRAEs mainly included anemia and neutropenia. Conclusions: ICIs offer clinical benefit for EGFR-TKI-resistant patients, particularly those with L858R and without T790M, liver, or brain metastases. The ICI-chemotherapy combination appears more effective than monotherapy or triple regimens. Careful patient selection is warranted to refine immunotherapy strategies in this population.

items.title: Management of prolonged air leaks following pulmonary resection
items.abstract: An air leak is the escape of air from a disrupted lung parenchyma and visceral pleura into the pleural space after pulmonary resection. Air leaks are often seen after pulmonary resection, and most tend to resolve without needing many interventions, usually within 24 to 48 hours. But an air leak that persists for more than five postoperative days becomes a prolonged air leak (PAL) and generally requires further investigation. A PAL following pulmonary resection remains a major source of postoperative morbidity with an increased susceptibility to complications such as an empyema. Additionally, PAL inevitably leads to increased utilization of healthcare resources and a imposes a heavier cost on the overall healthcare system. This review article will provide an overview of the clinical relevance of PALs and aims to provide a stepwise management of PALs after a pulmonary resection. The current proposed management starts with optimization of the chest tube drainage system and a comparison between the traditional and digital drainage systems. It will then discuss one-way valve devices, with indications for when patients with a PAL should remain in the hospital, followed by different pleurodesis options, and endobronchial valves. Surgical re-intervention is relatively uncommon for uncomplicated PALs but general indications for re-intervention in patients with a complicated PALs will be discussed.

items.title: Surgical outcomes for primary malignant melanoma of the esophagus: a retrospective cohort study
items.abstract: Background: Primary malignant melanoma of the esophagus (PMME) is a rare and aggressive malignancy with limited evidence regarding treatment outcomes and prognostic factors. This study aimed to describe the clinicopathological characteristics, perioperative treatment patterns and survival outcomes of patients with locoregional PMME treated with curative-intent esophagectomy. Methods: Sixteen patients with locoregional PMME who underwent curative-intent esophagectomy at a single center between 2017 and 2024 were retrospectively analyzed. Clinicopathological characteristics, perioperative treatment, recurrence patterns, recurrence-free survival (RFS) and overall survival (OS) were analyzed. Survival outcomes were estimated using the Kaplan-Meier method, and restricted mean survival time (RMST) analyses were performed for selected stratifying factors. Results: The median age was 59 years, and 10 (62.5%) patients were male. Most tumors (81.3%) were located in the lower thoracic esophagus. Perioperative therapy was administered to 12 (75.0%) patients: 6 received neoadjuvant therapy, of whom 3 also received postoperative adjuvant therapy, and 6 underwent upfront surgery followed by adjuvant therapy. All patients achieved R0 resection, and no 90-day mortality was observed. After a median follow-up of 35.9 (interquartile range, 24.3–60.4) months, 8 recurrences occurred, of which 7 were distant recurrences. The 1-year OS was 81.2% [95% confidence interval (CI): 64.2–100%] and the 1-year RFS was 75.0% (95% CI: 56.5–99.5%), respectively; and the corresponding 3-year OS and RFS rates were 64.0% (95% CI: 42.5–96.2%) and 51.1% (95% CI: 30.3–86.4%). In exploratory stratified analyses, patients with pathological node-negative disease had longer OS than those with node-positive disease, with an RMST difference of 13.0 months (95% CI: 1.1–24.8; P=0.03). Patients with tumors ≤4.5 cm had longer RFS than those with tumors >4.5 cm, with an RMST difference of 12.8 months (95% CI: 3.1–22.4; P=0.01). Conclusions: Curative-intent esophagectomy for locoregional PMME was associated with acceptable perioperative safety and survival. Distant metastasis was the predominant pattern of recurrence. Exploratory analyses showed longer OS in patients with pathological node-negative disease and longer RFS in those with tumors ≤4.5 cm. These findings are hypothesis-generating and require further validation.

items.title: Comparative outcomes of surgical pleurectomy versus talc pleurodesis for malignant pleural effusion: a retrospective cohort study from a South African tertiary centre
items.abstract: Background: Malignant pleural effusion (MPE) is a significant burden for patients with advanced cancer and there is still much debate as to what the best way to manage this symptom is. The two most common treatments for MPE are surgical pleurectomy and talc pleurodesis, but there is a general lack of evidence demonstrating their relative effectiveness specifically amongst patients in Africa. The purpose of this study was to examine the efficacy, safety, and quality of life (QoL) outcomes of surgical pleurectomy versus talc pleurodesis amongst a large cohort in a real-world setting. Methods: A retrospective cohort study was conducted on 607 patients diagnosed with MPE, treated at the Dr. George Mukhari Academic Hospital in South Africa from 2019 to 2024. All patients’ management involved either surgical pleurectomy (n=239) or talc pleurodesis (n=368). The main outcome measure was the time to recurrence, which was analysed using Kaplan-Meier survival curves, log-rank tests and Cox proportional hazards regression. Secondary outcomes were the complication rate, functional and dyspnoea measures [Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status, Medical Research Council (MRC) dyspnoea score, Shuttle Walk Test, Karnofsky Performance Index], and length of hospital stay. Results: Recurrence occurred in 11.0% of the surgical group and 9.0% of the talc group [absolute risk difference 2.0%, 95% confidence interval (CI): −3.5% to 7.5%; P=0.42]. Multivariable regression showed that procedure type is not an independent predictor of recurrence; however, there were significantly more complications (54.6% vs. 14.8%; P<0.001) and longer hospital stays (8.71±3.88 vs. 7.88±3.81 days; P=0.009) with surgical pleurectomy. Functional and dyspnoea measures favoured the surgical group, with 87.0% of surgical patients meeting ECOG performance status 1 vs. 74.7% for talc (P<0.001), 96.1% normal Shuttle Walk Test versus 86.0%, and 87.0% with MRC dyspnoea grade of 1 compared to 69.0%. Conclusions: In this non-randomised retrospective cohort, surgical pleurectomy was associated with better short-term functional measures, but also with a significantly higher complication rate. Talc pleurodesis was associated with fewer complications and comparable effusion control, particularly in older or higher-risk patients. Patient selection should be based on performance status and individualised risk tolerance. A large number of prospective multi-centre trials are now required to determine the long-term outcomes of talc pleurodesis in Africa.

items.title: A systematic review and meta-analysis of surrogate endpoints for overall survival in limited-stage small cell lung cancer
items.abstract: Background: Overall survival (OS) remains the gold-standard endpoint in randomized controlled trials (RCTs) of limited-stage small cell lung cancer (LS-SCLC), but prolonged follow-up requirements may delay therapeutic evaluation and implementation. Surrogate endpoints such as progression-free survival (PFS), response outcomes, and radiotherapy-related metrics may provide earlier indicators of treatment efficacy, although their validity in LS-SCLC remains unclear. We conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized trials to evaluate associations between surrogate endpoints and OS using published aggregate trial-arm data in LS-SCLC. Methods: We systematically searched MEDLINE, EMBASE, and CENTRAL from inception to January 2026 for phase II/III RCTs involving patients with LS-SCLC. Eligible studies evaluated local and/or systemic therapies and reported survival-related endpoints. Weighted linear regression and correlation analyses were performed to assess associations between OS and surrogate endpoints, including PFS, and radiologic best overall response (BOR). Results: Of 3,700 citations, 45 articles of 43 RCTs were included. Studies randomized 11,869 patients across over 765 sites in over 15 countries. PFS was reported in 23 trials and demonstrated a moderate arm-level association with OS (R2=0.49), although substantial cross-trial heterogeneity limited interpretation of this association. BOR was reported in 27 trials. Complete response demonstrated a weak positive correlation with OS (R2=0.11), and partial response showed minimal positive correlation (R2=0.052). Conclusions: PFS demonstrated a moderate arm-level association with OS and should not be considered a validated surrogate for OS based on currently published aggregate data. OS remains the most reliable endpoint, and further investigation using individual patient-level data and contemporary treatment cohorts are essential to discover and validate surrogate endpoints for LS-SCLC.

items.title: Genomic-immunophenotypic characterization of pulmonary sarcomatoid carcinoma: a cohort study and literature review
items.abstract: Background: Pulmonary sarcomatoid carcinoma (PSC) is a poorly differentiated non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) comprising pleomorphic carcinoma, carcinosarcoma, and pulmonary blastoma. Although multiple genomic studies of PSC have been reported, substantial inter-cohort heterogeneity remains in its molecular characterization. In this study, we sought to explore the clinicopathological characteristics and complex mutational profile of PSC. Methods: Twenty-one patients with histopathologically confirmed PSC were enrolled. Next-generation sequencing (NGS) was performed using a targeted panel of 520 genes. Programmed death-ligand 1 (PD-L1) expression was analyzed by immunohistochemistry (IHC), and tumor mutational burden (TMB) was calculated based on the sequenced megabase-scale DNA regions. For comparison, clinical and somatic mutation data from 566 lung adenocarcinomas (ADC) and 484 squamous cell carcinomas (SqCC) were retrieved from The Cancer Genome Atlas (TCGA). An integrated literature review was also conducted. Exploratory therapeutic annotation and drug prioritization analyses were additionally performed using CGI-Clinic, DGIdb, and PanDrugs2. Results: The cohort comprised 13 males (61.9%) and 8 females (38.1%), with a median age of 62 years (range, 44–79 years); 84.2% of patients had early-stage disease (stage I–IIIA). NGS revealed that all 14 sequenced cases harbored more than one detectable mutation. TP53 was the most frequently mutated gene (78.6%), followed by FAT3 and KRAS (28.6% each). After Benjamini-Hochberg false discovery rate (FDR) correction, KRAS (q=0.0023), RBM10 (q=0.0135), DNMT3A (q=0.0171), and JAK3 (q=0.0331) remained significantly enriched in PSC relative to TCGA lung squamous cell carcinoma (LUSC), whereas no individual gene remained significant in the comparison with TCGA LUAD. Mutation-frequency correlations showed positive associations between overall PSC and TCGA lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD) (Spearman R=0.7975, P<0.001) and between overall PSC and TCGA LUSC (R=0.9189, P<0.001). The median TMB was 13.5 mutations/Mb (mean 13.8; range, 0.8–38.9). PD-L1 positivity (TPS ≥1%) was observed in 85.7% of cases, and 35.7% showed high PD-L1 expression (TPS ≥50%). Integrated therapeutic annotation identified clinically actionable alterations including EML4-ALK fusion, EGFR L858R, and KRAS G12C mutations. DGIdb and PanDrugs2 analyses additionally generated exploratory drug-gene associations and candidate therapeutic annotations. Conclusions: Our findings as well as the data from the literature review suggest that PSC does not represent a single molecular subtype but rather a heterogeneous entity with potential lineage-associated genomic patterns. These patterns are characterized by a conserved mutational backbone, partial retention of epithelial lineage features, and alterations enriched in PSC relative to conventional LUAD and LUSC. Integrated therapeutic annotation further suggested that despite marked genomic heterogeneity, multiple altered genes converge on shared signaling pathways, highlighting potential therapeutic opportunities that warrant further validation in PSC.

items.title: Association of CA125 with all-cause mortality independently of progressive pulmonary fibrosis in patients with idiopathic interstitial pneumonia: post hoc analysis of a prospective and multicenter cohort study
items.abstract: Background: Progressive pulmonary fibrosis (PPF) is associated with poor prognosis in patients with idiopathic interstitial pneumonia (IIP). While serum cancer antigen (CA) 125 levels are linked to poor prognosis in patients with idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF), their association with PPF in patients with IIP remains unclear. This study aimed to evaluate whether serum CA125 levels are associated with all-cause mortality in patients with IIP and PPF. Methods: This post hoc analysis included consecutively enrolled patients aged ≥15 years with newly diagnosed IIP from a prospective and multicenter cohort from 2015 to 2022 (PAIR-2 cohort). Clinical records, serum samples, lung high-resolution computed tomography images, and lung biopsy specimens were collected. Information regarding the survival status was verified by the attending physicians each year. Serum CA125 levels were measured at diagnosis of IIP using multiplexed sandwich single enzyme-linked immunosorbent assays (ELISAs). Based on the optimal cut-off value of 31.64 U/mL in receiver operating characteristic curve analysis (Youden’s index), patients were classified into high and low CA125 groups. PPF was defined by the presence of as at least two of the following without alternative explanation within one year from the enrollment: (I) worsening respiratory symptoms; (II) physiological progression; and (III) radiological progression. Although PPF is formally defined for non-IPF cases, the criteria were applied to all patients, including those with IPF, to assess disease progression. Results: A total of 222 patients with IIP were enrolled and observed, with a median follow-up of 36 months. The mean serum CA125 level was 32.82 U/mL. Patients with elevated CA125 had lower percent predicted forced vital capacity (%FVC) (P<0.001) and percent predicted diffusing capacity of the lung for carbon monoxide (%DLCO) (P<0.001) at diagnosis compared with those with lower levels. Of these, 58 patients died during the follow-up period. Survival was significantly worse in patients with high CA125 (P=0.01), with the lowest survival observed in those with both high CA125 and PPF. In Cox proportional hazards models adjusted for age, sex, the diagnosis of IPF, %FVC, and PPF development (a time-dependent covariate), high CA125 remained an independent prognostic factor [hazard ratio (HR) 2.221, P=0.006, 95% confidence interval (CI): 1.269–3.890], irrespective of PPF progression. Conclusions: While PPF strongly indicates poor prognosis, patients with high CA125 further exhibited significantly poorer survival compared to those with low CA125 among patients with IIP including those who progressed to PPF.

items.title: Impact of preoperative rehabilitation on postoperative outcomes after lung cancer surgery: a systematic review and meta-analysis
items.abstract: Background: Postoperative morbidity remains a major challenge following lung cancer surgery. Preoperative rehabilitation (prehabilitation) has emerged as a strategy to improve postoperative outcomes, though its role and optimal execution in thoracic surgery remain unclear. This systematic review and meta-analysis aimed to evaluate the impact of prehabilitation on postoperative outcomes after elective lung cancer surgery. Methods: PubMed was searched systematically from inception to December 31, 2025 for randomized controlled trials (RCTs) and prospective observational studies comparing prehabilitation with standard care in patients undergoing thoracic surgery for lung cancer. Prehabilitation was defined as any structured physical training program initiated before surgery, with or without nutritional or psychological components. Primary outcomes were postoperative pulmonary complications (PPC), length of stay (LOS), and functional capacity (6-minute walking test, 6MWT). Meta-analyses were performed using random-effects models, including sensitivity analyses. Bias was assessed via Cochrane Risk of Bias tool version 2 and ROBINS-I-V2. Results: Of 213 studies screened, one duplicate and 203 records were excluded, leaving nine studies (seven RCTs, two prospective) comparing prehabilitation with standard perioperative care (1,098 patients). Each study incorporated structured exercise with four adding nutritional and four adding psychological components. Prehabilitation was associated with reduced PPCs [log odds ratio (log OR) −0.61, 95% confidence interval (CI): −1.09 to −0.12; P=0.02]. LOS and functional capacity did not differ significantly. Conclusions: Prehabilitation is associated with reduced PPCs after lung cancer surgery, without significant effects on LOS or functional capacity. Further well-designed RCTs are needed given heterogeneity and risk of bias.

items.title: High-insertion hybrid percutaneous dilatational tracheostomy after cardiac surgery through median sternotomy
items.abstract: Background: Tracheostomy after cardiac surgery through median sternotomy raises concerns about procedure-related bleeding and contamination of the adjacent sternal wound, particularly in patients receiving antithrombotic therapy. Evidence specific to high-insertion hybrid percutaneous dilatational tracheostomy (PDT) is limited. This study evaluated procedural, infectious, and clinical outcomes after high-insertion hybrid PDT and compared early and later procedures in an exploratory analysis. Methods: This retrospective single-center cohort included 159 adults who underwent high-insertion hybrid PDT within 30 days after cardiac surgery through full median sternotomy from 2014 to 2024. The primary outcomes were major tracheostomy-related bleeding requiring red blood cell transfusion or surgical re-exploration and deep sternal wound infection (DSWI)/mediastinitis diagnosed after PDT. Early (postoperative day ≤10) and later (days 11–30) procedures were compared using stabilized inverse probability of treatment weighting. Results: Median age was 73 years [interquartile range (IQR), 62–78 years], median European System for Cardiac Operative Risk Evaluation II score was 9.5% (IQR, 3.9–21.6%), and 125 patients (78.6%) received antithrombotic therapy at PDT. Major bleeding occurred in eight patients [5.0%; 95% confidence interval (CI): 2.2–9.7%], DSWI/mediastinitis was diagnosed after PDT in 4 (2.5%; 95% CI: 0.7–6.3%), and major airway complications occurred in 4 (2.5%). All-cause operative mortality, defined relative to the index cardiac operation, occurred in 56 patients (35.2%; 95% CI: 27.8–43.2%). Weighting reduced all absolute standardized mean differences below 0.10. The weighted early-versus-later difference in ventilator-free days through postoperative day 30 was 1.23 days (95% CI: −2.43 to 4.59; P=0.43); no analyzed timing outcome differed significantly. Conclusions: This study provides estimates of bleeding, sternal infection, and airway complications following high-insertion hybrid PDT in critically ill patients after cardiac surgery through median sternotomy. The exploratory timing analysis did not establish a benefit of earlier PDT. These findings may inform procedural risk assessment, but comparative studies are needed to determine relative safety and optimal timing.

items.title: Valve-sparing aortic root replacement in patients with aortic root aneurysms: a comparison of straight tube and Valsalva grafts
items.abstract: Background: The David I procedure has demonstrated both safety and durability; however, controversy continues as to which type of artificial graft should be used during the procedure. The study aimed to compare clinical outcomes between patients receiving the straight tube graft (STG) and those receiving the Valsalva graft (VG) during the David I procedure. Methods: Between July 2008 and April 2023, 228 consecutive patients underwent the David I procedure for aortic root aneurysms at our department. Among these patients, 95 received the STG and 133 received the VG. Perioperative and follow-up outcomes were compared between the two groups. Results: Thirty-day mortality was 1.05% in the STG group and 0.75% in the VG group (P=0.81). Follow-up was completed in 96.4% of patients, with an average follow-up time of 3.60±2.86 years, corresponding to a total of 822 patient-years. During follow-up, only one late death (>30 days after surgery) occurred in the STG group. The 5-year survival rate was 98.9% in the STG group and 99.2% in the VG group (P=0.34). The 5-year freedom from moderate or greater aortic insufficiency (AI) was 89.8% in the STG group and 95.1% in the VG group (P=0.15). The 5-year freedom from valve-related reoperation was 94.0% in the STG group and 97.9% in the VG group (P=0.25). Subgroup analyses stratified by Marfan syndrome (MFS) status did not demonstrate significant differences in overall survival (OS) or freedom from moderate or greater AI between the two groups. Conclusions: In patients undergoing the David I procedure for aortic root aneurysm, no statistically significant differences in early- and mid-term outcomes were observed between the STG and VG groups.

items.title: Laboratory testing and interpretation of pathogen next-generation sequencing for respiratory tract infections: a 2026 modified Delphi expert consensus from China
items.abstract: Background: Metagenomic next-generation sequencing (mNGS) and targeted next-generation sequencing (tNGS) are increasingly used to investigate respiratory tract infections. Interpretation remains difficult because respiratory specimens are usually obtained from open anatomical tracts and are affected by oropharyngeal carryover, airway colonization, host nucleic-acid background, low-biomass contamination, assay-dependent decision thresholds, and uncertain antimicrobial-resistance (AMR) findings. This consensus aimed to develop a respiratory-specific framework to distinguish analytical detection from clinically relevant infection and guide resource-conscious test selection. Methods: The working group searched five databases from inception to June 16, 2026, and reviewed relevant guidance and clinical and analytical studies. Sixty-three experts participated in a modified Delphi process that included written review, voting, three in-person meetings, and two online meetings. Agreement was calculated from the five-category voting matrix. A post hoc sensitivity analysis excluded nine industry-employed panelists. Consensus levels describe panel agreement, not evidence certainty. Results: Twenty-eight recommendations address test selection, specimen handling, laboratory quality control, bioinformatics, local validation, organism interpretation, resistance markers, and reporting. Twenty-six recommendations reached level II agreement, one reached level I, and one reached level III. No consensus level changed after industry-employed panelists were excluded. The framework distinguishes analytical detection from clinical causation and requires assay-, organism-, and specimen-specific interpretation. Conclusions: Respiratory pathogen NGS should complement conventional microbiology. Validated tNGS may be selected when the expected pathogens are covered, whereas mNGS can broaden investigation of unexplained or complex infection. Test choice should consider clinical utility, turnaround time, local capability, and resource use. Comparative economic and patient-outcome evidence remains limited. Laboratories require validated workflows, appropriate controls, qualified review, and explicit reporting of uncertainty; resource-constrained services can use referral testing and staged implementation within a verified scope.

items.title: Blind-end mucosal ischemia as a highly specific endoscopic marker of anastomotic leakage after cervical circular esophagogastric anastomosis
items.abstract: Background: This retrospective cohort study evaluated early postoperative endoscopy to identify mucosal ischemia before anastomotic complications develop after cervical esophagogastric anastomosis. In circular stapled end-to-side anastomosis, the blind-end segment is anatomically vulnerable to ischemia, but ischemic changes at this site have not been evaluated independently. We assessed the diagnostic value of blind-end mucosal ischemia and explored the Early Endoscopic Ischemic Score (EEIS) as a preliminary indicator of early ischemic changes. Methods: Among 216 patients who underwent minimally invasive esophagectomy, 57 with cervical circular esophagogastric anastomosis who underwent endoscopy on postoperative days 6–7 were analyzed. Ischemic changes were assessed at the anastomosis, blind end, and gastric conduit, and EEIS (0–3) was scored according to the number of involved regions. Diagnostic performance was evaluated for anastomotic leakage, overall stricture, and refractory stricture (≥5 dilations). Univariate and multivariate logistic regression analyses were performed to identify factors associated with each outcome. Results: Blind-end mucosal ischemia showed high specificity for anastomotic leakage (95.7%), with modest sensitivity (45.5%) and a positive predictive value (PPV) of 71.4%. For stricture, specificity was also high (92.9%), but sensitivity was low (26.7%), PPV was modest (57.1%), and discriminatory ability was limited [area under the curve (AUC) 0.598]. Thus, blind-end mucosal ischemia is a highly specific but insensitive indicator for leakage, whereas its value for stricture was limited. In multivariate analysis, anastomotic mucosal ischemia was associated with leakage [odds ratio (OR) 9.50, 95% confidence interval (CI): 1.43–188.56] and stricture (OR 6.44, 95% CI: 1.65–32.65), although estimates were imprecise because of the small number of events. EEIS 3 (n=3) was associated with leakage in 3/3 patients, stricture in 2/3, and refractory stricture in 1/3. EEIS showed exploratory diagnostic performance, including an AUC of 0.840 (95% CI: 0.707–0.973) for leakage. Overall survival (P=0.21) and relapse-free survival (P=0.43) did not differ significantly between EEIS 0–1 and EEIS 2–3 groups. Conclusions: Blind-end mucosal ischemia is a highly specific but insensitive alert sign for anastomotic leakage, whereas anastomotic mucosal ischemia was the ischemic finding most consistently associated with leakage and stricture in multivariate analysis. EEIS may serve as a simple, exploratory tool for early ischemic stratification after cervical circular esophagogastric anastomosis, although external validation is required.

items.title: Erector spinae plane blocks in cardiac surgery: are we closer to consensus?
Community-engaged methods for co-developing an urban air pollution monitoring network in a majority-black city facing environmental racism
items.abstract: Background: Communities of color can experience disproportionate exposure to air pollution due to environmental racism. Community-based air monitoring can empower community members, but methods for co-designing such networks are underreported. We describe the development of a community-engaged urban air pollution monitoring network surrounding an automotive facility in Detroit, a majority-Black city facing environmental racism. Methods: Community collaborators initiated this project and contributed to decision-making throughout. A hierarchical geospatial approach integrated historical pollution data, asthma burden, social vulnerability and population density to generate an initial set of proposed monitor locations near a large automotive manufacturing facility based on local health concerns. A brief assessment was conducted in the area to assess resident air quality concerns and interest in the project. Results: Community partners refined project area boundaries to reflect community-defined neighborhoods more appropriately and identified multiple existing monitoring projects that agreed to share data, expanding our network from a planned 30 to 52 monitors. The final network deployed two types of low-cost monitors across a gradient of asthma burden and environmental justice indicators, focusing on neighborhoods adjacent to the industrial facility. Assessment results were based on a survey from 1 (no interest) to 7 (very high interest) and showed high concern about air pollution and asthma, with a mean interest level of 5.60±1.73. Conclusions: Co-designing an air pollutant monitoring network with community stakeholders reshaped decisions about project area boundaries, monitor placement and resource use. Structured community engagement can build capacity for environmental health advocacy by generating locally meaningful data, strengthening cross-organizational coordination and creating a platform for dialogue and action. These approaches may assist other communities seeking to confront environmental racism through community-engaged air quality monitoring.

items.title: Preoperative anemia and mortality after open thoracoabdominal aortic repair: a retrospective cohort study
items.abstract: Background: Preoperative anemia is prevalent in cardiovascular surgery, but its effect on postoperative outcomes after thoracoabdominal aortic repair (TAAAR) remains insufficiently characterized. This study examined the association of preoperative anemia with 30-day mortality and long-term survival after TAAAR. Methods: This single-center retrospective cohort study included patients who underwent TAAAR at Beijing Anzhen Hospital between October 2008 and December 2023. Patients with erythrocytosis, any preoperative packed red blood cell transfusion, or incomplete data were excluded. Participants were stratified according to preoperative hemoglobin level. To reduce confounding, propensity score matching (PSM) was performed at a ratio of up to 1:4. Multivariable logistic regression was used to evaluate the association between preoperative anemia and 30-day mortality. Long-term survival was evaluated using Kaplan-Meier curves and the log-rank test, and Cox proportional hazards models were used to assess the association between anemia and overall survival. The cohort was characterized by young age, a high prevalence of hereditary connective tissue disorders (HCTDs) and Marfan syndrome (MFS), and a predominantly post-dissection composition. Results: The study included 569 patients, of whom 78 (13.7%) had moderate/severe anemia. After PSM, moderate/severe anemia was associated with higher 30-day mortality [odds ratio (OR), 3.7; 95% confidence interval (CI): 1.3–10.5; P=0.02]. In the propensity score-matched cohort, Kaplan-Meier analysis showed lower survival among patients with moderate/severe anemia at 2 years (80.9% vs. 91.9%), 4 years (75.2% vs. 90.7%), 6 years (70.0% vs. 84.0%), and 8 years (59.4% vs. 76.6%) (P=0.007). The adjusted hazard ratio for all-cause mortality was 2.4 (95% CI: 1.4–4.2; P=0.002). As a substantial proportion of deaths in the moderate/severe anemia group occurred within 30 days, this long-term difference may be partly or largely attributable to early postoperative mortality. Conclusions: Preoperative moderate/severe anemia was independently associated with higher 30-day mortality and poorer long-term survival after TAAAR, although the long-term difference may be partly or largely attributable to early postoperative mortality. Prospective studies are needed to determine whether correcting preoperative anemia improves postoperative outcomes.

items.title: Not all vasopressors are created equal: rethinking renal protection during cardiopulmonary bypass
Mediation does not mean prevention: blood transfusion in anemic patients undergoing cardiac surgery
Beyond mere relief: in search of the best treatment strategy for mild asthma
Physician perspectives and current practices in long-term lung cancer surveillance beyond 5 years in South Korea: a mixed-methods study
items.abstract: Background: Advances in lung cancer treatment have increased the number of long-term survivors, yet major guidelines lack clear recommendations for post-surgical surveillance beyond 5 years. This study aimed to evaluate current physician practices and perspectives regarding long-term lung cancer follow-up in South Korea. Methods: A sequential exploratory mixed-methods design was utilized. Initially, semi-structured interviews were conducted with 10 physicians to explore clinical experiences and inform a subsequent quantitative online survey. Interview transcripts were analyzed using inductive qualitative content analysis. This survey was then administered to 30 clinicians, including thoracic surgeons and pulmonologists involved in postoperative care. Results: Post-operative practices varied widely after 5 years; a 5 to 10 years, responsibility for follow-up was dispersed across thoracic surgery (33.3%), regional hospitals (23.3%), pulmonology (16.7%), and family medicine (16.7%). The absence of clear guidelines caused clinical difficulties for 73.3% of respondents. All surveyed clinicians (100%) identified the monitoring of residual pulmonary nodules as a reason to extend surveillance past five years, while 96.7% cited the risk of second primary lung cancers. Consensus therefore existed on the rationale for extended surveillance, but not on who should provide it, for how long, or for which patients. Establishing appropriate follow-up for never-smoking females was notably challenging; the perceived need for surveillance beyond ten years ranged from 42.3% for those without nodules to 96.3% for those with residual ground-glass nodules. Unanimously, 100% of participants expressed the need for a national standardized guideline. Conclusions: Physicians broadly agree on why surveillance should continue beyond five years, but the lack of formal guidelines leaves highly heterogeneous practice regarding its setting, duration, and intensity. Urgent standardization is needed, especially regarding residual nodules and never-smoking female patients.

items.title: Minimally invasive versus sternotomy for the David procedure: a systematic review and meta-analysis of short-term outcomes, long-term survival, and valve durability
items.abstract: Background: The David procedure (DP) can be performed through either a minimally invasive approach (MI-DP) or full sternotomy (ST-DP), yet the comparative effectiveness of these strategies remains uncertain. Prior analyses have largely focused on perioperative outcomes, with limited quantitative synthesis of long-term survival and valve durability. The objective of this systematic review and meta-analysis was to compare short-term outcomes, long-term survival, and valve durability between MI-DP and ST-DP. Methods: Electronic databases were searched for comparative studies of adults undergoing MI-DP or ST-DP. Perioperative outcomes were pooled by meta-analysis. For long-term time-to-event outcomes, Kaplan-Meier (KM) curves were digitised and reconstructed into individual patient data (IPD), and pooled hazard ratios (HRs) were estimated using a random-effects Cox frailty model, with parallel study-level meta-analyses performed for validation. Sensitivity analyses included exploratory meta-regression, leave-one-out analysis, and E-value estimation. Results: Seven observational studies comprising 1,124 patients (35% MI-DP) were included. MI-DP was associated with shorter intensive care unit (ICU) length of stay (LOS) [mean difference (MD)=−0.5 days; 95% confidence interval (CI): −0.6 to −0.4; P<0.001], shorter hospital LOS (MD =−2.8 days; 95% CI: −4.9 to −0.7; P=0.01), and reduced perioperative blood loss (MD =−123.1 mL; 95% CI: −150.1 to −96.1; P<0.001). No statistically significant difference in aortic cross-clamp (ACC) time was detected between approaches (MD =1.0 minute; 95% CI: −16.9 to 19.0; P=0.91). There were no significant differences in 30-day mortality or major complications. In reconstructed IPD analyses, MI-DP was associated with a lower hazard of long-term mortality compared with ST-DP (HR =0.34; 95% CI: 0.14–0.80; P=0.01), although the survival effect was attenuated in sensitivity analyses. Freedom from moderate-to-severe aortic regurgitation (AR) and/or aortic valve-related reoperation (AVRO) did not differ significantly between approaches (IPD HR =1.32; 95% CI: 0.82–2.13; P=0.20). Conclusions: MI-DP is associated with improved perioperative recovery and comparable valve durability relative to ST-DP, with an exploratory association suggesting improved long-term survival. However, as all included studies were observational, these findings should be regarded as hypothesis-generating.

items.title: Incidence and factors associated with cough after pulmonary resection in patients with lung cancer: a systematic review and meta-analysis
items.abstract: Background: Cough after pulmonary resection (CAP) is a frequent and clinically relevant symptom after lung cancer surgery, but its incidence and contributing factors remain inconsistently reported. This systematic review and meta-analysis aimed to estimate the pooled incidence of CAP and to identify surgical and clinical factors associated with its occurrence. Methods: PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, and the Cochrane Library were searched from inception to May 2026. Eligible studies included patients undergoing pulmonary resection for lung cancer and reported CAP incidence, associated factors, or both. The review was conducted in accordance with the PRISMA 2020 statement protocol and the protocol was prospectively registered with PROSPERO under CRD420261386085. Results: Among 10,283 retrieved citations, 19 studies involving 5,161 patients met the inclusion criteria. The pooled incidence of CAP was 34% [95% confidence interval (CI): 29–40%]. Factors significantly associated with higher odds of CAP included right-sided surgery [odds ratio (OR)=1.71, 95% CI: 1.28–2.28], right upper lobe resection (OR =1.92, 95% CI: 1.14–3.23), lobar resection (OR =1.96, 95% CI: 1.67–2.30), mediastinal lymph node dissection (MLND) (OR =3.38, 95% CI: 2.21–5.15), peritracheal lymph node dissection (OR =1.98, 95% CI: 1.51–2.60), and postoperative gastroesophageal reflux symptoms (OR =5.19, 95% CI: 1.78–15.19). Sublobar resection (OR =0.51, 95% CI: 0.43–0.60) and preoperative respiratory training (OR =0.35, 95% CI: 0.15–0.83) were associated with lower odds of CAP. However, the findings for postoperative gastroesophageal reflux symptoms and preoperative respiratory training were based on only three and two studies, respectively. No statistically significant associations were observed for sex, smoking history, histological subtype, pathological stage, or cardiovascular and metabolic comorbidities. Conclusions: CAP affects approximately one-third of patients after pulmonary resection for lung cancer. The available evidence suggests that CAP is mainly associated with surgical factors, especially right-sided and more extensive procedures, and lymph node dissection, whereas sublobar resection is associated with lower odds of CAP. Postoperative gastroesophageal reflux symptoms and preoperative respiratory training may also be relevant factors. These findings identify clinically relevant factors associated with CAP and may inform perioperative risk assessment, while the predominantly unadjusted estimates should be interpreted with consideration of potential residual confounding.

items.title: Pralsetinib, an effective oral tyrosine kinase inhibitor for RET fusion-positive non-small cell lung cancer: an editorial commentary on the ARROW trial
Thoracic surgeon-led review of radiology reports to improve pulmonary nodule management: a single-center retrospective study
items.abstract: Background: Appropriate management of pulmonary nodules is important for timely lung cancer diagnosis, but nodules may be overlooked or inadequately managed in routine practice. We evaluated whether systematic review of chest computed tomography (CT) radiology reports by a thoracic surgeon could identify inadequately managed pulmonary nodules requiring further evaluation. Methods: We retrospectively reviewed all CT examinations performed at St. Mary’s Hospital from April 1, 2024, to March 31, 2025. A thoracic surgeon screened radiology reports describing pulmonary nodules and assessed whether appropriate management had been implemented. When management was considered inadequate, the ordering physician was contacted, and further evaluation or specialist consultation was recommended. Results: Among 42,372 CT examinations, 18,033 included the entire chest, and pulmonary nodules were described in 2,410 reports (13.4%). Of these, 371 underwent detailed review of medical records and serial CT images. Appropriate management had already been implemented in 349 patients (94.1%), whereas management was considered inadequate for 22 patients (5.9%). Following the intervention, two patients underwent surgical resection within 2 months, CT surveillance was newly scheduled for 17, and further evaluation was not pursued in three because of poor clinical condition or patient preference. During follow-up through March 2026, four additional patients under surveillance underwent surgical resection. Overall, six of the 22 patients (27.3%) underwent resection, and all were pathologically diagnosed with primary lung cancer. Conclusions: Systematic specialist review of radiology reports may provide an additional safety net by identifying gaps in pulmonary nodule management and prompting further evaluation.

items.title: Three-dimensional computed tomography anatomy of the left lung: from anatomical variations to precision segmentectomy
items.abstract: Sublobar resection, particularly anatomical segmentectomy, has become an important surgical option for early-stage lung cancer. Its safety and efficacy depend on precise understanding of pulmonary segmental anatomy and its variations. Recent studies using high-resolution computed tomography (HRCT), three-dimensional computed tomography bronchography and angiography (3D-CTBA) were reviewed, with emphasis on segmental and subsegmental bronchovascular anatomy, anatomical variations, and their implications for segmentectomy. CT-based three-dimensional (3D) reconstruction has significantly enhanced the visualization of pulmonary anatomy and revealed substantial inter-individual variation in bronchovascular branching patterns. These variations may directly impact the intraoperative identification of segmental structures, intersegmental plane delineation, and venous preservation. A comprehensive understanding of left pulmonary bronchovascular anatomy, supported by 3D imaging, is essential for improving the safety and precision of anatomical segmentectomy and for facilitating individualized surgical planning.

items.title: Efficacy and safety of minimally invasive surgical repair for congenital pectus carinatum and carinatum-excavatum complex: a systematic review and meta-analysis
items.abstract: Background: Pectus carinatum (PC) and mixed carinatum-excavatum complex (PC/PE) are congenital chest wall deformities increasingly treated by minimally invasive extrathoracic bar repair. Evidence remains dispersed across small heterogeneous series, with no prior quantitative synthesis addressing PC/PE. We aimed to evaluate morphological efficacy, surgical safety, and sources of heterogeneity in minimally invasive repair of PC and PC/PE. Methods: We searched five databases from 1 January 2005 to 19 May 2026 for studies reporting minimally invasive repair of PC or PC/PE with extractable outcome data. Risk of bias was assessed with the ROBINS-I tool and certainty of evidence with the Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development and Evaluation (GRADE) approach. Prespecified outcomes were Haller Index change, early surgical complications, late implant-related complications, fixation wire breakage, unplanned reoperation and deformity recurrence after bar removal. Proportional outcomes were pooled by generalised linear mixed model and continuous outcomes by random-effects meta-analysis. Results: Twenty studies (2009–2026; seven countries) comprising 1,307 patient records from 1,211 unique patients met inclusion criteria. Overall risk of bias was Moderate in ten studies and Serious in ten; none was rated Low or Critical. Haller Index change in pure-PC cohorts improved by 0.50 [95% confidence interval (CI): 0.23–0.78; 95% prediction interval (PI): −0.17 to 1.18; k=5, I2=97.1%]. Early surgical complications occurred in 5.9% (2.6–12.8%; k=11) and late implant-related complications in 16.4% (8.8–28.6%; 95% PI: 1.6–70.1%; k=11). Fixation wire breakage was 10.6% (5.9–18.3%; 95% PI: 1.3–51.3%; k=11), varying 2–5× by radiographic surveillance protocol. Unplanned reoperation was 4.1% (1.6–10.0%; k=10) and deformity recurrence 1.3% (0.2–6.5%; k=7). GRADE certainty was Very Low for all outcomes. Conclusions: Minimally invasive repair achieves measurable morphological correction with acceptable perioperative safety, but prediction intervals are wide and that for Haller Index change crosses zero, so the outcome at any individual centre cannot be assumed from the pooled estimate. Wire breakage depends critically on the radiographic surveillance protocol. Multicentre prospective registries with standardised morphological outcomes are required.

items.title: How many eosinophil measurements does a chronic obstructive pulmonary disease patient need?—temporal variability, phenotypic classification and precision treatment decisions: a narrative review
items.abstract: Background and Objective: The blood eosinophil count (BEC) has become the pivotal biomarker steering two major therapeutic decisions in chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD): inhaled corticosteroid (ICS) initiation or withdrawal, and eligibility for dupilumab or mepolizumab. Both decisions rest on threshold values that were derived—and are applied—on the basis of a single measurement. This review examines whether a single BEC is sufficient for stable phenotypic classification, and how repeated measurement and trajectory-based phenotyping could refine precision treatment decisions. Methods: We searched PubMed/MEDLINE (January 2014 to August 2026) for studies combining terms for COPD, eosinophils and variability, stability, trajectory, longitudinal or repeat measurement, inhaled corticosteroid withdrawal and type-2 biologics, supplemented by citation searching of landmark trials, guidelines and their reference networks; the complete retrieval flow, search string and per-step exclusions are provided as Figure S1. Randomised trials, cohort studies and post hoc analyses were prioritised. Key Content and Findings: (I) Within-patient BEC variability is substantial [intraclass correlation coefficients (ICCs) 0.42–0.78 across studies and intervals; within-admission coefficient of variation (CV) up to 76.6%] and is driven by exacerbations, systemic corticosteroids, smoking status, infections and analytical factors. (II) In a decision-analytic simulation pooling five COPD cohorts, approximately one-third of patients show intermittent eosinophilia; a single measurement detects this state in only 43% of cases, whereas three measurements over 12 months achieve 81% detection, a point of diminishing returns rather than a statistically derived optimum. (III) Persistently low BEC identifies a high-risk phenotype, challenging the assumption that “low eosinophils equals low risk”. (IV) A stepwise algorithm integrating historical and prospective BEC values, fractional exhaled nitric oxide (FeNO) and exacerbation history is proposed. Conclusions: A single BEC misclassifies a clinically important proportion of COPD patients, particularly within the 100–300 cells/µL critical range. Stable-phase repeated measurement combined with multi-biomarker assessment should precede irreversible or expensive treatment decisions. These proposals remain expert opinion pending prospective validation.

items.title: Trials on therapeutic vaccines for lung cancer registered on ClinicalTrials.gov: a registry-based landscape analysis
items.abstract: Background: Therapeutic cancer vaccines are intended to induce or expand tumor-antigen-specific immunity. However, registered lung cancer trials have not been fully characterized as it pertains to platforms, designs, disease settings, targets, combination strategies, and endpoints. This study aimed to synthesize information from trial registrations on vaccine platforms, treatment settings, and study designs to describe the clinical development landscape of therapeutic lung cancer vaccines and provide a basis for setting research priorities for future clinical trials. Methods: We searched ClinicalTrials.gov for lung cancer vaccine-related studies registered through August 14, 2026. We excluded noninterventional studies and records that did not meet the prespecified disease, therapeutic purpose, or vaccine criteria, leaving 189 trials for analysis. Registry fields and predefined rules were used to describe geography, study status, phase, funding, design, vaccine platform, lung cancer subtype, treatment setting, antigen targets, combination partners, and endpoints. Results: Peptide, whole-cell/lysate, and dendritic-cell vaccines accounted for 70.9% of the trials. Phase I, phase I/II, and phase II studies together accounted for 160 (84.7%) trials, whereas 12 (6.3%) trials were phase III. Random allocation was explicitly reported in 44 (23.3%) trials, 92 (48.7%) used a single-group design, and 160 (84.7%) were open label. Non-small cell lung cancer accounted for 72.5% of trials, and advanced, metastatic, or recurrent disease for 50.3%. Neoadjuvant/perioperative studies made up 1.1%, and studies on small-cell cancer 8.5%. Conventional antigen sources remained common, although personalized neoantigens were the third-largest target category. Programmed cell death protein 1 (PD-1) and programmed death-ligand 1 (PD-L1) inhibitors were frequent combination partners. Safety was the most common primary endpoint, followed by overall survival, immunogenicity, and tumor response. Conclusions: The registry remains dominated by established platforms and early development. Controlled studies with prespecified clinical endpoints could strengthen evaluation of vaccine benefit, particularly in perioperative disease and small-cell lung cancer.

items.title: A machine-learning algorithm based on endobronchial ultrasound imaging for the diagnosis of intrathoracic lymphadenopathy
items.abstract: Background: Endobronchial ultrasound-guided transbronchial needle aspiration (EBUS-TBNA) plays a crucial role in the diagnosis of intrathoracic lymphadenopathy. Ultrasonographic features can aid in the differentiation of benign and malignant lymph nodes. With the rapid advancement of artificial intelligence, the integration of machine learning and medical imaging has shown considerable promise in the diagnostic assessment of intrathoracic lymph nodes. This study aimed to develop a machine-learning model for the differentiation of benign from malignant intrathoracic lymph nodes during EBUS-TBNA. Methods: A bimodal endobronchial automated machine-learning model (BEAM) was developed, and patients who underwent EBUS-TBNA for intrathoracic lymphadenopathy between August 2024 and October 2025 were retrospectively analyzed. The imaging data comprised images acquired using both conventional ultrasound greyscale mode (B-mode) and elastography mode (E-mode). The final diagnosis of each lymph node was determined based on cytological or histopathological findings and clinical follow-up results. For feature selection, a five-dimensional color histogram was employed to reduce feature dimensionality, and the grayscale values from the B-mode images, combined with the color values from the E-mode images, were used as features to calibrate the offset of the five-dimensional color histogram. During the training phase, BEAM was optimized using five-fold cross-validation. In the test phase, the diagnostic performance of BEAM was assessed in an independent test set using accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, positive predictive value (PPV), negative predictive value (NPV) and the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC). Results: Ultimately, 100 patients with 120 lymph nodes were enrolled in this study. The training set comprised 85 lymph nodes, and the test set comprised 35 lymph nodes. In the training set, BEAM achieved an accuracy of 84.71% [95% confidence interval (CI): 75.57–90.84%], a sensitivity of 100.00% (95% CI: 93.12–100.00%), a specificity of 60.61% (95% CI: 43.68–75.32%), a PPV of 80.00% (95% CI: 68.73–87.92%), a NPV of 100.00% (95% CI: 83.89–100.00%) and an AUC of 0.879 (0.777–0.963). In the test set, BEAM achieved an accuracy of 85.71% (95% CI: 70.62–93.74%), a sensitivity of 96.00% (95% CI: 80.46–99.29%), a specificity of 60.00% (95% CI: 31.27–83.18%), a PPV of 85.71% (95% CI: 68.51–94.30%), a NPV of 85.71% (95% CI: 48.69–97.43%) and an AUC of 0.792 (0.580–0.960). Conclusions: This study developed BEAM, a model that may provide valuable adjunctive support for EBUS-TBNA in the diagnosis of intrathoracic lymphadenopathy and may potentially improve clinical diagnostic efficiency.

items.title: Reply: colonic interposition and the value of standardization
Prognostic value of PTX3 gene polymorphisms in patients with HIV-negative pneumocystis pneumonia: a prospective cohort study
items.abstract: Background: Pentraxin 3 (PTX3), a key component of humoral innate immunity, plays an important role in host defense against fungal, bacterial, and viral infections. Genetic polymorphisms of the PTX3 gene have been associated with susceptibility to various pulmonary infections, including pulmonary aspergillosis, cryptococcosis, and coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19); however, their prognostic value in pneumocystis pneumonia (PCP) remains unknown. This study aimed to analyze the association between PTX3 gene polymorphisms and prognosis in human immunodeficiency virus (HIV)-negative patients with PCP. Methods: This prospective cohort study consecutively enrolled 56 HIV-negative patients with PCP, with the primary endpoint being 90-day all-cause mortality from admission. Three single-nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) of the PTX3 gene (rs2305619, rs3816527, and rs1840680) were genotyped by SNaPshot single-base extension assay. Hardy-Weinberg equilibrium and linkage disequilibrium analyses were performed. Plasma PTX3 levels were measured by enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay. Associations between genotypes and 90-day mortality were evaluated via Cox proportional hazards regression and Kaplan-Meier survival analysis. Results: All three SNPs were consistent with Hardy-Weinberg equilibrium, with minor allele frequencies greater than 5%. Moderate linkage disequilibrium was observed between rs2305619 and rs3816527 (D’=0.84) and between rs3816527 and rs1840680 (D’=0.90). PTX3 polymorphisms were associated with plasma PTX3 levels in pre-specified analyses: the AG genotype showed higher PTX3 levels than the combined AA + GG genotypes at rs1840680 [23.48 (15.27–40.91) vs. 10.32 (4.65–24.14) ng/mL, P=0.03] and at rs2305619 [21.03 (15.51–35.68) vs. 9.79 (3.88–26.15) ng/mL, P=0.02], whereas no association was observed at rs3816527; omnibus tests across the three genotypes were not significant at any locus. In the prognostic analysis, allele frequencies did not differ between survivors and non-survivors at any of the three loci; however, the proportion of the rs2305619 AG heterozygote was higher in the non-survivor group (55.6% vs. 27.6%, P=0.03). Cox regression showed that the AG genotype was associated with increased 90-day mortality risk [hazard ratio (HR) =2.383, 95% confidence interval (CI): 1.111–5.115, P=0.03], and the association remained after adjusting for age [adjusted hazard ratio (aHR) =2.545, 95% CI: 1.175–5.514, P=0.02]. Kaplan-Meier analysis showed 90-day survival rates of 0.636 and 0.348 in the AA + GG and AG groups, respectively (log-rank test, P=0.02). Conclusions: In this first exploratory investigation of PTX3 polymorphisms in HIV-negative PCP, heterozygosity at the rs1840680 and rs2305619 loci was associated with higher plasma PTX3 levels in pre-specified analyses, and the rs2305619 AG genotype showed an age-adjusted association with 90-day mortality. Given the exploratory design of this study, these hypothesis-generating findings require validation in larger, independent cohorts before any clinical application.

Efficacy and Safety of Ulinastatin in the Treatment of Patients with Sepsis: The ADJUST Trial
items.abstract: Background Urinary trypsin inhibitor (ulinastatin, UTI) has shown potential survival benefits in sepsis; however, conclusive clinical evidence is lacking. Research question In patients with sepsis, does adjunctive ulinastatin, compared with placebo, reduce 28-day all-cause mortality? Study design and methods In this multicenter, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial, adult ICU patients with sepsis meeting Sepsis-3 criteria within 48 hours of admission were randomized (1:1) to receive intravenous UTI (400,000 IU every 8 hours) or placebo, for up to 10 days in addition to standard care. Randomization was stratified by site and septic shock. The primary endpoint was 28-day all-cause mortality. Secondary endpoints included ICU, hospital, and 90-day mortality, and ICU/hospital length of stay. Results Of 347 patients randomized, 340 (169 UTI, 171 placebo) received intervention and were included in the safety analysis; after 5 post-intervention withdrawals, 335 (165 UTI, 170 placebo) were included in the intention-to-treat analysis. At 28 days, death had occurred in 39 of 165 patients (23.6%) in the UTI group and in 39 of 170 patients (22.9%) in the placebo group (absolute difference, 0.7% [95% CI -8.4% to 9.7%]; P = .98; hazard ratio 1.03, 95% CI 0.66 to 1.61, P = .90). Secondary outcomes were similar in the two groups. Adverse events occurred in 56.8% (96/169) of UTI and 42.7% (73/171) of placebo patients (absolute difference 14.1%, 95% CI 3.6%-24.6%; P = 0.009). Interpretation In patients with sepsis, adjunctive UTI did not reduce mortality compared with placebo. Routine use of UTI for sepsis is not supported by these findings. Clinical trial registration ClinicalTrials.gov; https://clinicaltrials.gov; NCT02647554.

items.title: From Response to Remission in Adult Severe Asthma
A Young Man With Hypereosinophilia and Pseudochylothorax
items.abstract: Case presentation A 31-year-old man presented with a 2-month history of dry cough, progressive dyspnea, intermittent fever, and unintentional weight loss of 8 kg. He had no wheezing, hemoptysis, chest pain, palpitations, or skin rashes. He did not smoke and reported occasional alcohol intake. One year earlier, he had been diagnosed elsewhere with pleuro-pericardial TB based on an ultrasound showing right-sided pleural effusion, and 2-dimensional echocardiography showed pericardial effusion. Pleural fluid analysis showed a lymphocytic exudative pleural effusion with elevated adenosine deaminase levels (46 IU/mL). The patient received anti-tubercular therapy along with tapering corticosteroids, showing initial clinical improvement. He was employed as a soldier in the army, and his last posting was in northeast India, where he frequently consumed raw crabs pickled in alcohol. There was no other significant environmental history.

items.title: A 63-Year-Old Man With Dyspnea and Loculated Pleural Effusion
items.abstract: Case presentation A 63-year-old man with a past medical history of hypertension and end-stage renal disease receiving scheduled hemodialysis via a left upper extremity fistula sought treatment for shortness of breath of 1 to 2 years' duration that worsened acutely for 1 day after missing a hemodialysis session. In addition, the patient reported mild central chest pain without radiation. He otherwise was in his usual state of health and did not report fevers, chills, cough, sputum production, wheezing, abdominal pain, or hemoptysis. He reported history of tobacco use, having smoked one-half a pack of cigarettes for 15 years and quit about 15 years ago.

items.title: Mediastinal Mass With Recurrent Hemorrhagic Pleural Effusion
items.abstract: CASE PRESENTATION: A 55-year-old man was admitted with a 2-year history of recurrent dyspnea and exertional breathlessness, accompanied by intermittent blood-tinged sputum. During this period, he had been hospitalized 7 times at external institutions, where he underwent extensive investigations including fiberoptic bronchoscopy, endobronchial ultrasound-guided transbronchial needle aspiration, mediastinoscopy, thoracoscopy, and CT imaging-guided biopsy of a mediastinal mass. Empirical antituberculosis therapy also was administered, but no definitive diagnosis was established.

items.title: Persistent Severe OSA Despite Ongoing CPAP Therapy
items.abstract: CASE PRESENTATION: A 51-year-old man was referred to our sleep medicine clinic for reevaluation of previously diagnosed OSA. The diagnosis had been established approximately 4 years earlier, at a body weight of 105 kg (BMI, 31.7 kg/m2). At that time, cardiorespiratory polygraphy documented severe OSA, with an apnea-hypopnea index of 97 events/h. Mean nocturnal oxygen saturation (Spo2) was 91%, and the cumulative time spent with Spo2 < 90% accounted for 38% of the total recording time, indicating a substantial nocturnal hypoxemic burden. Nocturnal CPAP therapy had been prescribed, delivered through an oronasal mask at a fixed pressure of 11 cm H2O.
