Bilateral Pulmonary Nodules After Lung Transplantation
items.abstract: Case presentation A 64-year-old man who underwent bilateral orthotopic lung transplant for emphysema related to α1-antitrypsin deficiency 8 months ago presented to the clinic for assessment of bilateral pulmonary nodules identified on routine postlung transplant surveillance without any symptomatic concerns. The donor was positive for cytomegalovirus and positive for Epstein-Barr virus, and the recipient was negative for cytomegalovirus and positive for Epstein-Barr virus. He denied any fever, chills, cough, chest pain, dyspnea, weight loss, or night sweats. The patient lived in South Florida with no recent travel history outside the United States or infectious contacts. His posttransplant course was complicated with antibody-mediated rejection at 1.5 months after lung transplant. Antibody-mediated rejection was successfully treated with our institutional multimodal regimen, including a combination of plasmapheresis, carfilzomib, and anti-thymocyte globulin followed by monthly IV immunoglobulin and tocilizumab injections. Also, because of calcineurin inhibitor (CNI)-related renal dysfunction, the patient's immunosuppression was converted to a belatacept-based CNI-sparing regimen in addition to prednisone, with a tacrolimus goal trough of 4 to 6 ng/mL. He was also placed on mycophenolic acid, which was soon held because of neutropenia.

Associations between temperatures, extreme temperature events, and onset of acute exacerbations of COPD: a time-stratified case-crossover study in China
items.abstract: Background Non-optimal temperatures and extreme temperature events may trigger acute exacerbations of COPD (AECOPD), but most evidence is admission based, potentially misclassifying exposure timing and obscuring susceptible groups. Research question Are non-optimal temperature and extreme temperature events associated with AECOPD onset, and which patients are most susceptible? Study design and methods We used the Acute Exacerbation of Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease Registry (ACURE) data and assigned residential temperature exposure using ERA5-Land, a reanalysis dataset of European Centre for Medium-Range Weather Forecasts. Cold spells (CS) were defined as consecutive days below location-specific low-temperature thresholds, and compound cold spells (CCS) as concurrent daytime and nighttime cold spells. Associations with reported symptom onset were estimated using a time-stratified case-crossover design, conditional logistic regression with distributed lag nonlinear models. Subgroup and cytokine analyses assessed susceptibility and inflammation. Results Among 5,634 patients with AECOPD (mean age, 69.4 ± 9.5 years; 78.8% male), lower temperature was associated with higher odds of AECOPD onset, whereas higher temperature was not. The strongest associations occurred for CS lasting ≥3 days and CCS lasting ≥2 days over lag 0-3 days, with ORs of 1.84 (95% CI, 1.22-2.78) and 4.31 (95% CI, 2.07-8.97), respectively. Nearly half had delayed admission within 14 days. Using admission rather than onset dates attenuated estimates by 88.8% for CS and 84.8% for CCS. Associations were stronger among older adults, men, smokers, patients with severe AECOPD in the past year or previously diagnosed COPD, and those using combination inhaler in the preceding year. CS were also associated with higher TNF-α, IL-6, and CXCL-11 concentrations. Interpretation Lower temperature and extreme cold events, particularly CCS, were associated with AECOPD onset. Symptom-onset timing may better capture temperature-related associations than admission timing. These findings highlight the need for targeted cold-weather prevention strategies to reduce AECOPD burden. Trial registry ClinicalTrials.gov; NO.: NCT02657525.

items.title: Pragmatic Clinical Indicators of TB Transmission Risk
items.abstract: Background Interrupting TB transmission is a priority in high-burden settings. Identifying highly infectious people with TB may guide targeted interventions. Research question Can readily available clinical characteristics (eg, lung cavitation, cough duration, modified Bandim TB score) indicate the transmission risk in participants with TB? Study design and methods We conducted an observational cohort study in Lima, Peru, enrolling 4,500 index participants. Of the 4,044 people with microbiologically confirmed TB, 3,109 had at least 1 household contact (HHC), yielding 12,767 HHCs. Index participants underwent chest radiograph and TB symptom assessment, from which we derived a modified Bandim TB score. We assessed HHCs for TB infection at baseline and 6 months, and for incident TB disease over 12 months. We analyzed associations between index participant indicators and TB outcomes in HHCs using modified Poisson regression with generalized estimating equations, adjusting for relevant covariates. Results Among child HHCs, baseline TB infection risk increased with greater cavitary extent (adjusted trend P = .005) and longer cough duration (adjusted trend P = .002), with similar trends at 6 months. Among cavitation categories, multiple-quadrant involvement was associated with the highest baseline infection risk (adjusted prevalence risk ratio, 1.62; 95% CI, 1.10-2.39), but not with incident disease (adjusted cumulative risk ratio, 1.20; 95% CI, 0.56-2.60). Among cough duration categories, ≥ 56 days showed the highest baseline infection risk (adjusted prevalence risk ratio, 1.59; 95% CI, 1.18-2.13), but not incident disease (adjusted cumulative risk ratio, 1.30; 95% CI, 0.85-1.99). The modified Bandim TB score was not associated with transmission risk. Interpretation Our results show that in this large household cohort, cavitary extent on chest radiograph and cough duration in people with TB were associated with increased TB transmission risk and showed dose-response relationships with TB infection. These simple, readily available indicators may help target preventive interventions in high-burden settings; however, associations with incident TB remain uncertain.

items.title: The Burden of Chronic Cough in Patients With Interstitial Lung Disease: a US Survey-Based Analysis of Its Effects on Daily Life and Emotional and Social Well-Being
items.abstract: BACKGROUND: Chronic cough (≥8 weeks) is highly prevalent among patients with idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF) and non-IPF interstitial lung disease (ILD) and imposes significant physical, social, and psychological burden. Research characterizing the burden of chronic cough in patients with IPF and non-IPF ILD from the patient perspective is limited. RESEARCH QUESTION: What is the multidimensional burden of chronic cough in patients living with IPF or non-IPF ILD? STUDY DESIGN AND METHODS: An online cross-sectional survey was distributed to adults from June to July 2025 via the Pulmonary Fibrosis Foundation's US Community Registry. Eligibility required a self-reported diagnosis of IPF or non-IPF ILD and chronic cough. Multiple-choice and open-text questions spanned six domains: demographics, disease history, cough characteristics, daily life impact, social/emotional and long-term impact, and healthcare experience. RESULTS: A total of 197 participants completed the survey: 75.63% reported a diagnosis of IPF, 21.32% reported non-IPF ILD, and 3.05% were awaiting further ILD diagnosis. Participants reported cough-related interference with daily activities (76.15%) and sleep disruption (79.69%) within the preceding week. Emotional burden was frequently reported: 95.94% of participants had cough-induced worry, 75.13% had depression, sadness, or low mood, and 67.01% reported avoiding social situations because of cough. Additionally, 60.91% of participants reported that chronic cough affected their platonic relationships, and 55.33% reported impact on their ability or desire to maintain physical or intimate relationships. To treat cough, participants reported using an average of 2.7 therapeutic classes historically and 2.0 classes currently, with many reporting limited or no relief. INTERPRETATION: Findings from this US survey of patients with IPF or non-IPF ILD and chronic cough indicate that, among respondents, chronic cough burden manifests physically, psychologically, and psychosocially. Reports of limited relief from available therapies suggest an unmet need in managing chronic cough in this patient population. CLINICAL TRIAL REGISTRATION: Not applicable.

items.title: Comparative Effectiveness of GLP-1 Receptor Agonists versus DPP-4 and SGLT2 Inhibitors in Patients with Bronchiectasis and Type 2 Diabetes
items.abstract: Background Bronchiectasis is a chronic inflammatory airway disease with limited disease-modifying therapies. Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1RAs) have demonstrated anti-inflammatory and immunomodulatory effects, but their impact on bronchiectasis outcomes remains unknown. Research question Is GLP-1RA use, compared with dipeptidyl peptidase-4 inhibitor (DPP-4i) or sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 inhibitor (SGLT2i) use, associated with better clinical outcomes in patients with bronchiectasis and type 2 diabetes (T2D)? Study design and methods Using the TriNetX global federated research network, we conducted a retrospective cohort study of patients with bronchiectasis and type 2 diabetes who initiated GLP-1RA therapy between June 1, 2022, and May 30, 2025. We compared clinical outcomes, including all-cause mortality, bronchiectasis exacerbation, acute respiratory failure, and lower respiratory tract infections, with patients receiving DPP-4i) or SGLT2i using propensity score matching to balance baseline characteristics. Results After propensity score matching, 1,029 patients per group were included in the GLP-1RA versus DPP-4i cohort, and 2,255 patients per group in the GLP-1RA versus SGLT2i cohort. Compared with DPP-4i, GLP-1RA use was associated with significantly lower all-cause mortality (hazard ratio [HR], 0.43; 95% CI, 0.33-0.56) and reduced risks of acute respiratory failure (HR, 0.46; 95% CI, 0.36-0.58) and lower respiratory tract infection (HR, 0.55; 95% CI, 0.46-0.65). Similar benefits were observed compared with SGLT2i for all-cause mortality (HR, 0.49; 95% CI, 0.40-0.60), acute respiratory failure (HR, 0.46; 95% CI, 0.39-0.55), and lower respiratory tract infection (HR, 0.77; 95% CI, 0.68-0.86). Stratified analyses demonstrated consistent mortality benefits across demographic and clinical subgroups, with particularly pronounced effects in obese patients but there was no statistically significant reduction in bronchiectasis exacerbations. Interpretation Among patients with bronchiectasis and type 2 diabetes, GLP-1RA therapy was associated with significantly lower mortality and reduced respiratory complications compared with DPP-4i or SGLT2i. These findings suggest potential disease-modifying benefits of GLP-1RAs in bronchiectasis beyond glycemic control.

items.title: How I Do It: An Intensivist's guide to RV Failure and Right Ventricular Assist Devices
items.abstract: Right ventricular failure (RVF) is a high-mortality form of cardiogenic shock frequently encountered in critical illness and is often underrecognized due to its heterogeneous presentation. This article presents a physiology-driven, stepwise approach to the diagnosis and management of acute RVF using a longitudinal case in the intensive care unit. We highlight practical bedside tools for recognition, including point-of-care ultrasound and invasive hemodynamics, and review targeted strategies for preload optimization, afterload reduction, and contractility support. Special emphasis is placed on airway management, vasoactive medications, and timely escalation to mechanical circulatory support (MCS) in appropriately selected patients. This bedside "How I Do It" guide is written for intensivists and pulmonary/critical care clinicians and translates advanced hemodynamic and device concepts into practical decision points for acute care management.

items.title: Atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease risk prediction in individuals with and without impaired spirometry
items.abstract: Background Cardiovascular disease risk scores likely underestimate risk in individuals with impaired spirometry (airflow obstruction and preserved ratio impaired spirometry (PRISm)). Research question How do risk scores perform between individuals with impaired and normal spirometry, and can they be improved by adding spirometry and dyspnea? Study design and methods Ten-year incidence of major cardiovascular events (MACE) ie., myocardial infarction, stroke or death from coronary heart disease, from 7 US population-based cohorts was used for this analysis. The pooled cohorts' equations' (PCE) ability to predict MACE was compared between normal and impaired spirometry. Cox-models adding spirometry, dyspnea to PCE variables were evaluated for improvement in MACE prediction. Results Among 26523 participants, those with impaired (N=7547) compared with normal (N=18932) spirometry had a higher incidence of MACE (14% vs 7%), hazard ratio 95%CI 1.25[1.17,1.34] adjusted for PCE variables. Discrimination using area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC)95%CI of the PCE for MACE was 0.792[0.780,0.803] vs 0.740[0.724,0.755] in normal vs impaired spirometry. Discrimination of MACE improved slightly by adding to the PCE: dyspnea plus 1)impaired spirometry 0.792[0.783,0.800], 2)PRISm, mild, moderate+ airflow obstruction 0.792[0.783,0.801], 3)FEV 1 %predicted, FEV 1 /FVC splines 0.793[0.784,0.802], compared with PCE variables 0.790[0.781,0.798]. The differences in AUC[95%CI] were: 1)0.002[0.001,0.003]p=0.002, 2)0.002[0.001,0.004]p=0.002, 3)0.003[0.002,0.005]p=0.0005 respectively. Among participants with impaired spirometry, only the model that added FEV 1 %predicted, FEV 1 /FVC continuous and dyspnea to the PCE showed improvement in AUC[95%CI], 0.750[0.735,0.765] vs 0.746[0.730,0.761] for PCE variables, difference of 0.004[0.001,0.008]p=0.008. There were no differences among models in calibration, sensitivity, specificity, overall performance, and after bootstrapping 1000 samples. Interpretation Performance of the PCE was better among individuals with normal vs impaired spirometry, despite the latter having an excess burden of MACE. Adding spirometry and dyspnea to PCE variables showed a small statistically significant improvement in MACE prediction, which may not be meaningful clinically, so other risk factors should be considered.

items.title: Liberation from Veno-venous Extracorporeal Life Support (VV-ECLS) for Acute Respiratory Distress Syndrome (ARDS): the Liberate VV-ECLS study: an international survey
items.abstract: BACKGROUND: The use of veno-venous extracorporeal life support (VV-ECLS) for severe acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) has increased substantially worldwide. However, approaches to liberation from extracorporeal support remain poorly defined, with no standardized protocols or validated readiness criteria. RESEARCH QUESTION: What are the global practices for VV-ECLS liberation among Extracorporeal Life Support Organization (ELSO) centers? Where is there variability in readiness assessment, liberation strategies, and use of standardized protocols? STUDY DESIGN AND METHODS: We formulated a cross-sectional survey of 25 questions regarding liberation practices among ECLS providers. Questions focused on assessed parameters for readiness to liberate, determination of liberation success, and strategies to optimize it. Surveys were distributed electronically to 765 institutions globally registered with ELSO between July 1st and Aug 15th, 2022. Descriptive statistics were used to summarize responses. RESULTS: Of 765 centers contacted, 340 (44%) responded, with 209 (61%) reporting use of VV-ECLS. Most centers were adult-focused, intensivist-led programs with moderate annual volumes. Most respondents (58%) prioritized VV-ECLS liberation before liberation from mechanical ventilation. Readiness for liberation was most determined by improvement in oxygenation under lung-protective ventilation (92%) and respiratory system compliance (90%), while fewer centers used inspiratory effort indices (34%). Liberation strategies were heterogeneous, with progressive reduction of sweep gas flow being most common (40%). Liberation trial duration varied widely (median 120 minutes; mean 497 ± 635 minutes), and most centers performed one trial per day. Arterial blood gas abnormalities (90%) and clinical signs of respiratory distress were the primary indicators of liberation failure. Only 42% of centers reported using a formal liberation protocol. INTERPRETATION: VV-ECLS liberation practices vary substantially across centers and are largely guided by institutional experience rather than standardized evidence. These findings highlight the need for validated physiologic predictors and protocolized strategies to optimize safe and timely liberation from VV-ECLS.

items.title: Social Functioning Is Impaired Among Long-Term Acute Care Hospital Survivors with Tracheostomy
Bedside ECMO Cannulation by Intensivists and Emergency Physicians
items.abstract: The number of centers capable of initiating extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO) for critically ill patients with refractory cardiac or respiratory failure is expanding. Historically, patients were taken to the operating room or catheterization laboratory for ECMO cannulation by cardiothoracic surgeons and perfusionists. More recently, non-surgeons who have undergone specialized training are performing percutaneous ECMO cannulation and initiation of support at the bedside at some centers. This approach is attractive, in part, because of the timely initiation of ECMO and avoidance of the risk of patient deterioration during transport to a procedural area. The purpose of this article is to provide a roadmap for intensivists and emergency physicians to lead ECMO bedside procedures including veno-venous (VV), veno-arterial (VA), and hybrid veno-arteriovenous (V-AV) cannulation at ECMO-capable centers. These procedures demand cognitive and technical skills that are already foundational to critical care practice, including vascular access guided by point-of-care ultrasound and leadership during a dynamic resuscitation. A team-based approach to bedside ECMO cannulation is presented and illustrated with figures and video, including preparation, procedural execution, subsequent patient management, and programmatic considerations such as training and credentialing requirements.

items.title: Real-World Outcomes of Long-Acting Beta-Agonist Add-On Therapy to Inhaled Corticosteroids in Preschool Children with Asthma: A Multicenter Retrospective Study
items.abstract: Background The role of long-acting beta-agonist (LABA) add-on therapy to inhaled corticosteroids (ICS) in preschool children with asthma remains uncertain. Although ICS+LABA is an established step-up strategy, data in children younger than 6 years are limited. Research question In children ≤6 years with asthma, how were morbidity outcomes associated with ICS+LABA therapy compared with ICS alone, before and after LABA initiation? Study design and Methods: This retrospective comparative effectiveness study used the TriNetX research network, a multicenter electronic health record database. Children aged ≤6 years with asthma treated with ICS+LABA were compared with propensity-matched children treated with ICS alone (n≈12,100 per cohort). To account for treatment timing and the age-related effects on asthma severity and incidence, analyses were conducted using two index definitions: asthma diagnosis with LABA initiation within 12 months, and the time of LABA initiation itself. Outcomes included systemic corticosteroid exposure, bronchodilator use, ED visits/hospitalizations, pneumonia, fractures, and gastroenteritis. Results When indexed at asthma diagnosis, ICS+LABA was associated with higher hazards of systemic corticosteroid exposure (HR, 1.37; 95% CI, 1.32-1.43), bronchodilator use (HR, 1.41; 95% CI, 1.36-1.46), and pneumonia (HR, 1.39; 95% CI, 1.28-1.52) compared to ICS alone. When reindexed to LABA initiation, these associations were attenuated, but not eliminated: systemic corticosteroid exposure (HR, 1.14; 95% CI, 1.09-1.18), bronchodilator use (HR, 1.17; 95% CI, 1.13-1.21), and pneumonia (HR, 1.11; 95% CI, 1.02-1.22). Direct comparison of the ICS+LABA cohort across index definitions showed lower rates of asthma-related outcomes after LABA initiation. Findings were similar in unmatched analyses, and in sensitivity analyses by younger age, later follow-up, Bayesian analysis and LABA type. Interpretation In young children selected for ICS+LABA escalation, excess morbidity was greatest compared to ICS alone before LABA initiation and attenuated after LABA initiation. These findings may provide real-world evidence for ICS+LABA effectiveness in a selected group of preschool children with uncontrolled asthma and the basis for future prospective studies.

items.title: Cardiopulmonary exercise testing responses to treatment in patients with pulmonary arterial hypertension and cardiopulmonary comorbidities
items.abstract: Background Current ESC/ERS guidelines suggest that initial monotherapy should be considered for pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH) with cardiopulmonary comorbidities. However, data on the cardiopulmonary physiological responses to treatment in this subset of patients remain limited. Our aim was to evaluate the cardiopulmonary exercise and gas exchange response to treatment in patients with PAH and cardiopulmonary comorbidities. Research question Do patients with PAH and a cardiopulmonary phenotype display a worse exercise capacity and gas exchange response to treatment? Study design and methods Incident treatment-naïve patients with idiopathic, heritable, drug/toxins-induced, HIV, and connective tissue disease-associated PAH were analysed at first follow-up. Comorbid patients were defined based on the presence of ≥3 risk factors among obesity (body mass index ≥30 Kg/m 2 ), systemic arterial hypertension, diabetes mellitus, coronary artery disease, smoking history and transfer factor of the lung for carbon monoxide (TLCO) Results A total of 178 patients were included: 52 with comorbidities and 126 without. Comorbid patients were older, predominantly male, and had a lower baseline exercise capacity, despite comparable hemodynamics. There were no differences in therapy, with approximately one third of patients receiving combination therapy in both groups at the time of reassessment. At follow-up, both groups demonstrated similar adjusted improvements from baseline in peak oxygen uptake, oxygen pulse, ventilatory efficiency and 6-minute walk distance, all known prognostic markers in PAH. However, comorbid patients exhibited a significantly worse gas exchange response to treatment, with an adjusted widening of the peak A-a gradient of +1.23 kPa compared with -0.35 kPa in patients without comorbidities (p=0.003). Interpretation PAH patients with and without cardiopulmonary comorbidities achieve similar improvements in exercise capacity after treatment. However, the worse gas exchange response to exercise among comorbid patients warrants caution, careful monitoring and further research to confirm this finding.

items.title: Combination acetazolamide and supplemental oxygen markedly improves ventilatory control instability and OSA severity
items.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Ventilatory control instability (elevated 'loop gain') is a key pathophysiological determinant of obstructive sleep apnea (OSA), but available interventions have modest potency. RESEARCH QUESTION: Since acetazolamide (ACZ) and supplemental oxygen (O2) independently lower loop gain via different mechanisms, can combination ACZO2 strongly reduce loop gain and therefore OSA severity? STUDY DESIGN AND METHOD: In a randomized, single-blind, crossover trial, 22 participants with moderate-severe OSA (15 M, 7 F), received ACZ (500 mg daily) or placebo for 7 days. On the final nights of each period, participants underwent two nights of polysomnography with O2 (3 L/min) or sham. Loop gain (LG1) and flow-based apnea-hypopnea-index (fAHI, events scored without desaturation/arousal criteria) were assessed from polysomnography at each visit. RESULTS: Compared with placebo+sham both ACZ and O2 monotherapies produced significant reduction in both LG1 and AHI. Combination ACZO2 markedly reduced LG1 by -0.26 [CI95%: -0.32, -0.20], and further significantly reduced LG1 compared to both ACZ (-0.07 [-0.13, -0.01]) and O2 alone -0.08 [-0.14, -0.02]. ACZO2 strongly reduced fAHI by -23.3/hr [-26.6, -13.1] (-55.2% [-63.9, -44.4]), however was not superior to ACZ alone (-3.4/h [-8.5, 1.6], -14.6% [-31.1, 5.8]). INTERPRETATION: In patients with OSA, combining acetazolamide and supplemental oxygen provides a potent reduction in loop gain and roughly halves the AHI. This combination intervention holds promise for individuals whose OSA is meaningfully driven by elevated ventilatory control. CLINICAL TRIAL REGISTRATION: ACTRN12616001297415.

items.title: Association between exertional dyspnea and insomnia in a population-based cohort.
items.abstract: BACKGROUND: Dyspnea is unexplained in 15% of patients. Insomnia has been associated with respiratory diseases, but its relationship with dyspnea in general population remains uncertain. RESEARCH QUESTION: Is there an association between dyspnea and insomnia, defined according to different criteria, using data from a population-based cohort? STUDY DESIGN AND METHODS: Participants underwent complete respiratory, psychiatric and sleep assessments. Dyspnea (dependent variable) was defined as modified Medical Research Council (mMRC) ≥ 1. Insomnia (independent variable) was defined with Insomnia Severity Index (ISI) cut-offs ≥8 or ≥15, and with ISI categories as subthreshold (ISI 8 to 14) or clinical (ISI≥15) insomnia. Logistic regressions were performed adjusted for age, sex, BMI, smoking, FEV1, AHI, psychiatric disorders and self-reported cardiac and respiratory disorders. We defined unexplained dyspnea with mMRC≥1 for participants of a healthy group (normal spirometry, normal Nt-proBNP, no anemia, no respiratory or cardiac disorders and normal electrocardiogram). RESULTS: We included 1'221 participants (mean age 62.2 years; female 52%) of whom 42% reported dyspnea and 18% reported insomnia (ISI≥8). The prevalence of dyspnea increased among ISI categories. After adjustment, higher odds of dyspnea were significantly associated with ISI cut-offs ≥ 8 (OR 1.87, CI95 1.31-2.67) and ≥ 15 (OR 1.96, CI95 1.09-3.64), as well as subthreshold insomnia (OR 1.76, CI95 1.17-2.64) and clinical insomnia (OR 2.17, CI95 1.16-4.05), all FDR p-value<0.05. Unexplained dyspnea was also associated with ISI≥8.

items.title: Sotatercept Improves AI Detected Electrocardiographic Signature of Pulmonary Hypertension
A PHASE 1 DIAGNOSE-AND- TREAT TRIAL OF VOLUMETRICALLY DOSED INTRATUMORAL CISPLATIN FOR EARLY-STAGE RESECTABLE NON-SMALL CELL LUNG CANCER
Pulmonary Function Estimation from Opportunistic Chest CT Using a Hybrid Image-plus-Quantitative-Feature Deep Learning Model
items.abstract: Background Spirometry is underused and most airflow obstruction remains undiagnosed. Chest CT acquired for lung cancer screening contains anatomical and densitometric information that may proxy lung function. Research question Can a deep learning model combining volumetric CT with CT-derived quantitative features estimate spirometric parameters and detect abnormal spirometry in independent external cohorts without retraining? Study design and methods A three-dimensional convolutional neural network trained on 10,371 low-dose CT reconstructions from 5,975 National Lung Screening Trial (NLST) participants was fused with 20 lung densitometry and tracheal geometry features to predict FEV 1 , FVC and FEV 1 /FVC. The frozen model was applied to an External Lung Cancer Screening Cohort (ELCSC, n = 268) and COPDGene (n = 10,302 scans). Ablation, two spirometric-pattern subgroups and prevalence-conditional predictive values were also evaluated. Reference spirometry was pre-bronchodilator in NLST and post-bronchodilator in COPDGene. Abnormal spirometry (FEV 1 /FVC 1 Results The model detected abnormal spirometry with AUROC 0.898 (sensitivity 89.9%, specificity 66.1%) in the ELCSC and AUROC 0.913 (sensitivity 66.9%, specificity 96.3%) in COPDGene, with CCCs of 0.80-0.88 for FEV 1 , FVC and FEV 1 /FVC. In held-out development data, CCCs were 0.86/0.85/0.71 (full model) versus 0.83/0.82/0.50 image-only and 0.55/0.65/0.35 feature-only. Agreement was lower, with systematic overestimation, in a COPD subgroup (FEV 1 /FVC Interpretation The model estimates spirometric parameters and detects abnormal spirometry across independent cohorts without retraining, with different sensitivity-specificity profiles at the same decision rule. It shows promise for opportunistic assessment of existing CT scans, but referral performance varies by population and prospective utility is unproven. Clinical trial registration COPDGene, ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT00608764.

items.title: Impact of Steroid-sparing Immunosuppressants on Lung Function and Mortality in Fibrotic Hypersensitivity Pneumonitis: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis
items.abstract: Background Evidence supporting steroid-sparing immunosuppressants (SSIs) in fibrotic hypersensitivity pneumonitis (f-HP) remains limited. Review question Do SSIs improve lung function or survival in adults with f-HP? Study design and methods Following Cochrane and PRISMA 2020 guidance (PROSPERO CRD420261413825), we searched MEDLINE, Embase, Scopus, Web of Science, and Google Scholar through May 2026 for studies of mycophenolate, azathioprine, methotrexate, leflunomide, tacrolimus, or cyclophosphamide. Two reviewers independently screened, extracted, and appraised studies using ROBINS-I, JBI, or Newcastle-Ottawa tools. DerSimonian-Laird random-effects models pooled percent-predicted FVC and DLCO changes and hazard ratios for death or lung transplantation. GRADE assessed certainty. Results Seventeen studies (1,341 patients) were included. SSIs were associated with modest FVC stabilization (13 studies; +1.11% predicted, 95% CI 0.37-1.84; I 2 =0%) and DLCO stabilization (9 studies; +3.73% predicted, 95% CI 2.56-4.90; I 2 =24%). The estimand-consistent mortality pool of two adjusted overall-effect studies demonstrated no survival benefit and could not exclude harm (HR 1.39, 95% CI 0.86-2.26; I 2 =0%). Certainty was low for lung function and very low for mortality. Descriptive benefit was concentrated in patients with identifiable antigens and less radiologic fibrosis. Interpretation Modest lung-function stabilization largely reflects uncontrolled within-group changes, not definitive disease modification. Controlled survival evidence remains insufficient; adequately powered randomized trials are needed.

Epigenetic Aging and Severity of Nocturnal Intermittent Hypoxia
items.abstract: BACKGROUND: Nocturnal intermittent hypoxia (IH) is a hallmark feature of obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) and contributes to oxidative stress and inflammation, which in turn may accelerate biological aging. Epigenetic clocks can estimate biological age from DNA methylation (DNAm) patterns. RESEARCH QUESTION: Is greater severity of IH associated with increased biological aging? STUDY DESIGN AND METHODS: We studied adults referred for suspected OSA in a multisite sleep and circadian research network, a cross-sectional observational cohort (2016-2021). IH severity was assessed using the 4% oxygen desaturation index (ODI) from home sleep apnea testing or in-laboratory polysomnography (PSG). DNAm from peripheral blood leukocytes was assayed using Illumina EPIC arrays. Epigenetic age acceleration (EAA) and pace of aging were calculated using multiple DNAm clocks. Linear regression models were adjusted for leukocyte composition, age, sex, ethnicity, BMI, smoking, site, alcohol, diabetes, and hypertension. A false discovery rate of 0.05 was used. RESULTS: A total of 1364 participants were included (median age, 56 yrs; median ODI, 16/h; median BMI, 32 kg/m2; 57% male). Higher ODI was associated with EAA for PhenoAge (β = 0.028, adjusted P = .0048) and with pace of aging (DunedinPACE, β = 0.0005, adjusted P =.0012). No significant associations were observed for first-generation clocks. INTERPRETATION: Greater IH severity, as assessed by ODI, was independently associated with increased biological aging as measured by PhenoAge and DunedinPACE clocks. These findings support a link between OSA and biological aging, raising the possibility of using epigenetic age measures as biomarkers of OSA-related morbidity.

items.title: DHEA-S in Pulmonary Hypertension: Insights from PVDOMICS
items.abstract: Background Dehydroepiandrosterone sulfate (DHEA-S) associates with disease severity in pulmonary hypertension (PH). However, prior studies focused on Group 1 disease; it is unknown whether DHEA-S associates with PH severity in other etiologies. It also remains unclear if DHEA-S associations with PH severity differ by sex or menopausal status. Research question Do associations between DHEA-S and measures of PH severity differ by PH etiology, sex, or menopausal status? Study design and methods We analyzed data from PVDOMICS, including 85 healthy controls and 710 participants with PH. Venous plasma DHEA-S levels were measured by ultraperformance liquid chromatography mass spectrometry. Multivariable regression models were used to examine associations between DHEA-S levels and invasive hemodynamics, right ventricular (RV) systolic function, and six-minute walk distance (6MWD). Analyses were stratified by sex and WSPH group, with exploratory stratification by menopausal status among subjects with Group 1 PH. Results DHEA-S levels were lower in all WSPH Groups compared with controls (adjusted p Interpretation Lower DHEA-S is a consistent feature across PH etiologies, but its association with disease severity appeared most pronounced in females with Group 1 PH. Modulation of DHEA-S levels or the pathways governing its regulation may represent a therapeutic target in PH, warranting further mechanistic study.

items.title: Delayed oxygen saturation recovery after the 6-minute walk test: Prognostic implications for COPD patients.
items.abstract: Research question The 6-minute walk test (6MWT) is a fundamental instrument in the clinical management of COPD patients, yet the prognostic value of specific physiological parameters during the recovery phase remains underexplored. This study aimed to determine whether the recovery time of oxygen saturation (SpO 2 -RT) following a 6MWT is associated with long-term prognosis (death and hospitalizations) in a cohort of patients with COPD. Study design and methods In this prospective observational cohort, 512 consecutive patients were recruited through the Galdakao University Hospital Respiratory Service and underwent pulmonary function and quadriceps strength assessments, multisensor accelerometry, and a 6MWT. Desaturation was defined as a ≥3% decrease in SpO 2 from baseline during the 6MWT; SpO 2 -RT was the time from test completion until SpO 2 returned to baseline. Results Of the 512 enrolled patients 25% were female. Those who experienced oxygen desaturation during the 6MWT exhibited significantly worse pulmonary function (FEV1%, RV%, IC/TLC and DLCO%) (p 2 -RT cut-off ≥ 80 seconds. Patients with a prolonged SpO 2 -RT exhibited more severe pulmonary function impairment (p values ranging from .02 to 2 -RT was associated with increased mortality (p =.03) and hospitalizations (p =.0003). In the adjusted analyses, prolonged SpO 2 -RT was associated with an approximately twofold higher risk of both hospitalization (p = .02) and mortality (p =.04). Interpretation A prolonged SpO 2 -RT ≥ 80 identifies a COPD phenotype characterized by diminished respiratory reserve and an increased risk of subsequent exacerbation-related hospitalizations and all-cause mortality. SpO 2 -RT is a simple, accessible metric that enhances the prognostic utility of the standard 6MWT.

items.title: Respiratory Therapists’ Intentions to Leave their Current Position
items.abstract: Background Many respiratory therapy departments face staffing shortages with high turnover rates. What drives turnover among respiratory therapists (RTs) is unclear. Research question What variables are associated with RT's intention to leave their current position. Study design and methods We performed a planned secondary analysis of a multicenter, multinational study of RT burnout. We compared those with an intent to leave score ≥ 50 to those with a score Results We received 1,014 responses and 536 (53%) had an intention to leave score ≥ 50. Statistically significant factors associated with intention to leave included: emotional exhaustion (OR 13.2), felt other RTs were burned out (OR 6.4), felt their workload was too high (OR 3.9), exposure to incivility (OR 3.4), unable to complete all their work (OR 2.4), inadequate staffing (OR 2.3), activities restricted due to illness (OR 2.0), worked 31-50 hours in the ICU (OR 1.6), bachelor's degree (OR 1.4) and missed work for any reason (OR 1.4). Statistically significant factors associated with low intention to leave included: felt valued by their organization (OR 0.1), a positive leadership score (OR 0.2), agreed their director/manager cared about them as a person (OR 0.2), satisfaction with total compensation (OR 0.3), Interpretation Over half of RTs had an intention to leave. Emotional exhaustion, incivility, leadership, staffing, workload, hours worked in the ICU, bachelor's degree, and perceived value were all associated with intent to leave while hours worked, and patient population were not associated with intent to leave.

Hospital at home for the acute care of patients with liver disease: A clinical review
items.abstract: Patients with liver disease experience frequent hospitalizations for complications such as hepatic encephalopathy, ascites, infections, and gastrointestinal bleeding, resulting in substantial healthcare utilization and reduced time spent at home. Hospital at Home (HaH) is an increasingly utilized care model that delivers hospital-level acute care in the patient’s home through multidisciplinary care teams, remote monitoring, and home-based diagnostic and therapeutic services. This review summarizes the rationale for considering HaH in liver disease and outlines key program components. We review the existing evidence supporting HaH, including the limited hepatology-specific literature as well as broader data from randomized trials and systematic reviews in related populations. We show early studies in patients with cirrhosis suggest that HaH is feasible and safe in appropriately selected individuals. Furthermore, the broader studies comparing HaH to traditional care have consistently demonstrated comparable or improved clinical and patient-centered outcomes such as mortality, readmission rates, cost of care, patient experience, and caregiver burden. HaH represents a promising patient-centered addition to the continuum of acute care for individuals with advanced liver disease. Broader implementation in hepatology will depend on establishing evidence-based patient selection frameworks, defining disease-specific models of care, and carefully designed studies to better understand the impact of HaH on clinical outcomes, healthcare utilization, equity in access to care, as well as patient-reported and caregiver outcomes.

items.title: Living donor–domino liver transplantation for maple syrup urine disease: Surgical and metabolic outcomes
items.abstract: This study evaluates the feasibility and safety of combining living donor liver transplantation (LDLT) with domino liver transplantation (DLT) for maple syrup urine disease (MSUD). MSUD causes neurological impairment due to branched-chain amino acid (BCAA) accumulation. Liver transplantation restores metabolic homeostasis via branched-chain ketoacid dehydrogenase (BCKDH) present in the donor graft. MSUD livers can be reused as domino liver grafts (DLGs) since enzyme deficiency in DLG is supplied by production in other recipients’ tissues. From October 2012 to September 2025, live donors (LDs), MSUD patients, and DLG recipients were enrolled for DLT and followed for at least 1 year after transplantation. Plasma BCAA levels in MSUD patients at 3 time points [pretransplantation, early (1–90 d), and late (>90–365 d) posttransplantation] were compared with age-matched pediatric controls without metabolic disorders. Surgical and metabolic outcomes were monitored up to 1 year after transplantation. Among 32 LDLT for MSUD, 27 (84.4%) grafts were reused. Patient/graft survival was 93.8% for MSUD recipients and 96.3%/85.2% for DLG recipients, respectively. Late hepatic artery thrombosis occurred in 3.1% of MSUD patients and 7.4% of DLG recipients. Primary factors for DLG disposal were double arteries and younger MSUD patients, related to small arterial caliber. No increased risk related to DLG donation was demonstrated. Combining LDLT and DLT expands the donor pool for pediatric patients while ensuring safety in MSUD treatment, with microsurgical arterial reconstruction supporting DLG reuse. Higher graft-to-recipient weight ratio (GRWR) was associated with better early metabolic control, but this association was not significant after adjustment for age, suggesting that the apparent contribution of graft size to early metabolic adaptation may be age-related.

A Composite AFP-PIVKA-II (AP) score for Hepatocellular Carcinoma Recurrence Risk Stratification in Living Donor Liver Transplantation
items.abstract: Background: The AFP–PIVKA-II (AP) score, a simplified derivative of the AFP–DCP (PIVKA-II)–tumor volume (ADV) score incorporating only serum AFP and PIVKA-II levels, was developed to predict the posttransplant hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) prognosis. This study evaluated prognostic performance of the AP score in predicting HCC recurrence and overall survival (OS) following living donor liver transplantation (LDLT). Methods: A high-volume single-center cohort (n=1,573) and a Korea-nationwide multicenter cohort (n=1,709) served as the development and external validation datasets, respectively. Results: In the development cohort, median pretransplant AFP, PIVKA-II, and AP scores were 10.2 ng/mL, 30 mAU/mL, and 2.6 log, respectively. Stratification by 1.0-log AP score intervals revealed stepwise incremental differences in both HCC recurrence and OS curves ( P <0.001 for both), with Harrell’s c-indices of 0.72 and 0.63, respectively. These findings were consistently reproduced in the validation cohort, where median AFP, PIVKA-II, and AP scores were 7.2 ng/mL, 31 mAU/mL, and 2.5 log, respectively, yielding Harrell’s c-indices of 0.65 and 0.61 for HCC recurrence and OS ( P <0.001 for both). When optimal cutoff values were determined using the Youden index J, the AP score demonstrated lower discriminatory performance than the ADV score for both HCC recurrence and OS, as reflected by Harrell’s c-indices in both the development and validation cohorts. Conclusions: This study demonstrated that AP score is a simpler serum biomarker-only prognostic tool that reproducibly stratifies risk of HCC recurrence after LDLT, but with lower discriminatory performance than ADV and with current evidence supporting prognostic use rather than definitive clinical decision replacement.

Von willebrand factor antigen identifies liver-related risk across surgical treatment pathways in hepatocellular carcinoma
items.abstract: Background: Treatment selection between resection and transplantation for hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) considers tumor characteristics and liver function, but may incompletely capture underlying hepatic risk. We assessed the prognostic value of von Willebrand factor antigen (vWF-Ag) across these treatment pathways. Methods: We studied 345 patients with HCC undergoing resection (n=105) or listed for transplantation (n=240) at two centers. vWF-Ag was measured before resection or at listing. Outcomes included survival, recurrence, and waitlist dropout, with the latter assessed using competing-risk methods. Analyses included cohort-specific vWF-Ag strata, continuous and spline models, adjustment for MELD, up-to-seven sum, and log 10 (AFP), and treatment interactions. Results: Overall survival was comparable between strategies when measured from listing or surgery, while recurrence was more frequent after resection (HR 10.0). After resection, rising vWF-Ag was independently associated with higher mortality (adjusted HR 1.042 per 10%) and recurrence (adjusted HR 1.046). At listing, vWF-Ag above 413% was associated with a higher cumulative incidence of dropout (41.6% vs. 25.2% at 24 months), driven by clinical deterioration or death rather than tumor progression, independently of MELD. After transplantation, vWF-Ag did not stratify survival or recurrence, and the vWF-Ag by treatment interaction was significant for mortality and recurrence (all p ≤0.01). Conclusions: In HCC patients, vWF-Ag was associated with adverse outcomes after resection and non-oncological waitlist dropout, but not post-transplant outcomes. This differential association supports the hypothesis that vWF-Ag captures risk linked to the underlying hepatic disease that persists after resection but is attenuated following transplantation. vWF-Ag may complement conventional selection criteria by identifying patients with technically resectable HCC whose prognosis remains compromised by underlying liver disease, supporting prospective evaluation of its role in selecting between resection and transplantation.

items.title: The leap beyond survival: Health literacy and the next frontier of success after liver transplantation
Utilization and outcomes of donation after circulatory death donors age greater than age 70 in liver transplantation in the united states
items.abstract: Advances in machine perfusion have transformed liver transplantation (LT) in the US with exponential expansion in donation after cardiac death (DCD) donors within the past five years. Utilization of higher risk DCD donors, such as age≥70, has also increased, but transplant center and organ procurement organization (OPO) use and outcomes compared to similar age donation after brain death donors (DBD) remain unquantified. DCD donors age≥70 and adult LT recipients of donors DCD age≥70, DBD age≥70, and DCD age 55-69 from 1/2022-12/2025 were identified using SRTR data. Utilization of normothermic regional perfusion (NRP) and DCD donors age≥70 by OPO were quantified. Characteristics and outcomes were compared between LT recipients among three donor groups using weighted Cox proportional hazards. Among 438 liver allografts from DCD donors age≥70 recovered, 347 (79%) were transplanted, and those transplanted were more likely to utilize NRP (70.6% vs. 52.7%, p <0.01) and machine perfusion (60.7% vs. 31.9%, p <0.01) compared to non-utilized allografts. Utilization of DCD donors age≥70 increased from 1 in 2022 to 297 in 2025. Over four years, 15 (26%) OPOs recovered zero liver allografts from DCD donors age≥70, and 57 (46%) centers utilized DCD donors age≥70. LT recipients of DCD donors age≥70 has similar mortality compared to LT recipients of DBD donors age≥70 (aHR(95%CI): 1.19(0.64 – 2.21), p =0.58) and DCD donors age 55-69 (aHR(95%CI): 1.08(0.59 – 2.00), p =0.80). Utilization of DCD age≥70 allografts in the US has exponentially increased in the last four years with higher NRP and machine perfusion utilization. Outcomes for LT recipients with DCD donors age ≥70 are similar to DBD donors age≥70. Strategies to increase donation and NRP use for DCD donors age≥70 at OPO and transplant center levels warrant exploration.

items.title: Impact of autoimmune liver disease on rejection risk and outcomes after liver transplantation: a comprehensive analysis
items.abstract: Autoimmune liver disease (AILD), including autoimmune hepatitis, primary biliary cholangitis, and primary sclerosing cholangitis, is a common indication for liver transplantation (LT). AILD has been proposed to increase T cell-mediated rejection (TCMR) risk, though published data are conflicting. Importantly, prior studies did not account for tacrolimus trough levels, a major determinant of TCMR risk. We conducted a single-center, retrospective cohort study of adult, transplant-naive, liver-only recipients maintained on tacrolimus-based immunosuppression between 2009 and 2022. TCMR and graft failure incidence were compared between AILD and non-AILD recipients using multivariable Cox models adjusted for median tacrolimus levels and relevant clinical variables. Separate Cox models for each covariate, adjusted for tacrolimus median, evaluated risk factors for chronic rejection (CR). Among 1101 LT recipients, 143 (13.0%) had AILD. Of the 298 recipients who developed at least one episode of TCMR, 18.8% had AILD. Multivariable sensitivity analysis demonstrated higher TCMR risk among AILD recipients (HR 1.54, 95% CI 1.12-2.13, p =0.01). This increased TCMR risk was further quantified using robust effect size index and found to be -0.08 (i.e., negligible to small effect). Independent predictors of CR included prior TCMR (HR 4.94, 95% CI 2.05-11.90, p <0.001), CMV mismatch (donor-positive/recipient-negative; HR 2.54, 95% CI 1.17-5.52, p =0.02), and sex mismatch (HR 2.63, 95% CI 1.22-5.68, p =0.01), whereas AILD was not associated with CR. Notably, CR, rather than TCMR or AILD, was independently associated with inferior graft survival. In conclusion, AILD is independently associated with an increase in TCMR risk after LT; however, this effect is small and does not translate into inferior graft survival. In contrast, CR is independently associated with reduced graft survival. Prospective studies are needed to validate these findings.

items.title: Liver Transplant Waitlist Outcomes Among HCC Exception Candidates with Durable Radiologic Complete Response to Locoregional Therapy
items.abstract: Some hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) patients achieve radiologic complete response (CR) after locoregional therapy (LRT) yet retain exception priority despite potentially lower dropout risk. We queried the United Network for Organ Sharing (UNOS) registry (10/2015–12/2023) for patients reaching the 6-month exception form (k=3 form). CR was defined as cumulative tumor diameter (CTD)=0 and AFP≤20 ng/mL at k=3; durable CR additionally required CTD=0, AFP≤20, and no new LRT through 1 year after k=3. We compared waitlist outcomes between CR and non-CR (nCR) patients. A secondary analysis stratified a previously established low-risk cohort (baseline single lesion ≤3 cm, AFP≤20, Child-Pugh A, MELD-Na≤15) by LRT count required for CR. Of 20,240 HCC exception candidates, 6,764 were Child-Pugh A with MELD-Na ≤15 at k=3; 6,037 (89.2%) were within Milan at baseline, of whom 3,714 (61.5%) achieved CR. From k=3, CR candidates had lower cumulative dropout incidence than nCR at 1 and 2 years (5.9% vs. 11.6%; 9.0% vs. 15.8%; p <0.001), with no difference in transplant rate (65.7% vs. 66.0%; 74.7% vs. 75.0%; p =0.12). At 18 months post-listing, 331 of 584 (56.7%) within-Milan CR candidates achieved durable CR and subsequently had lower dropout than those losing CR (3.7% vs. 13.5% at 1 y; 7.2% vs. 20.8% at 2 y; p <0.001). In the secondary analysis, CR conferred a dropout advantage among low-risk patients requiring 1 LRT (3.9% vs. 4.7% at 1 y; 6.0% vs. 11.9% at 2 y; p =0.002) but not ≥2 LRT (7.6% vs. 7.8% at 1 y; 12.2% vs. 10.3% at 2 y; p =0.40). CR was associated with a lower dropout risk than nCR, particularly when CR was durable. This advantage was amplified among baseline low-risk patients, though only in those requiring a single LRT. These findings identify HCC candidates with substantially lower dropout risk but no corresponding reduction in transplant priority, suggesting that exception policy could be better calibrated to individual risk.

items.title: Remote patient management reduces liver-related hospitalizations in patients with acutely decompensated cirrhosis
items.abstract: Background: Patients with decompensated cirrhosis experience frequent hospitalizations, yet evidence supporting remote post-discharge care remains limited. This study assessed the impact of cirrhosis-specific Remote Patient Management (CiRPM) program following hospitalization for acutely decompensated (AD) cirrhosis. Methods: Adults hospitalized for AD cirrhosis were included in a three-cohort observational study comparing CiRPM (2021-2024) with contemporary (C-control) and historical controls (H-control, 2018-2019). CiRPM enabled vital-sign and symptom transmission with 24/7 virtual nursing support. Subgroup analyses were conducted by disease etiology, CLIF-C AD score, and decompensation type. IPTW was used to adjust for confounding, and time-to-event outcomes were analyzed using Cox proportional hazards models. Results: Among 430 patients (156 CiRPM, 152 H-control, 122 C-control), mean age was 59 years, 65% had alcohol-associated liver disease (ALD), CLIF-C AD score of 56. CiRPM was associated with lower 90-day liver-related readmissions versus C-control (39% vs. 58%; HR 0.57, p =0.01) and a similar trend versus H-control (39% vs. 52%; HR 0.67, p =0.07). Associations were stronger among patients with CLIF-C AD ≥60 (HR 0.43 vs. H-control, p =0.005; HR 0.51 vs. C-control, p =0.02). Among ALD patients, fewer fluid-related readmissions (OR 0.40 and 0.37; both p <0.001) and recurrent hospitalizations (OR 0.51; p =0.001 and p =0.002) were observed in the CiRPM group. In non-ALD patients, hepatic encephalopathy readmissions were lower (OR 0.29, p =0.004; OR 0.36, p =0.02). Mortality did not differ across groups. Conclusion: CiRPM enrollment was associated with fewer liver-related hospitalizations, particularly among patients with ALD and CLIF-C AD ≥60, supporting targeted remote management as a scalable post-discharge strategy for this high-risk population.

Hyperammonaemia is associated with hospitalisation for bacterial infection: A multicentre cohort study
items.abstract: Background & Aims: Hyperammonaemia is traditionally linked to overt hepatic encephalopathy (OHE), but growing evidence suggests it also contributes to cirrhosis-associated immune dysfunction. We evaluated the association between plasma ammonia and bacterial infection and compared ammonia, the AMMON-OHE model and prognostic scores for predicting bacterial infection and other liver-related events in outpatients with cirrhosis. Approach & Results: This is a multicentre, retrospective study in 1855 cirrhosis patients on prospectively followed cohorts from five European and one Singaporean centres. The primary endpoint was hospitalisation with bacterial infection. Within one year, 8% of European patients developed infection; these patients had higher ammonia (1.75 vs. 0.97 times ULN; p <0.001) and a sevenfold higher risk of liver-related death (37% vs. 5%; p <0.001). Ammonia remained associated with infection, each unit increase raising risk by 12–14%, and was selected by every variable-selection method. The 1.4 times ULN threshold identified patients at increased risk of infection and OHE (both p <0.001). Ammonia alone discriminated well for infection (C-index 0.725 in Europe, 0.877 in Singapore), and integration into the AMMON-OHE model improved prediction (C-index 0.805 in Europe), with good calibration and clinical utility comparable to Child-Pugh and greater than MELD. Both also predicted OHE (C-index up to 0.904), whereas performance was weaker for ascites and variceal bleeding. Conclusion: Hyperammonaemia is associated with hospitalisation due to bacterial infection and predicts both infection and OHE. These findings support an ammonia-related vulnerability phenotype characterised by immune dysfunction and neurocognitive susceptibility, for which the AMMON-OHE model provides individualised risk stratification.

Efficacy and safety of oliceridine versus remifentanil for analgesia in mechanically ventilated critically ill adults (CO-ROAM): a multicenter, assessor-blinded, non-inferiority randomized controlled trial
items.abstract: PURPOSE: Remifentanil provides effective analgesia during invasive mechanical ventilation (IMV), but its utility is limited by opioid-related adverse events. Oliceridine, a G protein-biased μ-opioid receptor agonist, may decouple analgesia from these effects, but lacks evidence in critically ill patients. METHODS: This multicentre, assessor- and patient-blinded, non-inferiority randomised controlled trial was conducted across 19 intensive care units (ICUs) in China. Adults receiving IMV were randomised 1:1 to oliceridine or remifentanil, titrated to a Critical-Care Pain Observation Tool score below 3. The primary endpoint was time in target analgesic range (TTR; non-inferiority margin -10%). RESULTS: Of 307 randomised patients, 304 comprised the modified intention-to-treat population (151 oliceridine, 153 remifentanil). Median TTR was 96.0% versus 92.3% (absolute difference 3.7%, 95% CI -0.3-5.7%). Oliceridine was associated with fewer mild-to-moderate adverse drug reactions (ADRs), occurring at 15.9 versus 22.2 events per 100 patient-days (IRR 0.72, 95% CI 0.52-1.00, P = 0.049), and a lower rate of respiratory depression during the study period (0% vs. 4.6%, P = 0.015). Post-extubation respiratory depression (0% vs. 7.9%, P = 0.005) and analgesic-sedation costs were both lower with oliceridine. IMV duration, ICU stay, and 28-day mortality did not differ. Subgroup analyses identified a nominal ADR benefit in patients with Acute Physiology and Chronic Health Evaluation II > 17 and a larger nominal TTR difference in those without acute respiratory distress syndrome. CONCLUSION: Oliceridine provides non-inferior analgesia to remifentanil with a more favourable respiratory safety profile and lower costs in critically ill adults. TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov NCT06454292 (registered June 11, 2024).

Subphenotyping and precision medicine approaches to ARDS
items.abstract: Sixty years after its initial description, acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) remains defined by bilateral radiographic opacities and impaired oxygenation rather than by its underlying biology. This syndromic definition encompasses considerable clinical and biological heterogeneity, which may contribute to the ineffectiveness of pharmacotherapy trials to date. Subphenotyping aims to address this heterogeneity by identifying more homogeneous patient groups that differ in prognosis and/or treatment response. In this narrative review, framed by the research questions outlined in the 2023 European Society of Intensive Care Medicine guidelines, we synthesize current approaches to ARDS subphenotyping across complementary domains: clinical (etiology, rapidly improving ARDS), physiological (gas exchange, recruitability, elastance, and ventilatory ratio), morphological (focal versus non-focal radiological patterns), and biological (individual injury biomarkers and the hyperinflammatory and hypoinflammatory subphenotypes). We examine their pathobiological basis, temporal dynamics, and retrospective evidence for heterogeneity of treatment effect, and consider how parsimonious biomarker panels, machine-learning classifiers, and adaptive basket trial designs may support clinical implementation. Prospective validation across diverse populations, including resource-limited settings, remains a key priority.
