Natural ligand-based CAR T-cell therapy targeting BCMA and TACI for relapsed or refractory multiple myeloma (TriPRIL): a non-randomised, phase 1, first-in-human trial
items.abstract: Background Functional loss of B-cell maturation antigen (BCMA) is a recognised mechanism of relapse after BCMA-directed chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) T-cell therapy in patients with relapsed or refractory multiple myeloma. Targeting multiple tumour antigens simultaneously with a single CAR has the potential to mitigate antigen escape and prolong disease responses. Transmembrane activator and CAML interactor (TACI) and BCMA are both highly expressed on most myeloma cells and bind to the same natural ligand-a proliferation-inducing ligand (APRIL). We designed TriPRIL, a CAR that uses an engineered trimeric form of APRIL, to target both BCMA and TACI. We aimed to establish the safety, tolerability, preliminary efficacy, and recommended phase 2 dose of autologous TriPRIL CAR T cells. Methods In this first-in-human, open-label, dose-escalation and dose-expansion, phase 1 study, we evaluated TriPRIL in patients with relapsed or refractory multiple myeloma at Massachusetts General Hospital (Boston, MA, USA). Eligible patients had received at least three previous lines of therapy or had triple-class refractory disease. Previous CAR T-cell therapy and bispecific antibody therapy exposure were permitted. Patients received 3 days of lymphodepletion with intravenous cyclophosphamide (300 mg/m 2 ) and intravenous fludarabine (30 mg/m 2 ) daily on days -5, -4, and -3 before intravenous TriPRIL infusion on day 0. In the dose escalation phase, patients received 1·0 × 10 8 or 3·0 × 10 8 TriPRIL CAR T cells to establish the recommended phase 2 dose, which was further evaluated in the dose expansion phase. The primary endpoint was the incidence of study-related adverse events (graded according to Common Terminology Criteria for Adverse Events version 5) and dose-limiting toxicities in all patients who received an infusion of TriPRIL CAR T cells, until study completion at 24 months or progressive disease. The data cutoff date was March 24, 2026, when all infused patients had completed at least one assessment of disease response. This trial was registered at ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT05020444), has fully accrued, and is ongoing. Findings Between Sept 17, 2021, and Jan 27, 2026, 16 patients were enrolled and underwent leukapheresis, with 15 patients subsequently receiving a TriPRIL cell infusion. Ten (67%) of 15 infused patients were female, five (33%)were male, and the median age was 69 years (IQR 65-75). Nine (60%) of 15 infused patients had previously received BCMA-directed CAR T-cell therapy, and four (27%) had previously received a BCMA-directed or GPRC5D-directed bispecific T-cell engager. Six patients were treated with 1·0 × 10 8 CAR T cells, and nine were treated with 3·0 × 10 8 CAR T cells; there were no dose-limiting toxicities at either dose. The most common adverse events were neutropenia (14 [93%] of 15 patients), nausea (12 [80%]), hypogammaglobulinaemia (eight [53%]), fatigue (seven [47%]), and fever (seven [47%]). Non-haematological adverse events grade 3 or worse occurred in five (33%) patients and all resolved. Cytokine release syndrome (grade 1 or 2 only) occurred in 13 (87%, 95% CI 60-98) infused patients. One (7%, 0-32) patient had grade 2 immune effector cell-associated neurotoxicity syndrome, and one (7%, 0-32) had grade 2 immune effector cell-associated haemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis-like syndrome; both of these patients had received 3·0 × 10 8 CAR T cells, and both conditions resolved with corticosteroids. Infections occurred in six (40%, 16-68) infused patients, with a grade 3 infection in one patient (7%, 0-32). There were no treatment-related deaths. The recommended phase 2 dose of CAR T cells was set as 3·0 × 10 8 cells. Interpretation TriPRIL showed a favourable safety profile and warrants further investigation in patients with relapsed or refractory multiple myeloma, including those previously treated with BCMA-directed CAR T-cell therapy. The study findings support further development of this dual-targeted, natural ligand-based CAR T-cell approach. Funding Mass General Brigham and V Foundation.

items.title: APRIL-based CAR T-cell targeting of BCMA and TACI in multiple myeloma
Spontaneous coronary artery dissection: implications for women's health, clinical care, and future research
items.abstract: Spontaneous coronary artery dissection (SCAD) is an increasingly recognised cause of acute coronary syndromes, characterised by spontaneous separation of the layers of the coronary arterial wall. It predominantly affects younger women, and recent registry and imaging studies indicate that SCAD is more common than previously appreciated, challenging its historical classification as a rare condition. Clinically, SCAD is associated with a substantial early risk of adverse events, particularly in the first weeks after the index dissection. Given the high frequency of spontaneous healing, conservative management is preferred for most patients, whereas revascularisation is generally reserved for ongoing ischaemia or haemodynamic compromise. However, evidence to guide both pharmacological and interventional management remains scarce. This Review summarises current evidence on SCAD epidemiology, underlying mechanisms including genetic susceptibility, diagnostic approaches, management principles, implications for reproductive and women's health, and research priorities to improve outcomes for affected patients.

items.title: Seasonal mass vaccination with R21/Matrix-M against malaria in The Gambia and Burkina Faso: an open-label, cluster-randomised, controlled trial
items.abstract: BACKGROUND: The R21/Matrix-M (R21) malaria vaccine candidate, recommended by WHO for use in young children, could be extended to the whole population. Seasonal mass vaccination (SMV) before peak malaria transmission could be a promising tool to accelerate progress towards malaria elimination. We aimed to evaluate the safety and effectiveness of SMV with R21 in two malaria-endemic settings in west Africa. METHODS: This open-label, cluster-randomised, controlled trial was conducted in The Gambia, a setting with low-to-moderate seasonal transmission, and Burkina Faso, a setting with intense seasonal transmission. 54 medium-sized villages (30 in The Gambia and 24 in Burkina Faso) were randomly assigned (1:1) by use of computer-restricted randomisation to receive either SMV with R21 (intervention group) or no SMV (control group). All study villages received national standard malaria control interventions. In the intervention group, residents who were aged 5 months and older, willing to comply with trial procedures, and could provide written informed consent (from parents or guardians for children aged <18 years plus assent for children aged 12-17 years) were eligible for vaccination. The intervention was delivered as three monthly doses of 5 μg (participants aged <15 years) or 10 μg (participants aged ≥15 years) R21 plus 50 μg of Matrix-M. The primary outcome was malaria prevalence at peak transmission, defined as the proportion of participants with Plasmodium falciparum infection assessed by quantitative PCR. This trial is registered with ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT06578572) and the Pan-African Clinical Trials Registry (PACTR202404544467702), and is ongoing. FINDINGS: The intervention was delivered between May 30, and Aug 21, 2024. A cross-sectional survey to estimate the primary endpoint was conducted between Nov 18 and Dec 6, 2024. The population available for vaccination varied across the three rounds. In The Gambia, among 4311 total residents in intervention villages, 2565 (59·5%) received three vaccine doses; in Burkina Faso, among 6235 total residents in intervention villages, 4072 (65·3%) received three vaccine doses. SMV with R21 reduced the odds of malaria infection by 70% (adjusted odds ratio 0·30 [95% CI 0·20-0·44]; p<0·0001) in The Gambia and by 25% (0·75 [95% CI 0·58-0·98]; p=0·036) in Burkina Faso. In The Gambia, prevalence decreased across all age groups, whereas in Burkina Faso the largest effect was observed in children younger than 5 years. The vaccine was safe and well tolerated. 651 adverse events were reported in 581 (13·5%) vaccine recipients in The Gambia, and 795 adverse events were reported in 705 (11·3%) vaccine recipients in Burkina Faso. Among 69 serious adverse events reported overall, only one was considered related to vaccination (febrile convulsions in a female participant aged 8 years after the second dose in The Gambia). INTERPRETATION: SMV with R21 reduced malaria prevalence in both settings. It could become an additional strategy for malaria control in endemic areas of seasonal transmission. In low-to-moderate transmission settings, the vaccine could accelerate progress towards elimination; in high-transmission areas it could further reduce the malaria burden. FUNDING: UK Medical Research Council and the UK Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office.

items.title: Reproductive health in women in Britain from 2010 to 2024: findings from repeated, cross-sectional National Surveys of Sexual Attitudes and Lifestyles (Natsal)
items.abstract: BACKGROUND: Major policy and funding shifts threaten access to essential reproductive services and reproductive autonomy in Britain (England, Scotland, and Wales) amid growing attention towards hormone hesitancy and declining birth rates. We report on prevalence, changes, and sociodemographic differences in reproductive health indicators among women of reproductive age in Britain from 2010 to 2024. METHODS: Britain's National Surveys of Sexual Attitudes and Lifestyles (Natsal) are cross-sectional, nationally representative surveys (Natsal-3 Sept 6, 2010, to Aug 31, 2012; Natsal-4 Sept 20, 2022, to April 5, 2024). Using 3198 Natsal-4 probability sample participants (assigned female at birth, aged 16-54 years, and reported vaginal sex ever), we estimated weighted prevalences of key health indicators of reproductive autonomy: reporting no effective contraception use, hormonal contraception use, abortion, unplanned or ambivalent pregnancy, infertility, help-seeking for infertility, and fertility intentions, and compared these with Natsal-3. Age-adjusted regression assessed changes between Natsal-3 and Natsal-4 by sociodemographic subgroups. Using Natsal-4 combined probability and non-probability samples (N=7053), we examined associations with age, education, area-level deprivation, ethnicity, and country of birth. FINDINGS: In Natsal-4, 18·5% (95% CI 16·6-20·7) of women at risk of unintended pregnancy reported not using any effective contraception, and 41·9% (33·8-50·6) of past-year pregnancies were scored as unplanned or ambivalent. The prevalence of ever having had an abortion increased from Natsal-3 to Natsal-4 (from 16·0% to 20·7%, age-adjusted odds ratio [OR] 1·35, 95% CI 1·18-1·55), whereas overall prevalences of other indicators were stable. Subgroup analyses showed declining overall hormonal contraception use in those younger than 35 years (eg, from 64·6% to 50·3% for those aged 16-24 years, OR 0·55, 95% CI 0·39-0·79). The proportion of those aged 16-44 years reporting definitely not wanting children more than doubled from Natsal-3 to Natsal-4 (from 7·7% to 16·6%; adjusted OR 1·66, 95% CI 1·28-2·16), driven by women younger than 35 years. In Natsal-4, women with below degree-level education, living in more deprived areas, or of Black, African, Caribbean, or Black British ethnicity were more likely to report no effective contraception use and ever having had an abortion. Women living outside the most affluent areas or reporting below degree-level education were less likely to seek help for infertility. INTERPRETATION: The increase in women not intending to have children has major demographic implications and, alongside the persistent unmet need for effective contraception, underscores the importance of high-quality, easily accessible contraceptive services. The paucity of improvement in women's reproductive health in Britain and its entrenched inequalities demand person-centred, culturally competent policies and integrated services that uphold reproductive autonomy. FUNDING: The Wellcome Trust, the Economic and Social Research Council, and the National Institute for Health and Care Research.

Sexually transmitted infections, behavioural risks, and uptake of sexual health services in Britain from 2010 to 2024: findings from the repeated cross-sectional National Surveys of Sexual Attitudes and Lifestyles (Natsal)
items.abstract: BACKGROUND: Sexually transmitted infection (STI) diagnoses have increased in Britain since 2010, alongside major changes to sexual health policy, services, and disruptions owing to the COVID-19 pandemic. Meanwhile, sexual activity has decreased at population level, and more people report same-sex behaviours. To understand implications for HIV and STI control, we examined the general population prevalence of three STIs, sexual behaviours associated with STIs, and uptake of sexual health services, including HIV and chlamydia testing. METHODS: We conducted the fourth National Surveys of Sexual Attitudes and Lifestyles (Natsal-4) between Sept 20, 2022, and April 5, 2024. In this analysis, we used cross-sectional data from 5949 sexually experienced (who reported ever having sex) participants aged 16-59 years in Britain from the probability sample surveys. We estimated weighted prevalences for STIs using biosamples (vaginal swabs or urine samples; n=2721), self-reported STI-associated behaviours (including a composite of ≥4 partners, condomless sex with ≥2 partners in the past year, or overlapping partners in the past 5 years), and sexual health service uptake. Comparisons were made between groups defined by partners' sex and over time by comparing with Natsal-3 (2010-12). FINDINGS: In Natsal-4, overall prevalence of Chlamydia trachomatis, Neisseria gonorrhoeae, and Trichomonas vaginalis was less than 1·0%. C trachomatis prevalence was highest in women aged 16-24 years (4·0%, 95% CI 1·3-11·7). STI-associated behaviours (composite) were most prevalent in young people (aged 16-24 years) with only opposite-sex partners (women 26·5%, 95% CI 20·2-33·9; men 29·4%, 22·5-37·6), women reporting sex with women and men (WSWM; 60·0%, 49·0-70·1), and men reporting sex with men (MSM; 57·1%, 48·6-65·3). Among those with only opposite-sex partners, past-year uptake was higher in women than men for sexual health service use (women 8·3%, 7·2-9·6; men 3·9%, 3·0-5·1), HIV testing (women 5·8%, 4·9-7·0; men 2·8%, 2·1-3·7), and chlamydia testing (women 8·4%, 7·1-10·1; men 4·7%, 3·4-6·4). Among participants reporting STI-associated behaviours, apart from MSM (47·3%, 36·1-58·8), the majority of people who reported STI-associated behaviours had not taken up services (eg, for sexual health services in participants with opposite-sex partners: women 73·8%, 67·8-79·1; men 84·9%, 79·4-89·4; WSWM 68·6%, 54.1-80.2). Between Natsal-3 and Natsal-4, HIV testing increased in MSM, sexual health service use decreased in young men with only opposite-sex partners, and chlamydia testing markedly declined (eg, in all women aged 16-24 years: Natsal-3 54·2%, 51·4-57·0; Natsal-4 17·8%, 12·7-24·5). INTERPRETATION: Many people remain at behavioural risk for STIs, particularly young people, WSWM, and MSM. Most people with STI-associated behaviours had not used sexual health services in the past year. Declining chlamydia testing and high prevalence in young women might cause reproductive harm. Universal sexual health services remain essential. FUNDING: Wellcome Trust, Economic and Social Research Council, and the National Institute for Health and Care Research.

items.title: Human papillomavirus (HPV) infection, vaccination, and cervical screening in Britain from 1999 to 2024: findings from the repeated cross-sectional National Surveys of Sexual Attitudes and Lifestyles (Natsal)
items.abstract: BACKGROUND: Human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccination and cervical screening have substantially reduced overall cervical cancer risk, but differences in uptake must be quantified to inform equitable access. This study aimed to provide population-level evidence of the impact of HPV vaccination on HPV types 16 and 18 (hereafter HPV-16/18) prevalence in England, Scotland, and Wales (hereafter Britain), and uptake of cervical cancer prevention interventions (ie, vaccination and screening), 15 years after the introduction of the vaccination programme in 2008. METHODS: We conducted the National Surveys of Sexual Attitudes and Lifestyles (Natsal), which are nationally representative, cross-sectional population surveys with individual-level data and HPV testing of biosamples. Data from Natsal-2 (1999-2001; before the vaccination programme was introduced, and included urine biosamples), Natsal-3 (2010-12; early in the vaccination programme, and included urine biosamples), and Natsal-4 (2022-24; after the vaccination programme was established, and included vaginal swab and urine biosamples) were analysed. Age-adjusted prevalence ratios (aPRs) for HPV-16/18 infection were estimated among women eligible for routine vaccination (born from Sept 1, 1995) compared with same-aged women before the vaccination programme was introduced. Combined Natsal-4 probability and non-probability data assessed factors associated with self-reported HPV vaccination and cervical screening. FINDINGS: Among 10 418 Natsal-4 women (aged 16-59 years), 1059 women in the probability sample group (aged 18-44 years) provided usable biosamples (Natsal-2 n=1849; Natsal-3 n=2407). HPV-16/18 prevalence was 86% lower (aPR 0·14, 95% CI 0·02-0·84) among those aged 18-29 years in Natsal-4 (1·6%, 95% CI 0·3-8·2) than in Natsal-2 (8·7%, 95% CI 6·7-11·3). All HPV-16/18 infections reported in Natsal-4 occurred in unvaccinated women. Of 733 routine vaccination-eligible women, 23·0% (95% CI 19·4-27·0) reported being unvaccinated. Among 3530 women (aged 25-59 years) eligible for cervical screening, 5·3% (95% CI 4·4-6·3) reported never attending screening. Non-uptake of vaccination and screening was higher among minority ethnic groups, religious groups, and those born outside the UK. Prevalence of high-risk, non-vaccine-preventable HPV (HPV 35, 39, 51, 56, and 59) infections was 4·9% (95% CI 3·7-6·4) in the total population, without any statistically significant differences between these subgroups. Women with higher-risk sexual behaviours were more likely to both be vaccinated and attend for screening. INTERPRETATION: Britain's HPV vaccination programme has driven a dramatic decline in HPV-16/18 prevalence and WHO cervical cancer elimination targets might be achievable overall if this is sustained. However, women from minority ethnic groups, religious groups, and those not born in the UK are less likely to be vaccinated and screened while remaining at risk. It is crucial to improve the reach of prevention interventions to more equitably reduce cervical cancer morbidity and mortality. FUNDING: Wellcome Trust, Economic and Social Research Council, and the National Institute for Health Research.

items.title: Sexual and reproductive health: beyond the headlines
Prevalence and trends in sexual behaviour in Britain from 1990 to 2024: findings from the repeated cross-sectional National Surveys of Sexual Attitudes and Lifestyles (Natsal)
items.abstract: BACKGROUND: Contemporary data on sexual behaviour are needed to inform and evaluate sexual and reproductive health strategies and services and understand societal shifts. In this assessment of the National Surveys of Sexual Attitudes and Lifestyles (Natsal), we aimed to provide up-to-date prevalence estimates and examine changes in key sexual behaviours in Britain reported between 1990 and 2024. METHODS: The Natsal study is repeat cross-sectional probability-sample surveys of the British population, undertaken approximately decennially since 1990. Natsal-4 (2022-24) used interviewer-administered and self-completion questionnaires, among two probability samples: an address-based sample and a probability panel. Data were weighted to broadly align with Britain's sociodemographic structure. In Natsal-4, prevalence of sexual experiences, partner numbers, frequency of sex, and online behaviours are presented by age and gender among participants aged 16-59 years, with changes in prevalence across Natsal surveys presented by age and gender among participants aged 16-44 years. FINDINGS: Of 6719 Natsal-4 participants (aged 16-59 years), 89·4% (95% CI 88·3-90·4) reported ever having sex (median five lifetime partners for both women and men). In the past year, 77·0% (95% CI 75·6-78·4) reported having had sex, and 65·5% (63·9-67·0) reported one sexual partner. Reporting at least one new partner in the past year was highest among participants aged 16-24 years (21·7% [95% CI 17·3-26·8] in women, 30·1% [24·5-36·4] in men). Pornography use and sexting (sending or receiving sexual images) in the past year were more common among men (80·7% [95% CI 78·6-82·6] and 26·0% [23·9-28·3], respectively) than among women (36·6% [34·7-38·5] and 22·2% [20·5-23·9], respectively); both were higher among younger age groups. The proportion of 16-24-year-olds who reported never having had sex increased from 18·9% (95% CI 17·0-20·9) in Natsal-3 (2010-12) to 37·7% (36·2-43·1) in Natsal-4 (2022-24) among women; and 18·2% (16·2-20·4) to 28·4% (23·1-34·5) among men. Reporting of same-sex sex increased among 16-44-year-olds from 6·8% (95% CI 6·1-7·6) in 2010-12 to 14·0% (12·4-15·7) in 2022-24 among women, and from 4·0% (3·3-4·7) to 12·3% (10·4-14·5) among men. Among 16-44-year-olds, we found a decline in average frequency of sex from four times per month in Natsal-1 (1990) to twice per month in Natsal-4 (2022-24). INTERPRETATION: Sexual behaviour in Britain has shifted markedly since 1990, including a recent decline in sexual experience among young people and increased reporting of same-sex attraction and behaviour across all age groups. Sexual and reproductive health policies and services remain essential and must adapt to shifting needs and new areas of risk and vulnerability, including safe engagement in online sexual activity. FUNDING: Wellcome Trust, the UK Economic and Social Research Council, and the UK National Institute for Health Research.

items.title: Strengthened inequality monitoring is needed to progress global health equity goals
Population surveys reveal generational changes in sexual and reproductive health
Sexual wellbeing in Britain: findings from the fourth National Survey of Sexual Attitudes and Lifestyles (Natsal-4)
items.abstract: BACKGROUND: Sexual wellbeing is an individual state of feeling respected, safe, and comfortable with sex and sexuality, and having self-esteem, agency, and support in one's sexual life. It is related to, but distinct from, sexual function and sexual health. The epidemiology of sexual wellbeing in a general population is not well understood. We aimed to examine inequalities in low sexual wellbeing, and discover associations with sexual behaviour, sexual and reproductive health experiences, and general and mental health. We sought to understand which individual items within our validated 13-item measure of sexual wellbeing (the Natsal-SW) are most strongly associated with key sexual health behaviours and indicators. METHODS: We conducted the fourth National Survey of Sexual Attitudes and Lifestyles (Natsal-4), which is a large nationally representative cross-sectional study of people aged 16-59 years who are resident in Britain (data used here collected between Sept 20, 2022, and Dec 3, 2023). 4160 participants reporting sexual experience ever completed the Natsal-SW; standardised score range 0-52, low selected as ≤33, and high as ≥48. Focusing attention on those with most need, we used age-adjusted logistic regressions to examine associations with low sexual wellbeing. FINDINGS: The weighted prevalence of current low sexual wellbeing was similar in women (14·3% [95% CI 12·6-16·3]) and men (13·7% [11·7-15·9]), but high sexual wellbeing was slightly less prevalent in women than men (20·7% [95% CI 18·7- 22·8] vs 24·4% [21·8- 27·1]; p=0·024). Nine items on Natsal-SW differed by gender; notably women were more likely to report feeling upset with others about past sexual events, and men to report feeling ashamed about sexual thoughts. The odds of low sexual wellbeing were greater among young people (aged 16-24 years), individuals from sexual and gender minorities, individuals reporting lower income and, among women only, educational level. Low sexual wellbeing was associated with reporting first sex after age 25 years, symptoms of sexually-transmitted infections and less frequent sex in the past month, at least four partners, distressing sexual problems, and sexual violence in the past year, and at least one same-sex partner in the past 5 years. Low sexual wellbeing was associated with currently screening positive for depression (Patient Health Questionnaire-2-item) and anxiety (Generalised Anxiety Disorder-2-item) symptoms and low mental wellbeing, particularly among men. Associations between key sexual health and behaviour indicators, and low sexual wellbeing, remained after adjustment for mental health. INTERPRETATION: Low sexual wellbeing is unequally distributed, and patterns of association differ notably from sexual health. These data support future inclusion of sexual wellbeing in population health policy and intervention. FUNDING: Wellcome Trust, the UK Economic and Social Research Council, and the UK National Institute for Health and Care Research.

items.title: Myocardial injury with non-obstructive coronary arteries: diagnostic pathways and stratified treatment
items.abstract: Myocardial injury with non-obstructive coronary arteries (MINOCA), formerly known as myocardial infarction with non-obstructive coronary arteries, challenges the long-standing assumption that myocardial infarction is synonymous with obstructive coronary artery disease. Rather than a paradox, MINOCA reflects the limitations of angiography-centred paradigms and the complexity of contemporary cardiovascular pathophysiology. Consistent with this updated definition, this Review approaches MINOCA as a working diagnosis that encompasses diverse mechanisms, including plaque disruption, coronary vasomotor dysfunction, microvascular disease, and non-coronary conditions. We propose a pragmatic, mechanism-oriented framework for selecting and sequencing complementary investigations, highlighting how intracoronary imaging, cardiac magnetic resonance, and coronary functional testing can be integrated according to the clinical scenario to refine diagnosis, while balancing diagnostic yield with procedural risk and resource availability. We discuss the implications for management, emphasising that treatment should be guided by underlying pathophysiology rather than a uniform approach derived from obstructive myocardial infarction. Emerging evidence supports the implementation of a stratified therapy to improve patient-centred outcomes. Finally, we discuss research priorities for improving mechanism-specific diagnosis and treatment, arguing that MINOCA represents both a conceptual advance and a transitional step toward a mechanism-based taxonomy of myocardial injury and infarction.

items.title: Envudeucitinib in moderate-to-severe plaque psoriasis (ONWARD1 and ONWARD2): results from two replicate, multicentre, double-blinded, placebo-controlled and active comparator-controlled, phase 3 randomised controlled trials
items.abstract: Background Safe and highly effective oral treatment options for patients with moderate-to-severe psoriasis are scarce. Here, we aimed to assess the efficacy and safety of envudeucitinib (ESK-001), an investigational next-generation, highly selective, oral, allosteric tyrosine kinase 2 inhibitor, in patients with moderate-to-severe plaque psoriasis. Methods ONWARD1 (NCT06586112) and ONWARD2 (NCT06588738) are completed, replicate, multicentre, randomised, double-blinded, placebo-controlled and active comparator-controlled, phase 3 trials that enrolled patients in 333 sites (eg, research and medical centres, private practices, and hospitals) across 19 countries. Adults with a diagnosis of plaque psoriasis for at least 6 months, body surface area of at least 10%, and Psoriasis Area Severity Index (PASI) of at least 12 were randomly assigned 2:1:1 to oral envudeucitinib 40 mg twice daily, placebo, or apremilast 30 mg twice daily for 24 weeks of treatment. At week 16, patients receiving placebo were transitioned to envudeucitinib. Coprimary endpoints were at least 75% improvement from baseline in Psoriasis Area Severity Index (PASI 75) and static Physician's Global Assessment (sPGA) of 0 or 1 at week 16 (envudeucitinib vs placebo). Secondary endpoints were assessed at weeks 16 and 24 (envudeucitinib vs placebo and/or apremilast). Safety assessments included adverse events and laboratory parameters. Findings From July 25, 2024, to Dec 18, 2025, 912 and 859 patients were randomly assigned to ONWARD1 and ONWARD2, respectively (envudeucitinib, n=459 and n=433; placebo, n=230 and n=211; apremilast, n=223 and n=215). In both trials, coprimary and all key secondary endpoints were met (all p Interpretation Envudeucitinib improved both skin signs and patient-reported outcomes, and maintained favourable tolerability, supporting its role as a promising oral treatment for patients with moderate-to-severe plaque psoriasis. Funding Alumis.

Identifying which patients with metastatic hormone-sensitive prostate cancer benefit most from androgen receptor pathway inhibitors (STOPCAP): a systematic review and meta-analysis of individual participant data
items.abstract: BACKGROUND: Adding novel androgen receptor pathway inhibitors (ARPIs) to standard of care improves outcomes for patients with metastatic hormone-sensitive prostate cancer (mHSPC), but whether benefits are consistent across patient subgroups remains uncertain. We aimed to assess whether ARPI effects vary according to participant or tumour characteristics, or by docetaxel use. METHODS: In this systematic review and meta-analysis (STOPCAP), we sought individual participant data for completed trials adding ARPIs to standard of care. Intention-to-treat, two-stage, common-effect meta-analysis of hazard ratios (HRs) were adjusted for a common set of covariates and docetaxel use. Main effects were based on overall survival. Interaction effects were based on progression-free survival (PFS) to maximise power, then overall survival whenever significant PFS interactions were found. Prostate cancer-specific survival (PCSS), exploratory competing risk analyses of causes of death, and 5-year absolute effects were estimated overall and for key subgroups. FINDINGS: Individual participant data were available from seven eligible trial comparisons (two comparisons from STAMPEDE, LATITUDE, PEACE-1, SWOG-S1216, ENZAMET, and TITAN) and 7778 participants (66% of total eligible). In the primary analysis of six trials (6467 participants and 3322 events), adding an ARPI improved overall survival (HR 0·66 [95% CI 0·62-0·710]; p<0·0001), with a 13% absolute improvement in 5-year survival. Similar results were observed for PFS. No evidence of effect variation was observed by ARPI class, docetaxel use, disease volume, Gleason score, performance status, or metastatic burden. ARPI effects on PFS varied by continuous age (interaction p=0·0005) and by age group (interaction p=0·0027), with patterns differing by ARPI class (biosynthesis versus receptor inhibitors: p=0·022) and similar results for overall survival. Based on individual participant data from three abiraterone trials (100% of eligible participants), effects on overall survival varied by age group (interaction p=0·0006), with an absolute 5-year improvement of about 15% for patients younger than 75 years but minimal benefit (about 1%) in those aged 75 years or older. Abiraterone improved 5-year PCSS across all age groups (11-18%), with a similar reduction in cumulative incidence of cancer deaths. However, in patients aged 75 years or older, abiraterone was associated with a 12% increase in 5-year cumulative incidence of non-cancer deaths. Based on limited individual participant data for receptor inhibitors (two trials; 35% of eligible participants), there was no clear evidence that effects on overall survival varied by age group (interaction p=0·078), and results from the STAMPEDE trial comparison of combined abiraterone and enzalutamide were similar. INTERPRETATION: Adding an ARPI to standard of care significantly improved overall survival for most patients with mHSPC. Although abiraterone improved cancer-specific survival for all, non-cancer mortality was increased among older patients. Further individual participant data are needed to fully assess the effects of androgen receptor inhibitors by age. Current data highlight the importance of considering age and comorbidities when selecting ARPI therapy. FUNDING: UK Medical Research Council and Prostate Cancer UK.

items.abstract: Reporting guidelines are sets of recommendations and guidance for authors on how to report their research.Their aim is to improve the completeness and transparency of published research and, ultimately, its reproducibility and usability.Journals increasingly require authors to follow reporting guidelines and submit completed checklists alongside their manuscripts, yet poorly reported research is common. 1 Journals need to consider how they can better support authors to use reporting guidelines effectively.We discussed this issue repeatedly with the late statistician Doug Altman.In 2018, together we published a scoping review of interventions to improve adherence to reporting guidelines. 2 Journals requiring authors to submit a completed checklist was one of the most common approaches, but we found no evidence that it improved the completeness of reporting of published articles.Our own research made us increasingly sceptical that the problem could be solved simply by requiring more checklists to be completed.We found frequent discrepancies between what authors reported in submitted checklists and what appeared in their published papers.3 Other research, including a randomised trial, also questioned whether this approach improves reporting.

items.abstract: Objectives To evaluate trends in pregabalin use and overdose in Australia and examine temporal relationships with media coverage (December 2018), prescribing and dispensing restrictions (April 2020), and boxed warnings (February 2021). Design Retrospective observational study of dispensing and overdose data, with changepoint, interrupted time series, and latent class analysis. Setting and participants Pharmaceutical Benefits Scheme data (PBS; 10% random sample of people with drug subsidies) and overdose calls (self-harm, recreational use, and misuse) reported to Australia’s largest Poisons Centre (50% national sample), 2016-24. Main outcome measures Population adjusted rates of dispensing and overdose, timing of breakpoints and rate ratios, proportion of people who use pregabalin at high risk of misuse. Results 227 864 people were dispensed 3 441 851 pregabalin prescriptions in the PBS 10% sample and 4871 pregabalin overdose calls were made to the Poisons Centre. Pregabalin use peaked in 2018 before plateauing and declining. Three breakpoints were found in dispensing data, with major decreases in level and slope: December 2018, May 2020, December 2021. The combined rate ratio for dispensing was 0.748 (95% confidence interval 0.700 to 0.800). Compared with the projected historical trend in the absence of interventions (counterfactual), approximately 118 390 (93 960 to 140 940) fewer pregabalin prescriptions were recorded nationally in December 2021, and an ongoing reduction of 0.7% (0.5% to 0.9%) was found each month. All breakpoints were associated with declines in overdose rates, with a combined rate ratio of 0.532 (95% CI 0.406 to 0.695). This reduction corresponded to approximately 41.3 (26.9 to 52.4) fewer pregabalin overdose calls in December 2021 and an ongoing reduction of 1.6% (1.0% to 2.3%) each month. Latent class analysis of 57 744 people dispensed pregabalin in the 12 months after the final breakpoint revealed four groups. The high risk group (7790, 13.5%) were more likely male, younger, dispensed more pregabalin, with shorter refill interval and high rates of opioids and benzodiazepine co-use (5120 (65.7%) and 2455 (31.5%), respectively). Conclusions Pregabalin use and overdose in Australia have declined in recent years. Major decreases in trend corresponded with media coverage (December 2018) and prescribing and dispensing restrictions (May 2020). The third breakpoint may be a delayed impact of boxed warnings (implemented February 2021). These findings suggest that regulatory and risk communication measures may contribute to reducing pregabalin related harm.

Effect of discontinuing antihypertensives on perioperative hypotension in older patients before non-cardiac surgery: multicentre, randomised, double blind, controlled trial
items.abstract: Objective To determine whether discontinuing versus continuing angiotensin converting enzyme (ACE) inhibitors or angiotensin receptor blockers (ARBs) on the morning of surgery reduces perioperative hypotension in older patients undergoing non-cardiac surgery. Design Multicentre, randomised, double blind, placebo controlled trial. Setting Five tertiary teaching hospitals in China, November 2020 to December 2023. Participants 2036 older patients (60-80 years) using ACE inhibitors or ARBs for at least two weeks and scheduled for non-cardiac surgery under general anaesthesia. Interventions Patients were randomised to receive their usual ACE inhibitor or ARB or a placebo in identical capsules on the morning of surgery. Main outcome measures The primary outcome was the incidence of perioperative hypotension (mean blood pressure <65 mm Hg or a =30% decrease from baseline requiring treatment). Secondary outcomes included duration of hypotension, requirement for a vasopressor, intraoperative fluid volume, postoperative hypotension, and 30 day complications (neurocognitive disorders, major cardiocerebral events) or mortality. Results 2012 patients (mean age 68.8 years; 54.4% male) completed the study: 1004 were included in the antihypertensive group and 1008 in the no antihypertensive group. The incidence of perioperative hypotension was lower in the no antihypertensive group (314/1008, 31.2%) versus antihypertensive group (457/1004, 45.5%): adjusted odds ratio 0.52 (95% confidence interval (CI) 0.43 to 0.63); absolute risk difference -14.4% (95% CI -18.5% to -10.1%); P<0.001. The duration of hypotension and requirement for a vasopressor were both reduced in the no antihypertensive group: adjusted mean difference -1.3 minutes (95% CI -1.8 to -0.8 minutes) and 28.5% v 41.1%; adjusted odds ratio 0.54 (95% CI 0.44 to 0.66). Intraoperative fluid volume, postoperative hypotension, 30 day complications, and mortality did not differ significantly between groups. Conclusions Discontinuing ACE inhibitors or ARBs on the morning of surgery in older patients with hypertension statistically significantly reduced perioperative hypotension and the requirement for vasopressors without increasing 30 day complications or mortality. This simple strategy provides high certainty evidence for preoperative drug management in this patient population. Trial registration Chinese Clinical Trial Registry NCT2000039376 .

Effect of intensive blood pressure control on cognitive outcomes and brain structures in adults with type 2 diabetes: prespecified analysis of secondary outcomes of BPROAD randomised controlled trial
items.abstract: Objective To evaluate the effect of intensive compared with standard treatment of systolic blood pressure (SBP) on cognitive outcomes and brain structures in adults with type 2 diabetes. Design Multicentre, open label, outcome assessor masked, randomised controlled trial. Setting 145 clinical centres across seven geographical regions in China. Participants 12 821 adults aged ≥50 years with type 2 diabetes, raised SBP, and increased cardiovascular risk, of whom 12 434 without probable dementia at baseline were included in this cognitive ancillary study. Further assessments were performed annually and at the end of study. Interventions Participants were randomly assigned to receive intensive treatment targeting SBP <120 mm Hg or standard treatment targeting SBP <140 mm Hg for up to five years. Main outcome measures The primary cognitive outcome was a composite of all cause dementia or mild cognitive impairment. Secondary cognitive outcomes included all cause dementia, mild cognitive impairment, changes in cognitive functions, and changes in brain magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) characteristics. A subset of participants underwent brain MRI at baseline (n=862) and at the end of study (n=605) to assess changes in white matter lesion volume and total brain volume. Results 6219 participants were assigned to receive intensive treatment and 6215 to receive standard treatment. Baseline mean age was 63.7 years, and 5567 (44.8%) participants were women. After one year, mean SBP was 121.6 mm Hg in the intensive treatment group and 133.2 mm Hg in the standard treatment group. During a median follow-up of 3.8 years, the primary cognitive outcome of all cause dementia or mild cognitive impairment occurred in 747 participants (3.69 events per 100 person years) in the intensive treatment group and 783 participants (3.89 events per 100 person years) in the standard treatment group (hazard ratio 0.96, 95% confidence interval (CI) 0.86 to 1.06; P=0.38). In the MRI substudy (428 intensive treatment v 434 standard treatment), the intensive treatment group had a smaller increase in white matter lesion volume compared with the standard treatment group (between group difference −0.09 inverse hyperbolic sine (asinh) transformed cm 3 , 95% CI −0.15 to −0.02; P=0.01). Conclusions Over a median of about four years, no statistically significant difference in incidence of a composite of all cause dementia or mild cognitive impairment was observed among adults with type 2 diabetes receiving standard treatment of SBP (target <140 mm Hg) and intensive treatment (target <120 mm Hg). Intensive treatment was, however, associated with a reduction in the accrual of cerebral white matter lesion volume. Trial registration ClinicalTrials.gov NCT03808311 .

Effects of plastic exposure on human health
items.abstract: Plastic pollution is a critical environmental and public health challenge, with growing evidence linking human exposure to microplastics, nanoplastics, and associated chemicals to adverse health outcomes. This review summarises current knowledge on the health effects of plastic exposure, addressing both established findings and critical knowledge gaps. We examine human exposure to plastics and associated health risks based on available clinical and epidemiological evidence. Additionally, we explore chemicals associated with plastic, including their potential as carcinogens and disruptors of endocrine and immune function. Recognising the urgent need for preventive measures, we examine emerging strategies for reducing plastic burdens, including global regulatory efforts like the United Nations Plastics Treaty and proposed public health guidelines. By integrating current evidence, this review aims to provide a foundation for advancing research and informing strategies to mitigate health risks associated with plastic.

items.title: Effect of intrapartum hyoscine butylbromide and sodium bicarbonate on spontaneous vaginal birth in nulliparous women after induction of labour (SAINT): multicentre randomised placebo controlled factorial trial
items.abstract: Objective To determine whether intrapartum hyoscine butylbromide, sodium bicarbonate, and their combination increase the rate of spontaneous vaginal birth in nulliparous women undergoing induction of labour. Design Multicentre, randomised, double blind, placebo controlled, 2×2 factorial phase 3 trial (SAINT). Setting 11 Norwegian hospitals providing comprehensive obstetric care. Participants Nulliparous women aged 18-50 years with a singleton live fetus in cephalic presentation at term with an indication for induction of labour. Interventions Participants were randomly assigned (1:1:1:1) to oral sodium bicarbonate (4×1 g per dose) plus intravenous hyoscine butylbromide (20 mg per dose), oral sodium bicarbonate plus intravenous placebo, oral placebo plus intravenous hyoscine butylbromide, or double placebo. The investigational medicinal product was administered at the onset of active labour and repeated every four hours to a maximum of three doses. Main outcome measure Spontaneous vaginal birth (no instrumental or caesarean delivery). Results Between 4 January 2023 and 29 January 2025, 3094 nulliparous women were randomised, and 2963 comprised the full analysis set. Spontaneous vaginal birth occurred in 57% (422/741) in the bicarbonate plus hyoscine butylbromide arm, 61% (445/734) in the bicarbonate arm, 61% (449/741) in the hyoscine butylbromide arm, and 56% (422/747) in the double placebo arm. Marginal risk differences for spontaneous vaginal birth compared with double placebo were -0.2 (95% confidence interval -5.1 to 4.7; P=0.93) percentage points for combined treatment, 3.1 (-1.7 to 8.0; P=0.21) percentage points for bicarbonate, and 4.0 (-0.8 to 8.9; P=0.10) percentage points for hyoscine butylbromide. Serious adverse events were similar between groups, and no treatment related serious morbidity or deaths were observed. Conclusions No clear evidence was found that intrapartum hyoscine butylbromide, sodium bicarbonate, or their combination increased spontaneous vaginal birth compared with placebo. Although small beneficial effects cannot be excluded, the findings do not support routine intrapartum use of either agent to facilitate spontaneous vaginal birth after induction of labour. Trial registration European Clinical Trials Database (EudraCT; 2021-000392-37); EU Clinical Trials Information System (CTIS; EU CT number 2024-511848-55-00); ClinicalTrials.gov ( NCT05719467 ).

items.title: Physical activity coaching and text messaging for adults with mobility limitations (ComeBACK): hybrid type 1 effectiveness implementation randomised controlled trial
items.abstract: Objective To evaluate the effectiveness of a physical activity coaching intervention compared with text messaging intervention and waitlist control in adults with mobility limitations. Design Three arm, pragmatic, superiority, hybrid type 1 effectiveness implementation randomised controlled trial. Setting Health services and general communities across five Australian states, 19 December 2018 to 7 March 2023. Participants 512 community dwelling adults (=18 years) who self-reported mobility limitations (difficulty or inability to walk 800 m, with or without a walking aid) but were still able to leave home without physical assistance from another person. Interventions Participants were randomly assigned in a 1:1:1 allocation ratio to: a six month, multicomponent intervention including fortnightly physiotherapist delivered telephone coaching (coaching group, n=172); a six month, multicomponent intervention including regular unidirectional text messages (texting group, n=171); and no intervention for six months, followed by the six month text messaging intervention (waitlist control group, n=169). Participants and physiotherapists were unmasked to group allocation. Main outcome measure The primary outcome was device measured mean daily steps at six months, analysed according to treatment allocation using all available data. Outcome assessors and data analysts were masked to group allocation. Results Participants� mean age was 69 years (standard deviation (SD) 10 years) and 76% (n=388/511) were women. More than half (n=263/508, 51%) of participants reported multiple long term conditions as the main reason for their mobility limitation. At six months, mean daily steps were 931 higher (95% confidence interval 409 to 1452 steps; P=0.001) in the coaching group (mean 7256 (SD 3736) steps) compared with waitlist group (6526 (3003) steps); and 571 steps higher (58 to 1084, P=0.03) compared with the texting group (6529 (3029) steps). Mean daily steps in the texting group were 359 higher (-91 to 810, P=0.12) compared with the waitlist group, but this was not statistically significant. The number of adverse events was similar between groups (11/172 (6%) in the coaching group , 7/171 (4%) in the texting group, and 13/169 (8%) in the waitlist group) and none were serious. Conclusion A person centred coaching intervention produced modest increases in physical activity and was more effective than a less intensive texting intervention or no intervention among adults with mobility limitations. Trial registration Australian New Zealand Clinical Trials Registry NCT12618001983291 .

items.title: How to make the most of your paediatric emergency department placement
items.abstract: The paediatric emergency department (ED) can feel like a separate world from adult medicine. The patient population is different, the conditions unique, and there is often a whole new décor (I have yet to see a SpongeBob mural in majors). It’s little wonder students can feel daunted when embarking on their paediatric ED stint. The clinical emphasis here is less on establishing a definitive diagnosis and more on the rapid assessment of risk and the early identification of the sick child. With over 6.3 million attendances in 2024-25 alone,1 the ability to recognise deterioration in children who may decompensate quickly is an essential clinical skill. Given that many medical schools offer only a short attachment in paediatric emergency medicine, preparation is critical. This article provides practical, student focused strategies to help you approach the placement with confidence and make the most of this demanding but highly rewarding learning environment. ### Revise the basics You should learn common paediatric presentations and how they differ from adult medicine (box 1). The saying “children are not just small adults” rings true, especially as children often compensate better but deteriorate faster. items.title: Advances in the management of myasthenia gravis
items.abstract: Myasthenia gravis is an autoimmune disorder of the neuromuscular junction characterised by fluctuating fatigable weakness of skeletal muscles. Advances have led to the identification of distinct antibody subtypes and expanding therapeutic options, transforming myasthenia gravis from a disease of significant morbidity and mortality to one that is increasingly manageable. This review presents a comprehensive overview of myasthenia gravis, including its epidemiology, pathogenesis, classification, diagnostic strategies, and treatment modalities. Established therapies are discussed, including acetylcholinesterase inhibitors, corticosteroids, conventional oral immunosuppressants, intravenous immunoglobulin, plasma exchange, B cell depleting agents, complement inhibitors, neonatal fragment crystallisable receptor inhibitors, and thymectomy. A dedicated section highlights emerging treatments. Special considerations for pregnancy, myasthenic crisis, and individualised treatment approaches are emphasised. Physician-patient communication is highlighted as a critical factor in optimising adherence and outcomes. Effective integration of novel therapies into clinical practice depends on a clear understanding of their mechanisms, safety profiles, and applicability across diverse patient populations. As therapeutic complexity increases, improved clinical outcomes will require continued refinement of clinical tools, treatment algorithms, optimal communication strategies, and robust data to guide evidence based decision making.

Prenatal exposure to drug treatment for attention deficit/hyperactivity disorder and risk of neurodevelopmental disorders: Scandinavian multinational cohort study
items.abstract: Objective To assess whether prenatal exposure to drug treatment for attention deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) increases the risk of neurodevelopmental disorders in children. Design Population based cohort study. Setting Nationwide register data on births, dispensed drugs, and specialist healthcare diagnoses from Denmark, Norway, and Sweden. Participants 3 643 376 children born in 2000-21 followed up for a median 9 years after birth in Sweden and 10 years in Norway and Denmark. Interventions Prenatal exposure, defined as ≥1 filled prescription for ADHD drug treatment anytime during pregnancy or in the second/third trimester (≥98 days after the last menstrual period). Analyses were also done for monotherapy with methylphenidate, amphetamines, and atomoxetine. Unexposed pregnancies had no filled prescriptions for ADHD drugs during pregnancy. Main outcome measures Neurodevelopmental disorders (any, subgroups, and individual disorders), identified on the basis of inpatient and outpatient diagnoses in specialist healthcare. Propensity score overlap weighted Cox proportional hazards regression was used to estimate adjusted (weighted) hazard ratios and 95% confidence intervals. Data from Denmark were analysed separately, and results were pooled using random effects meta-analysis. Results 7595 (0.2%) children were prenatally exposed to any ADHD drug (5230 methylphenidate, 1510 amphetamines, 553 atomoxetine only). About one third (n=2389) were exposed in the second/third trimester. After control for confounders, neither any nor second/third trimester exposure to ADHD drugs overall or by drug type was associated with increased risk of any neurodevelopmental disorder (weighted hazard ratio 1.05, 95% confidence interval 0.98 to 1.12), behavioural and emotional disorders (1.04, 0.97 to 1.12), or disorders of psychological and intellectual development (1.06, 0.96 to 1.18). Some elevated hazard ratios for infrequent outcomes were observed but not consistently identified across analyses. Conclusions This multinational cohort study found no increased risk of childhood neurodevelopmental disorders associated with prenatal exposure to ADHD drugs. These findings strengthen existing evidence and can assist pregnant people and clinicians in weighing the benefits and risks of such treatment during pregnancy.

items.title: Preconception antidepressant use in fathers and risk of metabolic disorders in offspring: Danish population based cohort study
items.abstract: Objectives To investigate the associations between paternal antidepressant use during spermatogenesis and risk of metabolic disorders in offspring. Design Nationwide population based cohort study. Setting Danish national registers. Participants 1 365 887 liveborn singleton infants in Denmark from 2000 to 2023, followed from birth until 31 December 2023, death, emigration, or first occurrence of outcome, whichever came first. Main outcome measures Metabolic disorders in offspring, including type 2 diabetes, hypertension, hypercholesterolaemia, and overweight or obesity, were identified from hospital and prescription records. Offspring of fathers who took antidepressants during spermatogenesis (three months before pregnancy) were compared with those of fathers who did not take antidepressants during this period and fathers who used antidepressants only during pregnancy to further account for underlying paternal mental health conditions. Associations between paternal antidepressant use and metabolic disorders, collectively and individually, were estimated as propensity score weighted hazard ratios using Cox regression. Results 23 572 (1.7%) offspring were born to fathers who used antidepressants during spermatogenesis. During a mean follow-up of 12.1 years (standard deviation 7.0 years), 18 353 (1.3%) offspring were diagnosed with a metabolic disorder, including 364 whose fathers used antidepressants during spermatogenesis and 17 989 whose fathers did not use antidepressants during this period (1.39 v 1.11 events per 1000 person years, respectively). Offspring whose fathers used antidepressants during spermatogenesis had a slightly higher risk of developing metabolic disorders (weighted hazard ratio 1.20, 95% confidence interval (CI) 1.04 to 1.38) compared with offspring who were unexposed. The associations varied by specific metabolic outcomes, with weighted hazard ratios ranging from 0.81 (95% CI 0.45 to 1.47) for hypercholesterolaemia to 1.64 (95% CI 1.21 to 2.22) for hypertension. However, when compared with offspring of fathers who took antidepressants during the pregnancy period only, no increased risk was found of any metabolic disorders (0.75, 95% CI 0.58 to 0.98) or of specific metabolic disorders. Conclusions The slightly increased risk of metabolic disorders in offspring of fathers using antidepressants during spermatogenesis was probably attributable to underlying paternal mental health disorders. These findings offer reassurance for men treated with antidepressants before pregnancy.

Manually Abstracted vs Electronic Health Record Data for Risk Adjusting Hospital Postoperative Mortality
items.abstract: Importance National surgical quality improvement (QI) programs rely on manual data abstraction to produce hospital-level risk-adjusted outcomes, and while electronic health records (EHRs) could provide an efficient platform for automating data collection of model covariates, the robustness of this approach has not been explored. Objective To evaluate whether risk adjustment using EHR data performs similarly to manually abstracted model covariates for characterizing hospital-level 30-day postoperative mortality. Design, Setting, and Participants This is a national, hospital-level comparative effectiveness study using data from the Veterans Affairs Surgical Quality Improvement Program (VASQIP) and the VA Corporate Data Warehouse (CDW, a repository of national VA EHR data) to compare risk adjustment strategies within a national surgical QI program. VASQIP records were matched to patients’ corresponding CDW record. VASQIP variable correlates were created using VA EHR data. Patients aged 18 years or older who underwent a noncardiac operation at a VA facility from January 1, 2016, to September 30, 2020, with a record in VASQIP were included. Data were analyzed from April 2025 to September 2025. Main Outcomes and Measures The primary outcome was 30-day postoperative mortality. Quarterly observed to expected (OE) ratios were calculated using either EHR or manually abstracted (ie, VASQIP) variables as model covariates and compared to ascertain whether hospital performance was concordantly identified using these different risk adjustment strategies (ie, risk adjustment performed with the same variables but from different data sources). Results Among 386 157 unique patients who underwent 460 585 noncardiac operations at 113 VA facilities, mean (SD) age was 62.9 (13.4) years and 43 781 patients (9.5%) were female. Correlation in OE ratios was strong ( r = 0.98; 95% CI, 0.98-0.98). Across all quarters of data (n = 2111), 2096 hospital quarters (99.3%) were concordantly identified. Among quarters in which hospitals were identified as having higher-than-expected mortality after risk adjustment with VASQIP data (n = 42), 34 (81.0%) were concordantly identified after risk adjustment with parsimonious EHR data. Conclusions and Relevance In this comparative effectiveness study, risk adjustment with EHR data was shown to perform similarly to manually abstracted data for characterizing hospital performance in 30-day postoperative mortality. The use of EHR data for risk adjustment could facilitate automation of data extraction, increase programmatic efficiency, and improve the timeliness of data provision to stakeholders for QI efforts.

Fragmentation of Care in Violently Injured Patients
items.abstract: Importance Survivors of injuries due to violence are at risk for recurrent violent injury (RVI). After an initial violent injury, patients may seek care at multiple different health systems, leading to fragmentation of care, which is a barrier to secondary prevention efforts. Objective To quantify the missed opportunities for secondary prevention efforts in violent injury caused by fragmentation of care. Design, Setting, and Participants This retrospective cohort study used a regional health information exchange database for a major metropolitan area (Philadelphia, Pennsylvania) from January 1, 2018, through November 30, 2023. Rates of and time to RVI were calculated and then types and locations of visits within the first postinjury year were tabulated. Using multivariable logistic regression, patient and injury factors associated with RVI were identified. Patients with a visit for violent injury between January 1, 2018, through November 30, 2023, were included. Any patients without a full year of follow-up were excluded. These data were analyzed from February 2025 through December 2025. Exposure Fragmentation of care. Main Outcomes and Measures The primary outcome was RVI, defined as having another emergency department, observation or inpatient visit coded for injuries due to interpersonal violence. The association between fragmentation of care and RVI was examined, including the types of visits associated with RVI. Logistic regression modeling also examined demographic and clinical factors, as well as mechanism of injury associated with RVI. Results Of 26 368 patients with a violent injury (mean [SD] age, 38.0 [14.8] years; 10 456 [39.7%] female and 15 894 [60.3%] male), 2591 (9.8%) recurred within 1 year and 4247 (16.1%) total recurred during the study period. Risk factors for recurrence included initial firearm injury (odds ratio [OR], 3.3; 95% CI, 3.0-3.6), substance use diagnosis (OR, 1.8; 95% CI, 1.6-1.9), and psychiatric diagnoses (OR, 2.4; 95% CI, 2.2-2.6). Among those with RVI, 1701 (40.1%) received treatment for their second violent injury in a different hospital system from their index injury. All patients with RVI (4247) had at least 1 health care encounter between their index and their recurrent injury, 66.0% of which (n = 2803) sought care at multiple institutions during the study period and ultimately, on average, received 42.5% of their care in a health care system different from their index encounter. Conclusions and Relevance In this study, recurrent violent injury was common in this major metropolitan area, and single-center studies would have missed at least 40% of recurrences. All patients who went on to recur had additional health care encounters prior to that recurrence, with 66% accessing care in multiple health care systems. This study quantifies the missed opportunities for secondary prevention efforts in violent injury and highlights the importance of collaboration in areas with fragmentation of care.

items.title: Stereotactic Body Radiation Therapy vs Surgery for Stage IA Non–Small Cell Lung Cancer
items.abstract: Importance Stereotactic body radiation therapy (SBRT) is a well-established alternative to surgery for nonoperable patients with early-stage non–small cell (NSCLC) lung cancer. However, the role of SBRT in operable patients is unclear as 3 randomized clinical trials comparing SBRT with surgery were closed early because of poor accrual. Existing observational comparisons are limited by confounding because patients who receive SBRT are generally frailer and more comorbid. Objective To compare cancer-specific mortality between surgery and SBRT using proximal causal inference to adjust for unmeasured confounding due to frailty and comorbidity using proxy variables. Design, Setting, and Participants This cohort study was a national database analysis of the Surveillance, Epidemiology, and End Results (SEER)–Medicare dataset. Three treatment effect estimates were obtained with increasing control of confounding: unadjusted, standard-regression adjusted for measured confounders as in existing studies, and proximally adjusted for unmeasured confounders. Participants were patients with stage IA NSCLC who underwent sublobar resection or SBRT from 2010 to 2019, followed up through December 21, 2021. Data analysis was performed from April 2023 to August 2026. Exposures Sublobar resection vs SBRT. Negative control exposures were constructed from billing codes. Main Outcome and Measures Lung cancer–specific mortality. Negative control outcomes were constructed from other-cause mortality. Results are reported as hazard differences (HD) and 95% CI. Results A total of 4251 patients met inclusion and exclusion criteria; 2581 (60.7%) were female and 1670 (39.3%) were male. Their mean (SD) age was 75.6 (6.3) years. A total of 2558 patients underwent SBRT and 1693 underwent surgery. In the unadjusted and covariate-adjusted analyses, SBRT was associated with higher lung cancer cause-specific mortality, HD of 0.047 person-years (95% CI, 0.038-0.055) and 0.024 person-years (95% CI, 0.014-0.034), respectively. However, there was also compelling evidence of confounding due to a strong estimated association with other-cause mortality. In the proximal analysis, other-cause mortality together with negative control exposures were used to indirectly control for hidden confounders, yielding an HD of 0.012 person-years (95% CI, 0.0013-0.027). Conclusions and Relevance This study empirically showed that existing observational comparisons of SBRT and surgery are biased because of unmeasured confounding. When proximal causal inference was used to better control for confounding due to frailty and comorbidity, there continued to be a smaller but significant improvement in outcomes associated with surgery, though the effects of residual bias due to differences in pathologic and clinical staging could not be ruled out. This study demonstrates that proximal causal inference can be used to control for unmeasured confounders in a variety of settings.

Factor XI Inhibitor for Prevention of Venous Thromboembolism in Patients Undergoing Total Knee Arthroplasty
items.abstract: Importance Factor XI is critical for postoperative venous thromboembolism (VTE). Factor XI inhibition prevents VTE effectively in Western populations, yet its efficacy and safety in Chinese populations remain to be verified. Objective To investigate the efficacy and safety of a novel recombinant humanized factor XI inhibitor (KN060) in Chinese patients undergoing primary total knee arthroplasty. Design, Setting, and Participants In this multicenter, randomized, open-label, positive-controlled, phase 2 trial at 19 medical centers in China, 241 patients undergoing primary unilateral total knee arthroplasty were randomized to receive a single postoperative intravenous infusion of KN060 (2.5 mg/kg, 5.0 mg/kg, or 7.5 mg/kg) or subcutaneous enoxaparin (40 mg once daily). The study took place from December 19, 2023, through April 15, 2025, and these data were analyzed from from June 30, 2025, to September 27, 2025. Intervention Single infusion of KN060 vs daily enoxaparin. Main Outcomes and Measures The primary efficacy outcome was VTE, assessed by mandatory digital subtraction angiography (DSA) of the operated leg on days 10 to 14. The principal safety outcome was a composite of major or clinically relevant nonmajor bleeding. Results Of 241 patients enrolled, 213 were included in the efficacy analysis (157 were female [73.7%] and 56 were male [26.3%]; median [IQR] age, 68 [62-70] years). VTE occurred in 0 of 52 patients (0%) in the 2.5 mg/kg KN060 group, 1 of 52 patients (1.9%) in the 5.0 mg/kg group, and 1 of 54 patients (1.9%) in the 7.5 mg/kg group, as compared with 4 of 55 patients (7.3%) in the enoxaparin group. Each dose group of KN060 met the noninferiority end point. No major bleeding or clinically relevant nonmajor bleeding occurred in any of the patients. Minor bleeding occurred in 1.8%, 3.6%, and 1.7% of the patients in the 2.5 mg/kg, 5.0 mg/kg, and 7.5 mg/kg KN060 groups, respectively, and in 3.5% of the patients in the enoxaparin group. Conclusions and Relevance In this randomized clinical trial of a factor XI inhibitor in Chinese populations, a single intravenous dose of KN060 was effective for the prevention of VTE after total knee arthroplasty and was associated with a low risk of bleeding. Trial Registration ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT06180889

items.title: Identifying At-Risk Subgroups for Suboptimal Computed Tomography Imaging in Older Patients With Blunt Trauma
items.abstract: Importance Without standardized imaging algorithms for older trauma patients, there is high heterogeneity in the diagnosis of injuries in this vulnerable population. Objective To identify clinically distinct subgroups of older patients with blunt trauma and examine if any groups have a high likelihood of suboptimal computed tomography (CT) imaging. Design, Setting, and Participants This cohort study was a secondary analysis of the multicenter Scanning the Aged trial (November 2020 to December 2021), which included 5496 patients with blunt trauma 65 years or older from 18 trauma centers. Latent class analysis identified patient subgroups using 10 categorized indicators: origin of injury, age, Charlson Comorbidity Index, functional status, Glasgow Coma Scale score, intoxication, antiplatelet or anticoagulant use, emergency department intervention, time since injury, and Injury Severity Score. Data analysis was performed from August 2025 to February 2026. Exposure Latent class membership. Main Outcomes and Measures Suboptimal imaging (a mismatch between injuries and initial diagnostic CT performed), pan-scan utilization, and in-hospital mortality. Results Among 5496 patients with blunt trauma, 2990 (54.4%) were female and 2506 (45.6%) male; the median (IQR) age was 79 (71-86) years. The 4-class model was selected as the optimal solution based on a comparison of model fit indices and interpretability across competing latent class models. Class 1 (scene arrival and moderate injury, n = 417; 33.1%) comprised younger patients with preserved function. Class 2 (frail with fall, n = 519; 41.3%) included older adults (median [IQR] age, 84 [78-89] years) with functional dependence. Class 3 (transfer, n = 219; 17.4%) was defined by transfer status. Class 4 (critical trauma, n = 103; 8.2%) represented severely injured patients. Suboptimal imaging rates varied significantly across classes (from 2.5% to 11.0%), with class 3 showing nearly 4-fold higher odds (odds ratio [OR], 3.85; 95% CI, 1.67-8.90; P = .002). Class 4 had 45.6% mortality (47/103) with 16-fold higher adjusted odds of death (adjusted OR, 16.40; 95% CI, 5.40-49.81; P &lt; .001). Pan-scan utilization ranged from 49.8% (109/219) to 70.9% (73/103) across classes, with adjusted odds not differing between all classes. Conclusions and Relevance This study identified 4 distinct phenotypes of older patients with blunt trauma and varying imaging needs. Patients transferred from nontrauma centers to trauma centers demonstrated the highest risk for suboptimal imaging, highlighting care coordination gaps. Critical trauma patients had markedly elevated mortality, with a 16-fold higher adjusted odds of death. These findings may support developing targeted imaging protocols based on patient phenotype, with particular attention to patients with the highest risk of diagnostic gaps.

items.title: Sociobehavioral Comorbidities and Outcomes After Colectomy in a National United States Veteran Cohort
items.abstract: Objective: To evaluate the independent association between sociobehavioral comorbidities (SBCs) and complications after colectomies in a national Veteran cohort. Background: SBCs are determinants of health outcomes, and Veterans represent a high-vulnerability population. However, the relationship of SBCs with postoperative complications remains understudied, and current surgical risk models underestimate risk among patients with significant SBC burden. Methods: We conducted an observational study of Veterans undergoing elective colectomy included in the Veterans Affairs Surgical Quality Improvement Program (VASQIP). Structured data from the Veteran Health Administration Corporate Data Warehouse were used to identify 6 SBC phenotypes (mental health disorder, suicide risk, substance use, social isolation, housing instability, and food insecurity) across 3 preoperative ascertainment windows: ≤90 days, ≤365 days, and lifetime. The outcome was any 30-day VASQIP-defined postoperative complication. Multilevel logistic regression estimated associations between SBCs and complications. Results: Among 38,188 Veterans undergoing colectomy between 2009 and 2025, the median age was 66 years; 5% were female; 30% were non-white; and 48% had cancer. Mental health disorder, social isolation, or substance use were each associated with an 8%–40% increase in the odds of a complication across all ascertainment windows. Within the most proximal window, risk of complication increased as SBC burden increased: 16% increased odds with 1 SBC (aOR 1.16, 95% CI: 1.09–1.23) and 80% increased odds with 4–6 SBCs (aOR 1.80, 95% CI: 1.32–2.36). Conclusions: In a national Veteran cohort, SBCs were associated with postoperative colectomy complications. The strongest associations were observed with SBCs ascertained within the 90-day window, and the odds increased in a dose-response relationship with increasing SBC burden.

items.title: Metro-Pancreas Stratifies Survival After Neoadjuvant Chemotherapy and Surgery for Resectable Pancreatic Cancer
items.abstract: Objective: To assess the prognostic utility of the Metro-Pancreas framework in resectable pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) treated with neoadjuvant chemotherapy (NAT) and resection. Summary Background Data: Upfront surgery and NAT are options in anatomically resectable PDAC. Metro-Pancreas combines tumor size and CA 19-9 to stratify prognosis after upfront resection, but its applicability after NAT is unknown. Methods: We analyzed 623 patients with nonmetastatic, anatomically resectable PDAC who underwent NAT followed by resection from 5 institutions (2016–2024). Metro-Pancreas classification ( IN/OUT ) was determined by tumor size and CA19-9 levels. Treatment response followed NCCN 2026 definition based on radiologic and biochemical changes. Postoperative disease-free survival (DFS) and overall survival (OS) were evaluated. Results: At diagnosis, 263 patients (42.2%) were Metro-Pancreas OUT and had shorter postoperative DFS (13.3 vs. 16.7 mo; P =0.003) and OS (29.5 vs. 34.8 mo; P =0.006) than Metro-Pancreas IN patients. After NAT, 71.9% of OUT patients were reclassified as IN , while 5.0% of initially IN patients became OUT . Among baseline OUT patients, 35.7% had significant response, 46.0% had minimal response, and 18.3% had progression. Prognostic separation was greater at Metro-Pancreas restaging (DFS: 7.7 vs. 17.3 mo; OS: 15.8 vs. 36.7 mo; both P =0.001). Patients reclassified from OUT to IN had postoperative DFS and OS comparable to those initially IN ( P =0.806 and P =0.631, respectively). Conclusions: Among patients undergoing resection after NAT, Metro-Pancreas stratified prognosis at diagnosis and more effectively at restaging. Reclassification from OUT to IN was associated with favorable postoperative survival, supporting dynamic prognostic reassessment in the neoadjuvant setting.

items.title: Adjuvant Hepatic Arterial Infusion Pump Chemotherapy Without Systemic Therapy After Repeat Local Treatment for Patients With Liver-only Recurrence of Colorectal Cancer
items.abstract: Background: Approximately 30% of patients develop liver-confined recurrences after local treatment for colorectal liver metastases (CRLM), which may be reduced by adjuvant therapy. Hepatic arterial infusion pump (HAIP) chemotherapy delivers high-dose liver-directed chemotherapy. Objective: To investigate adjuvant HAIP chemotherapy without systemic therapy in patients with resectable liver-confined recurrence after prior local treatment of CRLM. Methods: This multicenter, single-arm phase II trial enrolled patients with resectable recurrent CRLM across 3 centers in the Netherlands. Patients with prior or present extrahepatic disease were excluded. Adjuvant HAIP with floxuridine was administered up to 6 cycles. The primary endpoint was hepatic disease-free survival (hDFS) estimated using the Kaplan–Meier method, with a prespecified efficacy boundary of 36 months. Results: Forty-five patients underwent local treatment followed by adjuvant HAIP chemotherapy without systemic therapy. Twenty-eight patients(62%) were treated for a first recurrent CRLM, and 17 patients for a second or higher. Twenty-five patients (56%) had ≥3 CRLM. All patients started HAIP chemotherapy, with a median of 6 cycles (interquartile range: 4 to 6). After a median follow-up of 38.7 months (95% CI: 33.0–42.3), the median hDFS was 16.5 months (95% CI: 9.1–25.8). The median progression-free survival was 14.0 months (95% CI: 7.7–23.0), and the 3-year overall survival was 71% (95% CI: 58%–87%). Initial recurrence included the liver in 23 patients (51%). HAIP implantation-related complications (Clavien–Dindo grade ≥3) occurred in 4 patients (9%), and HAIP chemotherapy-related complications (Common Terminology Criteria for Adverse Events grade ≥3) occurred in 6 patients (13%). Biliary sclerosis occurred in 4 patients; 3 required stent placement. Conclusion: Adjuvant HAIP chemotherapy without systemic therapy did not achieve the hypothesized hDFS in patients undergoing repeat local treatment for recurrent CRLM.
